chapters.title: Average
chapters.summary: A comprehensive guide to understanding arithmetic mean, weighted averages, age-related average problems, and shortcut techniques for competitive exams.
chapters.questionsJson: [{"id":"376d8370-6006-4929-9daa-960bc2b3d5c0","questionText":"If the ages of 4 students are 20 years, 22 years, 18 years, and 24 years, what is the average age of the students?","options":["20 years","21 years","22 years","23 years"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Average age = (20 + 22 + 18 + 24) \/ 4 = 84 \/ 4 = 21 years.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"ed7055fb-ef42-41f0-818f-5d83e29985a9","questionText":"The average age of 6 persons is increased by 2 years when one of them, whose age is 26 years, is replaced by a new man. When the teacher's age is excluded, the average decreases by 1. What is the age of the teacher?","options":["40 years","39 years","41 years","43 years"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Total initial members = 24 boys + 1 teacher = 25. \[
\frac{7}{10}+\frac{3}{5}-\frac{1}{2}

\[
\frac{(2+3)^3+(2-3)^3}{2^2+3^2}
\]","options":["2","3","4","5"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"2 \[ (2+3)³=5³=125 \] \[ (2-3)³=(-1)³=-1 \] Numerator: \[ 125-1=124 \] Denominator: \[ 2²⁺³²=4+9=13 \] \[ 124\div13=\boxed{?} \] Since \(124=13\times9.538...\), this does not give a clean answer. This question should be discarded/replaced. Replacement: \[ \frac{(2+3)³⁻(2-3)³}{2²⁺³²} \] \[ =\frac{125-(-1)}{13} =\frac{126}{13} \] Also not suitable. Discard both rather than memorising a flawed question.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"}]

chapters.title: LCM and HCF
chapters.summary: A comprehensive guide to Highest Common Factor (HCF) and Least Common Multiple (LCM), covering fundamental definitions, core algebraic formulas, fractional/decimal calculations, remainder theorems, and practical problem-solving techniques.
chapters.questionsJson: [{"id":"65a2f02a-428a-40f3-a096-9ca8060a89d4","questionText":"The LCM of two numbers is 2079 and their HCF is 27. If the first number is 189, find the second number.","options":["324","297","252","360"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Using the product formula: HCF x LCM = First Number x Second Number. Substituting the values: 27 x 2079 = 189 x Second Number. Second Number = (27 x 2079) \/ 189 = 2079 \/ 7 = 297.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"783469ce-c128-4286-8d14-7eca9431fa27","questionText":"Find the LCM and HCF of 25\/6 and 15\/4.","options":["73\/2, 5\/2","75\/2, 7\/12","75\/2, 5\/12","77\/2, 5\/12"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"LCM of fractions = LCM of numerators (25, 15) \/ HCF of denominators (6, 4) = 75 \/ 2. HCF of fractions = HCF of numerators (25, 15) \/ LCM of denominators (6, 4) = 5 \/ 12.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"4561408b-4b55-4d45-83d1-e0c7efaf74fe","questionText":"Find the LCM of 0.6, 9.6, and 0.12.","options":["9.60","9.70","8.90","10.12"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"First, equalize the decimal places: 0.60, 9.60, and 0.12. The greatest common factor is 12.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"6572880a-5695-4693-b6c5-766442957989","questionText":"Find the LCM of 8 and 12.","options":["16","24","32","48"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"24 Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24, 32... The first common multiple is 24.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"f1b8377c-0a5d-40f2-b5af-0b263ce44b17","questionText":"Find the HCF of 45, 60 and 75.","options":["5","10","15","20"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"15 15 divides all three numbers: 45 ÷ 15 = 3, 60 ÷ 15 = 4, 75 ÷ 15 = 5. So HCF = 18.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"5109c78a-b592-4fbe-8a3a-70fd7a622278","questionText":"Find the LCM of 16 and 24.","options":["32","48","64","96"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"48 16 = \\(2⁴\\) 24 = \\(2³\\times3\\) LCM = \\(2⁴\\times3=48\\).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"dd378632-fab3-487f-81c0-0e3a1abd69fd","questionText":"What is the HCF of 105 and 175?","options":["15","25","35","45"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"35 105 = 35 × 3 175 = 35 × 5 Therefore, HCF = 35.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"487bb283-da82-49a9-afd4-bc0941808c7a","questionText":"What is the smallest number which when divided by 8, 12 and 18 leaves no remainder?","options":["36","48","72","144"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"72 We need the LCM of 8, 12 and 18. LCM = 72.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"e629f7d4-0e6b-42c0-a270-cbfcca49ad15","questionText":"Find the HCF of 120 and 168.","options":["12","18","24","36"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"24 120 = 24 × 5 168 = 24 × 7 So the greatest common factor is 24.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"66a73d6d-7172-4a18-8bb2-4d1fa95c2a58","questionText":"Find the LCM of 14, 21 and 28.","options":["42","56","84","112"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"84 14 = 2 × 7 21 = 3 × 7 28 = \\(2²\\times7\\) LCM = \\(2²\\times3\\times7=84\\).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"748498bf-4325-4198-82eb-b26be182e568","questionText":"Two numbers have HCF 6 and LCM 180. Therefore, the correct answer should be 100, which is not given in the options.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"151d830a-3636-4587-bd88-f2d7bc967998","questionText":"Find the LCM of 25, 30 and 40.","options":["300","400","500","600"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"600 25 = \\(5²\\) 30 = \\(2\\times3\\times5\\) 40 = \\(2³\\times5\\) LCM = \\(2³\\times3\\times5²=600\\).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"4b200a62-d2a8-475a-bbac-9fa9bbc34dfa","questionText":"Find the HCF of 64, 80 and 96.","options":["8","16","24","32"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"16 64 ÷ 16 = 4 80 ÷ 16 = 5 96 ÷ 16 = 6 Therefore, HCF = 16.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"5cfa8a8b-656b-41d9-8f16-beb11297b692","questionText":"Find the smallest number which is divisible by 10, 15 and 25.","options":["50","75","100","150"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"150 LCM of 10, 15 and 25: 10 = 2 × 5 15 = 3 × 5 25 = \\(5²\\) LCM = \\(2\\times3\\times5²=150\\).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"f584b64d-6c32-41fb-9bd3-6c74d0e185b7","questionText":"Find the HCF of 54, 90 and 126.","options":["9","18","27","36"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"18 54 = 18 × 3 90 = 18 × 5 126 = 18 × 7 Thus HCF = 18.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"266b991d-b72c-4770-b040-7b800e6c8c60","questionText":"Find the LCM of 7, 11 and 13.","options":["91","1001","1101","1111"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"1001 These are different prime numbers, so their LCM is their product: \\[ 7\\times11\\times13=1001. \\]","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"91ad5925-4278-4355-9497-af7832fc1958","questionText":"The HCF of two numbers is 12 and their product is 1728. The required number is 5 more than 60: \\[ 60+5=65. \\]","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"10bc7a9e-ff6d-49b9-b15b-0b9462c19448","questionText":"Find the greatest number that divides 52, 78 and 104 exactly.","options":["13","26","39","52"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"26 52 = 26 × 2 78 = 26 × 3 104 = 26 × 4 Therefore, HCF = 26.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"484d4283-1b00-45e9-b8b8-3c1c4dee139c","questionText":"Three bells ring at intervals of 6, 8 and 12 minutes. Multiples near 1000 are 720, 960, 1200. chapters.title: Fairs and Festivals
chapters.summary: An exhaustive guide to the vibrant cultural tapestry of Jammu and Kashmir, detailing the major Hindu, Buddhist, and Islamic fairs and festivals, their legendary origins, and regional significance.

chapters.summary: This chapter provides a comprehensive analysis of the agricultural landscape, land use patterns, agro-climatic zones, and major crops of Jammu and Kashmir, alongside key legislative frameworks, irrigation systems, the Right to Information Act, and the transboundary Indus Waters Treaty.

chapters.title: History Of Kashmir
chapters.summary: This chapter provides a comprehensive historical account of Kashmir, tracing its origins from ancient legends and the Neolithic age through various dynasties, foreign invasions, and colonial transitions up to the modern Dogra rule.

page position and word count.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"acfc6e7a-3fa2-4cf5-b949-d79a0be9b309","questionText":"Which of the following is the correct sequence for moving existing text to another chapters.title: Operating System
chapters.summary: This chapter provides a comprehensive overview of Operating Systems, including processing models, core services, CPU scheduling metrics, scheduling algorithms, and memory management concepts.
chapters.questionsJson: [{"id":"31020ae6-c217-475d-b1e2-0d3df98d5a45","questionText":"Which CPU scheduling algorithm is prone to the Convoy Effect?","options":["Round Robin (RR)","First-In, First-Out (FIFO \/ FCFS)","Shortest Remaining Time First (SRTF)","Multi-Level Queue Scheduling"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"The Convoy Effect occurs in FIFO scheduling when a long process occupies the CPU, causing all subsequent shorter processes to wait for a long time.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"312401ac-81fe-4d02-8dab-9544bcc1faad","questionText":"What is the term used to describe a state where the operating system spends more time swapping pages in and out of virtual memory than executing actual instructions?","options":["Fragmentation","Segmentation Fault","Thrashing","Swapping"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Thrashing occurs when the system is low on physical memory, causing it to constantly swap pages between RAM and disk, severely degrading performance.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"81e5ef52-9481-499d-acc3-3b2827dce69a","questionText":"Which scheduler controls the overall degree of multiprogramming by selecting processes from the disk job pool and loading them into RAM?","options":["Short-Term Scheduler","Medium-Term Scheduler","Long-Term Scheduler","CPU Dispatcher"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"The Long-Term Scheduler (or Job Scheduler) determines which programs are admitted to the system for processing, thereby controlling the degree of multiprogramming.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"fc23d673-09c7-4443-a462-b640d596a2cc","questionText":"In dynamic memory allocation, which strategy allocates the smallest block that is large enough to satisfy the process request?","options":["First Fit","Best Fit","Worst Fit","Next Fit"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Best Fit searches the entire list of free blocks and allocates the smallest block that is large enough, minimizing leftover wasted space.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"6c31211c-6322-4265-b5b3-a2d8b1181102","questionText":"What is the formula to calculate Turnaround Time?","options":["Turnaround Time = Waiting Time - Burst Time","Turnaround Time = Completion Time - Arrival Time","Turnaround Time = Response Time + Arrival Time","Turnaround Time = Completion Time - Waiting Time"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Turnaround Time is the total time elapsed from the moment a process is submitted (Arrival Time) to the moment it completes execution (Completion Time).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"29720090-a80d-4d27-a5e7-f719f5cefbce","questionText":"What is an Operating System?","options":["Interface between user and computer hardware","Collection of software programs that manages hardware resources","System software that acts as a master control program","All of the above"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Operating System (OS) ek system software hai jo hardware aur user ke beech interface ka kaam karta hai aur saare system resources (CPU, Memory, I\/O devices) ko manage karta hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"053729cb-ff35-4194-ab89-e279ce0b55aa","questionText":"Which of the following is an example of a Real-Time Operating System (RTOS)?","options":["Windows 10","MS-DOS","VxWorks","Ubuntu"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"VxWorks, LynxOS aur RTLinux real-time operating systems ke udaharan hain, jahan strict time constraints me kaam karna hota hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"d2acbb99-51af-453b-a83f-6acd1b2e785c","questionText":"The core component of an operating system that remains in main memory and manages system resources is called ........","options":["Shell","Kernel","Command Prompt","Device Driver"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Kernel operating system ka sabse mukhya (core) hissa hota hai jo hardware aur software ke beech direct communication karwata hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"90f3e419-c7c8-41af-acc9-b1c0acba78a1","questionText":"The process of loading the operating system into the computer's main memory (RAM) when turned on is known as ........","options":["Formatting","Booting","Debugging","Processing"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"System start hote hi ROM se OS ko RAM me load karne ki prakriya ko 'Booting' kaha jata hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"06700054-4dd3-4290-8004-097014cbf25a","questionText":"A program in execution is called a ........","options":["Process","Instruction","Command","Function"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Jab koi program active state me run ho raha hota hai, toh use 'Process' kehte hain.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"9d4ab485-8918-4f7a-98a0-334df63f380d","questionText":"SPOOLING stands for ........","options":["Simultaneous Peripheral Operation On-Line","Sequential Processing Of Online Input Output","System Program Organization Online","Storage Performance"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"SPOOLING ka full form 'Simultaneous Peripheral Operation On-Line' hai, jo printer ya slow I\/O devices ke data ko buffer memory me hold karke process karne me madad karta hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"360ecd13-7442-4eb8-a219-c0945ca36a6f","questionText":"Restarting a restart\/reboot karne ko 'Warm Booting' (Soft Booting) kehte hain, jabki band computer ko start karne ko 'Cold Booting' kehte hain.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"a21d726a-38d9-41cb-a096-8beaf01acbf8","questionText":"Which scheduler dictates what processes are to run on a system, and the degree of concurrency to be supported processes ko queue se memory me laata hai aur degree of multiprogramming\/concurrency ko nishchit karta hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"c11fd8a7-add8-438f-9370-ce580fa8e98b","questionText":"Which scheduler temporarily removes processes from main memory and places them on secondary memory or vice-versa?","options":["Long-term scheduler","Mid-term scheduler","Admission scheduler","Short-term scheduler"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Mid-term scheduler processes ko main memory se secondary memory (swapping out) me bhejta hai taaki memory space free ho sake.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"2b9edd92-008b-47f0-8cd8-05dd12549ea7","questionText":"The short-term scheduler makes scheduling decisions much more frequently than ........","options":["long-term scheduler","mid-term scheduler","Both","and"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Short-term scheduler (CPU Scheduler) millisecond level par CPU allocation ke decision leta hai, isliye ye long-term aur mid-term dono se zyaada frequent hota hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"8b90d0bc-cd14-45bc-a314-860c7f8d98d7","questionText":"A long-term scheduler is also known as ........","options":["admission or high-level scheduler","adjust or low-level scheduler","active or mid-level scheduler","None of the above"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Long-term scheduler ko 'Admission Scheduler' ya 'High-level Scheduler' bhi kaha jata hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"c1c9e675-96a0-4bdb-bb97-b08ff27e9b8d","questionText":"Which technique is used to minimize resource starvation?","options":["Switching","Paging","Swapping","Scheduling algorithms"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Efficient scheduling algorithms (aur aging technique) ka istemaal karke starvation (kisi process ka lambe samay tak wait karna) ko roka ya kam kiya jata hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"61c0c330-f1d9-44a2-810d-e5e0aef04948","questionText":"First In First Out is also known as ........","options":["LCFS","FCLS","FCFS","None of these"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"FIFO (First In First Out) ko CPU scheduling me FCFS (First Come First Served) kaha jata hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"ec72e8e5-965d-4158-bf97-7c91bc1c65bd","questionText":"In which strategy the scheduler arranges processes with the least estimated processing time remaining to be jata hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"6c1a9edf-515e-4aaf-98ab-85039ed57be6","questionText":"FPPS stands for ........","options":["Final Priority Post Scheduling","First Priority Past Scheduling","Fixed Priority Pre-emptive Scheduling","Final Priority Pre-emptive Scheduling"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"FPPS ka full form 'Fixed Priority Pre-emptive Scheduling' hai, jisme unche priority wali process aate hi kam priority wali process ko rok deti hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"1ee4282e-b7ba-4a9e-a3b6-838c68878247","questionText":"The scheduler assigns a fixed time unit per process and cycles through them in ........","options":["FCFS","FPPS","SJF","Round-robin"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Round-robin scheduling me har process ko ek fixed time slice (Time Quantum) diya jata hai aur cycle me baari-baari mauka milta hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"00afb3bb-a6b5-4885-a3f5-61d5e67d4180","questionText":"Which scheduling is used for situations in which processes are easily divided into different groups?","options":["Multilevel queue","Round-robin","FPPS","FCFS"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Multilevel Queue Scheduling me processes ko unke nature ke aadhar par alag-alag queues (jaise Foreground\/Interactive vs Background\/Batch) me baanta jata hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"5495f9b6-ad9c-406d-ba02-beb4ea7651d5","questionText":"To prevent a bug within a process from affecting other processes, or the operating system itself, ........ is used.","options":["memory allocation","memory detection","memory protection","None of the above"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Memory protection mechanism ensure karta hai ki ek process doosri process ya OS ke reserved memory space me interfere na kare.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"9a11c642-20f6-4289-bbcc-4ac2c9d3cf30","questionText":"Which refers to dividing a computer's memory modules\/segments (jaise code, data, stack) me baanta jata hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"5b269fc3-8362-438e-9f28-8b3606e856ff","questionText":"The physical memory address space is divided into equal fixed-sized small pieces, called ........","options":["slots","segments","pages","None of these"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Paging memory management technique me logical memory ko equal-sized 'Pages' aur physical memory ko 'Frames' me baanta jata hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"0679b297-3d47-46d5-bd84-3d4f6ad7556a","questionText":"A protection key is a mechanism ........","options":["to divide virtual memory into blocks of a particular size","to divide physical memory into blocks of a particular size","to manipulate physical memory into blocks of a particular size","None of the above"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Protection keys physical memory blocks ke saath associate ki jati hain taaki unauthorized processes unhe access na kar sakein.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"1ef80cdd-3134-4550-8788-16b64f3711ff","questionText":"A computer can store and retrieve data from secondary storage for use in main memory by ........","options":["paging","segmentation","simulation","None of these"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Paging technique non-contiguous memory allocation allow karti hai jisse data secondary storage se RAM me laya jata hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"8aaa74ab-2b12-43c4-baba-789644c9dc95","questionText":"Anticipatory paging is also called ........","options":["swapping","swap prefetch","spooling","None of these"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Anticipatory paging (Prepaging) ko 'swap prefetch' bhi kehte hain, jisme zarurat padne se pehle hi pages ko predict karke ........","options":["segmentation","swapping","prevention","page replacement \/ virtual memory"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Demand paging me pages ko tabhi RAM me laya jata hai jab unki requirement (demand) hoti hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"81d0fe2b-a350-4245-96be-83267348e75b","questionText":"The page free queue is a list of page frames that are available for assignment after karta hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"1f5628c1-5d23-46de-9e02-7dd261194301","questionText":"Pages are swapped out and then accessed causing frequent page faults is called ........","options":["swapping","paging","segmentation","thrashing"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Jab OS ka zyada samay execution ke bajaye continuous page swapping in\/out me hi beeth jaye, toh us sthiti ko 'Thrashing' kehte hain.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"52ec3240-cd75-4a8a-aac0-1b142084a49e","questionText":"What is a process that reduces the amount of fragmentation in karta hai aur performance badata hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"ef5493b0-447b-4d38-a21f-7be964965baa","questionText":"Many operating systems can 'trick' programs into using memory scattered Memory ek illusion (aabhas) pradan karti hai jisse programs RAM ki vastavik kshamta se bade size me bhi run ho sakte hain.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"89c1fec9-9f09-4a2e-8aca-131b47d02e03","questionText":"A ........ is an interrupt\/trap raised by hardware when a program accesses a page that is mapped in the virtual address space, but not loaded in physical memory.","options":["starvation","thrashing","defragmentation","page fault"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Jab requested page RAM (physical memory) me maujood nahi hota, tab 'Page Fault' occur hota hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"1af46ee1-413e-4d17-a465-25338ac31db2","questionText":"If the page is loaded in memory at the time the fault is generated, but is not marked in the memory management unit as being loaded in memory, it is called ........","options":["minor page fault","major page fault","invalid page fault","None of the above"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Minor page fault tab hota hai jab page RAM me toh hota hai par Page Table me mapping missing hoti hai (bina disk read ke solve ho jata hai).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"a647b8bb-b16b-4b4c-a803-809443fc8aba","questionText":"If the page is not loaded in memory at the time the fault is generated, requiring disk I\/O, it is called ........","options":["invalid page fault","minor page fault","major page fault","None of the above"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Major page fault tab hota hai jab required page ko secondary storage (hard disk) se fetch karke RAM me lana padta hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"1b5bcc9f-a8f4-4bad-9805-5541464f42bc","questionText":"If a page fault occurs for a reference to an address process ek aise address ko access karne ki koshish karti hai jo uske address space me hai hi nahi, toh use 'Invalid Page Fault' (Segmentation Fault) kehte hain.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"c0b5c3ea-c517-4503-8277-a8b7074bccd3","questionText":"If the swapping algorithm is not efficient then a high page fault condition occurs known as ........","options":["paging","thrashing","scheduling","None of the above"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Inefficient swapping ki wajah se CPU ka zyadatar time page replacement me barbaad hone lagta hai, jise 'Thrashing' kaha jata hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"a4143fdf-0986-47f2-b29f-bc6419500539","questionText":"The three most popular strategies used to allocate space to processes above"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Memory allocation ke teen mukhya algorithms hain: First Fit (pehle milne wale block me rakhna), Best Fit (sabse sateek chhotey block me), aur Worst Fit (sabse bade block me).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"12b0fffa-a900-4a85-bacb-a7e1e8c125c6","questionText":"........ runs on computer hardware and serves as a platform for other software to run on.","options":["System software","Operating system","Application software","All of the above"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Operating System hardware par sidhe run hota hai aur Application Softwares ke chalne ke liye ek platform pradan karta hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"7e5793bc-8621-4a83-8eed-2005cf498c64","questionText":"The primary purpose of an operating system is ........","options":["to keep systems programmers employed","to make the most efficient use of the computer hardware","to allow people to use the computer","to make computers easier to use"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Operating system ka mukhya uddeshya computer hardware resources (CPU, Memory, Disk) ka kushal aur prabhavshali (efficient) istemaal karna hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"6a53c126-432c-4ae6-97bc-101d45f2e5d2","questionText":"A situation where two or more processes are blocked forever, waiting for each other to release resources, is called ........","options":["Starvation","Deadlock","Aging","Paging"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Deadlock ek aisi sthiti hai jahan do ya do se zyada processes ek doosre ke paas maujood resources ka intezaar karti rehti hain aur koi aage nahi badhti.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"32d2424a-f76f-4db3-a7aa-ab850793c6b2","questionText":"Which of the following is NOT one of necessary conditions for Deadlock to occur?","options":["Mutual Exclusion","Hold and Wait","Preemption allowed","Circular Wait"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Deadlock hone ke liye \"No Preemption\" zaruri hota hai. Agar preemption allowed hoga toh OS resource chheen sakta hai aur deadlock nahi hoga.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"659da8d6-cf9d-4328-be88-5aaa1d197e5b","questionText":"Banker's Algorithm is used for ........","options":["Deadlock Prevention","Deadlock Avoidance","Deadlock Detection","Deadlock Recovery"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Banker's algorithm ek mashhoor 'Deadlock Avoidance' algorithm hai jo safe state ensure karke deadlock hone se bachata hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"4f5b0243-ee42-4fe3-9788-9903f87dad44","questionText":"What is Context Switching in Operating Systems?","options":["Switching from one user account to another","Saving state of a process and loading state of another process into CPU","Moving data from RAM to Hard Disk","Changing screen resolution"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"CPU jab ek process se doosri process par switch karta hai, toh purani process ka state save karna aur nayi process ka state restore karna 'Context Switching' kehlata hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"390ce7dd-2786-4486-815f-9e2761084a91","questionText":"Multi-tasking operating systems are based on which scheduling concept?","options":["Time sharing","Batch processing","First Come First Served","Real-time execution"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Multi-tasking operating systems 'Time Sharing' par aadharit hote hain jahan CPU ka time sabhi tasks me tezi se divide hota hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"88736d90-4923-4e27-827d-a7388588dd28","questionText":"Which user interface allows users to interact with the OS using graphical icons and visual indicators?","options":["CLI (Command Line Interface)","GUI (Graphical User Interface)","TUI (Text User Interface)","API (Application Programming Interface)"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"GUI (jaise Windows, macOS) user ko mouse aur icons dwara aasan interaction ki suvidha deta hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"839c812d-4adf-49d4-8ed5-23c2328770d2","questionText":"MS-DOS is an example of which type of Operating System interface?","options":["GUI","CUI \/ CLI","Touch Interface","Voice Interface"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"MS-DOS ek Command Line \/ Character User Interface (CLI\/CUI) OS hai jahan text commands type karni padti hain.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"11d25599-493c-47b6-8778-bb265282813b","questionText":"Internal memory fragmentation occurs when ........","options":["total memory space is enough but not contiguous","allocated memory block is slightly larger than the requested process size","processes are frequently swapped out","page fault occurs repeatedly"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Fixed-size allocation me jab allocated space process ke size se bada hota hai, toh bacha hua space internal fragmentation ban jata hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"9327a4e8-8734-4fa9-be0c-c785a5d9233e","questionText":"What is a Semaphore in Operating Systems?","options":["A hardware device","An integer variable used for process synchronization and","A page replacement technique","A type of virus"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"ving critical section problems Semaphore ek synchronization tool (integer variable) hai jo multiple processes ko shared resources safely access karne me madad karta hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"2323a844-8b42-47d2-8be0-8d9f9aeb1b1a","questionText":"The region of memory shared between processes where concurrent access must be controlled is called ........","options":["Shared Section","Critical Section","Protected Section","Priority Queue"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Critical Section code ka wo hissa hai jahan shared resources access hote hain aur ek samay par ek hi process chalni chahiye (Mutual Exclusion).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"89e7a919-fefd-4641-ae6b-79ed8119a37d","questionText":"Aging is a technique used to solve the problem of ........","options":["Deadlock","Starvation","Thrashing","Page Fault"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Aging technique me lambe samay se wait kar rahi processes ki priority gradualy badhai jaati hai taaki 'Starvation' khatam ho sake.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"84ae5339-8bee-4c0c-9e41-6f36e91ec721","questionText":"Which file system is commonly used by modern Microsoft Windows operating systems?","options":["FAT32","ext4","NTFS","HFS+"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"NTFS (New Technology File System) modern Windows OS ka primary file system hai jo better security aur compression deta hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"1475d219-55ca-4630-838c-ac28fb74e5b6","questionText":"Virtual memory size depends directly on ........","options":["Size of RAM only","Size of Data Bus","Size of Address Bus \/ Swap space on disk","Processor Clock Speed"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Virtual memory ka maximum limit CPU ke address bus aur disk ke swap space (page file) ke size par nirbhar karta hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"c31f1afb-5257-472b-b68d-e3978ddf5c68","questionText":"In Page Replacement Algorithms, LRU stands for ........","options":["Longest Remaining Unit","Least Recently Used","Last Registered User","Least Rare Utility"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"LRU (Least Recently Used) ek popular page replacement algorithm hai jo us page ko replace karta hai jiska istemaal sabse purane samay me hua tha.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"}]

chapters.title: Articles
chapters.summary: This chapter covers the rules, usage, and exceptions of English articles, distinguishing between indefinite (a/an) and definite (the) articles, as well as the conditions for omitting articles entirely.
chapters.questionsJson: [{"id":"5a6ded63-35fd-45b9-8375-e07b8cd3c290","questionText":"Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct?","options":["He is an university student.","He is a honest man.","She bought an one-rupee coin.","He is an MP from our constituency."],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"'MP' is pronounced 'em-pee', which begins with a vowel sound \/e\/, so it correctly takes 'an'. 'University' starts with a consonant sound \/y\/, 'honest' starts with a vowel sound (silent h), and 'one' starts with a consonant sound \/w\/.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"8d1c7a01-8e4a-47a7-adbf-fe483b17ba29","questionText":"Choose the correct sentence regarding the use of articles with institutional places:","options":["The injured man was rushed to the hospital for treatment.","My father went to school to meet the principal.","The thief was sent to prison.","They go to the church every Sunday to pray."],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"When referring to the primary purpose of an institution (a thief going to prison as an inmate), no article is used. For secondary purposes (father visiting school, visiting hospital), 'the' is used. For primary worship, 'go to church' is correct without 'the'.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"9f6e5e63-58ef-4942-9f5a-2aa5f4574a0b","questionText":"Identify the sentence with the correct use of articles:","options":["The Mount Everest is the highest peak in the Himalayas.","Mount Everest is the highest peak in the Himalayas.","The Mount Everest is the highest peak in Himalayas.","Mount Everest is highest peak in the Himalayas."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Individual mountain peaks (Mount Everest) do not take 'the', but mountain ranges (the Himalayas) do. chapters.title: Computer Security
chapters.summary: This chapter explores the core principles of computer security, including the CIA Triad, various types of malware and digital threats, and the essential safeguards and solutions used to protect digital systems.
chapters.questionsJson: [{"id":"d8814c5f-eb3a-4c44-a140-833f232534bb","questionText":"Which of the following core principles of the CIA Triad ensures that digital information remains accurate, complete, and unaltered throughout its lifecycle?","options":["Confidentiality","Integrity","Availability","Non-repudiation"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Integrity ensures that files, messages, and databases cannot be edited, tampered with, deleted, or forged by unauthorized parties without detection.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"d18252c9-c2ef-4dba-9a25-3969789e6abe","questionText":"What is the primary difference between a computer virus and a computer worm?","options":["A virus is host file.","A virus only targets hardware, while a worm only targets software.","A worm requires a host file to execute, whereas a virus operates independently."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"A computer worm is a standalone, self-replicating program that spreads across networks automatically without requiring a host file or direct human action, unlike a virus which must attach to a host file.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"34784aae-6d0a-4a71-a664-c9ed4b87f98d","questionText":"A malicious program that disguises itself as a chapters.title: Analogy
chapters.summary: This chapter covers the core concepts of analogies, exploring various relationship types such as antonyms, synonyms, object-to-tool, and intensity, along with step-by-step solving strategies and common pitfalls.

chapters.title: Uses of Prepositions
chapters.summary: A comprehensive guide to understanding, classifying, and correctly applying simple, compound, and phrase prepositions in English grammar, complete with high-yield exam rules and comparisons.
chapters.questionsJson: [{"id":"5f84844f-6345-455e-8f58-fdaaa576ec8a","questionText":"Choose the grammatically correct sentence from the options below.","options":["He prefers tea than coffee.","He prefers tea to coffee.","He prefers tea over coffee.","He prefers tea for coffee."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"The verb 'prefer' is followed by the preposition 'to' when comparing two nouns. Sakshi.","options":["by","for","in","with"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Fixed idiomatic phrase: 'Fall in love' (pyar me padna).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"8957e797-407c-42de-8f86-bb320eab603a","questionText":"Fill in the blank with the suitable preposition: I got your parcel ........ Tuesday.","options":["since","for","to","on"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Saptah ke dino (days of the week) ke aage 'on' lagta hai (on Tuesday).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"f5bd150c-3d6d-4f18-b0f3-a4ee242b3e3b","questionText":"Fill in the blank with the suitable preposition: She was married ........ an early age.","options":["for","of","at","in"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Kisi umar ke padav ya bindu ko darshane ke liye 'at' preposition lagta hai (at an early age).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"426a2fe5-4d07-48aa-9e30-932072fef0c8","questionText":"Fill in the blank with the suitable preposition: His father died ........ the age of sixty three.","options":["at","in","for","of"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Age batane ke liye 'at the age of' ka prayog hota hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"877d73ce-d59e-46a2-a060-3242601438e8","questionText":"Fill in the blank with the suitable preposition: He has been unwell ........ Saturday.","options":["on","in","since","from"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Perfect\/Perfect continuous tense me nischit samay (point of time) ke liye 'since' lagta hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"62445aa8-5392-4d6e-ae2f-fb606a6d8191","questionText":"Fill in the blank with the suitable preposition: The man ........ a beard is my brother.","options":["in","of","for","with"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Kisi vyakti ki vaishishtya ya gun batane ke liye 'with' lagta hai (a man with a beard).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"a789b465-db1e-4f59-b2ca-5081d2d294a5","questionText":"Fill in the blank with the suitable preposition: His father died ........ cancer.","options":["in","of","by","for"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Kisi bimari se maut hone par 'die of a disease' (died of cancer) hota hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"06da20a0-7362-4194-8d4b-75269ff5634b","questionText":"Fill in the blank with the suitable preposition: He is not an honest man. You cannot rely ........ him.","options":["to","for","at","on"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Fixed verb-preposition: 'Rely on' (bharosa karna).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"16c69bbb-c895-470f-93c9-e1e87d9d21df","questionText":"Fill in the blank with the suitable preposition: He was fined ........ driving negligently.","options":["to","of","by","for"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Kisi karan ya apradh ke liye fine lagne par 'fined for' hota hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"b53d2523-6ce8-49e3-b2a7-a0fd03fc2c5e","questionText":"Fill in the blank with the suitable preposition: He is often late ........ his dinner.","options":["for","at","to","in"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Kisi ghatna ya bhojan ke liye der hone par 'late for' ka prayog hota hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"08d074c6-dfec-4400-b172-e38680033be4","questionText":"Fill in the blank with the suitable preposition: Try to reach the village ........ the sunset.","options":["before","by","from","of"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"kisi samay ya ghatna se pehle pahunchne ke liye 'before' preposition ka use hota hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"f1d77880-c92c-4427-855b-d0860c0ebf3b","questionText":"Find out which part of the sentence has an error: Mohan leapt (a) \/ on the opportunity (b) \/ that came in his way. (c) \/ No error (d)","options":["Part (a)","Part (b)","Part (c)","Part (d)"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Part (b) me galti hai. 'Leapt on' ki jagah 'leapt at' ka prayog hona chahiye (leapt at the opportunity = mauka lapakna).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"41a7c246-0420-408b-ba74-f91babda5fd8","questionText":"Find out which part of the sentence has an error: The lovers walked (a) \/ besides each other (b) \/ in silence. (c) \/ No error (d)","options":["Part (a)","Part (b)","Part (c)","Part (d)"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Part (b) me galti hai. 'Besides' ka matlab 'ke alawa' hota hai, jabki 'paas me\/saath me' ke liye 'beside' lagna chahiye.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"06378da1-cd3c-4796-a6ee-4bd3b516fddb","questionText":"Find out which part of the sentence has an error: Smoking is undoubtedly (a) \/ very injurious (b) \/ for health. (c) \/ No error (d)","options":["Part (a)","Part (b)","Part (c)","Part (d)"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Part (c) me galti hai. 'Injurious' ke saath hamesha preposition 'to' lagta hai ('injurious to health'), 'for' nahi.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"6bbf47c1-3a33-4c0b-bbe9-01498d3d3b98","questionText":"Find out which part of the sentence has an error: For a long time (a) \/ I did not know who was sitting besides me (b) \/ because it was so dark. (c) \/ No error (d)","options":["Part (a)","Part (b)","Part (c)","Part (d)"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Part (b) me galti hai. 'Besides me' (ke alawa) ki jagah 'beside me' (mere bagal me) hona chahiye.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"41407382-2ba7-4075-bbf8-c0630f03fc3d","questionText":"Find out which part of the sentence has an error: He is guilty (a) \/ for killing (b) \/ an innocent bird. (c) \/ No error (d)","options":["Part (a)","Part (b)","Part (c)","Part (d)"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Part (b) me galti hai. 'Guilty' ke saath fixed preposition 'of' lagta hai ('guilty of killing'), 'for' nahi.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"eed0aaba-f99a-4dd5-ab6d-6d961ac31610","questionText":"Find out which part of the sentence has an error: He is very angry on me (a) \/ because I failed (b) \/ to return his book. (c) \/ No error (d)","options":["Part (a)","Part (b)","Part (c)","Part (d)"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Part (a) me galti hai. Kisi vyakti se naraz hone par 'angry with me' ka prayog hota hai, 'angry on me' galat hai.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"bbc7f2fd-a106-48e4-ac25-8acec2bc9fbd","questionText":"Find out which part of the sentence has an error: The teacher advised to (a) \/ the student to borrow (b) \/ a book from the library within three days. (c) \/ No error (d)","options":["Part (a)","Part (b)","Part (c)","Part (d)"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Part (a) me galti hai. 'Advise' transitive verb hai jiske baad direct object (student) aayega, beech me 'to' lagana galat hai ('advised the student').","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"c7fe0583-76ae-4abf-bbd4-7c5c4fb3bc3b","questionText":"Find out which part of the sentence has an error: He served as President (a) \/ of the Lions club (b) \/ since fifteen years. (c) \/ No error (d)","options":["Part (a)","Part (b)","Part (c)","Part (d)"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Part (c) me galti hai. 'Fifteen years' samay ki avadhi (period of time) hai, isliye 'since' ki jagah 'for' ka prayog hoga.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"5a10f7f4-f65b-4663-b6ee-47c2cda95b79","questionText":"Find out which part of the sentence has an error: At his return (a) \/ we asked him (b) \/ many questions. (c) \/ No error (d)","options":["Part (a)","Part (b)","Part (c)","Part (d)"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Part (a) me galti hai. Correct prepositional phrase 'On his return' (uske lautne par) hota hai, 'At his return' nahi.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"a7538973-6a33-4940-a0de-803a3c85b9dc","questionText":"Find out which part of the sentence has an error: The Chief Guest (a) \/ entered into (b) \/ the room. (c) \/ No error (d)","options":["Part (a)","Part (b)","Part (c)","Part (d)"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Part (b) me galti hai. Jab 'enter' ka prayog kisi kamre ya sthan me bhautik roop se pravesh karne ke liye hota hai, toh uske saath 'into' nahi lagta ('entered the room').","difficulty":"MEDIUM"}]

chapters.title: Punctuation
chapters.summary: An essential guide to the rules, functions, and correct usage of punctuation marks in English writing to ensure clarity, precision, and readability.
chapters.questionsJson: [{"id":"df84e8b0-6d2c-40ad-92be-180cf532c6b9","questionText":"Which punctuation mark is used to connect two independent clauses that are closely related in thought without using a coordinating conjunction?","options":["Comma","Semicolon","Colon","Hyphen"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"A semicolon is used to link independent clauses that are closely related in thought when no coordinating conjunction (like 'and' or 'but') is present.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"9ba0033d-5f00-4347-8f74-51b89b821234","questionText":"Identify the sentence that is punctuated correctly.","options":["He asked me what time it was?","He asked me what time it was.","He asked me, what time it was?","He asked me: what time it was."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Indirect questions should end with a period (full stop), not a question mark.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"35435bc7-00df-4d47-8890-e43a37d5f739","questionText":"Which of the following compound numbers requires a hyphen when written as words?","options":["One hundred","Thirty three","Two thousand","Ten thousand"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Compound numbers from twenty-one to ninety-nine require a hyphen when written as words (e.g., thirty-three).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"7c71c40a-e6f5-4e20-91e5-df8e3399cd9f","questionText":"What is the primary function of a colon (:)?","options":["To indicate a sudden shift in thought or interruption","To direct the reader's attention forward to a list, concept, or explanation","To show possession or ownership","To separate coordinate adjectives describing the same noun"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"A colon is used to direct attention forward, introducing lists, concepts, or expanding explanations.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"7a727df2-a512-4e40-ac8d-9764090d85c5","questionText":"In which of the following sentences is the apostrophe used to show contraction?","options":["I believe that is Allen's pen.","The dog's tail wagged happily.","It's a beautiful day outside.","The teachers' lounge is down the hall."],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"'It's' is a contraction of 'it is', where the apostrophe replaces the missing letter 'i'. The other options show possession.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"caad605a-0d04-4c20-9b51-2fcdd7d86f76","questionText":"Choose the sentence that correctly follows the rule of starting every sentence with a capital letter.","options":["he had high fever yesterday.","He had high fever yesterday.","he Had high fever yesterday.","HE HAD HIGH FEVER YESTERDAY."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"According to Rule 1 of Capitalisation, the very first letter of every new sentence must always be a capital letter.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"513eb927-86de-4a6f-ae6a-0284a8f2515b","questionText":"Select the sentence that correctly uses capital letters for proper nouns and titles.","options":["her majesty, mr president visited delhi.","Her majesty, Mr president visited Delhi.","Her Majesty, Mr President visited Delhi.","Her majesty, mr President visited delhi."],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Specific names of people, honorifics, official titles, and places (Her Majesty, Mr President, Delhi) must start with capital letters.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"53871117-95b0-4229-a863-95852d01efce","questionText":"Choose the option that correctly formats acronyms using capital letters.","options":["He works in the cbi and his brother is in the bsf.","He works in the Cbi and his brother is in the Bsf.","He works in the C.b.i. and his brother is in the B.s.f.","He works in the CBI and his brother is in the BSF."],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Acronyms formed from the initial letters of an organization or proper entity (CBI, BSF) are written entirely in capital letters.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"57aa04f3-fe50-4d01-b59b-8aaafb3c6902","questionText":"Select the sentence that correctly uses a full stop (period) to end a declarative statement.","options":["The food was delicious?","The food was delicious!","The food was delicious.","The food was delicious,"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"A full stop \/ period (.) is used at the end of a standard declarative or imperative sentence.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"9afdda30-d986-4a02-8187-3623ffb7dff0","questionText":"Identify the sentence that correctly uses full stops for short forms and abbreviations.","options":["Dr Sharma and Mr Patel arrived at 9 am.","Dr. Sharma and Mr. Patel arrived at 9 a.m.","Dr, Sharma and Mr, Patel arrived at 9 a,m.","Dr; Sharma and Mr; Patel arrived at 9 a;m."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Periods are standardly used after abbreviations and short forms like Dr., Mr., e.g., and a.m.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"e5e569ce-d47f-4b38-8608-d6946c211b4e","questionText":"Select the sentence that correctly uses a question mark for a direct inquiry.","options":["What time is it.","What time is it!","What time is it?","What time it is?"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"A question mark (?) must be placed at the end of a direct interrogative sentence asking a question.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"6a262f4e-5e60-4e88-96a3-b2b56e0528ed","questionText":"Choose the correctly punctuated sentence that avoids using a question mark in an indirect question.","options":["He asked me what time it was?","He asked me what time it was.","He asked me, what time it was?","He asked me: what time it was!"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Indirect questions report what was asked and do NOT take a question mark at the end; they end with a full stop.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"880652fe-8dab-4b81-af91-f213ce95b305","questionText":"Select the sentence that correctly uses an exclamation mark to convey strong excitement or urgency.","options":["Watch out for that truck?","Watch out for that truck.","Watch out for that truck!","Watch out for that truck,"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Exclamation marks (!) are placed at the end of exclamatory sentences or urgent warnings to convey strong emotion or emphasis.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"3d4713ee-c565-46e0-a087-ea8e992385ac","questionText":"Select the sentence that correctly uses a comma to indicate a short pause after addressing a person directly.","options":["Malvika listen to me.","Malvika, listen to me.","Malvika; listen to me.","Malvika: listen to me."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"A comma is used to set off the name of a person being addressed directly in a sentence (Direct Address).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"1910ff1a-6911-4bb9-84c4-e8f604a4c676","questionText":"Choose the sentence that correctly uses commas to separate items listed in a series.","options":["Please buy eggs milk butter and bread.","Please buy eggs, milk, butter, and bread.","Please buy, eggs, milk, butter and bread.","Please buy eggs; milk; butter; and bread."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Commas are used to separate three or more individual words, phrases, or items in a list.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"784a17b9-706a-49f5-b285-1d8fc6c7613d","questionText":"Select the sentence that correctly uses a comma to separate multiple coordinate adjectives modifying the same noun.","options":["He is a charming attentive listener.","He is a charming, attentive listener.","He is a charming; attentive listener.","He is a charming: attentive listener."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"A comma is placed between coordinate adjectives that describe the same noun equally.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"8512da18-e3b0-45a9-9563-e0977478141c","questionText":"Choose the sentence that correctly uses a comma after an introductory prepositional phrase.","options":["After the show Ashok and I went out to dinner.","After the show, Ashok and I went out to dinner.","After, the show Ashok and I went out to dinner.","After the show; Ashok and I went out to dinner."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Introductory phrases at the start of a sentence should be set off from the main clause with a comma.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"28644556-f262-4723-984c-fe5f15f549ba","questionText":"Select the sentence that correctly uses a comma when a dependent clause comes before an independent clause.","options":["Unless you work hard you won't succeed.","Unless you work hard, you won't succeed.","Unless, you work hard you won't succeed.","Unless you work hard; you won't succeed."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"When a sentence begins with a dependent clause (e.g., \"Unless you work hard\"), a comma must follow before the main clause.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"88b759aa-99a0-4cf6-bb53-4072d1ef4a8f","questionText":"Choose the sentence that correctly uses a comma to separate a direct question in a direct address.","options":["Arvind could you come here for a moment?","Arvind, could you come here for a moment?","Arvind; could you come here for a moment?","Arvind: could you come here for a moment?"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Direct address (speaking directly to \"Arvind\") requires a comma to separate the name from the rest of the question.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"55b27716-a632-48b5-8be3-facb57baebc2","questionText":"Select the sentence that correctly uses a comma to separate direct speech quotes from the reporting clause.","options":["\"Silence in the class\" said the teacher.","\"Silence in the class,\" said the teacher.","\"Silence in the class;\" said the teacher.","\"Silence in the class\" : said the teacher."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Direct speech inside quotation marks should be separated from the reporting verb\/clause using a comma inside the quote.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"51b2bea7-4e87-4a7e-a5c0-358b0e451384","questionText":"Choose the sentence that correctly uses a semicolon to link two closely related independent clauses.","options":["My father never goes to bed early, he's afraid to miss his favourite TV serial.","My father never goes to bed early; he's afraid to miss his favourite TV serial.","My father never goes to bed early: he's afraid to miss his favourite TV serial.","My father never goes to bed early - he's afraid to miss his favourite TV serial."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"A semicolon (;) is used to connect two complete independent clauses that are closely related in meaning without using a conjunction.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"f97d8a0e-e50e-4ed6-8f08-157492a06cf2","questionText":"Select the sentence that correctly uses a colon to introduce an enumerated list.","options":["For Diwali, I want the following presents, a video game, a mobile phone and a cricket bat.","For Diwali, I want the following presents; a video game, a mobile phone and a cricket bat.","For Diwali, I want the following presents: a video game, a mobile phone and a cricket bat.","For Diwali, I want the following presents - a video game, a mobile phone and a cricket bat."],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"A colon (:) is used after a complete introductory sentence to direct attention to a following list.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"1bbc5632-b0ee-4a37-8005-6b01d844365c","questionText":"Choose the sentence that correctly uses a colon to introduce an example or concept.","options":["There's only one person old enough to remember that wedding, grandma.","There's only one person old enough to remember that wedding: grandma.","There's only one person old enough to remember that wedding; grandma.","There's only one person old enough to remember that wedding - grandma."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"A colon is used to highlight a specific example, core idea, or person that completes the thought of the sentence.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"8fe62d81-0faa-4878-b006-69c761931c62","questionText":"Select the sentence that correctly uses a colon to expand upon an explanation in a famous quote.","options":["Ask not what your country can do for you, ask what you can do for your country.","Ask not what your country can do for you; ask what you can do for your country.","Ask not what your country can do for you: ask what you can do for your country.","Ask not what your country can do for you - ask what you can do for your country."],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"A colon is used when the second clause directly expands, clarifies, or illustrates the statement before it.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"ba1777af-674e-4b44-8f3c-d307e273dfa5","questionText":"Choose the sentence that correctly uses a hyphen with a prefix attached to a proper noun.","options":["Trans Atlantic flights are costly.","Trans-Atlantic flights are costly.","Trans:Atlantic flights are costly.","Trans;Atlantic flights are costly."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"A hyphen (-) is used between a prefix and a proper capitalized root word (e.g., Trans-Atlantic).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"0df1923d-f34e-4569-ab00-9164f8de8f20","questionText":"Select the sentence that correctly uses hyphens for written compound numbers.","options":["I have lived in this house for thirty three years.","I have lived in this house for thirty-three years.","I have lived in this house for thirty,three years.","I have lived in this house for thirty;three years."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Compound numbers from twenty-one to ninety-nine must be hyphenated when spelled out as words.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"e7ca8554-983e-448a-a456-871b254af7e9","questionText":"Choose the sentence that correctly uses an em-dash to show an abrupt interruption or parenthetical shift in thought.","options":["Salim asked me, with a straight face, I might go, if he could borrow my bike.","Salim asked me—with a straight face, I might go—if he could borrow my bike.","Salim asked me: with a straight face, I might go: if he could borrow my bike.","Salim asked me; with a straight face, I might go; if he could borrow my bike."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Dashes (– or —) are used to signal an abrupt break or sudden parenthetical interruption in a statement.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"7c197822-b58f-41d3-ae20-1ba98bc98ba6","questionText":"Select the sentence that correctly uses quotation marks for enclosing direct spoken dialogue.","options":["\"If you pick up a starving dog and make him prosperous, he will not bite you,\" John said.","'If you pick up a starving dog and make him prosperous, he will not bite you,' John said.","If you pick up a starving dog and make him prosperous, he will not bite you, John said.","\"If you pick up a starving dog and make him prosperous, he will not bite you, John said.\""],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Quotation marks (\" \") enclose exact words spoken by a person, with the comma placed inside the closing mark before the reporting clause.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"9acf03c5-3f44-4fcf-8784-7c3639914f0e","questionText":"Choose the sentence that correctly uses an apostrophe to show singular possession.","options":["I believe that is Allens pen.","I believe that is Allen's pen.","I believe that is Allens' pen.","I believe that is Allen;s pen."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"An apostrophe followed by 's' ('s) is added to a singular noun to show ownership or possession.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"fcbdddd3-e7b2-42ab-85c5-3f7251b9b4ff","questionText":"Select the option that correctly uses an apostrophe for word contractions.","options":["Do not write like this: dont do it.","Do not write like this: don't do it.","Do not write like this: dont' do it.","Do not write like this: do'nt do it."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"In contractions, the apostrophe replaces missing letters (e.g., \"do not\" becomes \"don't\").","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"4a883094-cb18-4f22-bd78-79849b9d1413","questionText":"Choose the sentence that correctly differentiates the possessive 'its' from the contraction 'it's'.","options":["This tree is very recognisable: it's long slender branches droop to the ground.","This tree is very recognisable: its long slender branches droop to the ground.","This tree is very recognisable: its' long slender branches droop to the ground.","This tree is very recognisable: it's' long slender branches droop to the ground."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"\"Its\" (without apostrophe) is the possessive form, while \"it's\" is the contraction for \"it is\" or \"it has\".","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"20501edb-997e-4b40-a230-e4a5dbf8fb2d","questionText":"Select the sentence that uses full stops and capital letters correctly for abbreviating titles before names.","options":["mr President and dr Sharma arrived together.","Mr. President and Dr. Sharma arrived together.","Mr, President and Dr, Sharma arrived together.","mr. President and dr. Sharma arrived together."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Proper titles placed before names take capital letters and period abbreviations (Mr. and Dr.).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"fb6e7a6b-d40b-4df3-8e99-f5bbde46a94b","questionText":"Choose the sentence that correctly uses a comma to set off an introductory word or exclamation at the start.","options":["Yes I am coming to the party.","Yes, I am coming to the party.","Yes; I am coming to the party.","Yes: I am coming to the party."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Introductory words like Yes, No, Well at the beginning of a sentence are set off with a comma.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"dc985010-a4c0-498b-b1ee-b93a0bef93cd","questionText":"Select the sentence that correctly uses quotation marks around the title of an article mentioned in a sentence.","options":["I enjoyed reading Ananya's article How Not to Go Camping.","I enjoyed reading Ananya's article \"How Not to Go Camping\".","I enjoyed reading Ananya's article, How Not to Go Camping.","I enjoyed reading Ananya's article; How Not to Go Camping."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Titles of articles, short stories, or poems are enclosed in quotation marks.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"88b019e1-05ab-4b55-894f-5979238d900f","questionText":"Choose the sentence that correctly uses a semicolon to separate items in a complex list containing internal commas.","options":["We visited Paris, France, Rome, Italy, and Madrid, Spain.","We visited Paris, France; Rome, Italy; and Madrid, Spain.","We visited Paris France: Rome Italy: and Madrid Spain.","We visited Paris France- Rome Italy- and Madrid Spain."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Semicolons are used to separate items in a list if the items themselves already contain internal commas.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"b0aab090-1215-463e-8e28-7a534c74d631","questionText":"Choose the sentence that correctly places a question mark inside quotation marks for a direct question quote.","options":["\"What time does the train leave\"? asked Mary.","\"What time does the train leave?\" asked Mary.","\"What time does the train leave\", asked Mary?","\"What time does the train leave\"! asked Mary."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"When the quoted text itself is a direct question, the question mark is placed inside the quotation marks.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"adf8c906-a039-4756-be73-2c35860cb3ca","questionText":"Select the sentence with the correct use of capital letters for days of the week and months.","options":["The exam is scheduled for monday, 15 august.","The exam is scheduled for Monday, 15 August.","The exam is scheduled for Monday, 15 august.","The exam is scheduled for monday, 15 August."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Days of the week (Monday) and months of the year (August) are proper nouns and must be capitalized.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"c95cb0af-0a5f-4be2-b4ff-8e3b649f74bf","questionText":"Choose the sentence that correctly uses a hyphen in a compound adjective before a noun.","options":["The age of the gigantic high rise apartment block is far from over.","The age of the gigantic high-rise apartment block is far from over.","The age of the gigantic high:rise apartment block is far from over.","The age of the gigantic high;rise apartment block is far from over."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Compound adjectives placed before a noun (like \"high-rise\") are joined with a hyphen.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"4cbd3820-7e2d-4c5a-ae24-e9145e66f25d","questionText":"Select the correctly punctuated sentence using an exclamation mark with an interjection.","options":["Alas, we lost the match!","Alas! We lost the match.","Alas? We lost the match.","Alas; We lost the match."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Interjections expressing sudden grief or emotion (like \"Alas!\") are followed by an exclamation mark, and the next word begins with a capital letter.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"1d0f5ab1-7199-41e0-b7bf-cb2a307b8c72","questionText":"Choose the sentence that correctly uses an apostrophe for plural nouns ending in 's' to show possession.","options":["This is the teachers staff room.","This is the teachers' staff room.","This is the teacher's' staff room.","This is the teachers's staff room."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"For plural nouns already ending in 's' (teachers), ownership is indicated by placing an apostrophe after the 's' (teachers').","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"1291b1d3-026c-40ed-afc4-dbe9be2a6b10","questionText":"Select the sentence that uses commas correctly to enclose a non-essential relative clause (extra information).","options":["Rajiv who has been too busy to keep up with his courses took on too many activities.","Rajiv, who has been too busy to keep up with his courses, took on too many activities.","Rajiv; who has been too busy to keep up with his courses; took on too many activities.","Rajiv: who has been too busy to keep up with his courses: took on too many activities."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Non-essential clauses providing extra descriptive information about a noun are enclosed between two commas.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"d571a899-ef7e-4cad-9700-c109306c0b3b","questionText":"Choose the sentence that correctly avoids placing a colon directly after a verb.","options":["My favourite fruits are: apples, bananas, and grapes.","My favourite fruits are apples, bananas, and grapes.","My favourite fruits are; apples, bananas, and grapes.","My favourite fruits are - apples, bananas, and grapes."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"A colon should not be placed directly after a linking verb (\"are\"); a list following a verb flows without a colon.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"ffcb741e-78ff-45bd-baf4-f3dba229d518","questionText":"Select the sentence that uses a period correctly in decimal numbers.","options":["The total cost was Rs 45,50.","The total cost was Rs 45.50.","The total cost was Rs 45:50.","The total cost was Rs 45;50."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"A period \/ full stop is used as a decimal point in numerical figures.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"c2c7ecdc-c46a-4acd-9317-b39f3c0a8f49","questionText":"Choose the sentence that correctly uses quotation marks for direct speech with a tag in the middle.","options":["\"I will come,\" said John \"as soon as I can.\"","\"I will come,\" said John, \"as soon as I can.\"","\"I will come\" said John, \"as soon as I can.\"","\"I will come\", said John \"as soon as I can.\""],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Interrupted quotes require commas both before the closing of the first part and after the reporting tag.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"f074f3f6-7d44-4789-a7a5-0c8d17bdf97c","questionText":"Select the sentence that uses a hyphen to avoid ambiguous letter combinations in prefixes.","options":["Re-enter the room quietly.","Reenter the room quietly.","Re:enter the room quietly.","Re;enter the room quietly."],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"A hyphen is used with prefixes like 're-' when the root word starts with a vowel (re-enter) to prevent confusion.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"dcb25fa7-ee11-4726-a1a7-9e49f177f2c3","questionText":"Choose the sentence that correctly uses an apostrophe in a contraction for \"there is\".","options":["Theres only one person old enough to remember that wedding.","There's only one person old enough to remember that wedding.","Theres' only one person old enough to remember that wedding.","There;s only one person old enough to remember that wedding."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"\"There's\" is the contraction of \"There is\", requiring an apostrophe between 'e' and 's'.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"2ef4cbdb-1636-47b6-9865-4e71a14723a4","questionText":"Select the sentence that uses capital letters correctly for names of religions and sacred texts.","options":["He studies the bible and respects hinduism.","He studies the Bible and respects Hinduism.","He studies the bible and respects Hinduism.","He studies the Bible and respects hinduism."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Names of religions (Hinduism) and holy books\/texts (Bible) are proper nouns and must be capitalized.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"39b55350-2a27-46f5-8d59-debfe99e2b96","questionText":"Choose the sentence that correctly uses commas to separate city and country names.","options":["He lives in Paris France.","He lives in Paris, France.","He lives in Paris; France.","He lives in Paris: France."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"A comma is placed between the name of a city and its county\/state\/country.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"adf41bb5-0f44-4a03-83f6-454d176d2293","questionText":"Select the sentence that correctly uses a full stop at the end of an imperative command.","options":["Close the door quietly?","Close the door quietly.","Close the door quietly,","Close the door quietly:"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Imperative sentences (commands\/requests) end with a full stop when spoken normally without extreme emotion.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"}]

chapters.title: Synonyms and Antonyms
chapters.summary: This chapter provides a comprehensive guide to English synonyms and antonyms, complete with their Hinglish meanings to aid in vocabulary building and exam preparation.
