chapters.title: Time, Speed and Distance
chapters.summary: A comprehensive guide to understanding the core concepts of time, speed, and distance, including unit conversions, relative speed, train motion, boat and stream dynamics, and solved practice problems.
chapters.questionsJson:
[{"id":"231c72c5-2dee-402b-bf6a-2d894a83ef53","questionText":"Convert 90\text{ km/h} into \text{m/s}","options":["5\text{ m/s}","25\text{ m/s}","35\text{ m/s}","15\text{ m/s}"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"To convert \text{km/h} to \text{m/s}, multiply by \frac{5}{18}.
\text{Speed} = 90 \times \frac{5}{18} = 5 \times 5 = 25\text{ m/s}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"f7a3bae7-c1aa-4211-822d-426b796f0e87","questionText":"Convert 30\text{ m/s} into \text{km/h}","options":["100\text{ km/h}","105\text{ km/h}","101\text{ km/h}","108\text{ km/h}"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"To convert \text{m/s} to \text{km/h}, multiply by \frac{18}{5}.
\text{Speed} = 30 \times \frac{18}{5} = 6 \times 18 = 108\text{ km/h}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"45791a92-972a-463a-a3fb-d09ce7fbb04f","questionText":"A person riding a bike crosses a bridge with a speed of 54\text{ km/h}. What is the length of the bridge, if he takes 4\text{ min} to cross the bridge?","options":["3600\text{ m}","2800\text{ m}","3500\text{ m}","4500\text{ m}"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"\text{Speed in m/s} = 54 \times \frac{5}{18} = 15\text{ m/s}.
\text{Time in seconds} = 4 \times 60 = 240\text{ s}.
\text{Length (Distance)} = \text{Speed} \times \text{Time} = 15 \times 240 = 3600\text{ m}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"26521705-b63a-455d-85d8-a1244453e5aa","questionText":"A man covered a distance of 12\text{ km} in 90\text{ min} by cycle. How much distance will he cover in 3\text{ h}, if he rides the cycle at a uniform speed?","options":["36\text{ km}","24\text{ km}","30\text{ km}","27\text{ km}"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"90\text{ min} = 1.5\text{ h}.
\text{Speed} = \frac{12}{1.5} = 8\text{ km/h}.
\text{Distance in 3 h} = 8 \times 3 = 24\text{ km}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"4750d3a7-cae9-4223-8a96-3d9894085d48","questionText":"Walking at \frac{3}{4} of his normal speed, Abhishek is 16\text{ min} late in reaching his office. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and his office is:","options":["48\text{ min}","60\text{ min}","42\text{ min}","62\text{ min}"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Since speed becomes \frac{3}{4}\text{th}, time becomes \frac{4}{3}\text{rd} of the usual time (T).
\frac{4}{3}T - T = 16 \implies \frac{T}{3} = 16 \implies T = 48\text{ min}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"8e89731d-9177-4100-836c-653d3c5c9240","questionText":"Two trains for Bhopal leave Delhi at 9\text{ am} and 8:30\text{ am} and travel at 90\text{ km/h} and 80\text{ km/h} respectively. How many kilometres from Delhi will the two trains be together?","options":["360\text{ km}","320\text{ km}","270\text{ km}","280\text{ km}"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"First train starts at 8:30\text{ am} and runs for 30\text{ min} (0.5\text{ h}) before the second train starts at 9\text{ am}.
Lead distance = 80 \times 0.5 = 40\text{ km}.
Relative speed = 90 - 80 = 10\text{ km/h}.
Time to catch up = \frac{40}{10} = 4\text{ h}.
Distance from Delhi = 90 \times 4 = 360\text{ km}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"0de5a8b0-3e1b-4a26-a0f2-0adcdd91f9cb","questionText":"Prabhat covers a distance in 40\text{ min}, if he drives at a speed of 60\text{ km/h} on an average. Find the speed at which he must drive at to reduce the time of the journey by 25\%.","options":["60\text{ km/h}","70\text{ km/h}","75\text{ km/h}","80\text{ km/h}"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"\text{Distance} = 60 \times \frac{40}{60} = 40\text{ km}.
Reduced time = 40\text{ min} - (25\% \text{ of } 40) = 30\text{ min} = 0.5\text{ h}.
\text{Required Speed} = \frac{40}{0.5} = 80\text{ km/h}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"06e893c0-234c-4643-8e2d-3863830fa665","questionText":"Without stoppage, a train travels a certain distance with an average speed of 60\text{ km/h} and with stoppage, it covers the same distance with an average speed of 40\text{ km/h}. On an average, how many min per hour does the train stop during the journey?","options":["20\text{ min/h}","15\text{ min/h}","10\text{ min/h}","12\text{ min/h}"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"\text{Stoppage time per hour} = \frac{\text{Fast Speed} - \text{Slow Speed}}{\text{Fast Speed}} \times 60\text{ min}.
\text{Stoppage time} = \frac{60 - 40}{60} \times 60 = 20\text{ min/h}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"e38891ea-9ff7-440e-bd1f-ab23f6e23655","questionText":"Salabh, during his journey, travels for 20\text{ min} at a speed of 30\text{ km/h}, another 30\text{ min} at a speed of 50\text{ km/h}, next 1\text{ h} at a speed of 50\text{ km/h} and last 1\text{ h} at speed of 60\text{ km/h}. What is the average speed of the entire journey?","options":["51.18\text{ km/h}","48\text{ km/h}","53\text{ km/h}","39\text{ km/h}"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"\text{Total Distance} = \left(30 \times \frac{1}{3}\right) + \left(50 \times \frac{1}{2}\right) + (50 \times 1) + (60 \times 1) = 10 + 25 + 50 + 60 = 145\text{ km}.
\text{Total Time} = \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{2} + 1 + 1 = \frac{17}{6}\text{ h}.
\text{Average Speed} = \frac{145}{17/6} = \frac{870}{17} \approx 51.18\text{ km/h}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"250f4bf7-276a-42a4-9850-85a898ed4e45","questionText":"A certain distance is covered at a certain speed. If half of this distance is covered in 4 times of the time, find the ratio of the two speeds.","options":["1 : 8","1 : 4","4 : 1","8 : 1"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Let original distance = D, original time = T \implies S_1 = \frac{D}{T}.
New distance = \frac{D}{2}, new time = 4T \implies S_2 = \frac{D/2}{4T} = \frac{D}{8T}.
Ratio \frac{S_1}{S_2} = \frac{D/T}{D/8T} = \frac{8}{1} \implies 8 : 1.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"a1c8fb74-556b-4d45-9186-d40e5754c973","questionText":"A man covers half of his journey at 6\text{ km/h} and the remaining half at 3\text{ km/h}. Find his average speed.","options":["3\text{ km/h}","4\text{ km/h}","4.5\text{ km/h}","9\text{ km/h}"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"\text{Average Speed} = \frac{2AB}{A + B} = \frac{2 \times 6 \times 3}{6 + 3} = \frac{36}{9} = 4\text{ km/h}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"bbc8b252-ed19-4163-adfa-4a55765114c0","questionText":"The speeds of A and B are in the ratio of 3 : 4. A takes 20\text{ min} more than the time taken by B to reach a destination. In what time does A reach the destination?","options":["1\frac{1}{3}\text{ h}","2\text{ h}","1\frac{1}{2}\text{ h}","2\frac{2}{3}\text{ h}"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Speed ratio A : B = 3 : 4 \implies Time ratio A : B = 4 : 3.
Difference = 4x - 3x = x = 20\text{ min}.
Time taken by A = 4x = 80\text{ min} = 1\text{ h } 20\text{ min} = 1\frac{1}{3}\text{ h}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"61dfd1ce-6a5c-46ed-9eae-e5e437590fe1","questionText":"A is twice as fast as B and B is thrice as fast as C. The journey covered by C in 56\text{ min} will be covered by A in:","options":["5\frac{1}{3}\text{ min}","2\frac{1}{3}\text{ min}","7\frac{1}{3}\text{ min}","9\frac{1}{3}\text{ min}"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Speed ratio A : B : C = 6 : 3 : 1.
Time ratio is inversely proportional: C takes 6 times the time A takes.
Time taken by A = \frac{56}{6} = \frac{28}{3} = 9\frac{1}{3}\text{ min}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"c790d79c-5a81-4277-b0b7-fc78683da3d7","questionText":"A man is walking at a speed of 9\text{ km/h}. After every km he takes rest for 9\text{ min}. How much time will he take to cover a distance of 27\text{ km}?","options":["6\text{ h}","6\text{ h } 45\text{ min}","6\text{ h } 54\text{ min}","6\text{ h } 35\text{ min}"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Walking time = \frac{27}{9} = 3\text{ h}.
Number of rests = 27 - 1 = 26 rests (no rest after final destination).
Total rest time = 26 \times 9 = 234\text{ min} = 3\text{ h } 54\text{ min}.
Total time = 3\text{ h} + 3\text{ h } 54\text{ min} = 6\text{ h } 54\text{ min}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"00197bed-ff8c-4ed5-b440-7ea167ca9cd5","questionText":"A man covers a certain distance between his house and office on scooter, having an average speed of 60\text{ km/h} he is late by 20\text{ min}. However, with a speed of 80\text{ km/h} he reaches his office 10\text{ min} earlier. Find the distance between his house and office.","options":["120\text{ km}","90\text{ km}","80\text{ km}","60\text{ km}"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"\text{Distance} = \frac{S_1 \times S_2}{\vert{}S_1 - S_2\vert{}} \times \text{Time Difference in hours}.
Total time difference = 20\text{ min late} + 10\text{ min early} = 30\text{ min} = 0.5\text{ h}.
\text{Distance} = \frac{60 \times 80}{20} \times 0.5 = 240 \times 0.5 = 120\text{ km}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"7cd43da2-8339-41c5-a82a-8dac77b4d2c1","questionText":"Ram travels at the rate of 3\text{ km/h} and he reaches 15\text{ min} late. If he travels at the rate of 4\text{ km/h}, he reaches 15\text{ min} earlier. The distance Ram has to travel is:","options":["1\text{ km}","6\text{ km}","7\text{ km}","12\text{ km}"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Time difference = 15 + 15 = 30\text{ min} = 0.5\text{ h}.
\text{Distance} = \frac{3 \times 4}{4 - 3} \times 0.5 = 12 \times 0.5 = 6\text{ km}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"e1c2c2ea-d1eb-4c0b-be23-9bc3be9a3646","questionText":"A man walks to a town at the rate of 5\frac{1}{2}\text{ km/h} and rides back at the rate of 10\text{ km/h}. How far he walked, if the total time of the journey is 6\text{ h } 12\text{ min}?","options":["31\text{ km}","29\text{ km}","22\text{ km}","17\text{ km}"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Total time = 6 + \frac{12}{60} = \frac{31}{5}\text{ h}.
D \left(\frac{1}{5.5} + \frac{1}{10}\right) = \frac{31}{5} \implies D \left(\frac{2}{11} + \frac{1}{10}\right) = \frac{31}{5} \implies D \left(\frac{31}{110}\right) = \frac{31}{5} \implies D = 22\text{ km}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"8acb0eff-2bcf-4719-89f7-6a39615b078c","questionText":"A train leaves Manipur at 6\text{ am} and reaches Dispur at 10\text{ am}. Another train leaves Dispur at 8\text{ am} and reaches Manipur at 11:30\text{ am}. At what time do the two trains cross each other?","options":["7:56\text{ am}","7:56\text{ pm}","8:56\text{ am}","8:56\text{ pm}"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Train 1 takes 4\text{ h}; Train 2 takes 3.5\text{ h} = \frac{7}{2}\text{ h}.
Let distance = 28\text{ units} \implies S_1 = 7\text{ units/h}, S_2 = 8\text{ units/h}.
From 6\text{ am} to 8\text{ am} (2\text{ h}), Train 1 covers 14\text{ units}. Remaining = 14\text{ units}.
Time to cross after 8\text{ am} = \frac{14}{7 + 8} = \frac{14}{15}\text{ h} = 56\text{ min}.
Crossing time = 8:56\text{ am}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"df2a6676-e0a5-496a-9f60-defd1246f37c","questionText":"The average speed of a car is 75\text{ km/h}. The driver first decreases its average speed by 40\% and then increases it by 50\%. What is the new average speed now?","options":["67.5\text{ km/h}","60\text{ km/h}","90\text{ km/h}","60.5\text{ km/h}"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Decreased speed = 75 \times 0.60 = 45\text{ km/h}.
Increased speed = 45 \times 1.50 = 67.5\text{ km/h}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"13b81bbf-d671-46ad-9d7f-50bc5a8eba82","questionText":"Two cars run to a place at the speeds of 45\text{ km/h} and 60\text{ km/h} respectively. If the second car takes 5\text{ h} less than the first car for the journey, find the length of the journey.","options":["600\text{ km}","300\text{ km}","900\text{ km}","120\text{ km}"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"\frac{D}{45} - \frac{D}{60} = 5 \implies \frac{4D - 3D}{180} = 5 \implies D = 900\text{ km}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"6c4c12cc-bcf6-4db1-ad56-48c38bc1b38f","questionText":"A man takes 8\text{ h } 32\text{ min} in walking to a certain place and riding back. He would have gained 2\text{ h } 14\text{ min} by riding both ways. How long would he take to walk both ways?","options":["10\text{ h}","10\text{ h } 36\text{ min}","10\text{ h } 46\text{ min}","10\text{ h } 40\text{ min}"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"W + R = 8\text{ h } 32\text{ min}.
Gained 2\text{ h } 14\text{ min} by riding both ways \implies 2R = (8\text{ h } 32\text{ min}) - (2\text{ h } 14\text{ min}) = 6\text{ h } 18\text{ min}.
2W = 2(W + R) - 2R = (17\text{ h } 04\text{ min}) - (6\text{ h } 18\text{ min}) = 10\text{ h } 46\text{ min}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"2a3b4e1d-b19e-44ce-9214-9f150ab207bd","questionText":"Two cars A and B are running towards each other from two different places 88\text{ km} apart. If the ratio of the speeds of the cars A and B is 5 : 6 and the speed of the car B is 90\text{ km/h}, after what time will they meet each other?","options":["38\text{ min}","39\text{ min}","45\text{ min}","32\text{ min}"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Speed of B = 90\text{ km/h} \implies Speed of A = \frac{5}{6} \times 90 = 75\text{ km/h}.
Relative Speed = 90 + 75 = 165\text{ km/h}.
Time = \frac{88}{165}\text{ h} = \frac{88}{165} \times 60 = 32\text{ min}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"12408409-9bfb-4feb-b61f-6b085f2a6190","questionText":"Two trains, one 160\text{ m} and the other 140\text{ m} long are running in opposite directions on parallel rails, the first at 77\text{ km/h} and the other at 67\text{ km/h}. How long will they take to cross each other?","options":["7\text{ s}","7\frac{1}{2}\text{ s}","6\text{ s}","10\text{ s}"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Total Length = 160 + 140 = 300\text{ m}.
Relative Speed = 77 + 67 = 144\text{ km/h} = 144 \times \frac{5}{18} = 40\text{ m/s}.
Time = \frac{300}{40} = 7.5 = 7\frac{1}{2}\text{ s}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"ed6e4338-4e46-475b-922b-bbd0df91f6c8","questionText":"A train 150\text{ m} long, passes a pole in 15\text{ s}. It also passes another train of the same length travelling in opposite direction in 12\text{ s}. The speed of the second train is:","options":["45\text{ km/h}","48\text{ km/h}","52\text{ km/h}","54\text{ km/h}"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Speed of Train 1 (S_1) = \frac{150}{15} = 10\text{ m/s}.
Crossing each other: Total distance = 300\text{ m}.
Relative speed (S_1 + S_2) = \frac{300}{12} = 25\text{ m/s}.
S_2 = 25 - 10 = 15\text{ m/s} = 15 \times \frac{18}{5} = 54\text{ km/h}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"63a0c70f-aaf8-46bc-8921-3462890ec605","questionText":"Two trains, one from station A to station B and the other from B to A start simultaneously. After meeting, the trains reach their destinations after 9\text{ h} and 16\text{ h} respectively. The ratio of their speeds is:","options":["2 : 3","4 : 3","6 : 7","9 : 16"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"\frac{S_1}{S_2} = \frac{\sqrt{t_2}}{\sqrt{t_1}} = \frac{\sqrt{16}}{\sqrt{9}} = \frac{4}{3} = 4 : 3.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"10943ca5-ad81-407e-94fb-1894aad4124e","questionText":"A man rows a boat 18\text{ km} in 4\text{ h} downstream and returns upstream in 12\text{ h}. The speed of the stream (in \text{km/h}) is:","options":["1","1.5","2","1.75"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Downstream speed (u) = \frac{18}{4} = 4.5\text{ km/h}.
Upstream speed (v) = \frac{18}{12} = 1.5\text{ km/h}.
Speed of stream = \frac{u - v}{2} = \frac{4.5 - 1.5}{2} = 1.5\text{ km/h}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"5d5dc39e-bd40-46f0-b470-85b7a9041dac","questionText":"A man can swim 3\text{ km/h} in still water. If the velocity of the stream is 2\text{ km/h}, the time taken by him to swim to a place 10\text{ km} upstream and back is:","options":["9\frac{3}{5}\text{ h}","10\text{ h}","12\text{ h}","8\frac{1}{3}\text{ h}"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Downstream speed = 3 + 2 = 5\text{ km/h}.
Upstream speed = 3 - 2 = 1\text{ km/h}.
Total time = \frac{10}{5} + \frac{10}{1} = 2 + 10 = 12\text{ h}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"9f9514ab-1148-495a-af3a-e4431f33f9db","questionText":"A boat goes 6\text{ km} an hour in still water, but takes thrice as much time in going the same distance against the current. The speed of the current (in \text{km/h}) is:","options":["4","5","3","2"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Let stream speed = y. Upstream speed = 6 - y.
Since time taken is thrice \implies 6 - y = \frac{6}{3} = 2 \implies y = 4\text{ km/h}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"9bd7d3d3-2d6d-48de-93f2-f38597f9ffa8","questionText":"A man can row at 5\text{ km/h} in still water. If the velocity of current is 1\text{ km/h} and it takes him 1\text{ h} to row to place and come back, how far is the place?","options":["2.5\text{ km}","3\text{ km}","2.4\text{ km}","3.6\text{ km}"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Downstream = 6\text{ km/h}, Upstream = 4\text{ km/h}.
\frac{D}{6} + \frac{D}{4} = 1 \implies \frac{5D}{12} = 1 \implies D = 2.4\text{ km}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"1b25b08b-e1d2-4cde-aa1a-2270683c2d80","questionText":"The speed of a motor-boat and the speed of the current of water is in the ratio 36 : 5. The boat goes along with the current in 5\text{ h } 10\text{ min}. It will come back in:","options":["5\text{ h } 50\text{ min}","6\text{ h}","6\text{ h } 50\text{ min}","12\text{ h } 10\text{ min}"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Downstream speed = 36 + 5 = 41x; Upstream speed = 36 - 5 = 31x.
Downstream time = 5\text{ h } 10\text{ min} = \frac{31}{6}\text{ h}.
Distance = 41x \times \frac{31}{6}.
Upstream time = \frac{\text{Distance}}{31x} = \frac{41 \times 31 / 6}{31} = \frac{41}{6}\text{ h} = 6\text{ h } 50\text{ min}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"153a39c6-3985-4156-a061-f37b1c8af948","questionText":"A student starting from his house walks at a speed of 2\frac{1}{2}\text{ km/h} and reaches his school 6\text{ minutes} late. Next day starting at the same time he increases his speed by 1\text{ km/h} and reaches 6\text{ minutes} early. The distance between the school and his house is:","options":["1\frac{3}{4}\text{ km}","3\frac{1}{2}\text{ km}","6\text{ km}","4\text{ km}"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"S_1 = 2.5\text{ km/h}, S_2 = 3.5\text{ km/h}.
Time difference = 6 + 6 = 12\text{ min} = 0.2\text{ h}.
\text{Distance} = \frac{2.5 \times 3.5}{3.5 - 2.5} \times 0.2 = 8.75 \times 0.2 = 1.75 = 1\frac{3}{4}\text{ km}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"25913aa6-3956-423f-8b63-23f0aff0077d","questionText":"A plane can cover 6000\text{ km} in 8\text{ h}. If the speed is increased by 250\text{ km/h}, then the time taken by the plane to cover 9000\text{ km} is:","options":["9\text{ h}","8\text{ h}","6\text{ h}","5\text{ h}"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Initial speed = \frac{6000}{8} = 750\text{ km/h}.
New speed = 750 + 250 = 1000\text{ km/h}.
New time = \frac{9000}{1000} = 9\text{ h}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"1ada8f8e-05ad-429c-9a33-3e4ccb40ee01","questionText":"A train 100\text{ m} long, running at 36\text{ km/h}, takes 25\text{ s} to pass a bridge. The length of the bridge is:","options":["100\text{ m}","80\text{ m}","150\text{ m}","120\text{ m}"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Speed = 36 \times \frac{5}{18} = 10\text{ m/s}.
Total distance = 10 \times 25 = 250\text{ m}.
Length of bridge = 250 - 100 = 150\text{ m}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"c26ecb8c-7462-4ac7-b7e6-3c78d33dccf6","questionText":"The speed of a boat along the stream is 12\text{ km/h} and against the stream is 8\text{ km/h}. The time taken by the boat to sail 24\text{ km} in still water is:","options":["2\text{ h}","3\text{ h}","2.4\text{ h}","12\text{ h}"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Speed in still water = \frac{12 + 8}{2} = 10\text{ km/h}.
Time = \frac{24}{10} = 2.4\text{ h}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"373393b5-4f08-4e1b-9624-54454828e4f6","questionText":"In covering a distance of 30\text{ km}, Abhay takes 2\text{ h} more than Sameer. If Abhay doubles his speed, then he would take 1\text{ h} less than Sameer. Abhay's speed (in \text{km/h}) is:","options":["5","6","6.25","7.5"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Doubling Abhay's speed reduces his time by 3\text{ h} (from +2 to -1).
So, Abhay's original time = 6\text{ h}.
Abhay's speed = \frac{30}{6} = 5\text{ km/h}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"4585c012-ce03-405f-99f4-dcf8a35719b0","questionText":"A train of length 500\text{ ft} crosses a platform of length 700\text{ ft} in 10\text{ s}. The speed of the train is:","options":["70\text{ ft/s}","85\text{ ft/s}","100\text{ ft/s}","120\text{ ft/s}"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Total distance = 500 + 700 = 1200\text{ ft}.
Speed = \frac{1200}{10} = 120\text{ ft/s}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"e3aa0bb7-2cb4-4b00-98c8-ff860c53c098","questionText":"The speed of two cars are in the ratio 5 : 4. The ratio between the times taken by them to travel the same distance is:","options":["5 : 4","6 : 4","6 : 5","4 : 5"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Time is inversely proportional to speed when distance is constant.
Ratio of time = \frac{1}{5} : \frac{1}{4} = 4 : 5.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"}]

chapters.title: Percentage
chapters.summary: A comprehensive guide to understanding percentages, including basic calculations, conversions, percentage increases/decreases, successive changes, and practical solved examples.
chapters.questionsJson: [{"id":"bb18793a-ec34-4c19-abf4-dd019556e9b8","questionText":"If 20% of $x = 90$, find $x$.","options":["350","450","250","550"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"$\\frac{20}{100} \\times x = 90 \\implies x = 90 \\times 5 = 450$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"2b5fe80c-175a-4be1-8119-97f7ceeaaa8b","questionText":"What is 32% of $\\frac{3}{8}\\text{th}$ of 5000?","options":["606","610","580","600"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"$\\frac{32}{100} \\times \\frac{3}{8} \\times 5000 = 4 \\times 3 \\times 50 = 600$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"a73bd65e-f14a-4e86-9093-2ac75af93fa5","questionText":"P's income has increased by 10% over last year and will be 20% higher next year. If his last year's income is ₹ 7000 per month, what will it be next year?","options":["₹ 9240","₹ 7500","₹ 9000","₹ 7850"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"$7000 \\times \\left(1 + \\frac{32}{100}\\right) = 7000 \\times 1.32 = ₹ 9240$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"2fcd58c6-fc79-4775-acb7-4e4876b8fc27","questionText":"A mixture contains sand and gravel in the ratio $1 : 4$. The sand has 20% impurity. If total mixture weights $10\\text{ kg}$, how much impurity is there?","options":["$300\\text{ g}$","$450\\text{ g}$","$400\\text{ g}$","$500\\text{ g}$"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"$\\text{Sand} = \\frac{1}{5} \\times 10 = 2\\text{ kg} = 2000\\text{ g}$. $\\text{Impurity} = 20\\% \\text{ of } 2000\\text{ g} = 400\\text{ g}$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"e34392f5-2b0d-4b2f-94b9-2e25336cd3a6","questionText":"The population of a city is estimated to be 432000 after 2 yr. If the population growth is 20% per annum, what is the current population?","options":["310000","285000","380000","300000"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"$P \\times \\left(1 + \\frac{20}{100}\\right)^2 = 432000 \\implies P = \\frac{432000 \\times 100 \\times 100}{120 \\times 120} = 300000$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"e482e227-2cb3-4d28-9afe-2230ac1788b0","questionText":"The price of a house increased by 25% after 10 yr, reduces by 25% during the subsequent 10 yr. If the present cost is ₹ 10 lakh, what will be its cost after 20 yr?","options":["₹ 937500","₹ 900000","₹ 850000","₹ 725000"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"$1000000 \\times \\left(1 - \\frac{6.25}{100}\\right) = 1000000 \\times 0.9375 = ₹ 937500$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"f60bd1ca-84a5-48f1-aa33-3a543e34bef7","questionText":"The price of a product of a company increases by 10% and the turnover increases by 10%. What is the change in quantity sold?","options":["10%","8%","20%","No change"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"$\\text{Turnover} = \\text{Price} \\times \\text{Quantity} \\implies 110 = 110 \\times \\text{Quantity} \\implies \\text{Quantity} = 1$ (no change).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"b9b15e01-8ed3-4689-8356-dbdf71dc7b7e","questionText":"The monthly income of a person is ₹ 5000. If his income is increased by 30%, what is his monthly income now?","options":["₹ 7000","₹ 5500","₹ 4500","₹ 6500"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"$5000 \\times 1.30 = ₹ 6500$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"fc1e1657-0cb3-4451-a1a0-f8bc937de6c4","questionText":"The price of a certain article is ₹ 15000 but due to slump in the market, its price decreases by 8%. Find the new price of the article.","options":["₹ 14000","₹ 13800","₹ 16500","₹ 12600"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"$15000 \\times 0.92 = ₹ 13800$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"4076d6b0-2565-494a-aec7-83138aef2c9c","questionText":"The price of a television includes the manufacturing cost, 10% sales tax and 10% profit. What is the manufacturing cost, if the price is ₹ 14400?","options":["₹ 10000","₹ 12000","₹ 12500","₹ 9000"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"$1.20 \\times M = 14400 \\implies M = ₹ 12000$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"e35941ae-8571-403a-80ea-03a9d599afa6","questionText":"A class has girls and boys in the ratio $4 : 5$. What percentage of class comprises girls studying Mathematics?","options":["33.3%","30%","25%","18%"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"$\\text{Girls} = \\frac{4}{9}$; $\\text{Math girls} = \\frac{3}{4} \\times \\frac{4}{9} = \\frac{1}{3} = 33.33\\%$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"779b9ce3-d998-4123-8991-18b91c29f283","questionText":"Asha's income is ₹ 12000 per month. She pays 20% tax on monthly income above ₹ 2000 and she spends 30% of the remaining income. How much does she save annually?","options":["₹ 70000","₹ 60000","₹ 84000","₹ 50000"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"$\\text{Tax} = 20\\% \\text{ of } 10000 = 2000$. $\\text{Remaining} = 10000$. $\\text{Savings} = 70\\% \\text{ of } 10000 = 7000\/\\text{month} \\implies 7000 \\times 12 = ₹ 84000\/\\text{year}$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"f571190d-ee28-436b-8b0b-57fc5654a835","questionText":"A single discount which is equivalent to successive discounts 25% and 10% is:","options":["35%","34.5%","33%","32.5%"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"$25 + 10 - \\frac{25 \\times 10}{100} = 35 - 2.5 = 32.5\\%$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"0dbec3ca-8607-458b-bc1c-7f3adca69581","questionText":"A reduction of ₹ 2 per kg enables a man to purchase $4\\text{ kg}$ more sugar for ₹ 16. Find the original price of sugar.","options":["₹ 4 per kg","₹ 6 per kg","₹ 3 per kg","₹ 4.5 per kg"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"$\\frac{16}{x-2} - \\frac{16}{x} = 4 \\implies x(x-2) = 8 \\implies x = 4$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"acacd998-3d5f-4fc3-8a5b-ce76970944dd","questionText":"A reduction of 25% in the price of rice, enables a person to buy $5\\text{ kg}$ more for ₹ 120. Find the original price of rice per kg.","options":["₹ 8","₹ 10","₹ 12","₹ 15"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"$\\text{Reduced price} = \\frac{25\\% \\text{ of } 120}{5} = ₹ 6 \\implies \\text{Original price} = \\frac{6}{0.75} = ₹ 8$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"2d03434d-e653-4131-bc91-35680514aa86","questionText":"A litre of water evaporates from $6\\text{ L}$ of sea water containing 4% salt. Find the percentage of salt in the remaining solution.","options":["$5\\frac{1}{2}\\%$","$3\\frac{1}{2}\\%$","$3\\%$","$4\\frac{4}{5}\\%$"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"$\\text{Salt} = 0.24\\text{ L}$. $\\text{New solution} = 5\\text{ L} \\implies \\% = \\frac{0.24}{5} \\times 100 = 4.8\\% = 4\\frac{4}{5}\\%$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"1a5f7e86-adf9-4788-a5b1-112c717468f3","questionText":"Two numbers are 20% and 25% less than the third number. How much percentage is the second number less than the first?","options":["$5\\frac{4}{5}\\%$","$\\frac{20}{3}\\%$","$6\\frac{1}{2}\\%$","$6\\frac{1}{4}\\%$"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"$1\\text{st} = 80$, $2\\text{nd} = 75$. $\\text{Difference} = 5 \\implies \\frac{5}{80} \\times 100 = 6.25\\% = 6\\frac{1}{4}\\%$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"a291c370-7b54-4f81-9827-6251de4cadb3","questionText":"Due to increase of 30% in the price of a colour TV the sale is reduced by 40%, then what will be the percentage change in income?","options":["10%, increase","10%, decrease","35%, decrease","22%, decrease"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"$30 - 40 - \\frac{30 \\times 40}{100} = -10 - 12 = -22\\%$ (decrease).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"b8009025-91fe-4d91-a0e2-81ef10226e72","questionText":"Two numbers are respectively 20% and 50% more than a third number. What is the percentage of second with respect to first?","options":["125%","90%","64%","75%"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"$1\\text{st} = 120$, $2\\text{nd} = 150 \\implies \\frac{150}{120} \\times 100 = 125\\%$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"5d7161e0-a870-414f-915c-f442507a65d1","questionText":"From 2008 to 2009, the sales of a book decreased by 80%. If the sales in 2010 was the same as in 2008, by what percent did it increase from 2009 to 2010?","options":["80%","100%","120%","400%"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"$\\text{Sales 2009} = 20$, $\\text{Sales 2010} = 100 \\implies \\frac{100 - 20}{20} \\times 100 = 400\\%$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"f393ccc8-6313-4e6c-b735-2aea08e91f95","questionText":"Anand spends 75% of his income. His income is increased by 20% and he increased his expenditure by 10%. His savings are increased by:","options":["$10\\%$","$25\\%$","$37\\frac{1}{2}\\%$","$50\\%$"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"$\\text{Initial savings} = 25$, $\\text{New savings} = 120 - 82.5 = 37.5 \\implies \\frac{12.5}{25} \\times 100 = 50\\%$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"e29efa14-5f8a-4ba6-91a0-c87747ae6b9c","questionText":"In an examination, 35% candidates failed in one subject and 42% failed in another subject while 15% failed in both the subjects. If 2500 candidates appeared at the examination, how many passed in either subject but not in both?","options":["325","1175","2125","None of these"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"$\\text{Failed in only one} = (35 - 15) + (42 - 15) = 47\\% \\implies 47\\% \\text{ of } 2500 = 1175$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"c6aa06de-6090-43ea-9619-0dc6b133ee6d","questionText":"In an election between two candidates, a candidate who got 40% of total votes is defeated by 15000 votes. The number of votes received by the winning candidates is:","options":["6000","10000","22500","45000"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"$\\text{Difference} = 60\\% - 40\\% = 20\\% \\implies 20\\% = 15000 \\implies \\text{Winning votes } (60\\%) = 45000$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"081ad969-ee0b-4e69-b3ec-15bd9323b4e8","questionText":"The price of sugar increases by 20%. By what per cent must a housewife reduce the consumption of sugar, so that the expenditure on sugar is the same as before?","options":["$16\\frac{2}{3}\\%$","$20\\%$","$50\\%$","$83\\frac{1}{3}\\%$"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"$\\frac{20}{100 + 20} \\times 100 = \\frac{20}{120} \\times 100 = 16\\frac{2}{3}\\%$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"612858c8-75b7-4c43-8271-4c141a2ef52c","questionText":"The salary of an employee of a company increases every month by 4%. If his salary in August was ₹ 6300, what would be his approximate salary in month of October of the same year?","options":["₹ 6552","₹ 6967","₹ 6814","₹ 6627"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"$6300 \\times (1.04)^2 = 6300 \\times 1.0816 \\approx ₹ 6814$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"242b8a23-9497-4c83-9c4e-ebde8496d185","questionText":"Bina's monthly income is 90% of Anita's monthly incomes. The total of both their monthly income is equal to Mr Sen's monthly income. Mr Sen's annual income is ₹ 775200. What is Bina's monthly income?","options":["₹ 34000","₹ 36000","₹ 30600","₹ 30000"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"$\\text{Sen's monthly} = \\frac{775200}{12} = ₹ 64600 \\implies 1.9 A = 64600 \\implies A = 34000 \\implies \\text{Bina} = 0.9 \\times 34000 = ₹ 30600$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"7f706fce-0fa7-4f50-aca0-9e953634b883","questionText":"In a test, Rajesh got 112 marks which was 32 more than the passing marks. Sonal got 75% marks which was 70 more than the passing marks. What is the minimum passing percentage of the test?","options":["35%","45%","40%","48%"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"$\\text{Passing marks} = 112 - 32 = 80$. $\\text{Sonal} = 80 + 70 = 150 = 75\\% \\implies \\text{Total} = 200 \\implies \\text{Passing } \\% = \\frac{80}{200} \\times 100 = 40\\%$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"59e1997e-318a-4038-8d6c-32399373a103","questionText":"Anish spends 25% of his salary on house rent, 5% on food, 15% on travel, 10% on clothes and the remaining amount of ₹ 22500 is saved. What is Anish's salary?","options":["₹ 40000","₹ 40500","₹ 45000","₹ 50000"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"$\\text{Savings} = 100 - (25 + 5 + 15 + 10) = 45\\% \\implies 45\\% = 22500 \\implies \\text{Salary} = ₹ 50000$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"442e31fe-cea9-47cb-8d40-8f28b244b949","questionText":"Madan's salary is 25% of Ram's salary and Ram's salary is 40% of Sudin's salary. If the total salary of all the three for a month is ₹ 12000. How much did Madan earn that month?","options":["₹ 800","₹ 8000","₹ 600","₹ 850"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"$\\text{Sudin} = 100x$, $\\text{Ram} = 40x$, $\\text{Madan} = 10x \\implies 150x = 12000 \\implies x = 80 \\implies \\text{Madan} = 10 \\times 80 = ₹ 800$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"ae88a52d-ae76-4148-9448-0df914075e14","questionText":"If the cost of an article is ₹ $P$ after two successive reductions of 20% and 25%, the original price of the article was:","options":["₹ $\\frac{4P}{5}$","₹ $\\frac{5P}{3}$","₹ $\\frac{5P}{4}$","₹ $\\frac{3P}{5}$"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"$x \\times 0.80 \\times 0.75 = P \\implies x \\times 0.60 = P \\implies x = \\frac{5P}{3}$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"9be71bb6-87cb-4486-90df-45c3d42cbfff","questionText":"In a college election, a candidate secured 62% of the votes and is elected by a margin of 144 votes. The total number of votes polled is:","options":["600","800","1200","925"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"$\\text{Margin} = 62\\% - 38\\% = 24\\% \\implies 24\\% = 144 \\implies \\text{Total} = 600$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"f8d3370c-7446-43b0-92de-0d721bf9fd33","questionText":"If 90% of $x$ is $315\\text{ km}$, then the value of $x$ is:","options":["$325\\text{ km}$","$350\\text{ km}$","$405\\text{ km}$","$340\\text{ km}$"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"$0.90 \\times x = 315 \\implies x = \\frac{315}{0.9} = 350\\text{ km}$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"1a2b8994-ccc1-401e-af9f-238f22c9331d","questionText":"If $x\\%$ of $a$ is the same as $y\\%$ of $b$, then $z\\%$ of $b$ will be:","options":["$\\frac{xz}{y}\\%$ of $a$","$\\frac{zx}{y}\\%$ of $a$","$\\frac{xy}{z}\\%$ of $a$","$\\frac{yz}{x}\\%$ of $a$"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"$b = \\frac{x}{y} a \\implies z\\% \\text{ of } b = \\left(\\frac{xz}{y}\\%\\right) \\text{ of } a$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"183ab7ed-0551-4db5-90fe-fdd175d5d061","questionText":"The value of a machine depreciates by 5% every year. 1. DONE
2. NODE

Total = 2 words.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"228fbd2b-74e6-4e52-8954-a862a263012b","questionText":"From the following English alphabets find the letter that comes between 8th letter from your right and 7th letter from your left in English alphabetical series.","options":["K","L","M","N"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"1. 7th letter from left = G (Position 7)
2. 8th letter from right = $27 - 8 = 19^{\text{th}}$ position from left = S (Position 19)
3. Middle position between 7 and 19 = $\frac{7 + 19}{2} = \frac{26}{2} = 13^{\text{th}}$ position.
4. The $13^{\text{th}}$ letter in the English alphabet is M.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"a92e7778-15ce-46aa-a039-7bfcff45fb9e","questionText":"If the first half of English alphabetical series is written in reverse order, then find the letter which is 5th to the left of 17th letter from left end.","options":["B","M","L","I"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"1. Target position from left end = $17 - 5 = 12^{\text{th}}$ letter.
2. The first half of the alphabet (A to M) is reversed: M L K J I H G F E D C B A.
3. The $12^{\text{th}}$ letter from the left in this reversed sequence is B (since A is 13th).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"83c45ff7-83c0-4bf8-b50e-347d3039ca54","questionText":"Study the following arrangement carefully and answer the question:

`X U V M R S T M W N V O P M W U V A C W M V`

How many M's are there in the above series which are immediately preceded by 'W' and immediately followed by 'V'?","options":["3","2","1","5"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"We need to find the pattern: W $\rightarrow$ M $\rightarrow$ V (i.e., 'WMV').
Scanning the series:
`X U V M R S T M W N V O P M W U V A C` **W M V**

The pattern 'WMV' occurs exactly 1 time at the very end.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"ea4c4e8d-26d0-42ac-ba74-1198922ffd7e","questionText":"Study the following arrangement carefully and answer the question:

`X U V M R S T M W N V O P M W U V A C W M V`

If all the vowels are dropped from the above arrangement, which of the following will be 8th from right end?","options":["W","P","M","C"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"1. Drop all vowels (A, E, I, O, U) from the series:
Original: `X U V M R S T M W N V O P M W U V A C W M V`
After dropping vowels: `X V M R S T M W N V P M W V C W M V`

2. Count the 8th element from the right end:
- 1st: V
- 2nd: M
- 3rd: W
- 4th: C
- 5th: V
- 6th: W
- 7th: M
- 8th: P

Thus, the 8th element from the right end is P.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"bd367b4f-db6e-4e15-8748-e5a41861760c","questionText":"Study the following arrangement carefully and answer the question:

`# U N T A B C @ D % E R D V G H 7 8 L K M`

How many vowels are there in the above series which are immediately preceded by a symbol?","options":["None","One","Two","Three"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"We need to find the pattern: Symbol $\rightarrow$ Vowel.
Let's check the vowels in the arrangement:
- `U` is preceded by `#` (Symbol) $\rightarrow$ Yes
- `A` is preceded by `T` (Letter) $\rightarrow$ No
- `E` is preceded by `%` (Symbol) $\rightarrow$ Yes

Total count = 2 (namely, `#U` and `%E`).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"2f1f3548-d787-45b4-9b33-b1f9da2984b6","questionText":"Study the following arrangement carefully and answer the question:

`# U N T A B C @ D % E R D V G H 7 8 L K M`

Three of the following four are alike in a certain way based on their positions in the above arrangement and so form a group. Which is the one that does not belong to that group?","options":["V R %","M L 7","@ D","A N #"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Let's analyze the step patterns from right to left in the arrangement:
- For **V R %**: V is at index 14, R is at index 12, % is at index 10. (Step of -2, -2)
- For **M L 7**: M is at index 21, L is at index 19, 7 is at index 17. (Step of -2, -2)
- For **A N #**: A is at index 5, N is at index 3, # is at index 1. (Step of -2, -2)
- For **@ D**: @ is at index 8, D is at index 9. (Step of +1)

Therefore, '@ D' does not belong to the group.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"}]
