Who is the fourth in the descending order of age?","options":["Mohan","Raju","Kabir","Neelesh"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Descending Order of age: Lalit > Mohan > Raju > Neelesh > Kabir. The 4th person in descending order is Neelesh.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"42a122c9-4b03-4963-8859-b48b28c6c39a","questionText":"A, B, C, D and E are five rivers. A is shorter than B but longer than E. C is the longest and D is little shorter than B and little longer than A. Which is the shortest river?","options":["B","C","D","E"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Sequence: C > B > D > A > E. The shortest river is E.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"83e3c432-56e7-44a4-be82-03e6605dd890","questionText":"Shyam is taller than Pradeep and Pradeep is equal to Anurag. But Anand is smaller than Suresh who is equal to Anurag. If Pradeep is taller than Praveen, who is the tallest of all?","options":["Pradeep","Praveen","Suresh","Shyam"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Since Shyam is taller than Pradeep (who is equal to Anurag and Suresh), Shyam is the tallest.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"b4892c30-978b-48db-bd9f-80cc9411f353","questionText":"There are five friends Suresh, Kaushal, Madhur, Amit and Ramesh. Suresh is shorter than Kaushal but taller than Ramesh. Madhur is the tallest. Amit is a little shorter than Kaushal but little taller than Suresh. If they stand in the order of their heights, who will be the shortest?","options":["Amit","Madhur","Ramesh","Kaushal"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Order: Madhur > Kaushal > Amit > Suresh > Ramesh. The shortest person is Ramesh.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"dcbc56be-92c2-4d06-928e-b2c825c09a66","questionText":"Sumit ranked ninth from top and thirty eighth from the bottom in a class. How many students are there in the class?","options":["47","48","45","46"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Total students = Rank from top + Rank from bottom - 1 = 9 + 38 - 1 = 46.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"d65992ef-5877-460e-a653-31ca003ccbc2","questionText":"If Atul finds that he is twelfth from the right in a queue of boys and fourth from the left, how many boys should be added to the queue, so that there are 28 boys in the queue?","options":["12","13","14","20"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Current total = 12 + 4 - 1 = 15. Boys to add = 28 - 15 = 13.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"efbf0988-06cf-41ec-9a6a-ec38b49a68c1","questionText":"Manish ranked sixteenth from the top and twenty ninth from the bottom among those who passed an examination. Six boys did not participate in the competition and five failed in it. How many boys were there in the class?","options":["40","44","50","55"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Passed = 16 + 29 - 1 = 44. Total boys = 44 (passed) + 6 (did not participate) + 5 (failed) = 55.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"df126669-a420-404c-9530-0c683112ab15","questionText":"Aruna ranks twelfth in a class of forty six. What will be her rank from the last?","options":["33","34","35","37"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Rank from last = Total - Rank from top + 1 = 46 - 12 + 1 = 35.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"e1579def-ff48-4da3-add2-a0bd0f6d98e6","questionText":"Ravi is 7 ranks ahead of Sumit in a class of 39. If Sumit's rank is seventeenth from the last, what is Ravi's rank from the start?","options":["14th","15th","16th","17th"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Sumit's rank from last = 17th. Ravi's rank from last = 17 + 7 = 24th. Ravi's rank from start = 39 - 24 + 1 = 16th.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"412fc335-c379-4602-bc15-dcc35b29ce7d","questionText":"In a row of ten boys, when Rohit was shifted by two places towards the left, he became seventh from the left end. What was his earlier position from the right end of the row?","options":["First","Second","Fourth","Sixth"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"New position from left = 7th. Original position from left = 7 + 2 = 9th. Original position from right = 10 - 9 + 1 = 2nd (Second).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"c4a58f86-7f06-4dd1-b98c-5760798ec6df","questionText":"In a row of girls, Shilpa is eighth from the left and Reena is seventeenth from the right. If they interchange their positions, Shilpa becomes fourteenth from the left. How many girls are there in the row?","options":["25","30","27","28"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"After interchange, Shilpa occupies Reena's original spot (17th from right) and is 14th from left. Total girls = 14 + 17 - 1 = 30.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"15f2cf9d-fe17-4302-a803-ff2838c937c3","questionText":"In a class of 35 students, Kunal is placed seventh from the bottom whereas Sonali is placed ninth from the top. Pulkit is placed exactly in between the two. What is Kunal's position from Pulkit?","options":["9","10","11","13"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Kunal's rank from top = 35 - 7 + 1 = 29th. Sonali's rank from top = 9th. Students between them = 29 - 9 - 1 = 19. Pulkit's rank from top = 9 + 10 = 19th. Distance from Pulkit to Kunal = 29 - 19 = 10.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"2c537934-140d-4629-91da-7a5796fd4d88","questionText":"Six friends A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting in a row facing North. C is between A and E. B is just to the right of E but left of D. F is not at the right end. How many persons are to the right of E?","options":["1","2","3","4"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Arrangement: F A C E B D. Persons to the right of E are B and D (total 2).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"4e240d15-89c1-4fc1-83dd-01ae1c1bb3f8","questionText":"Which of the following are sitting diagonally opposite to each other?

[FIGURE:GRID 2x3]
Row 1: D B F
Row 2: A E C
[/FIGURE]","options":["F and C","D and A","A and C","A and F"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Based on the arrangement, the diagonal pairs are (D, C) and (A, F).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"58e6b577-b075-4b4f-b946-abe85a38c056","questionText":"Which of the following are in the same row?

[FIGURE:GRID 2x3]
Row 1: D B F
Row 2: A E C
[/FIGURE]","options":["A and E","E and D","C and B","A and B"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Row 2 contains A, E, and C.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"3edd38ec-7725-4031-822f-71e91ab5ddee","questionText":"Which of the following are in one of the two rows?

[FIGURE:GRID 2x3]
Row 1: D B F
Row 2: A E C
[/FIGURE]","options":["FBC","CEB","DBF","AEF"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Row 1 contains DBF.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"cdc7adfb-a7bc-4983-9a95-0146f97badf9","questionText":"After interchanging seat with E, who will be the neighbours of D in the new position?

[FIGURE:GRID 2x3]
Row 1: D B F
Row 2: A E C
[/FIGURE]","options":["C and A","F and B","Only B","Only A"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Moving D to E's middle spot in Row 2 gives neighbours C and A.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"af9d2afc-d348-404b-84e7-684c0be5892e","questionText":"Who is fourth to the left of G?

[FIGURE:SEATING circular]
Clockwise from G: G, B, F, C, E, D, A
[/FIGURE]","options":["D","E","C","Cannot be determined"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"4th to the left of G in a 7-person circle corresponds to C.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"67f39f66-7c66-4ec3-898d-2ef7848f7680","questionText":"Who is to the left of G?

[FIGURE:SEATING circular]
Clockwise from G: G, B, F, C, E, D, A
[/FIGURE]","options":["A","C","B","None of these"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Immediate left neighbour of G is A.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"76354f5e-fd3a-4033-a557-7bef080a8553","questionText":"Who are the neighbours of F?

[FIGURE:SEATING circular]
Clockwise from G: G, B, F, C, E, D, A
[/FIGURE]","options":["E and C","F and B","A and B","C and B"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Neighbours of F are C and B.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"4e4caa23-7e79-4a23-a62e-3e3f611c9d58","questionText":"In a row of students, Priya is 15th from the left end and 21st from the right end. How many students are there in the row?","options":["35","36","37","34"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Total students = 15 + 21 - 1 = 35.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"4b36726f-f9cc-4157-a9a4-93428c5846a7","questionText":"A is 10th from the left and B is 15th from the right. When they interchange positions, A becomes 18th from the left. What is B's new position from the right?","options":["22nd","23rd","24th","25th"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Increase in A's position = 18 - 10 = 8 steps. B's new position = 15 + 8 = 23rd.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"827f636f-564d-4462-a603-cce32ac129db","questionText":"In a class of 50 students, Rahul is ranked 18th from the bottom. What is his rank from the top?","options":["32nd","33rd","34th","31st"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Rank from top = 50 - 18 + 1 = 33rd.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"7dceb309-55ec-4391-ade5-62bd823bcbe6","questionText":"In a row of 30 children, Mahesh is 12th from the left and Suresh is 8th from the right. How many children are sitting between them?","options":["10","11","9","12"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Children between them = 30 - (12 + 8) = 10.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"205601bd-c638-479c-9aaf-a756fce9f150","questionText":"4 friends P, Q, R, S are sitting around a square table facing the center. P is opposite to R, Q is to the immediate right of P. Who is to the immediate left of R?","options":["Q","S","P","Cannot be determined"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Facing center: Right of P is Q. Opposite P is R. Since Q is between P and R on P's right, Q is to the immediate left of R.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"b4f1fe73-be56-4f07-a25c-7d125cd8bce6","questionText":"Weight of X is greater than Y. Weight of Z is less than Y. Weight of W is greater than X. Who is the heaviest?","options":["X","Y","Z","W"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Sequence: W > X > Y > Z. The heaviest is W.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"994c6f1d-a1ec-4573-9a4c-0a589a425b06","questionText":"7 boys A, B, C, D, E, F, G are standing in a line according to height. D is in the middle. How many boys are taller than D?","options":["2","3","4","1"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"In a line of 7, the middle position is 4th. Exactly 3 boys are taller than D.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"691aae5e-6319-4b5e-aa05-7d747a4c0059","questionText":"A book is 14th from the top and 14th from the bottom in a stack. How many books are in the stack?","options":["28","27","29","26"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Total books = 14 + 14 - 1 = 27.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"8d7e326c-f883-424a-9777-05fe3b8395f2","questionText":"Marks of A are more than B. Marks of C are equal to D. Marks of B are more than C. Who scored the lowest marks?","options":["A","B","C and D","D only"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Order: A > B > C = D. Both C and D scored the lowest marks.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"6f7677ee-1905-4713-8faa-77272342ddda","questionText":"In a row of 20 persons, A is 15th from left and B is 12th from right. How many persons are between A and B?","options":["5","6","7","5 (Overlapping case = (15 + 12) - 20 - 2 = 5)"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Since 15 + 12 = 27 > 20, it is an overlapping case. Between = (15 + 12) - 20 - 2 = 27 - 22 = 5.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"2a28d32a-939b-4ef7-9d53-18129e8a6a6a","questionText":"In a row facing North, Neha was 8th from the left. She moved 4 places to her right. What is her new position from the left end?","options":["12th","4th","11th","13th"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"New position = 8 + 4 = 12th.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"aa6c69c4-5118-4450-9d87-d11ea35aa338","questionText":"In a row, A is 10th from left and B is 9th from right. If 3 persons sit between them, what is the minimum number of persons in the row?","options":["22","14","16","18"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Minimum persons = (10 + 9) - 3 - 2 = 19 - 5 = 14.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"a4a1024e-c22e-4852-adc9-330d83eec8bb","questionText":"P is older than Q. R is younger than P but older than S. Q is older than R. Who is the youngest?","options":["P","Q","R","S"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Chain: P > Q > R > S. The youngest is S.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"0dfb1f87-51bb-4f35-a1dc-0a2eb8bf3c3e","questionText":"In a class of 30, Amit is 10th from top. If 5 new students join who rank above Amit, what is Amit's new rank from the top?","options":["15th","5th","16th","14th"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"New rank = 10 + 5 = 15th.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"a945949e-5676-4f85-ab0f-e3ace9226406","questionText":"6 persons A, B, C, D, E, F sit around a circular table facing center. A is opposite to D. B is to immediate right of A. Who is opposite to B?","options":["E","F","C","E or F"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Opposite of B is 3rd from B in either direction. Without further details on C, E, F placement, it can be E or F.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"c0cb2f47-d027-4e15-8254-fa2dde170850","questionText":"Out of 45 students, Sita ranks 11th from the top. What is her rank from the bottom?","options":["34th","35th","36th","33rd"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Rank from bottom = 45 - 11 + 1 = 35th.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"d52dde17-3cb8-477c-b7dc-deb1275854e6","questionText":"Salary of A is higher than B. Salary of B is higher than C. Salary of D is higher than A. Who gets the highest salary?","options":["A","B","C","D"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Order: D > A > B > C. Highest earner is D.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"9d6dacc2-3c3e-4772-a3dc-116dd5989f9f","questionText":"If Karan is 16th from both left and right ends of a line, how many total persons are standing in the line?","options":["32","31","30","33"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Total persons = 16 + 16 - 1 = 31.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"}]

chapters.title: Direction Sense Test
chapters.summary: A comprehensive guide to solving direction-based reasoning problems, covering cardinal directions, angular movements, shadow rules, and shortest distance calculations using the Pythagoras theorem.
chapters.questionsJson:
[{"id":"771bab6c-768f-4dd7-8dc5-764d5a51daa1","questionText":"A boy goes in South direction, then he turns towards left and travels for some distance. After that he turns right and moves certain distance. At last he turns left and travel again for some distance. Now, in which direction is he moving?","options":["South","West","East","North"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Starting facing South \xrightarrow{\text{Left turn}} East \xrightarrow{\text{Right turn}} South \xrightarrow{\text{Left turn}} East.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"493574e5-953e-43eb-b0aa-3636773c2163","questionText":"I was facing East from where I turned to my left and walked 12\text{ ft}, then I turned towards right and walked 6\text{ ft}. After that I walked 6\text{ ft} in South direction and at last I walked 6\text{ ft} in the West. Then, in which direction am I standing from the original point?","options":["West","East","South","North"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Starting point (0,0).
Facing East \rightarrow Turn Left (North) and walk 12\text{ ft} \implies (0, 12).
Turn Right (East) and walk 6\text{ ft} \implies (6, 12).
Walk 6\text{ ft} South \implies (6, 6).
Walk 6\text{ ft} West \implies (0, 6).
Point (0, 6) lies directly North of origin (0,0).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"d175a831-9921-4470-9dd2-9a4d78803a93","questionText":"Ram is to the South of Aishwarya and to the West of Rani. If Priyanka is to the South of Ram, then in which direction is Priyanka with respect to Rani?","options":["South","North-East","South-West","North"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Rani is to the East of Ram.
Priyanka is to the South of Ram.
Relative to Rani, Priyanka is located to her West and South, which is South-West.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"89d0cc1e-de86-48e2-a5f1-447020d45e89","questionText":"There are four roads. I have come from the South and want to go the temple. The road to the right leads me towards the coffee house while straight road leads to the college. In which direction is the temple?","options":["North","East","South","West"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Coming from South \rightarrow facing North at the crossroad.
Right road (East) \rightarrow Coffee house.
Straight road (North) \rightarrow College.
Back road (South) \rightarrow Entry road.
Remaining Left road (West) \rightarrow Temple.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"cdb02e3f-0b8d-4dad-9cd1-bdaec032cf51","questionText":"I am facing North. I turn 135^\circ in clockwise direction, then 180^\circ in anti-clockwise direction. What direction am I facing now?","options":["North-East","West","South-East","North-West"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Clockwise turn = +135^\circ
Anti-clockwise turn = -180^\circ
Net turn = -45^\circ (i.e. 45^\circ anti-clockwise).
Turning 45^\circ anti-clockwise from North gives North-West.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"72d554ef-8d34-4d96-b565-725137b5975c","questionText":"Rama is facing East. He turns 90^\circ in clockwise direction, and then 135^\circ in anti-clockwise direction and then again 90^\circ in clockwise direction. Which direction is she facing now?","options":["South-East","South","North-East","South-West"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Net turn = +90^\circ - 135^\circ + 90^\circ = +45^\circ (Clockwise).
Turning 45^\circ clockwise from East gives South-East.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"3aa8de85-d330-4ac2-b3bb-48e56ef0ca82","questionText":"A person walks away from his house at 8:00 am and observes his shadow to his right. Then, he turns towards his left and then again towards his right. Which direction is he facing now?","options":["West","South","North","East"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"At 8:00 AM (Morning), Sun is in East \implies Shadow falls in West.
Since shadow is to his right, he must be walking facing South.
Facing South \xrightarrow{\text{Left turn}} East \xrightarrow{\text{Right turn}} South.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"3a15db7e-8186-478d-afa9-95a8973c963c","questionText":"One day, during Sunset, two friends Sudhir and Amit were talking, facing each other. If Amit's shadow was on his right then in which direction is Aman facing, if Aman faces the direction opposite of what Sudhir is facing?","options":["North","West","East","South"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"At Sunset, Sun is in West \implies Shadows fall in East.
Shadow is on Amit's right \implies Amit faces North.
Since Sudhir talks facing Amit, Sudhir faces South.
Aman faces opposite to Sudhir \implies Aman faces North.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"2a777b90-a5f9-4b2c-a015-fe716a9db017","questionText":"The time in a clock is quarter past twelve (12:15). If the hour hand points to the East, then towards which direction the minute hand is pointing?","options":["South-West","South","West","North"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"At 12:15, Hour hand points near 12 (normally North), Minute hand points at 3 (normally East).
Given: Hour hand (12 position) points East (Rotated 90^\circ Clockwise).
Minute hand (3 position) rotated 90^\circ Clockwise points to South.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"de5a91dd-12a8-4754-88c8-4ce56122b259","questionText":"A house faces North. A man coming out of his house walked straight for 10\text{ m}, turned left and walked 25\text{ m}. He then turned right and walked 5\text{ m} and again turned right and walked 25\text{ m}. How far is he from his house?","options":["15\text{ m}","55\text{ m}","60\text{ m}","65\text{ m}"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Out of house (facing North): Walk 10\text{ m} North.
Turn left (West): Walk 25\text{ m}.
Turn right (North): Walk 5\text{ m}.
Turn right (East): Walk 25\text{ m} (cancels 25\text{ m} West displacement).
Total North displacement = 10\text{ m} + 5\text{ m} = 15\text{ m}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"241832df-5820-46cb-b045-eb16b0e4997a","questionText":"A cyclist goes 30\text{ km} to North and then turning East he goes 40\text{ km}. Again, he turns to his right and goes 20\text{ km}. After this, he turns to his right and goes 40\text{ km}. How far is he from his starting point?","options":["6\text{ km}","10\text{ km}","25\text{ km}","40\text{ km}"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"30\text{ km} North \implies (0, 30).
40\text{ km} East \implies (40, 30).
20\text{ km} South (Right turn) \implies (40, 10).
40\text{ km} West (Right turn) \implies (0, 10).
Distance from origin (0,0) to (0,10) = 10\text{ km}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"654a2fcf-6e89-4d89-9d94-8f26ebfca5ea","questionText":"A boat moves from port towards East. After sailing for 9\text{ miles}, she turns towards right and covers another 12\text{ miles}. If she wants to go back to the port, what is the shortest distance now from her position?","options":["21\text{ miles}","20\text{ miles}","18\text{ miles}","15\text{ miles}"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Base = 9\text{ miles}, Perpendicular = 12\text{ miles}.
\text{Shortest Distance} = \sqrt{9^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{81 + 144} = \sqrt{225} = 15\text{ miles}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"8e613270-e1cd-4ef7-8293-a9ede6dc467b","questionText":"A cyclist rides 40\text{ km} to the East, turns North and rides 20\text{ km}, again turns left and rides 20\text{ km}. How far is he from his starting point?","options":["0\text{ km}","10\text{ km}","15\text{ km}","20\sqrt{2}\text{ km}"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"40\text{ km} East \implies (40, 0).
20\text{ km} North \implies (40, 20).
20\text{ km} West (Left turn) \implies (20, 20).
\text{Distance} = \sqrt{20^2 + 20^2} = \sqrt{800} = 20\sqrt{2}\text{ km}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"9d449787-ee8e-4555-8bdf-81ff64d3e70c","questionText":"A man travels 4\text{ km} due North, then travels 6\text{ km} due East and further travels 4\text{ km} due North. How far is he from the starting point?","options":["6\text{ km}","14\text{ km}","8\text{ km}","10\text{ km}"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Total North displacement = 4\text{ km} + 4\text{ km} = 8\text{ km}.
Total East displacement = 6\text{ km}.
\text{Shortest Distance} = \sqrt{8^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{64 + 36} = \sqrt{100} = 10\text{ km}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"c8483896-550f-4635-9ba2-f78bd0729e41","questionText":"A and B starts walking from same point. A goes North and covers 3\text{ km}, then turns right and covers 4\text{ km}. B goes West and covers 5\text{ km}. Then, turns right and covers 3\text{ km}. How far apart are they from each other?","options":["10\text{ km}","9\text{ km}","8\text{ km}","5\text{ km}"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Position of A: (4, 3).
Position of B: (-5, 3).
Distance between A and B = 4 - (-5) = 9\text{ km}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"4948f6a1-efb8-42d5-8cf1-033a1c9d72d7","questionText":"Rohit walked 25\text{ m} towards South. Then he turned to his left and walked 20\text{ m}. He then turned to his left and walked 25\text{ m}. He again turned to his right and walked 15\text{ m}. At what distance is he from his starting point and in which direction?","options":["35\text{ m}, East","35\text{ m}, North","40\text{ m}, East","60\text{ m}, East"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"25\text{ m} South \implies (0, -25).
Turn left (20\text{ m} East) \implies (20, -25).
Turn left (25\text{ m} North) \implies (20, 0).
Turn right (15\text{ m} East) \implies (35, 0).
Position is 35\text{ m}, East relative to start (0,0).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"152c2971-e597-49d1-97f6-a66470df4330","questionText":"A person starts from point X, walks 8\text{ km} towards North, turns right and walks 6\text{ km}, then turns right and walks 8\text{ km}. In which direction is he from point X and how far?","options":["6\text{ km}, East","6\text{ km}, West","8\text{ km}, East","14\text{ km}, North"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"8\text{ km} North \implies (0, 8).
6\text{ km} East \implies (6, 8).
8\text{ km} South \implies (6, 0).
Distance = 6\text{ km} in East direction.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"bd1f6efe-8a18-4afe-b0a5-37d47ead1e36","questionText":"Mohan walks 10\text{ km} towards West, then turns left and walks 5\text{ km}, again turns left and walks 10\text{ km}. In which direction is he facing now?","options":["West","East","North","South"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Walking West \xrightarrow{\text{Left turn}} South \xrightarrow{\text{Left turn}} East.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"7cef0e8e-1bb0-4447-999a-3a14ef2963bf","questionText":"A girl walks 12\text{ m} towards East, turns right and walks 8\text{ m}, turns right again and walks 12\text{ m}. How far is she from her starting point?","options":["12\text{ m}","8\text{ m}","20\text{ m}","4\text{ m}"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"(0,0) \rightarrow (12, 0) \rightarrow (12, -8) \rightarrow (0, -8).
Distance from starting point = 8\text{ m}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"e3799087-8930-470f-a6e5-df252708ca2f","questionText":"Kausal walks 15\text{ km} towards North, then turns South and walks 20\text{ km}, then turns East and walks 5\text{ km}. In which direction is he with respect to his starting point?","options":["North-East","South-East","South-West","North-West"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"15\text{ km} North \implies (0, 15).
20\text{ km} South \implies (0, -5).
5\text{ km} East \implies (5, -5).
Position (5, -5) is in South-East relative to (0,0).","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"2ed5514b-6b60-48d5-bbe9-d069dc6a78f5","questionText":"A person moves 3\text{ km} East, 4\text{ km} North, 6\text{ km} West, and 8\text{ km} South. How far is he from his starting point?","options":["5\text{ km}","7\text{ km}","10\text{ km}","12\text{ km}"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Net East-West = 3 - 6 = -3\text{ km} (3 km West).
Net North-South = 4 - 8 = -4\text{ km} (4 km South).
\text{Distance} = \sqrt{(-3)^2 + (-4)^2} = \sqrt{9 + 16} = \sqrt{25} = 5\text{ km}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"96ae27e5-9188-48b1-83b1-8acc46f1513e","questionText":"A person is facing South-East. He turns 180^\circ clockwise. Which direction is he facing now?","options":["South-West","North-West","North-East","North"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"A 180^\circ turn points directly to the opposite direction.
Opposite of South-East is North-West.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"0a577ced-fd67-40b4-b855-8bcd63db6cb1","questionText":"At sunrise, Seema stands facing a pole. The shadow of the pole falls exactly to her right. Which direction is Seema facing?","options":["North","South","East","West"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"At sunrise, shadow falls towards West.
Since shadow is to her right, West is to her right \implies She faces South.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"8ae15a69-dc1f-46bc-b283-dbbbdfb8d7d9","questionText":"A clock is placed such that at 3:00 PM, the minute hand points to North-East. In which direction will the hour hand point?","options":["South-East","South-West","North-West","South"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"At 3:00 PM, minute hand is at 12, hour hand is at 3 (90^\circ CW from minute hand).
Minute hand points North-East.
90^\circ CW from North-East is South-East.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"166d927b-92ed-41a3-a875-52e75633fd7f","questionText":"Anitha walks 10\text{ m} West, turns left and walks 10\text{ m}, turns left and walks 10\text{ m}, turns right and walks 10\text{ m}. How far is she from the starting point?","options":["10\text{ m}","20\text{ m}","30\text{ m}","40\text{ m}"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"(0,0) \rightarrow (-10, 0) \rightarrow (-10, -10) \rightarrow (0, -10) \rightarrow (0, -20).
Distance from origin = 20\text{ m}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"df91b85c-4389-4add-b602-953f8126f476","questionText":"Town B is to the North of Town A. Town C is to the East of Town B. In which direction is Town C with respect to Town A?","options":["South-East","North-East","South-West","North-West"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"B is North of A (0, y).
C is East of B (x, y).
Position of C relative to A (0,0) is North-East.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"7a609336-f6ee-4e34-9484-96baa44cda64","questionText":"A driver drives 5\text{ km} North, turns left and drives 3\text{ km}, turns left again and drives 5\text{ km}. In which direction is he driving now?","options":["North","South","East","West"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"North \xrightarrow{\text{Left}} West \xrightarrow{\text{Left}} South.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"73a4a210-cfc2-4a56-bab1-d45e922b6bb6","questionText":"A runner runs 6\text{ km} South and 8\text{ km} West. What is the shortest distance to return to the start?","options":["14\text{ km}","10\text{ km}","12\text{ km}","2\text{ km}"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"\text{Distance} = \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{36 + 64} = \sqrt{100} = 10\text{ km}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"7d64a5e9-1f92-4c6a-8cdf-3aa167cf3e2d","questionText":"Facing South, a man turns 90^\circ anti-clockwise, then 180^\circ clockwise, then 90^\circ anti-clockwise. Which direction is he facing?","options":["North","South","East","West"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Net turn = -90^\circ + 180^\circ - 90^\circ = 0^\circ.
He remains facing South.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"4c4b3d19-0d6e-47b3-a045-5e110185270e","questionText":"At sunset, Rahul notices his shadow directly in front of him. In which direction is he facing?","options":["East","West","North","South"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"At sunset, light comes from West, shadow falls in East.
If shadow is in front of him, he is facing East.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"9fbb30fd-d704-49a1-8fcc-ded98bf5df36","questionText":"Two cars start from the same point and travel in opposite directions along a straight road. Car A travels 50\text{ km} East, Car B travels 30\text{ km} West. How far apart are they?","options":["20\text{ km}","80\text{ km}","1500\text{ km}","40\text{ km}"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Position of A = +50, Position of B = -30.
Distance = 50 - (-30) = 80\text{ km}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"6811cbda-7798-4223-ba33-dcefadbf76f1","questionText":"Village P is 10\text{ km} West of Village Q. Village R is 10\text{ km} South of Village P. In which direction is Village R from Village Q?","options":["South-East","South-West","North-West","North-East"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Village Q at (0,0), P at (-10, 0), R at (-10, -10).
Relative to Q, R is in South-West.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"ddc95d06-4b1f-4fbf-8c9f-fea4f822c996","questionText":"A person walks 5\text{ m} North, turns right and walks 5\text{ m}, turns right and walks 5\text{ m}. How far is he from starting point?","options":["0\text{ m}","5\text{ m}","10\text{ m}","15\text{ m}"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"(0,0) \rightarrow (0,5) \rightarrow (5,5) \rightarrow (5,0).
Distance from start (0,0) = 5\text{ m}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"a760095e-fd11-4ca1-a7ca-c7031d22d07c","questionText":"Facing East, a person turns 45^\circ CW, then 90^\circ CCW, then 135^\circ CW. What direction is he facing now?","options":["South","West","North","South-East"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Net turn = +45^\circ - 90^\circ + 135^\circ = +90^\circ (CW).
90^\circ CW from East is South.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"fb7ecbdf-344a-45ed-b27b-2ef9ffca2420","questionText":"At 7:00 AM, a morning walker sees his shadow to his left. In which direction is he walking?","options":["North","South","East","West"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"At 7 AM, shadow falls to West.
West is to his left \implies He is facing North.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"a3cc0fe9-25df-4d66-adda-b922ece0995f","questionText":"A man moves 12\text{ km} North, then 5\text{ km} East. How far is he from his starting point?","options":["13\text{ km}","17\text{ km}","7\text{ km}","15\text{ km}"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Distance = \sqrt{12^2 + 5^2} = \sqrt{144 + 25} = \sqrt{169} = 13\text{ km}.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"}]

chapters.title: Mathematical Operations and Reasoning
chapters.summary: This chapter covers the core principles of simplifying mathematical expressions using the VBODMAS precedence hierarchy, solving substitution-based operator problems, interchanging signs, and applying algebraic reasoning to word problems.
chapters.questionsJson:
[{"id":"8a61c066-d783-4799-9c0b-88ecc4c0d551","questionText":"If 'P' stands for '-', 'Q' stands for '\times', 'R' stands for '\div', and 'S' stands for '+', then what is the value of the given equation?

$$14 \text{ Q } 3 \text{ P } 12 \text{ S } 4 \text{ R } 2$$","options":["17","32","28","6"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Replacing the letter variables with their respective arithmetic operators:
$$14 \times 3 - 12 + 4 \div 2$$

Applying VBODMAS:
1. Division: $4 \div 2 = 2$
2. Multiplication: $14 \times 3 = 42$
3. Addition & Subtraction: $42 - 12 + 2 = 32$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"87164ed0-844e-4690-8d82-6d921f7525a7","questionText":"If 'A' stands for '+', 'B' stands for '-', 'C' stands for '\div', and 'D' stands for '\times', then which of the following expressions is correct?","options":["36 A 6 C 7 B 2 D 6 = 20","36 C 6 D 3 A 5 B 3 = 24","36 B 6 C 3 A 5 D 3 = 45","36 D 6 C 3 A 5 B 3 = 74"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Testing Option (d) with $\text{D} \rightarrow \times$, $\text{C} \rightarrow \div$, $\text{A} \rightarrow +$, $\text{B} \rightarrow -$:
$$36 \times 6 \div 3 + 5 - 3 = 74$$

Applying VBODMAS:
1. Division: $6 \div 3 = 2$
2. Multiplication: $36 \times 2 = 72$
3. Addition & Subtraction: $72 + 5 - 3 = 74$

Since LHS = RHS = 74, option (d) is correct.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"cddca7a6-e221-46e7-956a-a70f95cff3ed","questionText":"Which one of the given interchanges in signs would make the given expression correct?

$$30 - 6 + 8 \div 2 \times 3 = 7$$","options":["+ and \times","- and +","- and \div","+ and -"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Interchanging $-$ and $\div$ in the expression $30 - 6 + 8 \div 2 \times 3 = 7$ gives:
$$30 \div 6 + 8 - 2 \times 3 = 7$$

Applying VBODMAS:
1. Division: $30 \div 6 = 5$
2. Multiplication: $2 \times 3 = 6$
3. Addition & Subtraction: $5 + 8 - 6 = 7$.

Since LHS = RHS = 7, the interchange is correct.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"41a91e65-f5ce-44d9-9d6e-8a1f34bab3b1","questionText":"In the following question, correct the given equation by interchanging two numbers.

$$8 \times 4 + 3 - 9 = 11$$","options":["3 and 4","4 and 8","8 and 3","5 and 9"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"By interchanging the numbers 8 and 3, the equation becomes:
$$3 \times 4 + 8 - 9 = 11$$
$$12 + 8 - 9 = 11$$
$$20 - 9 = 11$$
$$11 = 11$$

Since LHS = RHS, the interchange of 8 and 3 is correct.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"2bfe0065-fb1e-476b-9d13-dc87ec55241c","questionText":"Correct the following equation by interchanging two signs:

$$5 + 3 \times 8 - 12 \div 4 = 20$$","options":["+ and \div","- and \div","\times and +","None of the above"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"By interchanging $+$ and $\times$, the equation becomes:
$$5 \times 3 + 8 - 12 \div 4 = 20$$

Applying VBODMAS:
1. Division: $12 \div 4 = 3$
2. Multiplication: $5 \times 3 = 15$
3. Addition & Subtraction: $15 + 8 - 3 = 20$
$$23 - 3 = 20$$
$$20 = 20$$

Since LHS = RHS, option (c) is correct.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"39a45c71-1f2e-41d3-a864-7494a068d868","questionText":"Correct the following equation by interchanging two signs:

$$12 - 4 + 8 \times 3 \div 6 = 12$$","options":["+ and -","+ and \times","- and +","\times and +"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"By interchanging $+$ and $-$, the equation becomes:
$$12 + 4 - 8 \times 3 \div 6 = 12$$

Applying VBODMAS:
1. Division & Multiplication: $8 \times 3 \div 6 = 24 \div 6 = 4$
2. Addition & Subtraction: $12 + 4 - 4 = 12$
$$16 - 4 = 12$$
$$12 = 12$$

Since LHS = RHS, option (a) is correct.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"50c1ca01-4f7d-4c71-be7e-1dd0b1d20f11","questionText":"Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace * signs and to balance the following equation:

$$8 * 6 * 2 * 24$$","options":["\div, =, \times","\times, =, \div","=, +, +","\times, \div, ="],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Replacing the '*' signs with the operators in option (d) ($\times, \div, =$):
$$8 \times 6 \div 2 = 24$$
$$48 \div 2 = 24$$
$$24 = 24$$

Since LHS = RHS, option (d) is correct.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"a7792aa6-104e-4148-ae46-d7bb2e9870ef","questionText":"Put the correct mathematical signs in the following expression from the given alternatives:

$$24 * 4 * 2 * 3 = 25$$","options":["+, -, \times","\times, \div, +","\div, \times, +","-, \div, +"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"By substituting the signs from option (d) ($-, \div, +$) into the expression:
$$24 - 4 \div 2 + 3 = 25$$

Applying VBODMAS:
1. Division: $4 \div 2 = 2$
2. Addition & Subtraction: $24 - 2 + 3 = 25$
$$22 + 3 = 25$$
$$25 = 25$$

Since LHS = RHS, option (d) is correct.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"306debd7-2141-4db9-9906-c2db74eb5593","questionText":"Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace * and balance the expression:

$$8 * 5 * 2 * 168 * 4$$","options":["=, \times, +, \div","\times, =, +, *","\times, +, =, \div","+, \times, =, \div"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"By substituting the signs from option (c) ($\times, +, =, \div$) into the expression:
$$8 \times 5 + 2 = 168 \div 4$$

LHS: $8 \times 5 + 2 = 40 + 2 = 42$
RHS: $168 \div 4 = 42$

Since LHS = RHS, option (c) balances the statement.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"7720226b-a01f-4417-8c3f-bae56fc4e0f3","questionText":"Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace * signs and to balance the given equation:

$$8 * 5 * 2 * 3 * 7$$","options":["+ , - , \times, =","+ , - , + , =","\times, - , + , =","+ , \times, + , ="],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"By substituting the signs from option (a) ($+, -, \times, =$) into the expression:
$$8 + 5 - 2 \times 3 = 7$$

Applying VBODMAS:
1. Multiplication: $2 \times 3 = 6$
2. Addition & Subtraction: $8 + 5 - 6 = 7$
$$13 - 6 = 7$$
$$7 = 7$$

Since LHS = RHS, option (a) is correct.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"626690b0-a246-45d3-a89d-70e9176779d6","questionText":"If $6 \times 4 \times 3 = 436$, $6 \times 9 \times 8 = 986$, and $8 \times 4 \times x = 468$, then what is the value of 'x'?","options":["9","5","3","6"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"The pattern rearranges the digits as: Middle digit + Last digit + First digit.
- $6 \times 4 \times 3 \rightarrow 436$
- $6 \times 9 \times 8 \rightarrow 986$
- $8 \times 4 \times x \rightarrow 4x8$

Given that $4x8 = 468$, we find $x = 6$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"b6ed464e-9fd4-4df5-a036-45d2f7dcea1d","questionText":"If $2 \times 2 = 16$, $2 \times 4 = 64$, and $2 \times 5 = 100$, then $2 \times 6 = ?$","options":["125","169","144","225"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"The logic applied is: $(A \times B)^2$.
- $2 \times 2 \rightarrow (2 \times 2)^2 = 4^2 = 16$
- $2 \times 4 \rightarrow (2 \times 4)^2 = 8^2 = 64$
- $2 \times 5 \rightarrow (2 \times 5)^2 = 10^2 = 100$

Therefore, for $2 \times 6$:
$$(2 \times 6)^2 = 12^2 = 144$$","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"036fdd36-7060-4ee3-bb78-2c6e7b2b8f5f","questionText":"If $4 + 3 = 25$ and $8 + 4 = 80$, then $3 + 2 = ?$","options":["15","10","13","12"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"The logic applied is: $A^2 + B^2$.
- $4 + 3 \rightarrow 4^2 + 3^2 = 16 + 9 = 25$
- $8 + 4 \rightarrow 8^2 + 4^2 = 64 + 16 = 80$

Therefore, for $3 + 2$:
$$3^2 + 2^2 = 9 + 4 = 13$$","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"5a2049a7-2848-4414-b383-a084a1e43d28","questionText":"If $19\ (36)\ 13$ and $37\ (81)\ 28$, then what is the value of 'A' in $43\ (\text{A})\ 38$?","options":["49","25","34","64"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"The logic for the middle number is: $(A - B)^2$.
- $19\ (36)\ 13 \rightarrow (19 - 13)^2 = 6^2 = 36$
- $37\ (81)\ 28 \rightarrow (37 - 28)^2 = 9^2 = 81$

Therefore, for $43\ (\text{A})\ 38$:
$$\text{A} = (43 - 38)^2 = 5^2 = 25$$","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"9d6051e1-2e08-4f00-be5c-22a57cc0ee8b","questionText":"If $5 \times 6 \times 9 = 659$ and $4 \times 7 \times 3 = 743$, then $9 \times 2 \times 8 = ?$","options":["928","298","982","829"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"The order mapping is: Middle digit + First digit + Last digit.
- $5 \times 6 \times 9 \rightarrow 659$
- $4 \times 7 \times 3 \rightarrow 743$

Therefore, for $9 \times 2 \times 8$:
$$9 \times 2 \times 8 \rightarrow 298$$","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"1a31d5bb-6a11-4842-87d1-e9eee5c84513","questionText":"If $7 \times 4 \times 8 = 4498$ and $3 \times 6 	imes 5 = 695$, then $5 \times 9 \times 4 = ?$","options":["9254","9144","954","949"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"The pattern is: Middle digit + First digit squared + Last digit.
- $7 \times 4 \times 8 \rightarrow 4 + (7^2) + 8 = 4498$
- $3 \times 6 \times 5 \rightarrow 6 + (3^2) + 5 = 695$

Therefore, for $5 \times 9 \times 4$:
$$9 + (5^2) + 4 = 9254$$","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"48ab60f7-0d05-4e71-931f-631b92c885e0","questionText":"A box has 15 dozen candles. There are 39 such boxes. How many candles are there in all the boxes?","options":["7020","6660","6652","3510"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"1 dozen = 12 candles.
Candles per box = $15 \times 12 = 180$ candles.
Total candles in 39 boxes = $180 \times 39 = 7020$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"450bf95a-982f-4275-9227-65f463b0f042","questionText":"Of the three numbers, first is double of second and second is 3 times of third. If their average is 100, then the largest number among them will be:","options":["120","150","180","300"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Let the third number be $x$.
- Second number = $3x$
- First number = $2 \times 3x = 6x$

Average = $\frac{6x + 3x + x}{3} = 100$
$$\frac{10x}{3} = 100 \implies 10x = 300 \implies x = 30$$

The largest number (first number) = $6x = 6 \times 30 = 180$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"39b19aff-1596-4867-afd1-59b1cffa3656","questionText":"A father increases pocket money of his son by 20%. If son gets ₹300 after increment, find his pocket money before increment.","options":["₹250","₹240","₹200","₹230"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Let the initial pocket money be $x$.
After a 20% increment, the pocket money becomes:
$$x + 20\% \text{ of } x = 1.20x$$

Given that the new pocket money is ₹300:
$$1.20x = 300 \implies x = \frac{300}{1.20} = 250$$

Thus, his pocket money before increment was ₹250.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"73944aea-8222-4884-9ada-a74eafe9a222","questionText":"In a Survey, 70% of those surveyed owned a car and 75% of those owned a TV. If 55% owned both a car and a TV, what percent of those did not own either a car or a TV?","options":["25","20","10","5"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Percentage of people owning at least one = $P(\text{Car}) + P(\text{TV}) - P(\text{Both})$
$$P(\text{Car} \cup \text{TV}) = 70\% + 75\% - 55\% = 90\%$$

Percentage of people owning neither = $100\% - 90\% = 10\%$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"842e27f8-d466-4bb4-9f00-afb8af9391b4","questionText":"In a survey of a town, it was found that 65% of the people surveyed watch the news on TV, 40% read a newspaper and 25% read a newspaper and watch the news on TV. What percent of the people surveyed neither watch the news on TV nor read a newspaper?","options":["5","10","20","15"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Total percentage of people doing at least one activity = $65\% + 40\% - 25\% = 80\%$.
Percentage of people doing neither = $100\% - 80\% = 20\%$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"fc7fb74e-2911-41f5-af8a-092a3e010fef","questionText":"60% of students in a school are boys. The number of girls in the school is 300, then the number of boys is:","options":["450","500","300","750"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Percentage of girls = $100\% - 60\% = 40\%$.
Let the total number of students be $T$.
$$40\% \text{ of } T = 300 \implies \frac{40}{100} \times T = 300 \implies T = 750$$

Number of boys = $60\% \text{ of } 750 = \frac{60}{100} \times 750 = 450$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"4ce8667f-5595-483c-a4c3-591eb199e63c","questionText":"In a group of equal number of cows and herdsmen the number of legs was 28 less than four times the number of heads. The number of herdsmen was:","options":["7","28","21","14"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Let the number of cows be $x$ and the number of herdsmen be $x$.
- Total heads = $x + x = 2x$
- Total legs = $4x$ (cows) + $2x$ (herdsmen) = $6x$

According to the question:
$$6x = 4(2x) - 28$$
$$6x = 8x - 28$$
$$2x = 28 \implies x = 14$$

Thus, the number of herdsmen was 14.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"5c95b37e-5d8b-4b1a-9c31-c41553c7c7bf","questionText":"The age of Ram is double that of Shyam and half of Sohan. Shyam is older than Mohan. Who is the oldest?","options":["Mohan","Ram","Sohan","Shyam"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Let Shyam's age be $x$.
- Ram's age = $2x$
- Ram is half of Sohan's age $\implies$ Sohan's age = $2 \times 2x = 4x$
- Shyam is older than Mohan $\implies$ Mohan's age $< x$

Comparing ages: Sohan ($4x$) > Ram ($2x$) > Shyam ($x$) > Mohan.
Therefore, Sohan is the oldest.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"c723773a-bfa8-4287-9d36-cef933995963","questionText":"A father is twice his son's present age. How many years ago, was he three times his son's age, if his son's age is now 20 yr?","options":["8 yr","10 yr","12 yr","15 yr"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Son's present age = 20 yr.
Father's present age = $2 \times 20 = 40$ yr.

Let $y$ years ago the father was 3 times his son's age:
$$40 - y = 3(20 - y)$$
$$40 - y = 60 - 3y$$
$$2y = 20 \implies y = 10\text{ yr}$$

Thus, it was 10 years ago.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"8c5a7a44-4ccc-4cd8-9f54-24758b777729","questionText":"The total age of a mother and her daughter is 60 yr. The difference between their age is 30 yr. Find out the age of mother.","options":["40 yr","50 yr","45 yr","55 yr"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Let Mother's age be $M$ and Daughter's age be $D$.
1) $M + D = 60$
2) $M - D = 30$

Adding both equations:
$$2M = 90 \implies M = 45\text{ yr}$$

Thus, the age of the mother is 45 yr.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"fd865bf8-29c1-4c99-baa0-780ef0748e2b","questionText":"A bus leaves Delhi with half the number of women as men. At Meerut, ten men get down and five women get in. Now, there are equal number of men and women. How many passengers boarded the bus initially at Delhi?","options":["36","45","15","30"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Let the initial number of women be $x$. Then the initial number of men is $2x$.
Initial total passengers = $x + 2x = 3x$.

At Meerut:
- New men count = $2x - 10$
- New women count = $x + 5$

Since the counts are now equal:
$$2x - 10 = x + 5 \implies x = 15$$

Initial total passengers = $3x = 3 \times 15 = 45$.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"}]

1) 'Reasoning is easy' \rightarrow 'la ja nu'
2) 'Take it Easy' \rightarrow 're sa nu'

The word 'Easy' and the code 'nu' are common to both statements. Therefore, the code for 'Easy' is nu.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"8333be7d-05b9-4f4a-97f4-0cc6f6030c6a","questionText":"In a certain code language 'Sun is bright' is written as 'pa ma la', 'Sky is blue' is written as 'da ma re' and 'Sun is hot' is written as 'pa ma go'. Find the code for Sun.","options":["pa","ma","Either 'pa' or 'ma'","re"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Comparing 'Sun is bright' (pa ma la) and 'Sky is blue' (da ma re): The word 'is' is common, so 'is' = ma.
Comparing 'Sun is bright' (pa ma la) and 'Sun is hot' (pa ma go): The words 'Sun' and 'is' are common, corresponding to codes 'pa' and 'ma'. Since 'is' = ma, the code for 'Sun' must be pa.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"c31841dd-186c-41fe-bc9d-b3b187eb5c45","questionText":"In a certain code language 'what I want' is written as 'su ma te', 'they want food' is written as 'ro te ko' and 'food and what' is written as 'ko le su'. What does 'te' mean in the above code language?","options":["want","food","they","and"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"'te' is common in Statement 1 ('what I want' = su ma te) and Statement 2 ('they want food' = ro te ko). The common word between Statement 1 and Statement 2 is 'want'. Therefore, 'te' means want.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"bfe36ac3-9342-43da-9a53-0082d2ccf14d","questionText":"In a certain code language 'what I want' is written as 'su ma te', 'they want food' is written as 'ro te ko' and 'food and what' is written as 'ko le su'. What is the code for 'I want food'?","options":["te ko ro","le te su","ma te ko","ko ma ro"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"From the previous analysis:
1) 'want' = te.
2) Comparing Statement 2 ('they want food' = ro te ko) & Statement 3 ('food and what' = ko le su): The common word is 'food' and the common code is 'ko' \implies 'food' = ko.
3) Statement 1 ('what I want' = su ma te) and Statement 3 share 'what' = su. Since 'want' = te and 'what' = su, the remaining word 'I' = ma.

Combining the codes for 'I want food' gives: ma te ko.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"}]

past.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"}]

chapters.title: Clauses
chapters.summary: This chapter provides a comprehensive guide to clauses, exploring their types—including principal, coordinate, and subordinate clauses—and detailing the functions of noun, adjective, and adverb clauses.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Pair of Words (Homonyms)
chapters.summary: This chapter covers homonyms—words that are similar in pronunciation or spelling but differ significantly in meaning and usage. It provides clear definitions, contextual examples, and comparative structures to master these commonly confused pairs.

chapters.title: Ratio And Proportion
chapters.summary: This chapter covers the fundamental concepts of ratios and proportions, including derived ratios, comparison methods, properties of proportions, and practical shortcut techniques for competitive exams.
chapters.questionsJson: [{"id":"f28c3357-98fb-4165-b0f0-e69b9d575525","questionText":"The ratio of 40 m and 2 km is:","options":["1 : 50","2 : 35","1 : 40","3 : 25"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Converting 2 km to meters gives 2000 m. The ratio of 40 m to 2000 m simplifies to 1 : 50.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"b0828e57-24d6-4f9e-b381-4afc95feca7b","questionText":"If x : y = 3 : 1, then the ratio of x³ − y³ : x³ + y³ is:","options":["12 : 11","13 : 21","13 : 14","21 : 42"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Substituting x = 3 and y = 1, we get (27 - 1) : (27 + 1) = 26 : 28, which simplifies to 13 : 14.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"b5687888-4af4-41c0-ad8a-a706c0ebb1be","questionText":"If two numbers are in the ratio 5 : 8 and 9 is added to each, the ratio becomes 8 : 11. The lower number is:","options":["10","13","12","15"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Solving the equation (5x + 9)\/(8x + 9) = 8\/11 gives x = 3. The lower number is 5x = 15.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"5298cd70-deac-4458-8825-5a1d2db1a5a3","questionText":"If x : y = 3 : 4, then the value of (5x - 2y) \/ (7x + 2y) is:","options":["7\/25","7\/23","7\/29","7\/17"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Substituting x = 3 and y = 4 into the expression yields (15 - 8) \/ (21 + 8) = 7\/29.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"c828e804-2392-4623-a1c2-50a083b81029","questionText":"The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 5 : 4. Which of the following cannot be the number of students in the class?","options":["45","72","108","98"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"The total number of students must be a multiple of the sum of the ratio terms (5 + 4 = 9). Since 98 is not divisible by 9, it cannot be the total number of students.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"40fb4d51-8fff-47b8-97d5-d43ab7360311","questionText":"Two numbers are in the ratio 2 : 3 and their product is 96. The sum of the numbers is:","options":["5","20","101","102"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Letting the numbers be 2x and 3x, their product is 6x² = 96, which gives x = 4. The sum of the numbers is 5x = 20.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"9b0f7462-db35-4637-bf4c-83a5b9baab0f","questionText":"The present ratio of ages of A and B is 4 : 5. Eighteen years ago, this ratio was 11 : 16. The sum of their present ages is:","options":["90 years","105 years","110 years","80 years"],"correctOptionIndex":0,"explanation":"Solving (4x - 18)\/(5x - 18) = 11\/16 gives x = 10. The sum of their present ages is 9x = 90 years.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"3648818f-c1f4-4e1d-a3e0-9b54ad3d79c4","questionText":"If a : b = c : d, then the value of (a² + b²) \/ (c² + d²) is:","options":["1\/2","(a + b)\/(c + d)","(a − b)\/(c − d)","b²\/d²"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"Letting a = bk and c = dk, the expression simplifies to (b²k² + b²) \/ (d²k² + d²) = b²\/d².","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"2faec143-b2fb-4246-abea-c090c79a81bd","questionText":"If p : q = 3 : 4 and q : r = 8 : 9, then p : r is:","options":["1 : 3","3 : 2","2 : 3","1 : 2"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Multiplying the ratios, p\/r = (p\/q) * (q\/r) = (3\/4) * (8\/9) = 6\/12 = 2\/3.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"1788be04-f190-4468-a231-32bb00d86352","questionText":"The ratio between the monthly incomes of A and B is 9 : 8 and the ratio between their expenditures is 8 : 7. If they save ₹500 each, then A's monthly income is:","options":["₹3,500","₹4,000","₹4,500","₹5,000"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"Since both save ₹500, the difference in ratio units for both income and expenditure is 1 unit (9 - 8 = 1 and 8 - 7 = 1), which equals ₹500. Thus, A's income is 9 * ₹500 = ₹4,500.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"fba10d5b-3311-4126-9847-83667de7e2dc","questionText":"The greater ratio between 2 : 3 and 4 : 5 is:","options":["2 : 3","4 : 5","Cannot be determined","Both are equal"],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"Converting to decimals, 2\/3 ≈ 0.67 and 4\/5 = 0.80. Since 0.80 > 0.67, 4 : 5 is the greater ratio.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"42024fa6-e12b-4a5b-8556-37f2cfb0d298","questionText":"The value of ? in 2 : ? :: ? : 32 is:","options":["64","34","30","8"],"correctOptionIndex":3,"explanation":"In a proportion, the product of the means equals the product of the extremes, so x² = 2 * 32 = 64, which gives x = 8.","difficulty":"MEDIUM"},{"id":"d6359d10-c2bb-4399-a537-fb2929bbae4c","questionText":"The third proportional to 10 and 30 is:","options":["40","30","90","33"],"correctOptionIndex":2,"explanation":"The third proportional x to a and b is given by b²\/a. chapters.title: Computer Fundamentals
chapters.summary: An introductory guide to computer fundamentals, covering core characteristics, the Von Neumann architecture, functional units, bus systems, and the step-by-step instruction cycle.

chapters.title: Computer Hardware
chapters.summary: This chapter provides a comprehensive overview of computer hardware, detailing the functions, mechanisms, and classifications of various input and output devices, display technologies, printers, and plotters.

chapters.title: Pronouns
chapters.summary: This chapter covers the definition, functions, classification, and essential grammatical rules of pronouns, focusing on personal, reflexive, demonstrative, indefinite, relative, and interrogative pronouns with high-yield exam tips.
chapters.questionsJson: [{"id":"685cfcd9-718d-4b89-803c-10cc515b70fd","questionText":"Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct according to traditional rules of pronoun order?","options":["I, you and he will study together.","You, he and I will study together.","He, you and I will study together.","You, I and he will study together."],"correctOptionIndex":1,"explanation":"For normal or positive statements, the pronoun order is Second Person (2) -> Third Person (3) -> First Person (1). {
  "chapterId": "chap_3c1261f5",
  "title": "Profit, Loss and Discount",
  "elements": [
    {
      "id": "9a688ca1-cde3-45a6-9dbd-816361ea42cf",
      "type": "HEADING_1",
      "text": "Chapter 8: Profit, Loss and Discount",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ddac0752-a493-4b33-985e-5308b8bf6a41",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Quick Overview",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e8531fd2-9d95-4e51-ba58-3ec2888da273",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Cost Price (CP): The price at which an article is purchased or manufactured.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a4ab3372-7639-44d7-bb27-cfcb1d966cea",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Selling Price (SP): The price at which an article is sold.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "07afc89d-1ce8-418d-ba2a-a440c010096a",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Profit or Gain: Occurs when selling price is greater than cost price (SP > CP).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0e988ed7-edd4-49cb-b15a-32703a144e3d",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Loss: Occurs when selling price is less than cost price (SP < CP).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9d379fac-530a-498f-bede-952ea1bc22ee",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Discount: A rebate given to the buyer by the seller to increase the sale. Discount is always given on the marked price or printed price of the article.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0c8d920b-4927-4fd0-ae64-c80457c86509",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Important Formulae",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "bcf531f7-fe6c-4dd3-8271-421147d2d6d6",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Core Formulas",
      "content": "1. Profit Percentage = (Profit \/ CP) * 100\n2. Loss Percentage = (Loss \/ CP) * 100\n3. Cost Price (CP) Formula:\n   - When there is profit: CP = (SP * 100) \/ (100 + Profit %)\n   - When there is loss: CP = (SP * 100) \/ (100 - Loss %)\n4. Selling Price (SP) Formula:\n   - When there is profit: SP = [CP * (100 + Profit %)] \/ 100\n   - When there is loss: SP = [CP * (100 - Loss %)] \/ 100\n5. Discount Percentage = (Discount \/ Marked Price) * 100"
    },
    {
      "id": "d7e7b1e6-f660-4276-8f8c-ef5574de7352",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Advanced Concepts & Rules",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "58c48769-e809-414e-9e7e-8f252110f228",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "1. Successive Discounts",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1bbb4444-e80e-4744-aaf1-64de97db06a5",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "If two successive discounts of x% and y% are given on an article, they can be simplified into a single equivalent discount.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "77504d4f-2da5-48de-a685-984548530f08",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Equivalent Discount Formula",
      "content": "Equivalent Discount = (x + y - (x * y) \/ 100)%"
    },
    {
      "id": "c706dc76-56c1-4080-ba81-49a3c4ce2326",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "2. False Weight",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "58d0d38e-f6ab-46a9-ad2a-2000b3b4ae33",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "When a trader uses a false weight instead of the true weight to sell goods, the profit percentage is calculated based on the error in weight.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8ae2845d-8369-42f6-bce5-11d40d3fe6a6",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "False Weight Gain Formula",
      "content": "Gain % = [Error \/ (True Value - Error)] * 100%"
    },
    {
      "id": "b135c7da-fd68-4846-a4af-b04750e6566c",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "3. Change in Selling Condition",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e24f211c-fcf0-4e5e-ba72-6bc423212177",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Case A: A person sells goods at a profit of x%. Had he sold it for Rs. X more, y% would have been gained. In this case, CP = [X \/ (y - x)] * 100.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "08c93a6a-2680-410a-81a2-3568747ee9ca",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Case B: A person sells goods at a loss of x%. Had he sold it for Rs. X more, he would have gained y%. In this case, CP = [X \/ (y + x)] * 100.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "28bc28d0-be3a-4402-86cf-945c7d9e1540",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Case C: When there is a gain of x% and a loss of y%, the net effect is given by: (x - y - (x * y) \/ 100)%.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0de7af98-a2a2-4fa5-a4fc-7f47feb157f9",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "4. Article Quantity Equivalence",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e52ad4e8-b41a-47e5-9ad4-28311a635ed0",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "If the cost price of x articles is equal to the selling price of y articles where x > y, then the transaction results in a gain.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "459309ba-4d2d-415c-9135-db94f9a5f396",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Quantity Equivalence Gain Formula",
      "content": "Gain % = [(x - y) \/ y] * 100%"
    },
    {
      "id": "39c8bbd8-46ad-4364-87cb-5b5d9909cb74",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "5. Ratio of MP and CP",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "957a4b8b-83a5-4dbb-969e-e8beef014e18",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The relationship between the Marked Price (MP) and Cost Price (CP) can be expressed directly as a ratio using profit and discount percentages.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e7b2f984-0cc0-463c-a449-44c43b6df381",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "MP to CP Ratio",
      "content": "MP \/ CP = (100 + P%) \/ (100 - D%)\nWhere P% is the Profit Percentage and D% is the Discount Percentage."
    },
    {
      "id": "5ef990ab-12c1-49bf-899d-2c46bee55314",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "6. Same Selling Price Transaction",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7510e287-8a69-4296-9511-edc589d6b073",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "IMPORTANT",
      "title": "Same Selling Price Rule",
      "content": "In cases where the selling price of two articles is the same, and one is sold at a loss of x% while the other is sold at a profit of x%, the overall transaction always yields a net loss.\n\nNet Loss % = (x \/ 10)^2 %"
    },
    {
      "id": "3cd6836e-8604-4d59-9cb1-61a256ec6a95",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Solved Examples",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "105ba15f-0173-47a4-88c2-c96d463fa228",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 1",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0fde8421-03d3-49e2-a904-37071d39c6be",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A person sells an article for a price which gives him a profit of 20% on a cost price of Rs. 500. Calculate the selling price of the article.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dcce9e9b-291d-4aea-8547-74139c1bc304",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "(a) Rs. 520",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f91d804e-a5d0-4ea4-80f6-276faa568907",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "(b) Rs. 600",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5c402943-92b2-4add-96e1-455e8ddf4873",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "(c) Rs. 720",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "03065f22-e0cf-4dbf-9978-0298b071e3f0",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "(d) Rs. 680",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "512257bb-747a-462d-afbb-4154ae3d12f9",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution to Example 1",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (b) Rs. 600\n\nCalculation:\nSP = CP * [(100 + Profit %) \/ 100]\nSP = 500 * [(100 + 20) \/ 100]\nSP = 500 * (120 \/ 100) = Rs. 600"
    },
    {
      "id": "0cffca0b-3de8-4dae-9c26-043010f5efa1",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 2",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "63d56c9b-5d0d-4125-8372-04448821c54f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A person marks his goods 20% more than the cost price and allows some discount on it. He still makes a profit of 10%. Find the discount percentage.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f1e36891-323d-4ec4-be02-1f72c2fac499",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "(a) 8.33%",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1249488c-1986-4f09-a672-8bf2fa2a877f",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "(b) 16.66%",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ea104aee-0c36-4e80-96b8-9f63c193a81f",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "(c) 10%",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c018bf90-56f7-42f4-a83a-92842dec2850",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "(d) 8.5%",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a2dbfd6f-eeda-408a-b29a-f05761d36e91",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution to Example 2",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (a) 8.33%\n\nCalculation:\n1. Let the CP of the article be Rs. 100.\n2. Then, MP of the article = Rs. 120 (20% markup).\n3. Since profit is 10%, SP = Rs. 110.\n4. Discount Amount = MP - SP = 120 - 110 = Rs. 10.\n5. Discount % = (Discount \/ MP)  100 = (10 \/ 120)  100 = 8.33%"
    },
    {
      "id": "8e55c3c6-6efc-47bb-b4e1-ff225a649fb0",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 3",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ad535e51-7e1d-4310-b258-60e83bc27abf",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "By selling two articles for Rs. 180 each, a shopkeeper gains 20% on one and loses 20% on the other. Find the overall percentage profit or loss.",

      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution to Example 3",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (a) 4% loss\n\nDetailed Method:\n1. Let the cost prices of the two articles be Rs. x and Rs. y.\n2. For the first article (20% gain): 180 = [x  (100 + 20)] \/ 100 => x = (180  100) \/ 120 = Rs. 150.\n3. For the second article (20% loss): 180 = [y  (100 - 20)] \/ 100 => y = (180  100) \/ 80 = Rs. 225.\n4. Total CP = 150 + 225 = Rs. 375.\n5. Total SP = 180 + 180 = Rs. 360.\n6. Net Loss = 375 - 360 = Rs. 15.\n7. Loss % = (15 \/ 375) * 100 = 4%.\n\nShortcut Method:\nSince SP is identical and profit % equals loss % (20%), there is always a loss:\nLoss % = (x \/ 10)^2 = (20 \/ 10)^2 = 4% loss."
