      "rawContent": "Real Numbers is split into Rational Numbers and Irrational Numbers. Rational Numbers is split into Integers. Integers is split into Negative Integers and Whole Numbers. Whole Numbers is split into Zero (0) and Natural Numbers."
    },
    {
      "id": "f73df4ea-89ca-48f2-a1c1-5749cfb966c9",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Core Number Classifications",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ead2e7a0-89cd-4242-9e99-a879a17beedf",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "1. Natural Numbers (N)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "32cab736-477f-48a3-9c47-94c7bad9a984",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "These are the numbers used for counting objects. They start from 1 and go up to infinity.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "693cd39a-81c5-483a-818d-e49ee69b3a89",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "Smallest Natural Number",
      "content": "The smallest natural number is 1."
    },
    {
      "id": "b9605b6b-5981-4aa2-be59-1c9a2889bf5c",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "2. Whole Numbers (W)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c16888a3-dd4f-4b58-9959-2a6ef27a87e7",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "All natural numbers together with zero form the set of whole numbers.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d225df3e-367b-4a67-be3d-51c2109368f7",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "Smallest Whole Number",
      "content": "The smallest whole number is 0."
    },
    {
      "id": "75561bcb-391b-4c02-bda3-685789deb8e2",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "3. Integers (I)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "271712b4-2c1b-43ce-a1f0-8a049d8e718e",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The set of numbers containing all whole numbers and the negatives of natural numbers.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "972ece97-8281-499a-9de6-0ae43353582b",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "4. Rational Numbers",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0f283b59-9df3-438d-bb92-27cf007d520b",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Numbers that can be expressed in the form p\/q, where p and q are integers and q is not equal to 0. Examples include 3\/2, -7\/9, 5, and -2.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8420512d-1845-45a9-9a53-10dfc0345efc",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "IMPORTANT",
      "title": "Density Property",
      "content": "There exists an infinite number of rational numbers between any two rational numbers."
    },
    {
      "id": "33df5d51-577e-4941-93a5-a6fd3b2e2ee5",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "5. Irrational Numbers",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7fa458e7-ae2d-47c0-a9ed-e498d58245ae",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Numbers that cannot be expressed in the form p\/q. These are non-recurring and non-terminating decimals, such as the square root of 3, the square root of 5, and the square root of 29.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ca0aaa57-d167-4dd8-a7bf-e711c2565c39",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "6. Real Numbers",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0cf8cdff-e5a2-486f-b5dd-91c9b9b9aabc",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The complete set of numbers containing both rational and irrational numbers.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b1b606ce-fe2d-497e-9144-354184185288",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Different Types of Numbers",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c79a0e4d-4251-4d1e-b5dc-c8b5d5de5c7b",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Even Numbers",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "417fa635-5056-444c-8fa8-916f8a7a0455",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Numbers that are exactly divisible by 2. Examples: 2, 4, 6, 8, etc.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0f713209-e17c-4a23-b340-24efb5f9f8ce",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Odd Numbers",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7f85df78-9b45-4520-84b8-d45235ffee4c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Numbers that are not exactly divisible by 2. Examples: 1, 3, 5, 7, etc.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a73565b4-7410-4771-bc6c-71a5e7f8b4c4",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Prime Numbers",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ecd25f40-2d13-4df7-b51b-a559bd287fb4",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Numbers greater than 1 that are divisible only by 1 and themselves. Examples: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, etc.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "985ed567-c224-4cb2-b708-609e9c5b571c",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Composite Numbers",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1941c4de-fa7c-41c5-82d6-0ed37851784f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Numbers greater than 1 that are not prime. They have more than two factors. Examples: 4, 6, 9, 15, etc.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "414ac6f1-30d3-4f0b-81d6-3aa4a9ee5489",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Relative Prime Numbers (Co-primes)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "957a7ed8-9256-4e06-abd9-f36e53f8496a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Two numbers are relatively prime if they do not share any common factor other than 1. Examples: (3, 5), (4, 7), (11, 15).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8f8853d5-e0f5-409d-a6bb-8a96d00eacab",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Twin Primes",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0b2551a9-2e97-4093-90b9-69a6236f16cc",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Two prime numbers that differ by exactly 2. Examples: (3, 5), (5, 7), (11, 13).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9c68adea-79f1-4230-a54d-338515fbf6c2",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Perfect Numbers",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f2ab3e93-7c9d-4a3c-bb6f-d8f036e49a80",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A number is perfect if the sum of all its factors (excluding the number itself) is equal to the number. For example, the factors of 6 are 1, 2, 3, and 6. The sum of the factors excluding 6 is 1 + 2 + 3 = 6. Thus, 6 is a perfect number. Other examples include 28, 496, and 8128.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5f1223d1-ace5-4af2-b264-4466c5137077",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "IMPORTANT",
      "title": "Key Facts on Prime & Composite Numbers",
      "content": "1. 2 is the only even prime number.\n2. 1 is neither prime nor composite.\n3. Every prime number greater than 3 can be written in the form (6k + 1) or (6k - 1), where k is an integer.\n4. There are 15 prime numbers between 1 and 50.\n5. There are 10 prime numbers between 50 and 100."
    },
    {
      "id": "c645bf18-4f88-46da-b475-cf3a1c82bc2d",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "DIVISIBILITY TESTS",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "11902390-e3d2-4d10-9ac1-375e27c05719",
      "type": "TABLE",
      "title": "Divisibility Rules Table",
      "headers": [
        "Divisor",
        "Rule \/ Condition"
      ],
      "rows": [
        [
          "By 2",
          "When the unit's place digit is even or zero."
        ],
        [
          "By 3",
          "When the sum of the digits is divisible by 3."
        ],
        [
          "By 4",
          "When the number formed by the last two digits is divisible by 4."
        ],
        [
          "By 5",
          "When the unit's place digit is 0 or 5."
        ],
        [
          "By 6",
          "When the number is divisible by both 2 and 3."
        ],
        [
          "By 7",
          "Subtract double the last digit from the remaining number. Check if the result is divisible by 7."
        ],
        [
          "By 8",
          "When the number formed by the last three digits is divisible by 8."
        ],
        [
          "By 9",
          "When the sum of the digits of the number is divisible by 9."
        ],
        [
          "By 10",
          "When the unit's place digit is 0."
        ],
        [
          "By 11",
          "The difference between the sum of digits at odd places and the sum of digits at even places is zero or a multiple of 11."
        ],
        [
          "By 12",
          "When the number is divisible by both 3 and 4."
        ],
        [
          "By 13",
          "Special test via step subtraction\/reduction (see detailed steps below)."
        ],
        [
          "By 25",
          "When the number formed by the last two digits is divisible by 25."
        ],
        [
          "By 27",
          "When the sum of the digits of the number is divisible by 27."
        ]
      ],
      "hasHeaderRow": true
    },
    {
      "id": "614d380e-bbb4-498c-aa6d-f53233276cb9",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Detailed Examples for Special Divisibility Tests",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8f27a72c-4642-4f5b-ab0e-0098cdce09a1",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Test for 7 Example: Check 2961",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a2c25679-3a58-4795-a1e2-4296df858d72",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Step I: Separate the last digit, double it, and subtract it from the remaining number: 296 - (1 * 2) = 294.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ffc295d7-2e32-4854-900c-3134c5fa8438",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Step II: Repeat the process for 294: 29 - (4 * 2) = 21.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b672391a-794f-4acc-a15d-f259e3314a4a",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Step III: Since 21 is divisible by 7, the original number 2961 is divisible by 7.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c4efe033-1ec9-4cdb-b532-c3c222abd62a",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Test for 13 Example: Check 265213",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3dcd3c78-9365-4cf0-9f73-c12bfb0ef26a",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Step I: Split the number into two parts: the last three digits and the remaining digits. Subtract the last three digits from the remaining digits: 265 - 213 = 52.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "82e2966c-0219-4c49-838f-59e99c3d7a23",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Step II: Since 52 is divisible by 13 (13 * 4 = 52), the original number 265213 is divisible by 13.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9b5aec8b-2e37-41d6-9e65-a52b0f958cf9",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Special Repetitive Divisibility Rules",
      "content": "1. 6-Digit Single Repetition: If a number is formed by repeating a single digit six times (e.g., 666666), it is divisible by 7, 11, and 13.\n2. 2-Digit Triple Repetition: If a number is formed by repeating a two-digit number three times (e.g., 676767), it is divisible by 7.\n3. 3-Digit Double Repetition: If a number is formed by repeating a three-digit number two times (e.g., 453453), it is divisible by 7, 11, and 13."
    },
    {
      "id": "87e5ad91-5e57-4acd-a658-bd9e4b4fa418",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "FINDING THE UNIT'S PLACE DIGIT",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,

      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "59db5895-1b15-4722-b744-b76a7e7b0b8b",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "To find the unit's place digit of a number in exponential form, analyze the unit digit of the base and apply the corresponding rule based on its cyclicity.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a476dcc1-8c6a-44b9-948b-51efc5f1712a",
      "type": "TABLE",
      "title": "Unit Digit Rules by Base",
      "headers": [
        "Unit Digit of Base",
        "Behavior \/ Rule"
      ],
      "rows": [
        [
          "0, 1, 5, 6",
          "The unit's place digit remains 0, 1, 5, or 6 respectively, for any positive integer power."
        ],
        [
          "4, 9",
          "If the power is odd: the unit's place digit is 4 and 9 respectively. If the power is even: the unit's place digit is 6 and 1 respectively."
        ],
        [
          "2, 3, 7, 8",
          "Divide the power by 4 and find the remainder 'r'. Use 'r' as the new power. If the remainder is 0, use 4 as the power instead of 0."
        ]
      ],
      "hasHeaderRow": true
    },
    {
      "id": "fcb931e0-5634-4784-9803-25c77d22ba01",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Method & Examples for 2, 3, 7, 8",
      "isBold": false,

    {
      "id": "eb4ceb57-f0fb-463c-a1d2-9d9db0a28d3d",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 1: Find the unit's place digit of (134647)^553",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ec789dcf-d80d-4ba7-bae7-85b69be67526",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Step I: Divide the power 553 by 4. The remainder r is 1. Take 1 as the new power.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2d8c7907-4054-4b69-a566-51b5caf2c480",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Step II: Evaluate the unit digit of the base raised to this new power: 7^1 = 7. Thus, the unit digit is 7.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "59840f5b-be65-4809-a86c-d91121fdcd3c",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 2: Find the unit's place digit of (134647)^552",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a7edd7f4-44a3-4df1-a543-93a30283278b",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Step I: Divide the power 552 by 4. The remainder r is 0. Since the remainder is 0, take 4 as the new power.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a5aa21ee-35d3-4674-9980-e0a165519f48",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Step II: Evaluate the unit digit of the base raised to the power of 4: 7^4 = 2401. The unit digit is 1.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"

      "id": "86a3423b-1fba-4100-b490-cc0816d4fb95",

    {
      "id": "0afc2b12-61b1-400b-8429-d8d543dbf2e1",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Standard Summation Formulas",
      "content": "1. Sum of first n natural numbers = [n * (n + 1)] \/ 2\n2. Sum of first n even natural numbers = n * (n + 1)\n3. Sum of first even numbers up to n = (n \/ 2) * [(n \/ 2) + 1]\n4. Sum of first n odd natural numbers = n^2\n5. Sum of squares of first n natural numbers = [n  (n + 1)  (2n + 1)] \/ 6\n6. Sum of cubes of first n natural numbers = [[n * (n + 1)] \/ 2]^2"
    },
    {
      "id": "0a90a150-d6eb-4910-bb5a-429fc67f4a81",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Additional Important Mathematical Properties",

      "id": "8d0d2768-6b94-44fe-840e-900c75080064",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "IMPORTANT",
      "title": "Advanced Number Properties",
      "content": "1. Terminating Decimal Condition: A rational number can be expressed as a terminating decimal if and only if its denominator has no prime factors other than 2 or 5.\n2. Factors Product Representation: The number of ways in which a number N can be expressed as a product of two co-prime factors is 2^(m-1), where m is the number of distinct prime factors of N.\n3. Difference of Squares: The difference of squares of two consecutive integers is always an odd number, and this odd number is equal to the sum of those two consecutive integers.\n4. Number of Prime Factors: The total number of prime factors of the expression (a^p  b^q  c^r * d^s) is equal to p + q + r + s, where a, b, c, and d are prime bases."
    },

      "id": "811a2cf0-204e-436a-8ed2-b7ade928b890",

    {
      "id": "e65605da-7da1-4740-90e5-36c9c7a62d20",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Example 1: Divisibility by 11",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "80fed1cf-2e42-4ba5-802f-d2b2e5758f36",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Question: Which one of the following numbers is divisible by 11?\n(a) 5697231\n(b) 4832718\n(c) 42922\n(d) 239560",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "decfc207-706d-43ba-8c3e-30f3d4d8bfee",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Solution: A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of its digits at odd places and the sum of its digits at even places is either 0 or a multiple of 11.\nLet us test option (b) 4832718:\nSum of digits at odd places = 8 + 7 + 3 + 4 = 22\nSum of digits at even places = 1 + 2 + 8 = 11\nDifference = 22 - 11 = 11, which is divisible by 11.\nTherefore, the correct answer is (b).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9f3a8e56-dad8-4ce0-bff6-db5a3cd1e1b6",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Example 2: Remainder with Prime Division",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d2403c3f-e476-4aaf-b6d7-f763ffbbb466",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Question: Which prime number, when dividing 2176, leaves a remainder of 9?\n(a) 197\n(b) 211\n(c) 223\n(d) 181",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "17895a60-72b1-470c-98c2-ac2dcabbdfad",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Solution: If a number leaves a remainder of 9 when dividing 2176, then the number must perfectly divide (2176 - 9) = 2167.\nLet us check the prime factors of 2167. Testing 197:\n2167 \/ 197 = 11.\nSince 197 is a prime number and divides 2167 perfectly, dividing 2176 by 197 leaves a remainder of 9.\nTherefore, the correct answer is (a).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },

    {

      "text": "Kalhana",
      "isBold": false,

    {
      "id": "969dec5c-64b8-4d0c-a5ee-094980d5798b",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Kalhana was a 12th-century Kashmiri Brahmin and the author of Rajatarangini. He is regarded as Kashmir's First Historian. He chronicled the rulers of the Kashmir Valley from the earliest times, from the epic period of the Mahabharata to the reign of Sangrama Deva. Rajatarangini is considered an important source for the history of Kashmir and also presents an authentic picture of contemporary social and political life.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "08369442-a1a4-4df1-9a72-52f731581ca2",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Key Points",

    {
      "id": "6920771c-d41d-4aa2-9e6f-a8d0a23be804",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "12th-century Kashmiri Brahmin.\nAuthor of Rajatarangini.\nKnown as Kashmir's First Historian.\nCovers Kashmir's rulers up to Sangrama Deva.",

    {
      "id": "d3d2abed-5a09-4031-8126-4c3b33aacec8",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Hari Singh",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b282d241-d5f5-4cb9-8ef5-ddf7bc244ebd",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Following the death of his uncle Pratap Singh, Hari Singh ascended the throne of Jammu and Kashmir in 1925. He introduced compulsory primary education in the state, brought laws prohibiting child marriage, and opened places of worship to the low castes. Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession (the legal document to join the Dominion of India) on 26 October 1947.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0e84f3bb-f5de-4157-9e9b-c1e3ea594b11",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Key Points",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ed769de6-5528-49d0-ac50-22baf5d1c608",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Became ruler of J&K in 1925.\nIntroduced compulsory primary education.\nTook measures against child marriage.\nOpened places of worship to low castes.\nSigned Instrument of Accession: 26 October 1947.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fda21130-4fdc-46ac-af81-1917a0a9a9b4",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "78c06307-2727-4e8a-bcf5-636c01d478ec",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Popularly known as 'Sher-e-Kashmir' (Lion of Kashmir), Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah was one of the most important political figures in the modern history of Jammu and Kashmir. He was the leader of the National Conference, Kashmir's largest political party. He completed his Master's in Chemistry and joined government service as a teacher but later resigned. He spearheaded the popular movement for the democratic rights of the people and founded the Muslim Conference in 1931, which was later changed to the National Conference. He agitated against the rule of Maharaja Hari Singh and urged self-rule for Kashmir. He became the Prime Minister of Jammu and Kashmir State soon after its provisional accession to India in 1947. He was later jailed and exiled. Following the 1974 Indira-Sheikh Accord, he again became Chief Minister of the state and remained in the top position until his death on 8 September 1982.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b8206cd0-80e9-4a50-937a-66af5bfa4123",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Key Points",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "86435c47-b5c8-4bb5-9550-43cf43780a16",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Popular title: Sher-e-Kashmir.\nLeader of National Conference.\nFounded Muslim Conference in 1931.\nMuslim Conference later became National Conference.\nBecame Prime Minister of J&K after accession in 1947.\nReturned as Chief Minister after 1974 Indira-Sheikh Accord.\nDied: 8 September 1982.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "050b7e37-a45e-4720-a003-6f7362e594eb",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Bakshi Ghulam Mohammad",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8cd52401-411e-4845-b248-d14aff6616a8",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "In 1948, during Sheikh Abdullah's absence from the state to represent India's case at the UN, Bakshi Ghulam Mohammad took over as Chief Administrator. In 1953, Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah was dismissed and arrested, after which Bakshi Ghulam Mohammad became Prime Minister of the State and President of the National Conference by majority vote of the State Cabinet. He is remembered as the Architect of Modern Kashmir because of his constructive work in the state. His eleven years as Prime Minister are generally acknowledged as a period of stability in the state's post-Independence history.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {

      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Key Points",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f41c7f15-e8f1-4879-81b5-037be40c609f",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Chief Administrator: 1948.\nBecame Prime Prime Minister: 1953.\nKnown as Architect of Modern Kashmir.\nEleven-year tenure associated with stability.",

      "isUnderline": false,

    {
      "id": "855b29fd-da99-401b-a9d9-ac98c0a3ee0e",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Mehr Chand Mahajan",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,

      "alignment": "LEFT"

    {
      "id": "e6da01a6-f111-4bb0-a955-33770e3359c5",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Mehr Chand Mahajan was the third Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of India. Before that, he served as the Prime Minister of Jammu and Kashmir during Maharaja Hari Singh's reign. He played a key role in the accession of Jammu and Kashmir to India. He was the Indian National Congress nominee on the Redcliff Commission (the boundary commission that demarcated the border between India and Pakistan), which defined the boundaries of India and Pakistan. He was also associated with the decision involving Lahore and Gurdaspur. Before becoming Chief Justice, he served as one of the first judges of the Supreme Court of independent India.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },

    {

      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Third Chief Justice of Supreme Court of India.\nPrime Minister of J&K during Maharaja Hari Singh's reign.\nPlayed a key role in J&K's accession to India.\nCongress nominee on Redcliff Commission.\nOne of the first judges of Supreme Court of independent India.",

    {
      "id": "99a81d5b-9a40-4543-8b93-14cb8053aae5",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Karan Singh",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "32452147-e151-401f-b9cc-c7987c2a2009",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Karan Singh is the son of the last ruler of the Princely State of Jammu and Kashmir, Maharaja Hari Singh. He became a member of India's Upper House of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) and was the titular Maharaja of Jammu and Kashmir. He served successively as Sadr-i-Riyasat (Head of State) and Governor of Jammu and Kashmir. In 1967, he resigned as Governor and became the youngest-ever Member of the Union Cabinet. He also served as Indian Ambassador to the USA and as Chancellor of Banaras Hindu University and Jawaharlal Nehru University.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7425b467-b021-4b54-9d56-906915a824d6",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Key Points",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "44d8a4c3-a1cc-42f8-a1f2-4beff25467c3",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Son of Maharaja Hari Singh.\nTitular Maharaja of J&K.\nServed as Sadr-i-Riyasat.\nGovernor of J&K.\nIn 1967, became youngest Union Cabinet Member.\nAmbassador to USA.\nChancellor of BHU and JNU.",

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "864da48a-af54-49de-99e3-430e4e676ab5",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Mufti Mohammad Sayeed",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "186cb45c-6977-4d2f-a957-ce08543bbb8f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Mufti Mohammad Sayeed was a politician in Jammu and Kashmir and served as Chief Minister from 2002 to 2005. He led the People's Democratic Party (PDP), a Jammu and Kashmir-based party formed by him in 1999, which sought to persuade the Government of India to initiate an unconditional dialogue with Kashmiris for resolution of the Kashmir problem.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5d47e21c-a07f-4987-ba89-cb62614bb04a",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Key Points",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,

      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "125bfd1f-e39d-4d7d-94bd-ae2566006445",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Chief Minister: 2002-2005.\nFounder of PDP - 1999.\nAdvocated dialogue for resolution of the Kashmir problem.",

      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,

    {

      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Mehbooba Mufti Sayeed",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ea27ec88-ad90-4b1c-bbe8-5252665654aa",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Mehbooba Mufti Sayeed is the President of the Jammu and Kashmir Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). She is the daughter of Mufti Mohammad Sayeed, former Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,

      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8366507b-12be-4528-9a25-4011b1818187",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Farooq Abdullah",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "93af57be-b286-469c-b3ee-eb250aae41b0",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Farooq Abdullah is the son of Sheikh Abdullah. He served as Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir on several occasions since 1982. He also served as a Cabinet Minister in the Manmohan Singh Ministry.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7b75ba80-2cfa-4042-a1b8-afe36d1c3c54",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Omar Abdullah",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d8b781d1-b56f-41b8-9d3e-3b9e26ab53ee",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Omar Abdullah is the son of Farooq Abdullah and grandson of Sheikh Abdullah. He served as a minister in Atal Bihari Vajpayee's Government and was re-elected as President of the National Conference for a second term in 2006. He has served as Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a45421a4-e9a7-4167-9f0d-1b77e21a7767",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "PN Dhar",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fe663109-466b-44e2-b7eb-26230e18de01",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "PN Dhar was the Principal Secretary to Prime Minister Indira Gandhi during the turbulent period of the Emergency (1973-77). He therefore had considerable influence in the unfolding of those events. He was also a Professor of Economics at Delhi University.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "78c5b364-dade-4ede-b54e-f3c029b49d53",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Syed Mir Qasim",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "218a8b81-d46c-49bc-b1f1-ab1691ed49ed",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Syed Mir Qasim was the Chief Minister of Kashmir from 1971-75 and was widely respected as a gentleman politician and statesman. His political career began during India's freedom struggle against Britain when he became a leader of the non-sectarian, pro-democracy Quit Kashmir Political Movement. His opposition to monarchical rule resulted in his imprisonment as a political prisoner by Maharaja Hari Singh. After India's independence, Syed Mir Qasim drafted the Kashmiri Constitution and served in various state and Union positions. He famously offered to resign from the Chief Ministership to encourage and institutionalise the landmark Indira Gandhi-Sheikh Abdullah Accord of 1975. He was posthumously awarded India's highest civilian award in 2005, as stated in the source.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1955660c-a1da-4f18-b9c2-e21d13aedc16",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Key Points",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2cea031c-cafc-4057-a6c5-3f9f11cd9fba",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Chief Minister of Kashmir: 1971-75.\nLeader in Quit Kashmir Political Movement.\nImprisoned by Maharaja Hari Singh.\nDrafted the Kashmiri Constitution.\nAssociated with Indira Gandhi-Sheikh Abdullah Accord, 1975.\nPosthumously awarded India's highest civilian award in 2005.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "63d17a5f-a68b-4c92-89a5-4cf5e3b7776c",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Ghulam Nabi Azad",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5c5c9059-e911-4d45-8e7a-e4c84d471bfb",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Ghulam Nabi Azad is a politician from the Indian National Congress. He served as Parliamentary Affairs Minister of India in the Manmohan Singh Government until 27 October 2005, when he was appointed Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0eefdec5-1f93-4a73-aff2-e5c450a3d56c",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Literary Personalities",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f26e7b03-3fef-4f1e-9863-9aa8591e1c44",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Rehman Rahi",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6f97c46e-4c05-4dc5-b1f6-c27f4a9c8372",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Rehman Rahi was a Kashmiri poet, translator and critic. He was awarded the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1961 for his poetry collection Nawroz-i-Saba. He received the Padma Shri in 2000 and India's highest literary award, the Gyanpith Award, for the year 2004. He was the first Kashmiri writer to receive the Gyanpith Award. His poetic collection Siyah Rud Jeare Man is associated with the Gyanpith recognition. As a translator, he translated Baba Farid's poetry from original Punjabi into Kashmiri. The influence of Dinanath Nadim is also visible in his poetry, especially his early work.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "24f97c60-625c-4bdb-8915-1aac78c9a0b9",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Key Points",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "174ded23-f33b-4c3c-ad6a-295effce0e62",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Kashmiri poet, translator and critic.\nSahitya Akademi Award: 1961.\nPadma Shri: 2000.\nGyanpith Award: 2004.\nFirst Kashmiri writer to receive Gyanpith.\nTranslated Baba Farid's poetry from Punjabi into Kashmiri.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c52d73d6-8d68-4037-b928-1b17aa685d03",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Dinanath Nadim",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1b55fe12-5e19-48e9-8cae-670fed1fecc7",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Dinanath Nadim was a prominent Kashmiri poet of the 20th century. His poetry introduced a new phase into Kashmiri literature. Born in Srinagar, Nadim introduced various poetic styles into Kashmiri. He was the first Kashmiri poet to write in blank verse. He used the Kashmiri language with great grace and craftsmanship and depicted the beauty, poverty and plight of Kashmir in his poetry. He also composed poetry in the folk style.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0a3fc579-27b4-4fc5-9791-389effc68491",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Awards",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "46d4abc8-8d16-416b-b50b-07aee23c926f",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Soviet Land Nehru Award - 1971\nSahitya Natak Akademi Award - 1986, for Shihil Kul (poetry)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,

      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"

    {
      "id": "2d942a40-1af7-4184-8831-5e53cfc1326d",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Key Points",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "75623997-bc2b-4928-ab76-4f6be7507509",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "20th-century Kashmiri poet.\nFirst Kashmiri poet to write in blank verse.\nIntroduced various poetic styles.\nWrote about Kashmir's beauty, poverty and plight.\nAlso wrote folk-style poetry.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cce8eea4-81ef-4c49-9a5c-978419c60f04",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Amin Kamil",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a24e8339-2086-46be-a8bf-b5e11097df7f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Amin Kamil was a major voice in Kashmiri poetry and one of the chief exponents of the modern ghazal in the language. Besides being a poet, he wrote short stories, a novel, literary criticism, plays, and radio musicals. He edited the collected verse of Nund Rishi and Habba Khatun. He received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1967 for his book of poems Laveh Te Praveh.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ce07e3fb-b35d-42f6-ac30-b27715ab7c6a",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Key Points",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1a9e671b-2ee9-4e67-840a-7c35b9769155",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Major Kashmiri poet.\nImportant exponent of modern Kashmiri ghazal.\nWrote poetry, short stories, novel, criticism, plays and radio musicals.\nEdited works of Nund Rishi and Habba Khatun.\nSahitya Akademi Award: 1967.\nAward-winning book: Laveh Te Praveh.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "418f0034-5fa1-477f-84b2-3abae4ba2409",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Dr Jitendra Udhampuri",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d2fa9b7e-729b-4ac7-8d12-00ca08cd1f1a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Dr Jitendra Udhampuri was an eminent poet, writer, scholar and critic. He worked for around 50 years for the enrichment of Dogri, Hindi and Urdu languages and literature. He was conferred the Padma Shri and received the Sahitya Akademi's prestigious award in 2011 for his Dogri translation of the famous Urdu novel Do Gaz Zameen. He was a trendsetter in modern Dogri poetry and introduced several innovative themes and styles.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a7107fb0-d894-4068-868d-7c19b7a5054c",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Key Points",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "005fe410-a3c7-497c-962f-53c3c65d18b6",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Poet, writer, scholar and critic.\nWorked for Dogri, Hindi and Urdu literature.\nPadma Shri recipient.\nSahitya Akademi Award: 2011.\nAssociated with Dogri translation of Do Gaz Zameen.\nTrendsetter in modern Dogri poetry.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4ebef094-138f-4448-8816-87c9218f3072",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Ram Nath Shastri",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b1069ee5-8443-466e-9356-0dc6f1a7181d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Professor Ram Nath Shastri, also known as the Father of Dogri, was a prolific and multifaceted Dogri poet, dramatist, actor and fiction writer who worked for over six decades. His writings brought Dogri onto the national stage and made a significant contribution to the development and advancement of Dogri language and literature. He edited the Dogri-Dogri dictionary, regarded as an important contribution to Dogri language.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0a337a38-e0cf-4dfd-a7c1-7b2b7b14fb9a",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Father of Dogri.\nPoet, dramatist, actor and fiction writer.\nWorked for over six decades.\nEdited Dogri-Dogri dictionary.\nMajor contributor to Dogri language and literature.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f69e4364-ad00-4ff2-a759-626998b999c2",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Ghulam Nabi Khayal",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e6b98cf5-0256-45cd-99f2-1ebd0a75b2e6",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Ghulam Nabi Khayal was a renowned poet, writer, researcher, critic and senior journalist of the state. He was selected for the Best Book Award and received honours from the Jammu and Kashmir Academy of Art, Culture and Languages. His book Leaves of Chinar is a research-based collection dealing with the culture, literature, folklore, mythology, history, tradition and heritage of Kashmir. He received the Academy Award in 1974 and the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1975. His contribution to literature and journalism spans about six decades.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2c21eaf6-6c82-44d4-b131-76c03afb2d05",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Ved Rahi",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a37f1695-17b2-4638-b612-a7c66dfff2ed",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Ved Rahi, born in 1933, was an Indian film director who made the film Veer Savarkar, a biopic on revolutionary Vinayak Damodar Savarkar. He also directed the Doordarshan show Gul Gulshan Gulfam, based on the life of Kashmiri saint-poetess Lal Ded. He was also an established novelist in the Dogri language.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e815742d-3168-4a51-8b81-a362b12610ed",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Other Personalities",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4e77c58f-ba88-44b6-8c34-68e3e81ba57c",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Hashmat Ullah Khan",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dcb02ff3-7fa7-41b0-b909-955730bd4565",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Hashmat Ullah Khan was a pioneer in working to revive the world-famous Kani shawls of Kashmir. Kani shawls are woven with special wooden needles called Kanis in Kashmiri. These exquisite shawls were favourites of the Mughal Emperors. He was an authority on Pashmina shawls and lectured on Kashmir shawls and culture in various gatherings in India and abroad. He was awarded the Padma Shri in 2009.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e072a504-7e59-4d6e-80bd-a67afc97ce25",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Moti Lal Kemmu",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "26ea920a-55f5-490c-a72b-e76970d3d5bb",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Moti Lal Kemmu was an important contemporary playwright from Kashmir. He was born in Srinagar and attended Jammu and Kashmir University. He received the Padma Shri in 2012. Several of his plays have been translated and produced in Hindi.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c0dd956f-0401-4229-8076-0129f9e6e6a9",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Plays",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3d5fb568-2f8e-48ac-af62-589f5ca327c6",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Nagar Udas\nTeen Asangati Aikanki\nLal Drayas\nLol Re\nTrunove\nTshai",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f937a3ad-9fcb-46ad-822d-061a04353d40",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Alla Rakha",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0f065d93-99d5-420e-b8dd-c3487ba5bea4",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Alla Rakha was a famous Tabla player. He was born in Punjab, Jammu, and his mother tongue was Dogri. He popularised Tabla internationally and helped bridge the gap between Carnatic and Hindustani music by performing with both. He received the Padma Shri in 1977 and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1982.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fcba0d76-78c8-489b-96f8-352da898b27b",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Shiv Kumar Sharma",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ecd992bc-601c-4308-8256-5bf431cdf7b4",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Shiv Kumar Sharma was a famous Santoor player. The Santoor is a folk instrument of Jammu and Kashmir. He was often referred to by the title Pandit. His mother tongue was Dogri. He was the first musician to play Indian classical music on Santoor. He received national and international honours, including honorary citizenship of Baltimore, USA.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e951d378-4f69-4281-8ccd-2c38afe573b7",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Deepali Wattal",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7d5d5443-1bba-44a4-8fb7-7f1333060a0c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Smt. Deepali Wattal is described as a melody queen who became a prominent figure in the Kashmiri music industry. She started her career in 1990 and has sung more than 2,000 songs in Kashmiri, Punjabi, Dogri, and Pahari.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "59251c3f-8096-48e3-a81b-688e417c4fa3",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Trilok Kaul",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "97466001-3081-4765-bd72-232be3b22c17",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Trilok Kaul belonged to the first generation of artists who formed the Progressive Artists Association of Kashmir. His approach to painting originated from the landscape, particularly the architecture of Kashmiri houses. His work gave space to his artistic imagination. He remained committed to the cubist, analytic approach to problems of space, movement and colour.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4a9291a4-c0cb-4870-ab21-c0ceb13c572d",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Ghulam Rasool Santosh",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0c793608-d1a4-4795-84b8-7d8404feee29",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Ghulam Rasool Santosh was a prominent Kashmiri painter, best known for themes inspired by Kashmir Shaivism. His paintings are known for vibrant colours, neat lines, spiritual energy, and sensuousness. He also wrote plays, poetry and essays in Kashmiri and was an authority on Kashmir Shaivism. He was among the few people able to read and write the ancient and almost extinct Sharda script. He received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1986, the Padma Shri in 1991, and the Padma Vibhushan in 2001.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "552a7b4b-47de-453b-966c-1111f781068a",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Bhajan Sopori",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "35f07f3b-b4dd-4b32-8bda-4b9faa69d4ab",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Bhajan Sopori was an instrumentalist and Santoor player. He hailed from Sopore in Kashmir Valley and belonged to the Sufiana Gharana of Indian classical music. He performed in many countries including Belgium, Egypt, England, Germany, Norway, Syria and the USA. He received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1993, the Padma Shri in 2004, the Baba Alauddin Khan Award, and the Jammu and Kashmir State Award, among other honours.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f89ca765-af2a-43f3-ac15-910bd971fec3",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Pran Kishore Kaul",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3253923f-e546-418c-82ed-8c490cc1fdbc",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Pran Kishore Kaul was a Kashmiri stage personality. Besides acting, he directed and wrote screenplays. He received a Sahitya Natak Akademi Award for his novel Sheen Tuw Wat Pud. He was one of the founders of the Miltsar Kashmir Music and Dance Group, which travelled widely to support Kashmiri music and fine arts.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6d38c819-3edf-41c2-9aef-fc3a55de8081",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Jaffar Ali",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "821146d6-538e-49bf-b11c-448c7f9be392",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Jaffar Ali was a world-renowned papier-mâché artist and entrepreneur from Hussainabad, Srinagar, Kashmir. He received numerous awards, including one from Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, for his exemplary work in promoting Kashmiri handicrafts. His skills in papier-mâché were inherited through his family tradition.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2de10d24-7709-4961-a518-aa5440f37e69",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Amitabh Mattoo",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "284c8506-29c9-4242-a67b-1e05fb566103",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Amitabh Mattoo is one of India's leading thinkers and writers on international relations. He became the youngest Vice-Chancellor of the University of Jammu in 2002 and continued in this position until 2008. He was the inaugural Director of the Australia India Institute and Professor of International Relations at the University of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. He received the Padma Shri in 2008.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4b155d83-9833-42f7-a47a-642b4b7b5c98",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Key Points",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cd290d77-b16f-40cb-84a8-79162b628162",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Expert in international relations.\nYoungest Vice-Chancellor of University of Jammu in 2002.\nVC until 2008.\nProfessor of International Relations, University of Melbourne.\nPadma Shri: 2008.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c0ed6dcc-7c70-48eb-94f3-126e0c1bd58f",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Mian Bashir Ahmed",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "835d827e-2455-4149-8bca-9ec8a2e46a5e",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Mian Bashir Ahmed was born in 1923 in Kashmir. He was a politician and religious personality. His native title\/name is given as Sajjada-Nasheen-Zayaarat Baba Jee Sahib Laarvi. He propagated the doctrines of Naqshbandi and Qadri Sufism among his followers through Bayyat. He received the Padma Bhushan in 2008 for his contribution to society.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3f620e99-3bb8-4ece-825f-ebc58068b601",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Riyaz Punjabi",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3cc7683d-6321-430b-81a2-78db7b8e0f47",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Riyaz Punjabi was formerly the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Kashmir. He had a distinguished career spanning more than 40 years in academics, research and voluntary action. For his contribution to education, culture and promotion of communal harmony in Jammu and Kashmir, he received the Fazil Memorial Award in 2009, the Adbi Markaz Kamraz Award in 2010, and the Padma Shri in 2011.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
