      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b5107d12-9447-4497-8727-9b7d4f24d304",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Jammu and Kashmir celebrates a wide variety of fairs and festivals reflecting its religious, cultural and traditional diversity. The commonly celebrated festivals include Lohri, Baisakhi, Bahu Mela, Jhiri Mela, Mansar Food and Craft Mela, Chaitra Chaudas Mela and Purmandal Mela.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "970fd6c2-41a6-48c8-b5cf-1e5138d9493a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Navratras are celebrated with festivities throughout the state, while a special mela (fair) is held at the Kheer Bhawani Temple in Tulla Mulla village.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "eeeec331-595c-4941-a8b8-9e0ef2e1aa0d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Jhiri Mela is held annually in memory of Baba Jitu, a poor farmer who, according to popular belief, committed suicide in protest against the unfair demands of his landlord.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "510b2a8e-c718-4238-a4c7-272d25cf39fe",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Purmandal Mela is held at Purmandal, about 39 km from Jammu, and has special significance on the occasion of Maha Shivratri.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1d0702c5-c1e1-48a8-9505-4ec4fce55aa2",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Hemis Festival is a major religious fair held at Hemis Gompa (Buddhist monastery) in Ladakh. Other important Ladakh festivals include Sindhu Darshan, Galdan Namchot, Losar, Phyang Tse-dup, Sachukul Gustor and Yuru Kabgyat.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2a6570f5-280f-439e-88d8-385625a4ea4f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Chaitra Chaudas Mela is held during March–April at Uttar Behni, about 25 km from Jammu. Shab-e-Barat and Muharram are also celebrated with festivities in the state.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2dd16940-6d73-4f82-b0f4-3b0bea04bab2",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "2. Important Fairs and Festivals",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8ecd1f79-f77d-49af-a087-a0a89c4f4c57",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Hemis Festival",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "294c6176-0fd4-4fa9-96cb-42e22acc6ae3",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Hemis Festival is held in the courtyard of Hemis Gompa (Buddhist monastery), the biggest Buddhist monastery in Ladakh. It celebrates the birth anniversary of Guru Padmasambhava.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5509afc1-16de-4227-82c7-77b5a614636d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The colourful two-day pageant falls on the 10th day (Tse-Chu) of the Tibetan lunar month. During the festival, local people dress in their finest traditional clothes. The Lamas (Buddhist monks), called Chhams (masked dancers), perform splendid masked dances and sacred plays accompanied by cymbals, drums and long horns. The head lama presides over the function.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "876d490f-d859-45a6-9aa8-c0deaf2188a0",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Hemis Monastery",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "485ea734-65ba-4540-8681-fd4a3f4dc810",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "It is described as the wealthiest, best-known and biggest gompa (monastery) of Ladakh.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5f32f2a5-4c93-4a14-a7c6-06fa30b1350a",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Its popularity comes from the major annual festival held there in summer.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "01cfee72-64ca-4cf6-bd91-4d43bcd5c9ab",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "It also has the largest Thangka (Tibetan Buddhist painting on cotton or silk) in Ladakh, which is unfurled once in twelve years.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ee17c2ab-b924-45b8-af56-7a838f754bbb",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Hemis was built in 1630, during the reign of Sengge Namgyal, an illustrious ruler of Ladakh.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "75d237e0-0203-4027-b89a-77f0cb1f3c3e",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "It flourished under the Namgyal dynasty, which favoured the Drugpa sect that managed the monastery.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3eedb734-3eb8-4336-a4b6-5fba45db2828",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "Hemis Monastery Divisions",
      "nodes": [
        "Hemis Monastery",
        "Assembly Hall (Dukhang)",
        "Main Temple (Tshogkhang)"
      ],
      "rawContent": "[Hemis Monastery]\n   \/         \\\n[Assembly Hall] [Main Temple]"
    },
    {
      "id": "7c257382-91aa-4d66-b806-db77e98ce074",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Assembly Hall (Dukhang)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f39db351-150e-48a4-97f1-28444d464f45",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The assembly hall on the right, known as Dukhang, is also used as a green room by dancers during the festival.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dae0bf13-c9e7-4190-846c-d1d1faeac9cd",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Main Temple (Tshogkhang)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5475b4c3-c3fd-457d-88a7-21e439f88a5c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The main temple on the left is known as Tshogkhang. The verandahs contain frescoes, including among them the Buddhist wheel of life (Kalachakra) and the lords of the four quarters, besides the prayer wheel.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2c8be9b2-7ec0-405e-b78f-3cc3bff206b5",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "3. Jhiri Mela",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "156c97b8-0782-4cf5-a784-86eb794e5995",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Jhiri Mela is an annual fair held in Jammu during October–November. It rejuvenates people's mood and provides some rest and relaxation from the hardships of daily life.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ac978061-2716-4dcd-8573-86bd79b2137a",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "Core Values of Jhiri Mela",
      "nodes": [
        "Jhiri Mela Values",
        "Courage",
        "Honesty",
        "Compassion"
      ],
      "rawContent": "          [Jhiri Mela Values]\n         \/         |         \\\n  [Courage]    [Honesty]   [Compassion]"
    },
    {
      "id": "13536d0c-80c7-49b9-9280-d2d276a87a37",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Core Values of the Mela",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "286ea3be-fa0e-4a57-ade8-67dab13c59cb",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Courage: Reflects the spirit of standing up against injustice.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "390e4577-f3bd-4616-9081-ba6e76358184",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Honesty: Represented by Baba Jitu's truthful and uncomplicated life.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "152b17f7-3ab5-4b59-97b8-778461308a06",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Compassion: Celebrated by the community to remember the hardships and sacrifices of the peasant.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "679650ab-af6a-4049-8b18-a942cb2fb54b",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Legend of Baba Jitu",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6ecfa58d-cad8-44c4-932b-6b30c0b9237d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "According to the legend, Baba Jitu was a local farmer who was truthful and uncomplicated. He lived with his family at Jhiri, located about 14 km from Jammu.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a87421bb-1d9c-4839-a1e5-68dfbee82879",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "His local landlord demanded that he share his crop with him. Baba Jitu regarded this as an injustice because he had spent days working in the fields to produce the crop. Unable to accept the unfairness, he committed suicide.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "95226e19-54fa-4b0a-9f62-0363d10dc0fa",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "There was no one to help him: there was neither a police station nor was the king ready to listen to the complaint of a mere peasant.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "90fc674e-d595-4138-8d8f-8774bd835d3e",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The people of Jhiri began to worship Baba Jitu because of his honesty and self-respect. They believed that his soul was eternal and needed to be worshipped.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e6727d48-601b-4150-bec8-65b195150980",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Every year, the people of Jhiri celebrate the Jhiri Mela towards the end of October to commemorate the great sacrifice of the peasant.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "eff1d3e2-677e-444a-ac91-afef1074b5a2",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "4. Tihar",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c9f62f54-14ba-4f37-93f2-c46773364a46",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Tihar is an interesting festival observed in Bhaderwah and Kishtwar during the months of Chaitra (March–April).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8896e5e2-fd7a-48ff-8130-392ad6681bdb",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Springs and baulis (natural water springs or stepwells) receive a spring-cleaning.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1e8a5f33-deb6-47d0-9aa8-7c536ced9660",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The cleaning is followed the next day by worship of Nagas (serpents).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "525605ba-f04f-4598-91b5-0bc3b597e105",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Rice and floral offerings are made to the Nagas.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0616c6af-72ed-4f41-a679-2c083dc8e866",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Samkrat (the beginning of a month in the Bikrami era) is regarded as a sacred day by Hindus.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dc5618b1-1a54-46cb-870e-f76bfb0d8381",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Women bathe in rivers and observe a day's fast.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b9e1a4cb-4aa1-4325-b565-687a0dc7226a",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "5. Amarnath Yatra",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "abb2c661-9bce-4e1d-b287-6c05a0488104",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Amarnath Yatra is described as virtually a paradise for Hindus. The pilgrimage connects with the story of Lord Shiva narrating the secret of immortality to Goddess Parvati.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ca5f3159-115b-4b1d-8bcd-fb6a93400176",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Legend of Amarnath",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "031a7e94-7a90-484e-9252-8f2f1602129f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Lord Shiva began his journey to Amarnath and, on the way, left behind everything to ensure that no one listened to the secret.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "144705fa-e3c7-454a-b697-936a1c6f15f7",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "FLOWCHART",
      "title": "Lord Shiva's Journey to Amarnath",
      "nodes": [
        "Pahalgam",
        "Chandanwari",
        "Sheshnag",
        "Mahagunas Parvat",

      ],
      "rawContent": "[Pahalgam] -> [Chandanwari] -> [Sheshnag] -> [Mahagunas Parvat] -> [Panjtarni] -> [Amarnath Cave]"
    },
    {
      "id": "dcc7c0d0-419f-48f4-a424-8e93ba7ec496",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "The Sacred Trail Stations",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "395bc0cb-6177-4d76-b312-6ce216e56d24",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Pahalgam: He left his bull, Nandi, here.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1c484f68-8bcf-4016-98c7-223ca6b45948",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Chandanwari: He released the moon from his hair here.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3bc07235-f248-482f-a802-78aa6d2edd20",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Sheshnag: He left his snakes on the banks of Lake Sheshnag.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "13e3ac30-ebef-4966-b4c7-4e7272c00640",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Mahagunas Parvat: He left his son Ganesha here.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f4db8f9c-75ce-40a1-af5d-888d744d9c9b",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Panjtarni: He left the five elements (Earth, Water, Fire, Air, and Sky) here.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "20f7e261-766d-4b77-be7a-141fd85a58d1",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "The Cave and the Secret",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2beb8207-aaaa-4a62-a756-3583894cf8b8",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "After reaching Amarnath, Lord Shiva rid himself of his deerskin and took his Samadhi (deep state of meditation) so that no one could hear his secret. He created Rudra and Kalagni to eliminate all traces of life around the cave. However, an egg escaped his notice under the deerskin. A pair of pigeons emerged from the egg and, according to the legend, became immortal because they heard the tale of immortality.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "61635f19-dc7b-4750-acd6-1df786f04435",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Importance and Journey",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a4e4e638-b20b-4538-a89a-a5b581f388f6",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Himalayan pilgrimages are described as among the oldest organised travel systems.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "42b174b5-9f47-43a7-ad04-87a75b1fa1f9",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Numerous tourists visit Amarnath during Shivratri and at other times of the year.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b061e435-fc6d-4b3a-84fa-7626c95aea27",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Amarnath combines spirituality and adventure.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "99f71e68-f1af-4c94-b800-e93e87713c90",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The two pigeons are often seen by visitors.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "76981414-56ac-4101-8664-35e9b3c25189",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The journey requires courage and enthusiasm, passing through large mountainous regions.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "97c4862b-8e7e-474e-b836-354bc49f374c",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Donkeys or horses may be available on portions of the route. At higher elevations, tourists may have to walk on their own with sticks.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2b86e723-cb48-4843-8878-e2e4978e5f61",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Hot springs are also found on the route, which is an amazing natural occurrence amid snowy terrain.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ce2aa483-c5f0-4537-bedd-83619e089a33",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "6. Purmandal Mela",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6c5cb634-09b9-477a-9e6c-240b24d3ca7d",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The Purmandal Mela is held at Purmandal, located about 39 km from Jammu.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9ca453a8-0096-4343-bd62-b85da9265e19",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "It has special significance because it is celebrated on the occasion of Maha Shivratri.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e108bf83-0d11-496d-b938-d64af9a5b7de",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The festival marks the wedding celebrations of Lord Shiva with Goddess Parvati.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4d96d382-20c2-4559-9270-6595d03fc6db",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "7. Kheer Bhawani",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3193191e-b033-4d80-a05d-891749ce0428",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Kheer Bhawani is a major Hindu festival celebrated at the Kheer Bhawani Temple.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d8a347c9-57e8-4d5e-8719-0dca7c11368d",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The temple is dedicated to Goddess Ragnya Devi.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0bd55d3f-9c67-405d-8b5f-ee1858116227",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "It is located in Tulla Mulla village, about 27 km from Srinagar.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a309d6c0-cdbd-4476-b8ab-fb2c353c2a78",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The temple was originally built by Maharaja Pratap Singh in 1912 and later renovated by Maharaja Hari Singh.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b21a22c5-c46c-401f-a814-4fa3640748ad",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The festival is celebrated on Jyeshtha Ashtami, the birthday of Goddess Kheer Bhawani.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a415b966-26ee-448d-8b9c-91145c95689b",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "8. Mansar Food and Craft Mela",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "52d8a4ae-2ec5-450f-8711-79f9be08f8b8",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The Mansar Food and Craft Mela at Jammu is an annual fair.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b5d13a31-7bcb-4a5f-a2a3-989ec9a43ec2",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "It is usually held during the month of Baisakhi (April).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f9b89595-c8c3-435f-bce2-30193e7d5cef",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "It has gained considerable reputation and attracts people from different parts of the world to enjoy the splendid display of Indian arts and crafts.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "40974849-c595-410a-84af-e77538188d08",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The mela is organized by the Jammu and Kashmir Travel and Tourism section.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c0a42995-7bbd-4a73-8003-bbca60103983",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "9. Baisakhi",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "bdde993f-032b-4192-9f25-43f8a8b07cb9",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The name Baisakhi is derived from Vaishakh, the first month of the Hindu calendar.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "27755278-593e-4d28-a143-22c676357bb4",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "It is normally celebrated on 13 April and serves as the harvest festival of Northern India.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8d03698c-ac46-4de8-9a49-cf8c300c525c",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "It is considered especially auspicious for marriages, and devotees take ritual dips in rivers and canals.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "824b5af5-e119-48df-bdfe-e283c408a4b4",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "It marks the beginning of the New Year and holds special significance for the Sikhs. In 1699, the Khalsa was created, and Sikhs celebrate the festival as a collective birthday.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "89413146-a5ad-40b0-877a-649fdf92d1b7",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "10. Lohri",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f1bb3e85-592b-47f3-8b3c-53bd111b5dbe",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Lohri is celebrated to welcome spring with a special fervour.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e47b7c63-1857-4d20-892c-13db4963e620",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "In the Jammu region, it is celebrated on 13 January, one day before Makar Sankranti.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3e1f3656-0966-49fb-a007-31ed37c8cab0",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Thousands of devotees take a holy dip in rivers, and Havans and Yagnas are performed in houses and temples.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c4afc746-3697-4b35-8246-dc38cb4d3899",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "In rural areas, boys traditionally go around asking for gifts from newly-weds and new parents.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7f58efdf-8c94-412c-bc2a-70c519f7acf9",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Chajja dance is performed on this occasion. Boys carry elaborately decorated Chajjas (structures made of bamboo and paper) and dance in a procession on the streets accompanied by drumbeats.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "984e943a-9c88-49db-8fef-39c2fd4f7a8d",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "11. Chemrey Angchok",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d0832765-4bb4-49f0-be62-3ca4edd85bbd",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Chemrey Angchok is an important festival of Ladakh celebrated in the month of November.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0920c841-0fef-48d1-868d-10bb6311012b",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "It falls on the 28th and 29th day of the ninth month of the Tibetan calendar.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9405d703-38a8-49c7-b600-66c7259d62dc",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The Chemrey Monastery has celebrated the festival annually since 1664.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "49d5afcf-6176-4ae5-8113-19049b63ebc2",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The festival is marked by a unique dance performance where dancers portray the victory of good over evil and the lives of Buddhist and Tibetan divinities.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cdc43201-0ee9-4781-af14-133daa85c1ac",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "12. Dosmoche",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b92d245d-a423-4715-841b-1e54b65ea878",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Dosmoche is a festival held every year in the month of February.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "548cc0e0-cb25-4d7a-affe-49f20117d836",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "It is celebrated at the majestic Leh Palace, and is also observed with equal zeal at the monasteries of Likir in Lower Ladakh and Deskit in Nubra Valley.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e04fff6f-8ebc-4177-a151-be26f3d1a323",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The festival falls at the start and end of the Tibetan New Year and is observed for two days.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7a92d0dc-d99b-49fb-a745-6cedc371073a",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "13. Korzok Gustor",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "15937845-a270-44c1-b082-8ec4eb188d11",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Korzok Gustor is an ancient festival associated with Korzok Monastery at Tsomoriri Lake, usually held in July or August.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "40f82697-791e-4155-a026-d624c56630b8",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The festival is famous for its Black Hat Dance conducted by monks.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "20c39fdf-5a42-49a0-ab77-b203fcc0b05b",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The Gustor ceremony symbolises the sacrifice of the evil forces, culminating in the sacrifice of a symbolic cake called Argham, which is dismantled by the head of the Black Hat Dancers.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3193c111-b69d-45b9-a133-ec1cf762e479",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The ceremony is linked to the traditional belief of eliminating evil forces of nature, and the assassination of the traitor king by a monk (Padma Sambhava) forms an integral part of the ritual.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5ba4fbff-79b3-45ac-8ca5-2b7aca3e3198",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The Gustor festival is also held at Spituk, Karsha, and Thiksey monasteries.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c258df1d-ce43-4a3a-8cd5-4fd93f2cadb3",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "14. Matho Nagrang",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "99eb5916-b405-4ad3-8504-e6da6e7f93e4",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Matho Nagrang is celebrated on the 15th day of the first month of the Tibetan calendar. It is held at Matho Monastery, which is the only monastery belonging to the Sakya School of Tibetan Buddhism.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "230c703c-fc02-47a2-933e-bd1fef41060f",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Main Features",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4f41f10a-499b-4690-80ea-387711b3e5d5",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "During the first two days, monks perform splendid mask dances wearing colourful silk brocaded robes and masks representing gods and goddesses.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6b6a9d90-3e60-4840-867a-0933821d01be",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The festival is famous because after two whole months of dedicated meditation in absolute isolation, two oracles appear.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "24928fea-b568-4e01-ab13-c9d642971896",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "These oracles come into the courtyard of the monastery, accompany the masked monk dancers, and predict future events.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "144d2bc8-43f9-4356-aa10-33e6bcb1190f",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "15. Sant Naro Nasjal (Zangskar)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ba68ff7e-d447-4218-be28-7701dacb8b40",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Sant Naro Nasjal is widely celebrated by the monks of the Sant Naro Nasjal Monastery with great zeal and enthusiasm.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5275ab4c-e0a4-41ff-8658-1770a8b32dee",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The Lamas (Buddhist monks) perform the Black Hat Dance in colourful attire to symbolically ward off the evil forces of nature.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "544c5546-2760-4084-94a1-fae0c3e40a2f",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The festival is usually held during July–August.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5dc52e7a-8906-4551-b3c4-e96521f5f437",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "16. Sindhu Darshan",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c1c46a85-c041-4b9b-947b-094d2947a728",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Sindhu Darshan is held in the Ladakh region with extensive pomp and gaiety, with Leh being the main place of celebration. It is a carnival for paying homage to the river Indus, whose local name is Sindhu.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9b624186-02ef-46db-8aac-1818d934bd16",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Main Rituals",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a98eb3cf-d0a8-4181-b0bf-a836c26ae826",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "A holy dip into the sacred river.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "50aa878e-eece-452e-8ce2-b444342536a6",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Men and women wear their best costumes.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3db826be-a475-4cd1-b3e3-7fb27e8d2197",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "They pay homage to the mighty river for its blessings, considering the river itself as God.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "58525689-5431-4d2c-bd18-d97195ad5517",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Devotees offer flowers and fruits to worship the great river.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2ccf8160-bb9b-40c2-a03c-7b9a50c22d77",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "17. Stok Guru Tsechu",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "96106641-f5b1-494c-a3c3-915e0d35fce6",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Stok Guru Tsechu is another important Buddhist festival of Ladakh, falling every year in February, one week before Matho Nagrang.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "aaf33e00-572b-4a90-8b96-dd31840393a1",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Buddhist monks of Stok and Spituk Monasteries in Ladakh celebrate it for two days.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5724f3b0-d70b-49fa-afd0-7a33ba3c29fa",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "It is celebrated in almost the same manner as Matho Nagrang, but with one key difference: the oracles are not monks, but laymen from the village who are formally prepared by the monks to invoke the deity and holy spirits.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "aa108c25-8cce-4622-9517-7eea6cc84034",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "18. Dak Thok Tse-Chu",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "29c12dd8-9f62-40a4-ad1a-872e90572a71",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Dak Thok Tse-Chu is an important festival held in July and August, attracting a large number of tourists and locals.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "57f5de39-be77-4c27-8f16-ddad571bf41a",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "According to the Buddhist calendar, these festivals celebrate the exploits of Padma Sambhava (Guru Rimpoche), the founder of Tibetan Buddhism.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f09849d1-40f4-4aad-a92c-0c62301e5f6f",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The Tse-Chu festivals highlight the enlightening works of Guru Rimpoche's life through Cham (sacred masked) dances.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5f2bbd7a-0346-4493-b0ae-6995db04663b",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Both monks and local people participate in the dances, which depict different aspects of wrathful and compassionate deities, as well as various animals.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4c5679f7-f512-4ae6-8051-0eb5e2b8585c",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "19. Other Fairs and Festivals",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "923c41de-72c0-4a3e-a696-88acd0fb1f52",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Eid-ul-Zuha",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dd58854f-a2ec-4581-84f2-874fef33a47a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Celebrated in July; commemorates Prophet Abraham, who agreed to sacrifice his son to God.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ec7545c9-2923-4333-9e69-b3f9a06653ac",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Eid-ul-Fitr",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d9c47cfb-ee65-477b-a541-d201479509e6",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Celebrated in October\/November; marks the end of the fasting month of Ramazan. Sweets are prepared, and Muslims buy new clothes and prepare delicious feasts.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "abb86d88-26e3-4353-a937-f345aef54400",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Bahu Mela",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "398dae73-c6e5-483b-9443-1b5f79251a07",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Celebrated twice a year, in March\/April and September\/October; a major festival at the Kali Temple in Bahu Fort, Jammu.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fb226a2e-a095-4908-9125-b55a0f1f8d8b",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Chaitra Chaudas",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f9911a1f-a60f-4f4e-af90-5505ac6cfe76",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Usually celebrated in March\/April at Uttar Behni, about 25 km from Jammu. The name refers to the Devak river, which flows towards the north.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },

      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5c01862e-4e24-46c4-83ce-7b35db847885",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Korzok Gustor: Tsomoriri; July\/August; Black Hat Dance; Argham\/symbolic cake.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c671c972-03d6-45d2-8f37-134ce2b5edfa",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Matho Nagrang: 15th day of first Tibetan month; Matho Monastery; two oracles predict future events.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3f71ffb2-7312-476d-b42f-3ae4c3bfbd50",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Sant Naro Nasjal: Zangskar; July–August; Black Hat Dance.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "221967ec-e55d-478d-a16a-21ccacf30a8f",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Sindhu Darshan: Leh\/Ladakh; homage to the River Indus; holy dip and offerings.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1646beb5-9b2c-4342-9aad-8a2f7e9b67be",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Stok Guru Tsechu: February; one week before Matho Nagrang; celebrated by Stok and Spituk monasteries for two days.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cf36b7a6-2129-4ba1-bed6-a149676d7f9b",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Matho vs Stok Guru: Matho's oracles are associated with monks, while Stok Guru's oracles are laymen from the village, prepared by monks.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "803dfb94-9e0e-4775-b86e-d80256d7b62b",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Dak Thok Tse-Chu: July\/August; dedicated mainly to Padma Sambhava; famous for Cham dances.",

      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,

    },
    {
      "id": "79547b85-3fb3-4d3e-a147-f1285bc3d8f0",

      "text": "Other fairs: Eid-ul-Zuha, Eid-ul-Fitr, Bahu Mela and Chaitra Chaudas.",

    }
  ]
