    {
      "id": "153d5ae5-d17a-4563-b792-49e9db6c0ef0",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Revision",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "11d10990-fe3c-496b-a083-dd7c11d52037",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Jammu and Kashmir is one of the energy-starved states despite having tremendous hydro-power potential.\nEstimated hydro-power potential of J&K is over 20,000 MW.\nHardly 10% of the hydro-power potential has been harnessed.\nThe state generates about 25% of its actual electricity demand.\nPower transmission and distribution losses were over 58.82% in 2016 according to the chapter.\nThe Indus Water Treaty is a major constraint on tapping hydro-power potential.\nThe Treaty prohibits reservoir storage of water on major rivers of J&K.\nHydro-power generation is therefore restricted to a large extent to run-of-the-river projects.\nDifficult topography, remote villages and dispersed habitations make transmission and distribution difficult.\nConsumption of power comes before Rural Electrification and Hydro Power in the chapter.\nDomestic sector is the biggest consumer of power, followed by agriculture and industry.\nDomestic consumption increased by 65%.\nAgricultural consumption increased by 13.84%.\nIndustrial consumption increased by 59.39%.\nThe state depends on external sources to fill the gap between demand and supply of power.\nBy the end of 2005–06, 102 villages were unelectrified.\nThe total number of inhabited villages mentioned is 6417, according to the 2001 Census.\nVillage electrification was made part of Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana, 2015.\nFunds for the programme flow to the state as central assistance.\nNHPC is a Central Public Sector Undertaking with the mandate of developing hydro power in the country.\nNHPC power generated in J&K is transmitted and pooled in the Northern Grid.\nNHPC provides 12% royalty of power generated on J&K rivers.\nSPDC is the nodal agency for development of Small Hydro Power (SHP).\nSPDC undertakes identification of potential sites, pre-feasibility reports, detailed project reports and execution of projects.\nSPDD provides necessary power evacuation, transmission and distribution infrastructure.\nJKSPDCL was incorporated as a Private Limited Company on 16 February 1995.\nJKSPDCL handles power-project assets, planning, investigation, research, design, construction, generation, operation, maintenance and transmission works.\nSmall and medium hydro projects are particularly useful in difficult and inaccessible areas.\nLadakh is not connected to the grid and villages generally depend on diesel sets.\nLadakh's hydel plants remain closed for months because of freezing of water in winter and high siltation in summer.\nLadakh has more than 300 sunny days in a year.\nDiesel generation costs around ₹10–₹12 per unit.\nSolar energy can be used for lighting, cooking, water heating, space heating and water pumping.\nSPV directly converts sunlight into electricity without moving parts and without causing pollution.\nA 40 kW solar power plant has been installed in Ladakh.\nThe Ladakh solar plant provides electricity to 500 households.\nPuga Valley, Ladakh has high geo-thermal potential.\nEstimated geo-thermal potential of Puga Valley is around 40 MW.\nJ&K's first Wind Power Project is at Reasi.\nReasi has wind potential of about 336 W\/sq m at 50 m height.\nThe first-stage Reasi wind project is around 10 MW.\nMohra Hydro Electric Plant is a 9 MW plant developed as early as 1905.\nJammu and Kashmir was the first state in India to award the 690 MW Ratle HEP Mega Hydro Power Project on BOOT basis through tariff-based competitive bidding.\nBOOT means Build, Own, Operate and Transfer.\nJKSPDCL is pursuing the development of a Geo-thermal Project at Puga Valley, Leh (Ladakh).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    }

    {

      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Forests are one of the most important resources of Jammu and Kashmir.       "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Jammu and Kashmir has diverse geographical regions, climates, and vegetation, which supports a rich wildlife population. The Himalayan range provides a suitable habitat for many animal species. The Leopard is described as a beautiful and elusive survivor from the Pleistocene era (the geological epoch lasting from about 2.58 million to 11,700 years ago). Hangul or Kashmiri stag is one of the important endangered species of the region. Bhalal is an important mammal of the region. Musk deer, Markhor, Ibex, and Serow are among the important species. During winter, many high-altitude bird species move to lower valleys.",

      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Zoological parks and Animal Rescue Centres are developed as centres of environmental and wildlife education. Special attention is required to address the man-animal interface (interactions between humans and wild animals).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b05003a6-7c90-48c9-92fa-e7a13c75e0f0",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Coordination Requirements",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d04c306f-a943-47dd-9b9c-769c59048e6d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Wildlife conservation requires active coordination among the following departments and groups:",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cf956711-6114-4530-abf8-8b15ace7d7a8",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Forest Department\nForest Protection Force\nWildlife Protection Department\nRevenue Department\nPolice\nLocal administration\nLocal institutions\nGeneral public",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "41e39a63-ba01-4f0a-a1bb-5234a491adbc",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Key Revision Points",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "de65f1d6-a477-4e0e-a434-be6dc00513bc",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Forests require abundant moisture.\nKashmir Valley has mainly deciduous vegetation.\nThere are five major forest types mentioned in the chapter.\nRecorded forest area is 21,386.84 km².\nForest area forms 39.15% of the geographical area.\nReserved forests constitute 87.21%.\nProtected forests constitute 12.61%.\nUnclassed forests constitute 0.18%.\nJammu Division has 13,114 sq km forest area.\nKashmir Valley has 8,273 sq km forest area.\nConiferous forests constitute 90.68%.\nNon-coniferous forests constitute 9.32%.\nPer capita forest area is 0.17 hectare.\nHangul = Kashmiri Stag.\nHangul is Critically Endangered.\nMarkhor is Critically Endangered.\nChiru is the Tibetan antelope.\nChiru is Critically Endangered.\nHemis National Park has an area of 3350 sq km.\nKishtwar National Park has an area of 425 sq km.\nDachigam National Park has an area of 141 sq km.\nKarakoram Wildlife Sanctuary has an area of 5000 sq km.\nChangthang Wildlife Sanctuary has an area of 4000 sq km.\nJasrota Wildlife Sanctuary has an area of 10.04 sq km.\nWildlife conservation includes Zoological Parks, Animal Rescue Centres and coordination among concerned departments.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    }
  ]
}

{
  "chapterId": "chap_c084f8db",
  "title": "Agriculture and Industrialisation",
  "elements": [
    {
      "id": "3f7fec65-dc1b-4a3e-aa2c-3f8338588a08",
      "type": "HEADING_1",
      "text": "CHAPTER 5: AGRICULTURE AND INDUSTRIALISATION",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2a4858f0-fe26-4149-807c-b49a61812720",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "1. Agriculture in Jammu and Kashmir",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b614c149-789d-4a60-84db-a2c10a061505",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Agriculture is the predominant sector in the economy of Jammu and Kashmir. Directly and indirectly, it supports about 70% of the population and contributes nearly 16% of the State GDP, according to the 2017–18 Economic Survey. This explains the considerable dependence of the population on agriculture.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8df3e83f-27cc-4373-8595-2cba291bac4c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The overall economic growth of the State depends largely on the progress of the agricultural sector. Its development becomes even more important because of the relatively nominal progress made in the secondary sectors.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d4601d62-b894-4432-bd45-0905f2ff53f3",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "With the introduction of planned development during 1951–56, the production of foodgrains and fruits increased considerably.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "49c98e8d-0bfd-47ec-8291-b0484195dcf8",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "2. Land Use Pattern",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0fa9c592-ac30-4a29-96cc-57a4695340a9",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The land utilisation statistics of Jammu and Kashmir reveal a high proportion of forest cover and limited net area available for active cultivation. The following table details the land use pattern based on statistics from the Ministry of Agriculture, Government of India (2006).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "68f8dfb7-8c7f-466c-9395-6d4c9a9be7f6",
      "type": "TABLE",
      "title": "Land Use Pattern in Jammu and Kashmir",

    },
    {
      "id": "1083df7a-0be7-4bff-9381-8be29afbd0d7",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "3. Agro-Climatic Zones",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f9fd3bc9-6e2a-4375-8881-657ce991c62d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Jammu and Kashmir is divided into three distinct agro-climatic zones. Each zone has its own geo-climatic conditions, which determine its cropping pattern and productivity profile.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0523a537-c634-41d9-9812-c05cb6899cdc",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Zone 1: Humid Sub-Tropical Region of Jammu",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cfc5135f-be97-44a4-9b4c-cc086a288144",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "In Jammu province, a small portion of the land lies along the borders of Punjab, while the rest of the area is hilly. The Jammu region dominates both maize and wheat production, with about 67% of the area dedicated to these two crops.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0a633f93-1346-4e55-af38-582c5e64907e",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Maize production yield: 21.25 q\/ha",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "15cf23f1-eeb7-41df-a6c2-382957acb067",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Wheat production yield: 15.36 q\/ha",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4bcb3a98-f29f-46b5-9bb7-b060da5d7d09",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Contribution to total maize production: Jammu contributes about 79.65%",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cee43fd4-2088-49e4-8674-39ad5f8d29a9",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Contribution to total wheat production: Jammu contributes about 95.69%",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "295cec24-a4ea-4292-9216-62c6c9d81f4a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Although the yield is not very high, the region makes an appreciable contribution to the production of groups of cereals classified as other cereals and millets.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "24ac6452-99ca-4547-b2c4-6c99fa30689d",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Zone 2: Temperate Kashmir Valley",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6c8e07cb-d8ec-4bf7-b491-b06770916775",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The agro-climatic zone of Kashmir is also known as the 'cultivator's paradise.' The region practically depends on irrigation, which is easily available. A large area of level land has alluvial soil.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e405d2de-e840-4047-8ff0-e89b90891d65",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "Karewas",
      "content": "Karewas are extensive elevated plateaus of alluvial or lacustrine material found locally in the Kashmir Valley. They are highly productive when there is sufficient rainfall or adequate irrigation."
    },
    {
      "id": "588b68c3-1011-4723-8a93-97fe79c05591",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The chief crop of the Kashmir Valley is rice, followed by maize, barley, and wheat. Kashmir region accounts for about 61% of the total cultivable land under rice, and about 90% of the area under rice is irrigated. Kashmir alone contributes more than 74% of the total rice produced in the State, boasting the highest rice yield of 26.13 q\/ha (compared to approximately 15.96 q\/ha in Jammu).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "03938dcc-dfc1-4340-8a9c-2851b9cb0c75",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Zone 3: Cold Arid Desert Areas of Ladakh",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "68fd6c27-8398-4f74-acae-a3e16c819509",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Ladakh zone is characterised by bare rocky mountains, bare gravel slopes, small pockets of level land, and irrigation facilities clustered around villages. Cultivation is possible mainly where suitable level land and irrigation facilities are available.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fc32317c-1a6a-40b9-8c76-98269718b7eb",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Barley is the major cereal crop, followed by summer wheat. Millets and wheat are also important and are grown particularly in the warmer belt of the region.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "816e439f-cd4d-40c6-b490-86d5dde44770",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "4. Agricultural Development and Land Constraints",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "715fa2c0-23fb-47b5-b293-84a1361eef2c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The physical and climatic conditions act as inhibiting factors in some parts of the State. Another major limitation is the extremely small size of holdings, with the average holding being about 0.73 hectare, along with the absence of further scope for extension of cultivation.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0fe141f1-e03f-4b99-a6c9-85be4518cce5",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Therefore, agricultural land has to be used optimally so that limited land gives maximum production. This can be achieved through the judicious application of modern technology adapted to local conditions. The disadvantage of limited land can be partly overcome by increasing the area under double cropping and introducing a short-duration rabi crop in the Valley, where traditionally only one crop a year has been grown.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "84c38419-e82e-4832-8f5c-9519c3d82e22",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "It is essential to exploit the potential of irrigation in the State. Schemes involving new khuls, wells, pumping sets, and the renovation and repair of zamindari khuls should receive due attention.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "54b9a637-7442-4830-9a5d-f70819bff3c5",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Agricultural Legislation Constraints",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8bab3bda-054a-4ff9-98fc-c82333984019",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "State legislation has historically contributed to the slow growth of agriculture and horticulture. Two notable legislations mentioned are:",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7acca102-6808-430a-9cb5-d1fb5a535e58",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Conversion Act: Restricts cultivators from converting irrigated agricultural land into orchards.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3902d4db-bef6-434f-b970-e8332d9e6204",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Kuth Act: Restricts cultivators from growing wild trees having medicinal value, which hampers growth in some areas.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "82d93ab1-1b62-4b52-a7f7-026a90c4b25e",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Once these issues are addressed, significant improvement can come through modern technology, high-yielding varieties, and greater use of fertilizers.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "621f7f1b-b03b-48ee-ad05-87fbce56f9af",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "5. Main Crops",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6425c0f0-79bc-4c4c-9e4e-4c30264beb68",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Rice",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4ca5211b-20de-435e-a368-3c186bdbf76a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Rice is a Kharif crop that requires a hot and moist climate. It is sown in March–April and harvested in autumn. Sufficient water must cover the fields during its growth. It is mainly grown in the Kashmir Valley, up to about 2100 m above sea level. The total area under rice cultivation in the Kashmir Valley is about 3,74,000 acres, with a yield of about 25.5 quintals per acre.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "18d36063-da08-4fe9-bb16-93f4e5c27ca9",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Wheat",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b92adb7b-444c-4d3d-ad91-c1f38550983f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Wheat is a Rabi crop that requires a cool and somewhat moist climate in the beginning and warm weather at harvest. It requires an average rainfall of 50–70 cm at regular intervals. It is sown in August and harvested in March–April. It is cultivated throughout the outer plains and outer hills.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6722becd-2f5f-4934-b163-dbbb0055fd26",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Important wheat-producing areas: Kathua, Kabir Singh Pora, Samba, and Reasi.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "001cbf10-264c-452c-8bfd-ea3c4e313841",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Area under wheat cultivation: Jammu (31,000 acres), Kashmir (78,000 acres), and Ladakh (7,000 acres).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "44e51ee5-000d-45ba-ad6d-fc7cfdafcd45",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "In Kashmir, wheat is grown like grass.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "842d3a2d-1e78-4f6b-b696-ecc3b50c5d05",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Maize",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "97074127-c2d2-480d-ac46-17e7ac8c1858",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Maize requires a hot and dry climate with a rainfall requirement of 75–125 cm. It is sown in May–July and harvested in August–November. It is extensively cultivated on Karewa lands in the Kashmir Valley. The total area under maize cultivation is about 3,03,000 acres.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "439ae580-96d0-49e3-aa7e-d8af83f44ef9",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Tobacco",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f940c288-003f-43a2-b493-9ce2330e55b7",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Tobacco requires a warm and moist climate and rich soil containing lime. It is largely grown in the Kashmir Valley, where soil conditions are highly suitable.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5978d931-4202-476f-9ada-34c0fda08f50",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Oilseeds",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5583537b-6c4b-4a26-8629-278de1b6deee",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Oilseeds require a hot and moist climate. They are grown throughout Kashmir Province, with Anantnag and Srinagar being the chief oilseed-producing areas. About 6,700 acres in the Kashmir region produce oilseeds.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "79cdfaae-b2df-4575-aa77-236e43b00676",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Pulses",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "66f8e6a4-8127-4638-bc8d-4ccfa171b23f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The hot and dry climate of the State is suitable for pulse cultivation. Pulses are largely grown on small patches of land, and those from the Kashmir Valley are well known for their high quality.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e9b0ae11-26f0-498d-b24c-42f9119895a9",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Saffron",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "992a496d-564f-4f72-8901-98226d1e81f6",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Saffron is a highly valuable cash crop. It is mainly cultivated in Pampore, with cultivation taking place during July–August. About 3,000 acres are under saffron cultivation in Pampore.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fce5896f-38d2-4b6e-8db9-b74b89a24de4",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "6. Horticulture, Floriculture, and Sericulture",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4ed77020-cd78-404e-9663-bca8d9ea1655",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Horticulture",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "63ce130f-bcf7-4314-abfc-873420e7d27c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Jammu and Kashmir is famous for its horticultural produce in India and abroad. The State provides good scope for cultivation of both temperate and sub-tropical fruits. Horticulture is an emerging and fast-growing sector, contributing about 7–8% to the State's economy and about 45% to the agricultural sector of the State.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "463b318d-ab38-42ad-be7e-e43418caf0e1",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Temperate Fruits: Apple, Pear, Peach, Plum, Apricot, Almond, Cherry, Walnut, Grape, Pomegranate, and Mulberry. These require a cool climate, moderate rainfall, and bright sunshine.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f892ef21-9bf3-409d-89f2-5df4cb818dde",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Sub-tropical Fruits: Mango, Guava, and Litchi.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5c10fa63-5ee0-4582-a921-c9db5ab5327d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "According to the Horticulture Department report for 2008–09, about 3.06 lakh hectares were under horticulture, showing an increase of 3.73% over the previous year. The largest area was under apple (43.30%), followed by walnut (27.80%). Total fruit production during 2008–09 was 16.91 lakh tonnes (a 3.36% increase over the previous year), with apple accounting for the largest share.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "45394e2f-4235-4d26-93e5-838f2feab62e",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Floriculture",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2476bbbc-caa2-404f-8983-ab2f74dc43af",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Floriculture has become a major focused segment of horticulture because of increasing demand for flowers in domestic and foreign markets. To promote this sector, floriculture nurseries have been developed, ornamental and medicinal plants are produced, and seed multiplication programmes are undertaken. The Directorate of Floriculture produces more than 4 lakh seedlings of different kinds of flowers and ornamental plants.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c9b1976a-e915-4ca6-b4ea-b9935e7a3245",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "IMPORTANT",
      "title": "The Tulip Garden of Srinagar",
      "content": "One of the landmark achievements of the Floriculture Department has been the establishment of the Tulip Garden at Siraj Bagh, Srinagar. Described as the largest Tulip Garden in Asia, it is situated at the foothills of the Zabarwan Mountains and attracts a large inflow of tourists and film-making crews."
    },
    {
      "id": "e597dd8a-cc37-44d4-94fd-8c162c26dc92",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Sericulture",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d3f7b7cd-935c-4e78-94b4-3ddd4f897a79",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Sericulture is one of the traditional occupations of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a traditional means of producing silk comparable to the finest qualities of raw silk in the international market. Kashmir has introduced better silk, both in quality and quantity, compared with silk from Japan and Italy.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a2998097-ff9f-4fb7-bebe-7dc1510ab58a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The climate of Kashmir is temperate and congenial for rearing both Univoltine and Bivoltine silkworm species. The cocoons produced are superior to the multivoltine cocoons produced in the rest of the country. However, the silk industry has been on the decline due to several major problems:",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5a15517b-a4cd-452a-82c8-d1d5f6dbb2b2",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Inadequacy of mulberry leaves",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ab3dc708-e7a5-4bea-9e88-e55898763bb8",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Damage caused by insects and pests",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "73b1bbd1-b725-4694-9a65-50a461c85901",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Problems in the development and expansion of mulberry trees",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2d5dde16-fe8a-4249-8d8d-5eb66df052fc",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Sericulture Development Department is actively promoting dwarf mulberry trees to supplement and replenish traditional tall mulberry trees.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1bd1f029-c6b8-4401-a306-1cf7775f3dd3",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "7. Irrigation and Hydro-Geological Units",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6f253e7f-0640-443b-9e3b-b19d5a0d52f4",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Irrigation is an important indicator for measuring the development of agriculture in a State because it directly affects agricultural productivity. In 1950–51, the net area irrigated through canals, tanks, wells, and other sources was about 2.61 lakh hectares (41.96%). The State Government has since created an irrigation potential of about 5.62 lakh hectares, with about 41% of the net sown area currently irrigated.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "685b577e-dca0-4426-b806-99b8a004f199",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Hydro-Geological Units",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "92e82613-aa80-4419-89ef-6925fed19f44",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The State can be divided into three distinct hydro-geological units:",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "262708e3-f79d-4aa6-9a90-48299b2b374a",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Outer Plains of Jammu Region: Located at the foothills of the Shiwalik Hills, with altitudes ranging between 260 and 440 m above mean sea level. Numerous seasonal streams, locally called khads, cross the area. These plains are further divided into Bhabar (where groundwater is deep and under water-level conditions) and Tarai (where groundwater occurs under both water-level and confined conditions).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8d806c1e-52f4-476d-b8fb-a413e69212c8",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Kashmir Valley: Characterised by soft alluvial soil and extensive canal networks fed by the Jhelum and its tributaries.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "febc6ca9-5d1d-4a21-a1dd-a54d19cc173e",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Ladakh Region: Characterised by hyper-arid conditions where irrigation is restricted to small pockets near glacial melt streams.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9c8e5d6a-afb4-47b5-970a-157298f247ea",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Methods of Irrigation",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "189ed160-db74-4384-bb87-01a97c31744c",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Canals: The most important irrigation system in the outer plains and the broad Kashmir Valley. The soil in these areas is soft and alluvial, making canals easy to construct. The Jhelum and its tributaries are snow-fed and generally do not run dry, supplying water to canals throughout the year. About 4,86,072 acres of agricultural land in Kashmir is irrigated by canals.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "75991afe-7114-451f-8d89-9d7898689c96",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Lift Irrigation: Water is mechanically pumped to a higher level and then distributed to fields through gravity canals.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cb5bea72-f756-41d1-9cd3-b99222e0aa46",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Lever System: Used where water is available at a shallow depth of about 1–2 metres. At present, about 6,000 such wells are working in the State.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dfda99f0-1bc5-4182-9a01-8d2051ff86bd",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "8. Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "66d12519-0dac-46eb-a9b5-2f94218044f7",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Right to Information (RTI) is derived from the fundamental right of freedom of speech and expression under Article 19 of the Constitution. If citizens do not have information about how the Government and public institutions function, they cannot express an informed opinion.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "03ff1eba-ed80-422b-8ced-5bf472937111",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "Objectives of the RTI Act",
      "content": "The basic objectives of the RTI Act are to empower citizens, promote transparency and accountability in the working of the Government, contain corruption, and enhance people's participation in the democratic process."
    },
    {
      "id": "047c0648-0cdf-4778-a564-06c492724f20",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Factors responsible for the adoption of the Information Act include rising public awareness against corruption and scandals, international pressure and activism, and the transition towards a modernised information society.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3c2bbe88-23a4-4a33-b28f-99372557c26d",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Key Provisions of the RTI Act",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "19d5d729-55bb-474f-a0e2-ad17d3075da7",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Section 1(2): Historically, it extended to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (as per the historical context of the source text).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "62435d21-c55b-4301-8f2d-b028b051ee4e",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Section 2(f) - 'Information': Defines information as any material in any form, including records, documents, memos, e-mails, opinions, advices, press releases, circulars, orders, logbooks, contracts, reports, papers, samples, models, and data material held electronically.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "bb33a9bb-6b36-4961-925d-98ad5f4adeea",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Section 2(j) - 'Right to Information': Defines the right to inspect works, documents, and records; take notes, extracts, or certified copies; take certified samples of material; and obtain information through electronic modes or printouts.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a826ec60-9f35-49c1-a2ff-f9bd15b8c2b1",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Section 4: Requires suo motu (proactive) disclosure of information by every public authority.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f3fa0ff3-3c16-4075-87fc-52c5c29b028e",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Section 8(1): Provides exemptions from furnishing certain sensitive information.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "bea71cfc-381e-4d76-ba5f-ac285c0fc6f9",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Section 8(2): Provides for disclosure of information otherwise exempt under the Official Secrets Act, 1923, if the larger public interest outweighs the harm to protected interests.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "10af936b-78bf-4431-8bfd-70b3c83213c6",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Information Commissioners: Appointed at Central and State levels to oversee compliance. Public authorities designate Public Information Officers (PIOs) to process applications.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "37741b6d-422f-40ed-a3e4-cff7230dfe5c",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Time Limits for Providing Information",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "db51332c-7702-4955-970a-2ad5de0aac01",
      "type": "TABLE",
      "title": "RTI Response Timeframes",
      "headers": [
        "Scenario",
        "Statutory Time Limit"
      ],
      "rows": [
        [
          "Normal Application",
          "Within 30 days from receipt"
        ],
        [
          "Information concerning Life or Liberty of a person",
          "Within 48 hours"
        ],
        [
          "Application submitted through APIO or to a wrong authority",
          "An additional 5 days are added to the limit"
        ]
      ],
      "hasHeaderRow": true
    },
    {
      "id": "da36164e-5350-4510-91b4-ad3d0e777567",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "9. Indus Waters Treaty (IWT)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3350d4eb-09e9-47af-b8b9-1975351d7669",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) is a water-distribution treaty signed on 19 September 1960 between Jawaharlal Nehru (then Prime Minister of India) and Ayub Khan (then President of Pakistan). The treaty was brokered by the World Bank, then known as the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), after nine years of negotiations following water disputes that arose after the Partition of India in 1947.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b933f6a8-a807-4afb-84fd-19fac3a71ccf",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "River Allocation and Water Share",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7f2e2bd3-206c-455e-8fc8-e48c2a0aa26e",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The treaty establishes conditions for sharing the waters of the Indus River System, which originates in Tibet and flows through India and Pakistan. The rivers are divided as follows:",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "100d974b-93c3-4c4a-9f42-a2439bdda5bb",
      "type": "TABLE",
      "title": "Indus Waters Treaty River Allocation",
      "headers": [
        "Category",
        "Rivers",
        "Primary Control",
        "Permitted Uses & Conditions"
      ],
      "rows": [
        [
          "Eastern Rivers",
          "Ravi, Beas, Sutlej",
          "India",
          "Unrestricted use by India."
        ],
        [
          "Western Rivers",
          "Indus, Chenab, Jhelum",
          "Pakistan",
          "India can use water for domestic, non-consumptive, storage, irrigation, and run-of-the-river power generation."
        ]
      ],
      "hasHeaderRow": true
    },
    {
      "id": "3e46a7c1-6749-4ac6-8ca2-3c646e5cfaa1",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Overall, the treaty allocates approximately 20% of the total water of the Indus River System to India, with the remaining 80% allocated to Pakistan. Both countries are required to avoid causing material damage to each other when implementing flood-protection schemes.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2b912bc2-96ed-4990-b562-2186d4ac642a",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Key Disputes and Projects",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1496b24c-28a5-404b-905a-bcdc38a2f7a3",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Kishanganga and Ratle Projects: In 2016, Pakistan raised objections with the World Bank regarding India's Kishanganga and Ratle hydroelectric projects in J&K. India requested neutral technical experts, arguing the concerns were technical rather than legal. The World Bank eventually permitted India to proceed.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c3162678-7a4d-4be5-bf55-63a411ebe68f",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Tulbul Project: A navigation lock-cum-control structure at the mouth of Wular Lake on the Jhelum River. The project was suspended in 1987 following objections from Pakistan, though India has periodically reviewed this suspension.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a18a1c5d-7e0b-4cf7-b844-00d982847a99",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Left Bank Outfall Drain (LBOD): A Pakistani drainage project passing through the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat. India objected to its construction because it was built without India's consent and caused flooding concerns in Gujarat.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6859d28c-889b-4598-b10d-1645371970a8",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Unutilised Indian Share: India historically does not utilise its entire allocated share of water. Around 2 million acre-feet (MAF) of water from the Ravi River flows into Pakistan unused. Following the 2019 Pulwama attack, the Indian Government announced plans to divert this unutilised water from the Eastern Rivers to Haryana, Punjab, and Rajasthan.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dad6cd8b-9e91-4195-98c0-a0a273a75f83",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Infrastructure on Eastern Rivers",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "806ed843-b25a-41ac-91e5-ebe0db9f5b63",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "To fully utilise its allocated share of the Eastern Rivers, India has constructed several major dams and water-transfer links:",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a2be82c8-21b7-4242-b813-a411edafc6a8",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Bhakra Dam on the Sutlej River",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ca3deade-be2e-49c7-b5b2-55d70703413c",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Ranjit Sagar Dam on the Ravi River",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "29e6dbde-d9fe-413b-9d4d-5172ccc8a35c",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Pandoh Dam on the Beas River",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "356af3c4-5769-4852-980a-4fb515b5bba0",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Beas-Sutlej Link, Madhopur-Beas Link, and the Indira Gandhi Nahar Project (enabling 95% water utilisation)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "bcde2c87-1a47-4be7-8c93-2d848adbcdd7",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Proposed 2nd Ravi-Beas Link Project: A planned National Project (with a 6-year implementation period) designed to tap excess water flowing down to Pakistan below Ujh by constructing a barrage across the Ravi to divert water to the Beas basin.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "264f7095-fb58-456a-b7d7-5b7ba85c754b",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Key Revision Points",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2cdb0299-7d5e-41db-9b3f-a1b70a8b2311",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Agriculture is the backbone of J&K, supporting 70% of the population and contributing 16% to the State GDP.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ae58b663-c7f2-4a35-8ebd-636dff81e1b5",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "The State is divided into three agro-climatic zones: Humid Sub-Tropical Jammu, Temperate Kashmir Valley, and Cold Arid Ladakh.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a46a6ac6-8630-4c18-b879-6529747fc45e",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Karewas are highly fertile elevated lacustrine plateaus in the Kashmir Valley, famous for saffron and fruit cultivation.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6773de14-a336-4c2c-b0c9-a6cd52bd5003",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Rice is the primary Kharif crop of Kashmir, while Wheat and Maize dominate Jammu's agricultural output.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "af6ced0c-2811-4bc5-82ef-186951003a9d",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Saffron cultivation is highly localized, centered primarily in the Pampore region of Kashmir.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ed63e4d3-451b-45a4-8e02-94acfc9cbf99",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Horticulture contributes 7–8% to the State's economy, with Apple (43.30% area) and Walnut (27.80% area) being the leading crops.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "74180119-f699-45a9-9fae-9912a6c62c2b",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "The Siraj Bagh Tulip Garden in Srinagar, located at the foothills of the Zabarwan Mountains, is the largest Tulip Garden in Asia.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "73a98fea-8d1b-47fc-988f-d89745935748",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Sericulture in J&K utilizes Univoltine and Bivoltine silkworm species to produce high-grade silk.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "763857b0-8a76-4ba2-b95e-0edb014580fe",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Canals are the primary source of irrigation, covering over 4.86 lakh acres of agricultural land in Kashmir.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b5e9c797-1e5b-4bc3-8293-d55d2a512902",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "The RTI Act 2005 mandates a 30-day response limit for standard queries and a strict 48-hour limit for cases involving life or liberty.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b8e86c57-7f53-497a-aef5-18d06fed252d",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "The Indus Waters Treaty (1960) allocates the Eastern Rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) to India and the Western Rivers (Indus, Chenab, Jhelum) to Pakistan.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a341cf94-e876-4a5c-97e2-cfc5e32d8556",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "The Tulbul Project is a controversial navigation lock-cum-control structure on the Jhelum River at the mouth of Wular Lake.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    }
  ]
}

{
  "chapterId": "chap_54d91de7",
  "title": "Soils and Minerals",
  "elements": [
    {
      "id": "c93c09d8-4dd6-4fa0-bb6e-87abe9118bc7",
      "type": "HEADING_1",
      "text": "CHAPTER 5: SOILS AND MINERALS",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0eddaad6-3f5c-4614-ba41-25e5cc1a1fa3",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "1. Soils in Jammu and Kashmir",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "24258148-6400-4753-a098-a1c28d7f06b7",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "In the regions of Jammu and Kashmir, the soils are generally loamy with a low clay content. They are characteristically poor in lime but rich in magnesia. Prior to cultivation, these soils typically require treatment with chemical fertilizers and enrichment using green manure and legumes.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4c736633-5636-44ff-863f-8030a7e7ef3c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The alluvium of the Kashmir Valley contains sufficient organic matter and nitrogen, primarily accumulated from plant residues, crop stubble, natural vegetation, and animal excretion.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4ce4f6fe-3aa9-4828-a25c-01954d17d7bd",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "1.1 Major Soil Types",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7d99b4b1-02d3-48a5-adb3-45ba80c9913a",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Hill Soil",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7bcc1678-d460-4e78-a924-1e870bfff433",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Hill soils are acidic in nature and contain lower amounts of potash, phosphorus, and lime. Despite these deficiencies, orchards of apple, walnut, and pear thrive exceptionally well on this soil type.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cfbf2c69-3e32-48a8-9cee-656913bc6e5a",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Alluvial Soil",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "67eba05a-e787-4de8-9c9a-dfba2625d2fb",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Alluvial soils are highly productive and fertile. They are formed from sand, silt, and mud deposited by rivers during seasonal floods.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "84566e5c-d969-4a7b-90ca-fa0cf13897e5",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "These soils are primarily distributed across:",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "562e297d-723c-40d0-8eab-c6d668a225fe",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The southern plains",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3884e206-003f-4195-8130-eb922cb15eb4",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The valley bottom of Kashmir",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "413a24a6-8076-4862-93e0-ac2d5752704b",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Along the banks of the Jhelum and Chenab rivers",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ed03de23-5e76-4ef1-905e-daf58ffb94be",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Karewa Soil",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2b98b355-e9e5-442a-b91f-0b98f87227d9",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Karewa soils occur in the form of flat, low-lying mounds. These soils are highly specialized and globally famous for being exceptionally suitable for growing saffron and various temperate fruits.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fd7a565b-59e5-436d-b38c-a6980e04c454",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Karewa deposits are predominantly found in:",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f44284af-9db5-4b76-ab2c-0d30647a070a",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Kashmir Valley",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5c7a094a-8a2d-4e50-9c3b-3c9089664af5",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Kishtwar district",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d77774c4-b4d3-4ab6-aec5-bce848dcbeed",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Pampore",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "aa57b0ea-852f-4540-b9d8-4748543348de",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Mattan",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ab0e29bc-58c7-4421-a92a-fb9d1f60a32a",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Kulgam",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {

      "id": "de117691-84a0-423e-8f11-ae521e86df9c",

    {
      "id": "5a68394b-3fac-463e-8ce2-71e4661d6367",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Jammu and Kashmir possesses limited mineral and fossil-fuel resources, with a significant portion of these reserves concentrated in the Jammu region. Small reserves of natural gas are located near Jammu, while bauxite and gypsum deposits occur in the Udhampur district. Other notable minerals found in the state include limestone, coal, zinc, and copper.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e7e4c2b5-5053-4035-bbf4-73f58231645e",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "IMPORTANT",
      "title": "History of Mineral Surveys in J&K",
      "content": "The first systematic survey of the state's mineral wealth was conducted in 1924 by the renowned geologist Mr. Middlemiss in collaboration with the Government of Jammu and Kashmir. A more intensive, modern mineral survey was later undertaken in 1956, leading to organized and systematic mineral exploitation."
    },
    {
      "id": "0c897b6e-1436-4140-ad2b-e657c0f7d947",

    {
      "id": "321dfc15-88f4-462b-827b-77a718ba86d6",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Coal found in Jammu and Kashmir is of high-grade semi-anthracite quality. Approximately 10% of the total production is extracted as steam coal.",

      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,

    {
      "id": "904a68c2-7540-4473-b22b-a63ffe8a3a8b",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "Properties of J&K Coal",
      "content": "The coal is characterized by a high heat value, a low ash content of about 5%, and a high calorific value ranging between 6000 and 7800 kcal\/kg."
    },

      "id": "78e1727a-d907-4c44-8bd7-445f447d98ce",

    {

      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "World-famous sapphire deposits occur in the remote Paddar area of Doda district. The Paddar sapphire is globally renowned for its deep blue color and exceptional purity, often rated superior to varieties found in Sri Lanka.",

      "content": "Historically, sapphire extraction in Paddar has suffered from unscientific and primitive mining techniques. Experts suggest that introducing international expertise and private-sector investment is crucial for systematic, high-yield development of these reserves."

      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "64b05e86-9e1f-4aee-ad73-70a320047e20",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "8.3 Gold",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "af1602c8-1ee6-4046-9bf2-5e2107d5cb78",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Gold deposits have been identified in Kargil, Ladakh, and Sonamarg.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d18927e5-ceaa-488b-9086-144f3e99c305",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "9. Other Minerals and Energy Resources",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "15cfbe42-d2df-4a7a-92ec-250a8bbfa5d1",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "9.1 Mica",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "618f9e3c-5af1-4341-b800-7fdb17aa22b6",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Mica deposits are located in Doda, Ramban, and Reasi.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "be143bea-79dc-49c9-b3db-f80ab6c9ef4a",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "9.2 Uranium",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "56fde2f5-e3cc-4643-a788-b73aa883a472",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Uranium reserves have been identified in the Ladakh region.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4521d931-48cf-4fda-a1e1-5ba742e5fc6e",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "9.3 Petroleum",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1972e52a-1cf6-4a89-919f-be9145fbf868",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Petroleum reserves have been detected at Ramnagar, Kakra, Udh, and Surinsar.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "69a93b2b-8a7f-4294-a069-5dfa3124d778",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "9.4 Graphite",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "938ac40f-f10e-4eb9-a7cc-3bff36fa8eab",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Graphite, primarily used in manufacturing lead pencils, is found in the Kashmir Province at Bararipora, Uri, Karmah, Malogam, and Piran.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d9ba06d7-33c4-4a6d-9012-903bb3d736e4",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "9.5 Sulphur",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9e5f9b88-4c11-4a19-aa7b-1d012e90504a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Sulphur is found in the Pugga Valley of Ladakh. Additionally, sulphur associated with thermal spring water is found at Anantnag and Khrewa.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c8825e19-e867-499b-a4b9-55ff873951cf",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Revision: Key Takeaways",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "eb026834-1794-44c5-9e2f-dd2d759d3c60",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Soils in J&K are generally loamy, poor in lime, and rich in magnesia.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "99c28f88-7f61-4697-a582-482de8a1f0a7",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "The three primary soil types are Hill Soil (acidic), Alluvial Soil (highly fertile), and Karewa Soil (famous for saffron and fruits).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "be38dca8-e64d-4a22-9322-def5ed1cc55e",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Local soil names include Gurti (clay), Bahil (loam), Sekil (sandy), Nambaal (peat), Surzamin (loses fertility), Lemb (nutrient-deficient), Kharzain (acidic patches), and Tand (mountain slopes).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3c171db0-0125-4b6a-ba4f-d8f7d6a5a4de",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "The first systematic mineral survey of J&K was conducted by Mr. Middlemiss in 1924.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
