      "id": "6d934731-e44c-408c-a0f3-16aa3f197153",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Coal in J&K is semi-anthracite, with major mines at Melka, Moghla, Baryal, and Kalakot.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cfcd8809-85f8-4e90-aab6-44e0fa8a27e5",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Paddar in Doda is world-famous for high-purity deep blue Sapphire.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1fd3ebb7-f0d2-4f06-a1a9-ad90608e9b1d",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Pugga Valley in Ladakh is a major source of Borax and Sulphur.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "600bf00e-f46b-46f4-9de1-705c3a86bf67",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "High-quality limestone is mined at Wuyan and Khrewa for cement manufacturing.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    }
  ]
}

{
  "chapterId": "chap_c0935301",
  "title": "Rivers, Lakes and Glaciers",
  "elements": [
    {
      "id": "9c3e3c58-eadb-426a-b38d-aecc770c0fc8",
      "type": "HEADING_1",
      "text": "CHAPTER 4: RIVERS, LAKES AND GLACIERS",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f528c443-3866-49d7-803b-42314e3fcaee",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Jammu and Kashmir region is home to a vast network of rivers, lakes, and glaciers that originate primarily from the Himalayas. These water bodies play a crucial role in the geography, ecology, and economy of the region.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ad3d94d5-7319-403b-ba40-6c386433062d",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Important Rivers",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "32841713-83f2-4cf7-ad74-eadcce23b9d6",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The primary rivers flowing through Jammu and Kashmir are the Jhelum, Chenab, and Indus. These rivers are of Himalayan origin and are characterized by their perennial flow and deep gorges.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "bc302877-b43f-44fd-8765-976d5347845b",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Jhelum River",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "88f0edb4-faf6-43c5-8d5d-52a26f6c07a5",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Jhelum is the main waterway of the Valley of Kashmir. It rises from the famous Verinag spring, located on the northern slope of the Pir Panjal Range. A number of tributaries join the Jhelum, making it navigable from Khannabal to Wular Lake. Its total length within the valley is approximately 177 km.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "470433e3-def9-49f0-ad33-b93c3e5d80fc",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "Ancient Name of Jhelum",
      "content": "The Jhelum River was known in ancient times as the Vitasta. In the Kashmiri language, this name was historically transformed into Veth."
    },
    {
      "id": "a1b75631-46e2-4ede-88bd-2baebb59ee36",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Ravi River",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a907c00b-4ab8-4e02-8ef9-a98c6bc8fdc2",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Ravi River rises in the Himalayas at Basoli. It passes close to Kathua, near Madhopur, where it exits the hills and enters the fertile plains of Punjab.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e05f896a-d3e7-4d69-8708-eddf8a928eba",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Tawi River",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b7a49e28-fea4-4977-9e03-04bd3f445eac",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Tawi River drains the outer hill region of Jammu. It collects drainage from the interior mountains to the north-east of Jammu and flows directly around Jammu city.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3555c414-d314-4e45-b68e-46a02c8e2ce2",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Chenab River",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "58af95cf-239b-455f-9b0e-68ef300e04f5",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Chenab River rises in the Himalayan region of Lahaul and Spiti. It is formed by the confluence of two parallel streams, the Chandra and the Bhaga, which together are known as the Chandrabhaga or Chenab. The river drains the eastern section of the southern slope of the Pir Panjal Range.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "14d947c6-cff8-4daf-8a75-1ef9f1b462ba",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Indus River",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "27b6b6a7-cb15-489f-add7-ef698233a2cd",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Indus is one of the most significant rivers of the subcontinent. It originates near Mansarovar Lake in Tibet, close to the Kashmir border. A considerable portion of this massive river flows through neighbouring countries.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "50535be6-6a23-4230-9316-b950c3436bda",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Zanskar River",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ad6e9a0f-4a9a-4c4b-8522-e117e3ff93eb",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Zanskar River is a major northern tributary of the Indus River. It has two main branches in its upper reaches: the Doda and a second branch formed by the Kargyak and Tsarap rivers.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1e6eb3b8-444b-44f4-96ae-9c7e02161b04",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Branches of the Zanskar River",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f397ffad-a231-491d-93ff-8a948378759b",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Doda Branch: Originates near Pensi La at an altitude of about 4,400 meters and flows through the main Zanskar Valley.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1bc38a93-e339-4ec7-9046-5b0dc4555c63",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Kargyak River: Has its source near Shingo La at an altitude of 5,091 meters.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1a592989-6d5a-4c0f-9924-ee6b7802b8a9",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Tsarap River: Has its source near Baralacha La.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "737e0497-ed3b-46a4-97a4-87363792f243",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Shyok River",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "67057052-886f-4f97-995c-df864cce9fc4",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Shyok River is a key tributary of the Indus River, passing through the Ladakh region of India and northern Pakistan for about 550 km. It originates from the Rimo Glacier, which is a tongue of the Siachen Glacier. The Shyok River widens significantly at its confluence with the Nubra River.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "29ecd7b2-f212-4d07-a326-8d664bf54e7e",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Kishanganga River",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7b7a4874-72c1-411e-91d0-0ea38019ad02",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Also known as the Neelum River, the Kishanganga flows through the Kashmir region and enters Pakistan in the Gurais sector of the Line of Control (LoC). It eventually meets the Jhelum River north of Muzaffarabad. The controversial Kishanganga Power Project is constructed on this river.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7e1434b2-2b6e-4495-984e-8c6fa8461a49",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Doda River",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "29add941-bbeb-4bb7-b656-b4c7098b20e3",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Doda River originates from the Drang Drung Glacier near Pensi La. It flows through the Ladakh region and joins the Tsarap River to form the larger Zanskar River.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "01582ee8-4a5f-412f-8af5-116e24500b07",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Dras River",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dc8449cb-49b0-4640-9c17-57eaeac922ce",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Dras River is a tributary of the Suru River. It originates in the Machoi Glacier near the strategic Zoji La Pass.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3ab9e5ba-279d-49ea-8712-2888b47080ec",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Nubra River",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "83fbfa21-e1c4-44fe-993e-83f54722e766",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Nubra River is a tributary of the Shyok River, flowing through the Ladakh region. It originates directly from the Siachen Glacier.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e1655914-dd0f-48e9-8a23-952e61119a27",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Important Lakes",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "89ffd444-36af-46fd-a112-fb1a5900565d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Jammu and Kashmir region is dotted with numerous scenic lakes, most of which are of glacial origin. These lakes serve as major ecological habitats and tourist attractions.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "11376a86-c6c6-438f-a21c-d9de53da4472",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Wular Lake",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c6bd74f5-a8e0-4049-b9eb-0b4562c2183f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Wular Lake is the largest freshwater lake in India. It is approximately 16 km long and 9.6 km wide, featuring well-defined shores. The lake lies between Bandipore and Sopore, at a distance of about 75 km from Srinagar.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "736de349-f861-40b6-8e8e-373c49e38f63",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Dal Lake",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3a07dcbc-8669-42ec-8c16-8d5143955c34",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Dal Lake is a world-famous, beautiful lake located near Srinagar. It is about 8 km long and 6.4 km wide. It acts as a flooding lake for the Jhelum River. The famous Mughal gardens are situated around its shores, and it is well-known for its floating gardens where a large variety of vegetables are cultivated.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "29bf1a78-176f-4559-8cad-b989f68b24c5",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Nagin Lake",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3be417a6-846d-411a-853b-9b3c566f3f93",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Nagin Lake is located a short distance from Dal Lake and is interconnected with it by a small water channel. Like Dal Lake, Nagin Lake freezes during the peak of winter.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "27c5953c-f18b-41aa-b56a-ae33f692c56f",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Anchar Lake",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5634f5b2-49f7-4461-89cb-19bfa428b0ff",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Anchar Lake is a swampy lake measuring about 8 km in length and 3 km in width. The Sind Nallah enters the lake from one side and flows out from the other. Ganderbal is a famous township situated on its north-western bank.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "91d83177-551e-47a5-a685-9d6e9532c401",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Mansbal Lake",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2410bf1d-0466-458c-8db5-230b9d3d1f96",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Mansbal Lake is situated about 29 km from Srinagar near Sopore. It is approximately 5 km long and 1 km wide. It is connected to the Jhelum River by a canal near Sumbal.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "537bd4a0-f608-407c-ad0d-d5b8e83f068b",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Mansar Lake",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ab34aad9-192e-4822-b0ae-e28e2c1b33d6",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Located about 62 km from Jammu, Mansar Lake is more than a mile long and half a mile wide. It is a popular excursion destination and a holy site sharing the sanctity of Lake Mansarovar. The shrine of the mythological serpent Sheshnag lies on its eastern bank, where devotees take holy dips during festive occasions.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6b54abcf-9511-45b6-8d4d-6812f148468c",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Harwan Lake",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f958ce76-484c-4202-9bed-eb732121bd13",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Harwan Lake is situated about 21 km from Srinagar. It is 278 m long, 137 m wide, and 18 m deep. This lake serves as a primary source of water supply to Srinagar city.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7aab95e9-4ec4-4e3c-9a81-7849bc530280",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Hokarsar Lake",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e04417bc-98e8-46ca-9630-be42f98bb9f8",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Hokarsar Lake lies on the Baramulla road, about 13 km from Srinagar. It is 5 km long and 1.5 km wide, with abundant willow trees growing along its banks.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7de66558-b190-4684-8abf-055bd8603613",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Vishno Pad Lake (Kounsarnag)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "37adc562-3d74-4797-a18e-94afd486505b",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Also known as Kounsarnag, this lake is situated in the Pir Panjal Range at an elevation of 13,124 feet (4,000 m) above sea level. It is 5 km long and 3 km wide. It is the source of the Vishav River and is located about 34 km from Shopian.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "edf0e847-95d2-4726-86d0-e6120fdf2fe3",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Gangabal Lake",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c690427e-6306-4bb3-ba6c-88a4878b149c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Gangabal Lake is situated at a height of 11,713 feet (3,570 m) on the peak of Harmukh Mountain.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5fdce47b-6b0d-4a3f-bd8d-264ed88acd4a",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Sheshnag Lake",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d263bfb5-5199-465a-9304-e71497def76f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Sheshnag Lake is situated near Vayjan, en route to the holy Shri Amarnath Cave. It is located about 28 km from Pahalgam.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "01ca4535-30cc-4329-8050-4d8c30d6a5d5",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Neelang Lake",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f562f0ff-2436-4041-b578-7cec12f272d0",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Neelang Lake is located in tehsil Badgam, about 10 km from Nagam, and is surrounded by dense forest.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1c762463-5400-4057-ab09-19414a09ea3e",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Tarsar and Marsar Lakes",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4dbc7f8d-0658-4a88-8440-073b9caa0d92",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "These twin lakes lie on the northern slopes of Harmukh Mountain.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ca8a941d-cf1b-4d2e-bc22-35e5dfc0697a",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Important Springs",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6e9102d1-5674-4dfd-9849-f57c835ffcd4",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Kashmir Valley is abundant in natural springs, many of which serve as the headwaters or major contributors to the Jhelum River. Some of the most famous springs include:",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4bd1302c-c28d-47aa-b292-ec752a614f4f",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Verinag: The primary source of the Jhelum River.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "caa4b438-ead1-455d-853a-af6ed88b1cc3",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Martand, Achnabal, and Kokernag: Located in the Anantnag district.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "16921048-7ebe-489b-973e-44e34216f62e",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Chashma Shahi: Situated near Srinagar on Boulevard Road, famous for its fresh and digestive water.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2a814dd3-3e7a-4742-9bc8-81ccfdd9552e",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Khir Bhawani: A highly sacred spring and temple site at Tullamarg.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "baee3e60-98b6-430e-95e6-9c459ac3b481",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Other notable springs: Vicharanag, Sukhnag, Vishnosar, Harmukat Gang, Chinmagad, and Vasanag (Anantnag).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7b6846e1-fb3d-4b43-85fb-cf8d49d20a9f",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Glaciers",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1429eed3-3621-46d6-b630-b2e5860217cc",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "What is a Glacier?",
      "content": "Glaciers are slowly moving masses of ice formed by the accumulation and compaction of snow on high mountains or near the polar regions."
    },
    {
      "id": "fdad09c9-0d63-4da6-865a-864204f25e3d",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Siachen Glacier",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5c20b83f-12f6-4daf-b82a-7d3bb3456511",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Siachen Glacier lies in the extreme north-central part of Jammu and Kashmir, near the border of India and Tibet. It has a length of about 72 km, making it the largest glacier outside the polar regions. It is located on the northern-facing slopes of the Karakoram Range and feeds the Muztagh (or Shaksgam) River. Large tributary glaciers like Shelkar, Chorten, and Mamostang open into it.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e2133459-d689-4aee-967f-5d17e945005c",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Rimo Glacier Group",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0e5a549e-1471-4154-88b9-3c25bfb9de29",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Located to the east of Siachen, the Rimo Glacier group consists of three glaciers: North, Central, and South. Situated at an altitude between 6,000 and 7,000 meters, they contain nearly 700 sq km of ice, which reaches depths of up to 100 meters.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6d8e36e6-348a-4d13-adcd-ffe0f62e4e83",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Biafo Glacier",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "935ce47f-b6d1-4693-88a5-f60d4bfc4671",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Located on the southern-facing slopes of the Karakoram Range in the Baltistan area of Ladakh, the Biafo Glacier is about 60 km long. Its meltwater flows into the Shigar River, a tributary of the Indus.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "495ae208-5369-4303-9607-9861da65191e",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Baltoro Glacier",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f89fd159-142f-4e1f-b4b9-c1810415e914",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Situated on the southern slopes of the Central Karakoram Range in Baltistan, the Baltoro Glacier is 62 km long and is the second-largest glacier in the Great Himalayan Range. It feeds the Shigar River and receives tributaries from the Gasherbrum and Masherbrum peaks.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "99ab6f96-8066-4a45-b227-4612e9446f64",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Hispar Glacier",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "aa0735ab-6b9b-4c82-b949-417dd62581be",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Located on the southern slopes of the Karakoram Range in Baltistan, the Hispar Glacier is 60 km long, making it the third-largest glacier in the region. It feeds the Shigar River. Its central portion is a vast snowfield, while its sides are covered in debris, and the entire tract completely lacks vegetation.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d920bb16-ea8e-4dad-8c09-1b9e195d66b0",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Nubra Glacier",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "894f7278-8041-490a-bc9d-b99b3da9e1f5",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Located on the southern slopes of the Karakoram Range in Ladakh, the Nubra Glacier gives rise to the Nubra River, which flows into the Shyok River. It is fed by valley glaciers from the Saser La Massif and the Karakoram Range.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "22b4210b-141e-44da-bc8e-3ec5ff6f2df0",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Other Notable Glaciers",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "48786bef-5865-44c2-96a4-4d882437f90f",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Saltoro Glacier: Located near the India-Pakistan border in the Saltoro Massif; feeds the Saltoro River.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cabbe9d5-708a-42b9-8e15-0f9e1a59bf51",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Rakaposhi Glacier: Located on the lower slopes of the Karakoram Range in Gilgit; its tributaries flow into the Hunza River.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "049e209b-b64d-45ec-845a-8acd281f7072",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Chong Kumdan Glacier: Surrounded by high peaks; feeds the Shyok River.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a412d22c-0f7d-4870-aaf6-b12dfb9cd303",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Key Revision Points",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e1455431-f4b0-4d50-be93-d47257de8305",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "The three main rivers of Jammu and Kashmir are the Jhelum, Chenab, and Indus.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d757135d-d84c-4c32-96a9-a3b8aff78fa4",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "The Indus River originates near Mansarovar Lake in Tibet.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "220762a7-da02-436a-b7d5-5ad905a39376",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "The Jhelum River originates from the Verinag spring and was anciently known as Vitasta (Veth in Kashmiri).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d6819c64-75e6-4c7b-aefd-db7f43688655",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "The Jhelum has a navigable length of 177 km within the Kashmir Valley.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0ed5342f-b5fd-430d-830f-825a5f0d5335",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "The Chenab River is formed by the confluence of the Chandra and Bhaga streams (Chandrabhaga).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "942dbf63-e534-4cb1-86a9-1b7c47cb4a2d",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "The Ravi River rises at Basoli and enters the Punjab plains near Madhopur.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e86a34d7-b214-4c09-8d9d-478cadd93fb8",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "The Tawi River flows around Jammu city, draining the outer hill region.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "94dc1b84-357c-4d0d-913e-174199a197da",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "The Zanskar River is formed by the confluence of the Doda and Tsarap rivers.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "93887c80-04cd-48cb-bb27-f6b824397350",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "The Shyok River originates from the Rimo Glacier and is a major tributary of the Indus.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "560527b4-9371-43a9-919c-9230fe930f44",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "The Kishanganga River (also called Neelum) meets the Jhelum north of Muzaffarabad.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "99b56040-e0da-4d62-b241-b3aee26c5f8f",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Wular Lake is the largest freshwater lake in India, measuring 16 km by 9.6 km.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "afa881fd-756d-4a81-bc17-e476c76e6263",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Dal Lake is famous for its floating gardens and surrounding Mughal gardens.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6fbcf5d1-ee38-411a-8205-6e6d7ec49f39",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Nagin Lake is connected to Dal Lake and freezes during winter.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d0f8d275-efbe-4a33-b887-312d5007c3d7",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Anchar Lake is a swampy lake through which the Sind Nallah flows.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1dd3f8bb-f36b-4705-91fe-0583d67c238e",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Mansar Lake near Jammu is associated with Sheshnag and Lake Mansarovar legends.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1152fc70-98d4-41a7-a6c7-0241fd9ccccf",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Kounsarnag (Vishno Pad) Lake is situated at 13,124 ft and is the source of the Vishav River.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cb96125d-3bbf-4656-8f55-d6d29bc1578b",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Gangabal Lake is located at 11,713 ft on the peak of Harmukh Mountain.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9e6204e1-f835-49c1-bb7f-448dfc03d6c0",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Siachen Glacier is 72 km long and is the largest glacier outside the polar regions.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1f128024-b886-4686-aa44-e8344e1d8496",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "The Biafo, Baltoro, and Hispar glaciers all feed the Shigar River, which drains into the Indus.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "76e49ede-228d-4cb3-b54d-d56819ff58f2",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "The Nubra Glacier feeds the Nubra River, which is a tributary of the Shyok River.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    }
  ]
}

{
  "chapterId": "chap_ac6852b7",
  "title": "Physiography",
  "elements": [
    {
      "id": "0a35451e-3a11-48aa-ab41-f42a59c02bc5",
      "type": "HEADING_1",
      "text": "Physiography of Jammu and Kashmir",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7ad1dc8e-5615-4d54-b5e5-7da55433c3c4",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Jammu and Kashmir is home to several valleys such as the Kashmir Valley, Tawi Valley, Chenab Valley, Poonch Valley, Sind Valley and Lidder Valley. The main Kashmir Valley is about 100 km wide and covers an area of about 15,520.3 km². The Himalayas divide the Kashmir Valley from Ladakh, while the Pir Panjal Range, which encloses the valley from the west and south, separates it from the Great Plains of Northern India.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a93d6e52-7b7e-4600-bedd-a05e41af6ecf",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Along the north-eastern flank of the valley runs the main range of the Himalayas. This densely settled and beautiful valley has an average height of 1,850 m above sea level, while the surrounding Pir Panjal Range has an average elevation of about 5,000 m.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "19bd39ea-bf91-4e51-84d5-a10cf5776afc",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Physiographic Zones",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d2364762-3b80-4545-b4d2-ed6ad1c6f3ca",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The territory of the state is divided into seven physiographic zones, closely associated with the structural components of the Western Himalayas:",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "419b4ed0-b403-4d03-b43a-9be1d713f97c",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "1. Plains",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e48a2bdb-bc2f-4d38-9a64-591b80299b62",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The plains of the Jammu region are characterised by interlocking sandy alluvial fans deposited during the Pleistocene Age by streams flowing from the foothills. They also contain a much-dissected pediment, or eroded bedrock surface, covered by loams and loess (fine deposits of silt).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8fa54a4a-fd1f-43a1-b21a-f2dc2323359e",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "2. Foothills",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5a4b40c0-a884-4316-912f-ca259b15acce",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Rising from about 2,002 to 7,002 ft, the foothills form the outer and inner zones.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b5af8121-3ed1-44b0-927d-797eae558a39",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "3. Lesser Himalayas",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "56433773-1b93-4752-87c1-b8f3a10a5683",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Lesser Himalayas are composed of Permo-Carboniferous volcanic rocks, granite, gneisses, quartz and slates. The Pir Panjal constitutes the first mountain rampart comprising the westernmost part of the Lesser Himalayas.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cb09f2d4-ec95-4182-be58-e4abaec8ea54",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "4. Greater Himalayas",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cef5e5dd-8695-489e-b386-8744516e925c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Greater Himalayas contain ranges reaching more than 20,013 ft (6,100 m) in altitude. These ranges act as a climatic divide and stop the cold wind coming from Central Asia.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6bf74235-6b8b-485c-9b96-ed6744070aff",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "5. Valley of Kashmir",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b9cf43d8-b140-4de4-8f2f-a418b875fb22",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Between the Pir Panjal and the western end of the Great Himalayan ranges lies a deep asymmetric basin called the Valley of Kashmir.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ed50ae64-9fa8-4830-bea5-f73fd1fd89e4",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "6. Upper Indus Valley",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7e722ebe-34d1-4798-aa9f-f962a191b914",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The valley of the Upper Indus River follows the geological strike, or structural trend, westwards from the Tibetan border to a point in the Pakistani sector, where it rounds the great mountainous mass of Nanga Parbat to run southwards in deep gorges cut across the strike.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f5d305ac-d078-4010-9320-23f5ef0fc025",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "In its upper reaches, gravel terraces flank the river. Each tributary builds an alluvial fan in the main valley. The town of Leh stands on such a fan, at about 11,483 ft (3,500 m) above sea level.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fefb4545-7029-4ba7-9538-00d6e4c0696a",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "7. Karakoram Range",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7ceb149e-398b-4495-8e6e-64d544250503",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The great granite-gneiss massifs of the Karakoram Range, which straddle the Indian and Pakistani sectors of Kashmir, contain some of the world's highest peaks.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "62d21d9a-f5c8-45e8-8d4b-0888a074a70a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "These include K2 on the Pakistani side and one of the peaks in the Chinese-administered enclaves. K2 has an elevation of about 28,251 ft (8,611 m). At least 30 other peaks exceed 24,000 ft (7,300 m).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b81b3a4f-020d-48ee-b66c-515bc683d45d",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "IMPORTANT",
      "title": "Roof of the World",
      "content": "The Karakoram Range, which is still heavily glaciated, rises starkly from dry, desolate plateaus characterised by extreme temperature variations and shattered rock debris. The Karakoram, along with other areas in and around the Himalayan region, is often called the 'Roof of the World'."
    },
    {
      "id": "d0d70791-4839-4948-af1b-84ef3b95f15f",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Climate of Jammu and Kashmir",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d9a252ff-1843-4910-ae6d-0825993d2324",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Climate exerts a profound influence on the inhabitants of the region. Their social, cultural, economic and other aspects of life are directly or indirectly governed by climate.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "25b85870-deaa-4c18-9fcd-31bdaf7ea939",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The climate of the state ranges from the burning and scorching heat of the plains of Jammu Division to the snow-capped heights of Gulmarg, and further to the snow-covered peak of Mount Godwin Austin (K2) in Ladakh, rising to about 28,264 ft above sea level, the second-highest peak in the world.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a70be879-dd15-49b0-a0d7-28cad81bdda3",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "All these represent three different climatic zones. From the alpine Ladakh region to the sub-tropical Jammu region, the extreme variations in climate in Jammu and Kashmir are due to its location and topography. The sheltered Valley of Kashmir, however, exhibits an exception to its peripheral regions.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fe1948be-1020-4e28-b185-be58cba3a15f",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Three Broad Climatic Regions",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a109a82c-1e32-4046-b5a6-4487d2bc506a",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "• Cold and desert areas of Ladakh\n• Temperate Kashmir Valley\n• Humid sub-tropical region of Jammu",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c15487e5-a59b-4e7c-91ba-7909e3ddd083",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The temperature in the region varies spatially. Leh is the coldest, with an average temperature of about −28°C, while Jammu is the hottest. Mean monthly temperature is lowest in January and highest in July, except in Jammu, where the highest temperature is experienced in June. At Jammu, Kargil and Leh are other stations where January temperatures can fall considerably below the average. At Drass, the January temperature may fall to about −17°C.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c02d8d67-399e-4b77-81ce-8df23f1684a5",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Four Climatic Units",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e37104f7-c89e-4088-bbcd-2dd20deb3b11",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "1. The windward region (Jammu region)\n2. The leeward (Ladakh region)\n3. The high-altitude Kashmir (Himadri, Pir Panjal)\n4. The Kashmir Valley",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d18c1ee8-ff04-410c-af2d-b2bb4f8a78ac",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Seasons of the Valley",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6ad47225-9ad6-43e2-a7db-acb150d57d5c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The climate of the Valley of Kashmir has its own peculiarities. The seasons are marked by sudden changes and the climate can be divided into six seasons of two months each.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e2089cf4-f5d6-4d9c-8fd0-581aad019478",
      "type": "TABLE",
      "title": "Six Seasons of the Kashmir Valley",
      "headers": [
        "Season",
        "Period",
        "Local Term"
      ],
      "rows": [
        [
          "Spring",
          "16th March to 15th May",
          "Sont"
        ],
        [
          "Summer",
          "16th May to 15th July",
          "Rethol (Grishm)"
        ],
        [
          "Rainy",
          "16th July to 15th September",
          "Waharat"
        ],
        [
          "Autumn",
          "16th September to 15th November",
          "Harud"
        ],
        [
          "Winter",
          "16th November to 15th January",
          "Wandah"
        ],
        [
          "Ice Cold",
          "16th January to 16th March",
          "Shishir"
        ]
      ],
      "hasHeaderRow": true
    },
    {
      "id": "04aec990-4d24-442b-b409-2adad4f3f4a1",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The above-mentioned climatic division does not apply only to the Kashmir Valley but also to parts of Jammu which, like Kashmir Valley, are subject to snowfall and a severe winter. Many parts of the Ladakh region are also subjected to heavy snowfall, while others experience severe dry cold. There is such heavy snowfall on the way to Ladakh from the valley that it remains cut off by road for about 5–6 months every year.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3736aa7d-cf3e-41e9-b9cb-619fa605397c",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Mountains and Their Passes",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ecef85b9-7067-490d-b5a4-c752b1a74b81",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Kashmir Valley is enclosed by high mountain chains on all sides, except for certain passes and a narrow gorge at Baramulla. There are Shiwalik hills towards the south and very lofty mountains in the north, the peaks of which are always covered with snow. There are volcanic mountains too in the state.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8aec0717-111a-47f9-b63e-64661153566e",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Karakoram and Kunlun",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "86b2d988-9c2e-43ac-9f38-4b9a3cf79466",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Both these mountain ranges lie to the north and north-east of the state and separate it from Russia, Turkistan and Tibet. In the north-west, the Hindukush Range continues towards the Karakoram ranges, where K2, the second-highest peak of the world, is situated. Two lofty peaks of Gasherbrum (8,080 m) and Masherbrum (7,821 m) also lie here.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7d8d8d89-e63d-491c-83b6-9fa457b8dba3",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Passes of Karakoram & Kunlun",
      "content": "People of Ladakh pass through Karakoram Pass (5,352 m) while going to Chinese Turkistan and Khotan. One can reach Tibet from Ladakh via Khardung La Pass (5,359 m) and Chang La Pass (5,360 m)."
    },
    {
      "id": "9f590712-14ae-489f-8b91-f34b60cdf3f1",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Zanskar",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1a79a584-6a42-4cc4-bc99-882523b51fab",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "It is about 600 m above sea level and separates the Indus Valley from the Valley of Kashmir. It prevents south-west coastal winds from reaching Kashmir. The Ladakh region terminates at Zoji La Pass (3,529 m), from where begins the Valley of Kashmir. Poa Pass (5,716 m) is also a famous pass in this range.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "357d646a-2139-4cb8-a9ba-19746a8a2c1c",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Nanga Parbat",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9354ab4c-03d4-4c47-aa7a-4facadc46bd7",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "This range spreads in Gilgit. Its height is 8,126 m above sea level and it is utterly devoid of vegetation. It was conquered by Italian mountaineers in 1954. This area is now under the unlawful possession of Pakistan.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fb9b8aa5-66f4-412c-bd4c-4a927a175ae7",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Nun Kun",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7488e0aa-5268-4f9c-aff3-b64420e16cf3",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Nun Kun lies between the Ladakh and Kashmir border. It is 7,055.1 m above sea level. To its south-east is situated Kullu, and to its north-west is situated Kargil tehsil of Ladakh. One has to pass through Bawalocha Pass (4,891 m) to reach Leh (Ladakh) from Kullu.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "bf44d842-5c8f-4773-a577-f65e2efebe40",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Burzil",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e1f1b8e6-1768-4a71-98d2-42465337834c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Burzil range bifurcates Kashmir and Ladakh, on which Burzil Pass is situated at a height of about 3,200 m above sea level.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9afd8447-f75d-40a1-a702-60862611c29d",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Amarnath",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f69461e1-683b-42bc-a309-a600d5dad95c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Amarnath Mountain is famous for its holy Amarnath Cave, at a height of 5,372 m above sea level. Pilgrims have to pass through Mahagunas Pass (4,475 m) on their way to Shri Amarnathji. Gwasharan (5,450 m) is situated in the Lidder Valley towards Pahalgam; on it lies the famous Kolahai Glacier. Sheshnag Mountain also spreads in this valley. It is called Sheshnag because its peaks resemble the heads of seven snakes.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5f7afbb6-35fb-4733-ae64-13bee087cf41",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Toshmaidan",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f251ebc2-eeb6-481d-91b2-8911698a0d5c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Toshmaidan (4,270 m) and Kajinag (3,700 m) mountains lie in the inner Himalayas. They remain covered with snow throughout the year, but during summer, when the snow melts, the water flows down into the Jhelum River.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9a11b994-5894-45d4-830f-e8f9efe0909e",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Afarwat",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fa60b94e-4bb1-492b-b9cb-f9a0707839ab",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "This mountain spreads through the Gulmarg Valley. The famous spring Alpathar lies on its peak, from which Nullah Nagal comes out and flows down into Wular Lake.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5c6e4cfe-df8a-4668-8ab9-4beccdb9b1e7",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Pir Panjal",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ae80b6ca-af8a-4624-8baf-42682de5c849",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Pir Panjal Range separates the Kashmir Valley from the outer Himalayas. It is about 2,621 km in length and 50 km in breadth. The famous Banihal Pass (2,832 m) lies in the form of a tunnel on its peak. It remains covered with snow during winter, making it impassable.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4c8467f1-4a74-41c6-818e-aabd808dd91b",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "IMPORTANT",
      "title": "Jawahar Tunnel",
      "content": "At a height of about 2,200 m above sea level, a new tunnel, namely the Jawahar Tunnel, has been constructed. The tunnel is 2,825 m long and was opened for traffic on 22 December 1956."
    },
    {
      "id": "2375750c-2909-4423-a8e6-0bc88c78774a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "On the other end of this range lie Baramulla Pass (1,582 m) and Hajipir Pass (2,750 m). Hajipir joins Poonch and Uri. During the 1965 Indo-Pak War, the Indian Army occupied this pass. Later, it was handed over to Pakistan.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "bc651a65-f5e5-4206-99ed-36569c8ffe8f",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Shiwalik",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "791625d7-f77a-4956-994d-ba729ddbb03f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "These hills extend from the north of the outer plains to the middle mountains of the state, reaching heights varying from about 600 m to 1,500 m above sea level.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "44de60b9-b25c-45ef-8bc7-2ad00cf38d77",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Volcanic Peaks",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6fa4fdc8-030b-4381-96ac-3f0e2cfd09fd",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "One volcanic peak, Soyamji (1,860 m), is situated in North Machhipura (Handwara), while the other, Kharewa Peak, lies in tehsil Pahalgam and is now dead or extinct. However, continued eruption of lava for about thirteen months during 1934 has now left the former in a dormant state. There is a temple on this peak and many sulphur springs are found at the foot of the hill.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4c44c25e-b1f4-4e53-87c6-af8cb87421a3",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "IMPORTANT",
      "title": "Earthquakes in Kashmir",
      "content": "These volcanic mountains are considered a cause of earthquakes in Kashmir. So far, twelve devastating earthquakes have occurred in Kashmir. Of these, the earthquake of 1885 was the most devastating. Hundreds of houses collapsed, thousands of people died, and cracks appeared in the Earth as a result of this earthquake."
    },
    {
      "id": "eac01299-fde7-46d5-ae8f-d46d43130cd5",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Revision",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6e353577-2110-4a1c-9891-6ae388bf31cc",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "• Kashmir Valley: About 100 km wide and 15,520.3 km² in area.\n• Pir Panjal Range: Separates Kashmir Valley from the Great Plains of Northern India.\n• Average Elevations: Kashmir Valley is ~1,850 m; Pir Panjal is ~5,000 m.\n• Seven Physiographic Zones: Plains, Foothills, Lesser Himalayas, Greater Himalayas, Valley of Kashmir, Upper Indus Valley, and Karakoram Range.\n• Karakoram Range: Often called the 'Roof of the World'; contains K2 (8,611 m).\n• Three Climatic Regions: Cold\/desert Ladakh, temperate Kashmir Valley, and humid sub-tropical Jammu.\n• Six Seasons of Kashmir: Sont (Spring), Rethol\/Grishm (Summer), Waharat (Rainy), Harud (Autumn), Wandah (Winter), and Shishir (Ice Cold).\n• Key Passes: Karakoram Pass (5,352 m), Khardung La (5,359 m), Chang La (5,360 m), Zoji La (3,529 m), Bawalocha Pass (4,891 m), Burzil Pass (~3,200 m), Mahagunas Pass (4,475 m), Banihal Pass (2,832 m), Baramulla Pass (1,582 m), and Hajipir Pass (2,750 m).\n• Jawahar Tunnel: 2,825 m long, opened on 22 December 1956.\n• Volcanic Peaks: Soyamji (1,860 m, dormant since 1934 eruption) and Kharewa Peak (extinct).\n• 1885 Earthquake: The most devastating of the twelve recorded earthquakes in Kashmir.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    }
  ]
}

{
  "chapterId": "chap_c516e365",
  "title": "History Of Kashmir",
  "elements": [
    {
      "id": "1d7a458f-8087-4759-9a5b-7d4fd4c2d476",
      "type": "HEADING_1",
      "text": "CHAPTER 2: HISTORY OF KASHMIR",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0b4cce93-3d8f-446e-93c6-133be366ba51",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "INTRODUCTION AND SOURCES OF KASHMIR HISTORY",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "aa885fb9-ea92-4e54-8b63-28d721f02a07",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "There are several ways of finding out about the past of Kashmir. Kashmiris, who distinguished themselves in many branches of Sanskrit learning, were also good historians and left almost continuous written records of the history of the valley.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1a087a64-81c9-48b7-87ed-6c53447d274b",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Primary Historical Sources",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ff7def18-3d77-4feb-870b-f31049b6e6d5",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Written records of history",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "821bd85f-29c9-4502-a60f-be34980530f0",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Archaeological evidence",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "930a13db-e9de-430a-a191-a89e3393fe8b",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Numismatic evidence, especially ancient coins",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9c15540f-4add-42c0-ba1c-c1a2ce9b12a1",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Accounts of foreign travellers who visited Kashmir from time to time",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "22ddd81e-9f5f-467e-aa1d-12ebeb5e728a",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Kalhana and the Rajatarangini",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "138400ef-018d-413e-8b9f-e4c45e4231e2",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Kalhana, a 12th-century poet-historian, wrote the Rajatarangini (AD 1148–1149). He mentioned about eleven earlier chronicles which he had consulted. The Rajatarangini, or the River of Kings, contains valuable political, social, and other information about Kashmir and the rest of India.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cc8580d0-12ce-444c-9c72-17844c0ca6ea",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Nilamapurana is the earliest known text of Kashmir. It contains sacred legends regarding the origin of the valley and describes the rites and worship prescribed by Nila, the Lord of Kashmir Nagas.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9f6ade4a-33c1-4e52-a9b3-939006d63ab8",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Among the texts dealing especially with sacred sites is the Haracharitachintamani of Jayadratha.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b08271bd-8c76-4ce3-8b44-2b3611929356",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Muslim Period Chronicles",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d747987a-f1ff-43a6-ba93-cb3089d22743",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "During the Muslim period, Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin attracted chroniclers and poets to his court and showed great interest in Sanskrit, although Persian was the language of the court. He had the Rajatarangini brought up to date through two famous chroniclers of his reign:",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "661bae87-70bd-4731-b3f4-c987cbc7e6d1",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Jona Raja, who wrote in Sanskrit (his chronicle, Rajavali, deals with the reign of the later Hindu rulers from Jayasimha to Queen Didda)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0582ad3e-e23a-4c87-b67e-c39177755772",
