    {
      "id": "396cb809-7f6c-4b4f-9eb6-2ce61a97943f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "## 8. THE MODERN PERIOD: DOGRA RULE (AD 1846 – 1950)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b7c4b63d-d64f-4ef7-9e44-9edbc555dc87",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### Foundation of the Princely State\nDogra rule over Jammu and Kashmir was established through two historic treaties following the defeat of the Sikh Empire in the First Anglo-Sikh War:",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3d596d5f-a234-4a9a-a825-7790562fdbf1",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "1. **Treaty of Lahore (9 March 1846):** Signed between the young Maharaja Duleep Singh and the British Governor-General Sir Henry Hardinge. The Sikhs ceded Kashmir, Hazara, and the Jalandhar Doab to the British East India Company. The legendary **Kohinoor diamond** was surrendered to the British, and Sir Henry Lawrence was appointed British Resident at Lahore.\n2. **Treaty of Amritsar (16 March 1846):** Often referred to historically as the *\"Sale of Kashmir\"*. The British transferred the territory of Kashmir to **Gulab Singh** of Jammu for **75 Lakh Nanakshahi Rupees**. Gulab Singh formally entered Srinagar on **9th November 1848**, consolidating the territories of Jammu, Kashmir, Ladakh, and Gilgit into a single princely state under British suzerainty.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "430ef94e-9775-4dd6-b1aa-94f138f907c7",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "```\n       [Sikh Cession of Territory] ──────> [Treaty of Lahore (9 March 1846)]\n                                                      │\n                                                      ▼\n       [Sale of Kashmir for 75L]  ──────> [Treaty of Amritsar (16 March 1846)]\n                                                      │\n                                                      ▼\n                                         Dogra Princely State Formed\n```",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6dbfb224-edbd-47c3-a366-3a06d9f84f25",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "---",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2e197f2b-0c86-4c88-9e05-b02867933efa",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### Dogra Monarchs and Administration",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5879a6f7-6e3c-4162-adb6-379dc06d742f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "#### Maharaja Gulab Singh (1846–1856)\n* A stern administrator who restored order across the territory.\n* Disarmed the lawless *Galwan* bandits, suppressed revolts by the Bambas and Khokhas, and established garrisoned outposts along volatile frontiers.\n* Systematically mapped and integrated his conquests, which included Bhimber, Rajouri, Skardu, Ramnagar, Bashohli, Bhaderwah, Kishtwar, Astor, Gilgit, Chitral, Hunza, and Nagar.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "eb44c77c-5855-468b-b5fa-a354fdc5c5b1",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "#### Maharaja Ranbir Singh (1856–1885)\n* **Administrative Divisions:** Divided Jammu into **7 Wazarts** (districts) and Kashmir into **6 Wazarts** to decentralize authority.\n* **Departmental Reorganization:** Restructured the administrative machinery into three distinct branches: **Civil**, **Revenue**, and **Military**.\n* **Judicial Reforms:** Codified the law by introducing the **Ranbir Penal Code (RPC)**. He upgraded the judiciary by establishing the **Adalat-ul-Saddar** (Chief Court) and **Adalat-ul-Aliya** (High Court).\n* **Darbar Move:** Initiated the **Darbar Move** practice, wherein the durbar (government) shifted biannually between Jammu (winter capital) and Srinagar (summer capital).\n* **Infrastructure & Currency:** Introduced a modern postal system, laid telegraph lines, and issued the state's first paper currency, known as the **'Srikar'**.\n* **Architecture:** Planned and built **R.S. Pura** (originally called *Nawa Shahar*), J&K's first planned town. He constructed the **Ranbireshwara Temple** (the largest Shiva temple in North India) and completed the **Raghunath Temple** complex in Jammu in 1857.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "193e32bc-06ba-4672-a41f-c6e5b3dd86d6",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "#### Maharaja Pratap Singh (1885–1925)\n* **Abolition of Begar:** Completely abolished the centuries-old **Begar System** (forced labor).\n* **Connectivity & Roads:** Completed the construction of the **Banihal Road** in 1915 (engineered by Laxman Joo Tickoo; opened to the public in 1922) and the **Jhelum Valley Road**, connecting the valley to the plains.\n* **First Railway Line:** Inaugurated the **Sialkot-Jammu Railway Line**, marking the state’s entry into the railway era.\n* **Hydroelectric Power:** Commissioned J&K’s first hydroelectric station, the **Mohra Hydroelectric Project** (1907), built on the Jhelum river near Uri.\n* **Silk Industry:** Established modern silk factories in Srinagar (1907) and Jammu (1909), with the Jammu Silk Factory winning a gold medal at an international exhibition.\n* **Education:** Founded **Sri Pratap (SP) College** in Srinagar (1905) and **Prince of Wales College** (now GGM Science College) in Jammu (1905).\n* **Irrigation Canals:** Engineered major irrigation canals, including the **Ranbir Canal**, **Pratap Canal**, **Ujh Canal**, and the **Upper Jhelum Canal**.\n* **Forestry & Print Media:** Established the State Forestry Department in 1891 and opened a Forestry School in Bandipora. The state's first Urdu newspaper, **Ranbir**, was launched on 24 June 1924 by Mulk Raj Saraf.\n* **Tourism:** The construction of the iconic wooden **houseboats** in Kashmir began during his reign.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4051e267-0130-41a9-a841-c30056fdcfcd",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "#### Maharaja Hari Singh (1925–1947)\n* **The Father of Renaissance:** Known for his progressive outlook and reformist policies in education and social welfare.\n* **State Subject Law (1927):** Enacted the **State Subject Law** on 27 June 1927, which restricted the right to own land and hold state employment to native residents (*Mulkis*).\n* **Social Reforms:** Passed the **Infant Marriage Prevention Regulations (1928)** and the **Widow Re-marriage and Property Act (1932)**.\n* **Praja Sabha (1934):** Established J&K's first legislative assembly, the **Praja Sabha**, which had 75 members.\n* **Education & Diplomacy:** Enacted the **Primary Education Act**, making primary education free and compulsory. He also represented the Indian Princely States at the **First Round Table Conference** in London (1930).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8c1140c3-1ebf-4686-bd05-49cbebc4039c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "---",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2e46d0c7-504e-4f9e-a5a4-d85dbb58166b",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### Treaties, Accords & Modern Events (1932–1952)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5e0a7753-e348-41f8-94c1-873805b7bfd2",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "#### Rise of Local Political Parties\n* **All J&K Muslim Conference (1932):** Founded under the leadership of **Chaudhary Ghulam Abbas** and **Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah** to advocate for representation in state services.\n* **National Conference (1939):** In 1939, the Muslim Conference was converted into the **All J&K National Conference** to make the movement secular and inclusive.\n* **J&K Bank:** Established on **1st October 1938** under a royal charter issued by Maharaja Hari Singh, with its headquarters in Srinagar.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a5df1f03-47ad-492d-be0b-bbbda0a7fe23",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "#### Partition, Tribal Invasion, and Accession (1947)\n* **Tribal Attack (22 October 1947):** Pakistan-backed tribal raiders (*Lashkars*) invaded the state. Maharaja Hari Singh dispatched **Brigadier Rajinder Singh** with a small force to halt their advance. Brigadier Rajinder Singh successfully destroyed the Uri bridge and held off the invaders at the cost of his life. He was posthumously awarded India's first Maha Vir Chakra and is remembered as the **\"Saviour of Kashmir\"** or **\"Sparrow of Kashmir\"**.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "596478a1-634d-43b5-80e7-c10b9c33321f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "```\n[Tribal Raiders Invade (22 Oct)] ──> [Brig. Rajinder Singh's Defense] ──> [Accession Signed (26 Oct)]\n```",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "da2ae15c-529b-4413-b064-59bad68c8878",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "* **Instrument of Accession (26 October 1947):** Facing imminent military collapse, Maharaja Hari Singh signed the **Instrument of Accession** with the Government of India (represented by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and Governor-General Lord Mountbatten). Under this treaty, Jammu and Kashmir acceded to the Dominion of India. The Union Parliament was granted legislative authority over only three core subjects:\n  1. **Defence**\n  2. **External Affairs**\n  3. **Communications**\n* **Delhi Agreement (1952):** Signed between Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and the Prime Minister of Jammu and Kashmir, Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah. It defined the constitutional relationship between the state of Jammu and Kashmir and the Indian Union, laying the groundwork for Article 370.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dc49d4d6-0b9e-48b7-ad92-cec1b9066911",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "---",

      "id": "c46d7bf4-83a8-4f36-a147-cdc6800472a0",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "## 9. REVISION AND TIMELINE",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,

      "alignment": "LEFT"

    {
      "id": "c1d34aa4-1aa8-4a62-9366-9322b4a4817b",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### Chronological Timeline of Kashmir History",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "129813c8-2afe-4766-ae02-8e47652f33ed",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "```\n  Ancient Era               Medieval Era                 Afghan\/Sikh\/Dogra         Modern Era\n 3000 BC     AD 625       AD 1339     AD 1587            1753         1846         1947       1952\n   │───────────│─────────────│───────────│────────────────│────────────│────────────│──────────│\nBurzahom   Karkota       Shah Miri    Mughals          Afghan\/Sikh   Dogras     Accession   Delhi Accord\n```",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8b494eb0-1a51-40a4-b98b-bae9d379d389",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "| Period \/ Date | Important Ruler \/ Historical Event | Key Historical Significance |\n| :--- | :--- | :--- |\n| **c. 3000 BC** | Neolithic Settlement at **Burzahom** | Early pit-dwellings, stone tools, and red ochre burials. |\n| **3rd Century BC** | Mauryan rule under **Emperor Ashoka** | Founded Pandrethan (old Srinagar) and built temples. |\n| **1st Century AD** | Kushan rule under **Kanishka** | Convened the **Fourth Buddhist Council** at Kundalvan (Harwan). |\n| **AD 625–661** | **Durlabhavardhana** (Karkota Dynasty) | Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang visited the valley. |\n| **AD 724–761** | **Lalitaditya Muktapida** | Built Martand Sun Temple and expanded empire across Northern India. |\n| **AD 855–883** | **Avantivarman** (Utpala Dynasty) | suyya designed flood-control systems; Sopore founded. |\n| **AD 980–1003** | Reign of **Queen Didda** | Resisted Mahmud of Ghazni’s early military incursions. |\n| **AD 1320–1323** | Reign of **Rinchen** (Sultan Sadr-ud-din) | First Buddhist prince to convert to Islam. |\n| **AD 1339** | Coronation of **Shah Mir** | Founded the Shah Miri Dynasty; introduced formal Muslim rule. |\n| **AD 1354–1373** | Reign of **Sultan Shihab-ud-din** | Medieval conqueror; extended territory to Lahore and Kabul. |\n| **AD 1420–1470** | Reign of **Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin** | Golden Age of religious tolerance, crafts, and public works. |\n| **AD 1561–1587** | **Chak Dynasty** rule | Defied early Mughal incursions; patronized Kashmiri music. |\n| **AD 1587** | Annexation by **Emperor Akbar** | Kashmir integrated into the Mughal Empire; revenue reforms. |\n| **AD 1753–1819** | **Afghan (Durrani) Rule** | Despotic governorships; Sher Garhi and Amira Kadal built. |\n| **5 July 1819** | **Battle of Shopian** | Maharaja Ranjit Singh’s forces defeated the Afghans, initiating Sikh Rule. |\n| **AD 1834** | Conquest of **Ladakh** | Dogra General Zorawar Singh integrated Ladakh into the Jammu state. |\n| **9 March 1846** | **Treaty of Lahore** | British took control of Sikh territories, including Kashmir. |\n| **16 March 1846** | **Treaty of Amritsar** | Gulab Singh purchased Kashmir; Dogra Rule established. |\n| **AD 1856–1885** | Reign of **Maharaja Ranbir Singh** | Introduced Ranbir Penal Code, Wazarts, and the Darbar Move. |\n| **AD 1885–1925** | Reign of **Maharaja Pratap Singh** | Abolished Begar; built Mohra power plant, Banihal road, and schools. |\n| **AD 1927** | Enactment of **State Subject Law** | Defined privileges and land rights for native residents (*Mulkis*). |\n| **AD 1934** | Establishment of the **Praja Sabha** | Maharaja Hari Singh established J&K’s first Legislative Assembly. |\n| **22 October 1947** | **Tribal Invasion** | Pakistan-backed tribal raiders invaded; defense of Uri by Brig. Rajinder Singh. |\n| **26 October 1947** | Signing of the **Instrument of Accession** | Maharaja Hari Singh signed the agreement acceding to India. |\n| **AD 1952** | **Delhi Agreement** | Constitutional agreement between Jawaharlal Nehru and Sheikh Abdullah. |",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4fb36058-1ea8-4cc2-9746-567a595ff063",

    },
    {
      "id": "0652c36b-b10e-419a-8252-4c4340520113",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### Key Revision Points",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ccea45e7-a0d7-4d57-bdf7-3bfb4bb728bc",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "1. **The River of Kings:** Written by the 12th-century poet-historian Kalhana, the *Rajatarangini* is a foundational historical chronicle for Kashmir.\n2. **Earliest Recorded Text:** The *Nilamat Purana* contains Kashmir’s earliest geographical details and local myths.\n3. **Neolithic Pit-Dwellers:** Burzahom is famous for its early underground dwellings and polished stone and bone tools.\n4. **Ancient Capitals:** Pandrethan (founded by Ashoka as Puranadhisthana) and Parihaspur (built by Lalitaditya) served as key political centers.\n5. **The Split of Buddhism:** The Fourth Buddhist Council at Kundalvan (Harwan) saw the historic division of Buddhism into the Hinayana and Mahayana sects.\n6. **Suyya’s Engineering:** The engineer Suyya stabilized Kashmir's agricultural economy by desilting the Jhelum and reclaiming farmland.\n7. **Religious Toleration:** Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin (Budshah) is remembered for abolishing Jaziya, patronizing Sanskrit scholars, and introducing Paper Mache.\n8. **Bridges of Srinagar:** Zainakadal was the first wooden bridge constructed over the Jhelum river in Srinagar.\n9. **The Founders of Jammu & Kashmir:** The Treaty of Amritsar (1846) unified the regions of Jammu, Kashmir, Ladakh, and Gilgit under Maharaja Gulab Singh.\n10. **Administrative Reforms:** Maharaja Ranbir Singh codified J&K's laws through the Ranbir Penal Code (RPC) and initiated the Darbar Move.\n11. **Infrastructure Upgrades:** Under Maharaja Pratap Singh, the state built its first major roads (Banihal and Jhelum Valley roads) and the Mohra Hydroelectric Project.\n12. **Democratic Assembly:** The state's first legislative body, the Praja Sabha, was established by Maharaja Hari Singh in 1934.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    }
  ]

      "text": "To find the internal angle $\\theta$ between the hour hand and the minute hand at any given time $h$ (hours) and $m$ (minutes):",

    {
      "id": "3617b113-fc59-463a-af9c-e498594aea2c",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "Definition",
      "content": "Incorrect Clock – A clock that runs faster or slower than standard time. Consequently, its hands coincide at intervals not equal to $65 \\frac{5}{11}$ minutes."
    },
    {
      "id": "e48733aa-0776-4c2c-9e6f-ef2469d2d15d",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "4.1 Key Formulas for Incorrect Clocks",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2dc8d66c-a8a2-41b1-b8e1-6206d3b69dc0",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "If the hands of a clock coincide every $T$ minutes (where $T \\neq 65 \\frac{5}{11}$):",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "34ee8995-ea32-4c49-9aa0-306e883f2951",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "If $T < 65 \\frac{5}{11}$, the clock is gaining time (running fast).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT",
      "spans": [
        {
          "start": 39,
          "end": 51,
          "isBold": true,
          "isItalic": false,
          "isUnderline": false,
          "isStrikethrough": false,
          "textColorHex": "",
          "highlightColorHex": ""
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "50d5c8e7-7f8b-44a3-a119-0afeb0792247",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "If $T > 65 \\frac{5}{11}$, the clock is losing time (running slow).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT",
      "spans": [
        {
          "start": 39,
          "end": 50,
          "isBold": true,
          "isItalic": false,
          "isUnderline": false,
          "isStrikethrough": false,
          "textColorHex": "",
          "highlightColorHex": ""
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "1f22203c-88fe-40dc-a05a-0cbc71b59b7f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "$$\\text{Error (Gain or Loss) in } T \\text{ minutes} = \\left| 65\\frac{5}{11} - T \\right| \\text{ minutes}$$",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1c8fa52e-4426-4bc3-914f-5ffb3207cdc4",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "$$\\text{Total Gain or Loss in } X \\text{ hours} = \\frac{\\left( 65\\frac{5}{11} - T \\right)}{T} \\times (\\text{Total minutes in } X \\text{ hours})$$",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },

    {
      "id": "a1079d59-0310-42da-ad78-d639a081a0da",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "100 years contains 76 ordinary years and 24 leap years.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT",

    {
      "id": "6a9f47ad-456a-4e51-b40a-538776e5dbc4",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Total odd days in 100 years = $(76 \\times 1) + (24 \\times 2) = 76 + 48 = 124$ days.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "67c5dd7d-561e-4cec-9958-1b2fdd7035c7",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Convert to weeks: $\\frac{124}{7} = 17 \\text{ weeks and } 5 \\text{ days}$.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c215b47a-3dfd-4690-b890-3c59f15b7c46",

      "text": "Therefore, 100 years contains 5 odd days.",
      "isBold": false,

      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",

    {
      "id": "a5887b5c-4fa0-4ebd-8974-79ccece5fa3b",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "$$\\text{Odd days in 200 years} = (5 \\times 2) = 10 \\text{ days} = 1 \\text{ week} + 3 \\text{ days} \\implies \\mathbf{3\\text{ odd days}}$$",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,

    {
      "id": "d9a1b505-7a9d-4f28-94e5-788b09b7ea59",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "$$\\text{Odd days in 300 years} = (5 \\times 3) = 15 \\text{ days} = 2 \\text{ weeks} + 1 \\text{ day} \\implies \\mathbf{1\\text{ odd day}}$$",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",

    {
      "id": "1b7de730-bfb3-4c57-8502-681c99bccfdf",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "$$\\text{Odd days in 400 years} = (5 \\times 4 + 1\\text{ [extra day for 400th leap century]}) = 21 \\text{ days} = 3 \\text{ weeks} \\implies \\mathbf{0\\text{ odd days}}$$",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,

{
  "chapterId": "chap_9e49c6f1",
  "title": "Indian History",
  "elements": [
    {
      "id": "80bacf35-5dec-447b-9710-27d7083eb6b4",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "# Indian History",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9273bc31-3105-48d5-9bbd-54971d4c7ddd",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "During the late 16th and 17th centuries, European trading companies competed fiercely with one another in India. By the last quarter of the 18th century, the English had outdone all other competitors and established themselves as the dominant power in India. The British administered India for a period of about two centuries and brought about revolutionary changes in the social, political, and economic life of the country.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4b14b8ef-07b0-47c1-9744-46a4586ddaaa",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "---",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "095adc26-5785-432b-a7e5-8f49593c4d83",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "## 1. The Coming of Europeans",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "03cf2c35-3904-45e2-a863-54a603ddbb6a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### Portuguese\n* **Key Arrival:** The Portuguese voyager **Vasco de Gama** reached Calicut on **17 May 1498**. At that time, Calicut was ruled by a king named **Zamorin**. \n* **Significance:** Vasco de Gama’s voyage was successful in establishing a sea route from Europe to India, allowing trade with the Far East without using the costly and unsafe Silk Road caravan routes of the Middle East and Central Asia.\n* **Early Settlements:** \n  * Established a factory at **Cochin** in **1502**.\n* **Key Administrators:**\n  * **Francisco Almeida:** The first Governor of the Portuguese in India.\n  * **Alfonso d’Albuquerque (1503):** Succeeded Almeida and raised Portuguese power to new heights. He captured **Goa in 1510** from the Ruler of Bijapur.\n* **Territorial Shift:** In **1661**, the Portuguese king gave **Bombay** to Charles II of England as a dowry for marrying his sister.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dc0f4744-b432-4322-a419-552b3c916e2a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### Dutch\n* **Establishment:** The **Dutch East India Company** was formed in **1602**.\n* **Key Settlements:**\n  * Set up their first factory at **Masulipatnam in 1605**.\n  * Other factories were established at Pulicat, Chinsura, Patna, Balasore, Nagapattanam, Cochin, Surat, Karikal, and Kasimbazar.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "bbbdb49b-df85-4c0b-860a-7055dea2f377",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### British\n* **Establishment:** The **British East India Company** was formed in **1599** and was granted a Royal Charter by Queen Elizabeth I in **1600** to trade in the East.\n* **Diplomatic Missions:**\n  * **Captain William Hawkins** stayed in Jahangir’s court from **1609–1611** but failed to get the king's permission to erect a factory at Surat.\n  * **Captain Middleton** succeeded in this effort in **1611**.\n  * **1613:** An imperial farman allowed the Company to set up a permanent factory at Surat.\n  * **Sir Thomas Roe** played an important role in these negotiations.\n* **Key Settlements & Factories:**\n  * **1616:** Established their first factory in the South at **Masulipatnam**.\n  * **1633:** Established their first factory in East India at **Hariharpur, Balasore (Orissa)**.\n  * **1639:** Built **Fort St. George** in Madras, which acted as its headquarters on the Coromandel coast.\n  * **1668:** **Bombay** was made the Company's main settlement on the West coast.\n* **Bengal Expansion & Concessions:**\n  * **1667:** Aurangzeb gave the Company a *farman* to trade in Bengal.\n  * **1690:** A factory was set up at **Sutanuti** village. Sutanuti and nearby villages of Kalikata and Gobindpur grew into the city of Calcutta (now Kolkata).\n  * **1696:** The Company fortified the Calcutta factory into **Fort William**.\n  * **1717:** John Surman obtained a *farman* from Emperor Farrukhsiyar, which gave large concessions to the Company. This farman is called the **'Magna Carta' of the Company**.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "17189b16-dcdb-4146-9f94-e958d5a5c51f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### Danish\n* **Establishment:** The **Danish East India Company** was formed in **1616**.\n* **Key Settlements:** Established settlements at **Serampur (Bengal)** and **Tranquebar (Tamil Nadu)**.\n* **Exit:** They finally sold their settlements to the English in **1845**.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d38abf69-4894-4ecb-943e-b9f4b9ecdf3b",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### French\n* **Establishment:** The **French East India Company** was set up in **1664** at the instance of minister Colbert, during the reign of Louis XIV.\n* **Nature of the Company:** Unlike the English private venture, the French Company was created, financed, and controlled by the State.\n* **Key Settlements:**\n  * Established their first factory at **Surat in 1668** and another at **Masulipatnam in 1669**.\n  * **1673:** The foundation of **Pondicherry** was laid, which afterwards became its capital.\n  * Developed a factory in **Chandernagar**.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2850bac8-ac7b-4a72-8aaa-20bb3ea4b1ca",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "---",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9e0fcc25-f9b0-4b0c-a321-917853e632ee",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### Comparative Summary: European Powers in India",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "087286b2-19bf-4d26-8f4e-ca78a0b0f760",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "| European Power | Year of Company Formation | First Factory Location (Year) | Key Headquarters\/Settlements | Exit\/Transition |\n| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |\n| **Portuguese** | - | Cochin (1502) | Goa (Captured 1510), Bombay | Gave Bombay to England as dowry in 1661 |\n| **Dutch** | 1602 | Masulipatnam (1605) | Pulicat, Chinsura, Nagapattanam | Gradually eclipsed by the British |\n| **British** | 1599 | Surat (1613) | Madras (Fort St. George), Bombay, Calcutta (Fort William) | Became dominant colonial rulers |\n| **Danish** | 1616 | Serampur (Bengal) | Serampur, Tranquebar | Sold settlements to English in 1845 |\n| **French** | 1664 | Surat (1668) | Pondicherry (1673), Chandernagar | Eclipsed by the British |",
      "isBold": false,

    {
      "id": "1ff8b23b-fb84-4f90-b230-c1b210d41829",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "## 2. The British Conquest of Bengal",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d9fa51ba-a4e0-481a-9d8d-05b1bc94ff5a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### Rulers of Bengal\n1. **Murshid Quli Khan (1717–1727):** Made Bengal virtually independent of the Mughal Empire.\n2. **Shuja-ud-Daula:** Succeeded Murshid Quli Khan and ruled for 12 years.\n3. **Alivardi Khan:** Ruled Bengal after Shuja-ud-Daula's death until **1756**. Under these three rulers, Bengal enjoyed a long reign of peace and orderly administration.\n4. **Siraj-ud-Daula:** Grandson and successor of Alivardi Khan.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,

      "text": "```\n[1757] Battle of Plassey ──> [1764] Battle of Buxar ──> [1765] Treaty of Allahabad (Dual Government)\n```",

    {
      "id": "53b8f84a-5725-493d-a390-11e84be66c29",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "#### A. Battle of Plassey (1757)\nThe British constantly increased their power by taking advantage of corrupt officers in Bengal.\n* **The Conflict:** Fought in **1757** between the British and Siraj-ud-Daula.\n* **The Betrayal:** A major part of the Nawab's army, led by **Mir Jafar** and **Rai Durlabh**, did not take part in the battle.\n* **Outcome:** The Nawab was defeated and killed.\n* **Political Significance:**\n  * Regarded as the starting point of British Rule in India.\n  * Mir Jafar was made the next Nawab of Bengal.\n  * The British East India Company was granted the undisputed right to free trade in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa, and received the **Zamindari of 24 Parganas**.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6463c8c2-5812-463d-81d9-30ad0cd5ff13",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "#### B. Battle of Buxar (1764)\n* **Cause:** Mir Qasim (successor of Mir Jafar) revolted against the British because they were misusing the *dastaks* (free duty passes).\n* **The Combatants:**\n  * **British Forces:** Led by **Major Munro**.\n  * **Triple Alliance:** Nawab Mir Qasim of Bengal, Nawab Siraj-ud-Daula of Awadh\\*, and Mughal Emperor Shah Alam.\n  \n  *\\*Note: While the source text lists \"Nawab Siraj-ud-Daula of Awadh,\" historical accounts recognize the Nawab of Awadh during this battle as Shuja-ud-Daula.*",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "92edffd3-916c-46f3-9a9e-5d53cf6f65c7",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "* **Outcome:** The Triple Alliance was defeated by the British.\n* **Significance:** \n  * More decisive than the Battle of Plassey because the British defeated not only the Nawab of Bengal but also the Emperor of India.\n  * Made the English a great power in North India and serious contenders for supremacy over the entire country.\n  * Placed the Afghans and Marathas as their remaining rivals for the Empire of Hindustan.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "071e5803-ca69-40dd-863b-01954a68a691",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "#### C. Treaty of Allahabad (August 1765)\nFollowing the Battle of Buxar, the Treaty of Allahabad was concluded:\n* **Diwani Rights:** The English obtained the *Diwani* (the right to collect revenue) of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa, becoming the virtual masters of these territories.\n* **Imperial Captivity:** The Mughal Emperor became a virtual prisoner of the Company at Allahabad.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dfd9a3b5-50d4-4fea-aeba-af8dfaa4155c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "#### D. The Dual Government of Bengal\nThe Treaty of Allahabad introduced the system of **Dual Government** in Bengal:\n* **The Company:** Acquired the real power and revenue control (Diwani).\n* **The Nawab of Bengal:** Retained the responsibility of administration without actual power.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ad76100e-adf3-41d2-a9bb-f6523c8aa124",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "---",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,

      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "19eacaad-be64-41ce-8d55-b548f109b1d8",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "## 3. Governor-Generals of India",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "80fe6305-bb32-4383-9cc4-12dd17d99786",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### Warren Hastings (1772–1785)\n* **Administrative Reforms:** \n  * Brought the Dual Government of Bengal to an end via the **Regulating Act, 1773**.\n  * Deprived *zamindars* of their judicial powers.\n  * Established Civil and Criminal courts.\n  * Made the maintenance of records compulsory.\n* **Key Wars & Treaties:**\n  * **First Anglo-Maratha War (1776–82):** Ended with the **Treaty of Salbai (1782)**.\n  * **Second Anglo-Mysore War (1780–84):** Ended with the **Treaty of Mangalore (1784)**.\n* **Cultural Contributions:**\n  * As a great patron of oriental learning, he co-founded the **Asiatic Society of Bengal** with William Jones in **1784**.\n  * Wrote the introduction to the first English translation of *'The Gita'* by Charles Wilkins.\n* **Impeachment:** Impeachment proceedings were started against him in England on charges of taking bribes. After a 7-year trial, he was finally acquitted.\n* **Succession:** Sir John MacPherson served as the acting Governor-General from 1785 to 1786.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0569d7b1-ccbf-4e35-9bed-38b091c643ac",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "---",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7a90ee4f-68ad-49f4-8df8-9838c6996659",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### Lord Cornwallis (1786–1793)\n* **Land Revenue:** Introduced the **Permanent Settlement of Bengal** (also known as the *Zamindari System*).\n* **Legal Reforms:** He was the first person to codify laws in India. The **Cornwallis Code** separated revenue administration from the administration of justice.\n* **Police Reforms:** Divided each district into areas of 400 square miles, placing them under a police superintendent assisted by constables.\n* **Civil Services:** Brought the Civil Service into existence in India.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c98b9022-a6c6-4ceb-a18a-040518cd35e2",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "---",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "83e417e0-ba34-4f7f-abdb-debe75da9b9d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### Sir John Shore (1793–1798)\n* Played an important role in the introduction of the **Permanent Settlement** under Cornwallis.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d5edd04e-53f8-4d15-aaf7-7f316ebc1389",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "---",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "796c0de0-50f8-4b7c-a5f5-639f6a0d4441",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### Lord Wellesley (1798–1805)\n* **Subsidiary Alliance:** Adopted the policy of *Subsidiary Alliance*—a system designed to bring Indian rulers under British control and establish British paramountcy.\n* **Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799):** Defeated and killed Tipu Sultan, dismantling the Mysore force.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f6501632-025f-4396-aa20-6031eed48878",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "---",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fe9e8f7e-ace4-412f-800c-28223e66a100",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### George Barlow (1805–1807)\n* Key event: The **Vellore Mutiny (1806)**.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0a0b3d86-f4ba-4839-870d-8427e61e791e",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "---",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4a044000-a166-41d3-b313-08fc0dedfe1b",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### Lord Minto-I (1807–1813)\n* Concluded the **Treaty of Amritsar** with Maharaja Ranjit Singh in **1809**.\n* Passed the **Charter Act of 1813**.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f32af9b7-d31e-4faf-a8ec-743ba67a31c1",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "---",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ed99dd49-192a-4127-a02b-777a8de32847",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### Lord Hastings (1813–1823)\n* **Anglo-Nepal War (1814–16):** Fought during his reign, ending with the **Treaty of Sagauli (1816)**.\n* *Note on Chronology:* The source text duplicates the entry *\"First Burmese War (1824-26), Treaty of vandaboo (1826) & capture of Bharatpur (1826)\"* under both Lord Hastings and Lord Amherst. Officially, these events occurred during Lord Amherst’s tenure.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "87aa35c1-6d70-4ac7-af8e-01cbddcc1144",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "---",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5fe4dcf2-da0a-4b2e-bb39-3fe2b0898389",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### Lord Amherst (1823–1828)\n* Fought the **First Burmese War (1824–26)**, leading to the **Treaty of Vandaboo (1826)** (historically *Yandabo*).\n* Captured **Bharatpur (1826)**.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e50a8dc8-9933-4fa7-a8da-2bec545b7940",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "---",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0d87b21b-7e86-482b-8b6b-318c3100ec9b",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### Lord William Bentinck (1828–1835)\n* **Social Reforms:**\n  * Promulgated the **Prohibition of Sati (1829)**.\n  * Eliminated the menace of **thugs (1830)**.\n  * Suppressed female infanticide and child sacrifice.\n* **Educational Reforms:** Made English the medium of higher education in India following the recommendations of **Macaulay**.\n* **Constitutional Shift:** Passed the **Charter Act of 1833**, which changed his designation from *Governor-General of Bengal* to **Governor-General of India**. He was the first to hold this unified title.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2fabbf4a-4d5b-4b10-8147-29c896f1b0ff",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "---",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8cea43a1-4412-49c7-9ce3-ba3a497c0e95",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### Sir Charles Metcalfe (1835–1836)\n* Abolished all restrictions on the vernacular press, earning him the title **\"Liberator of the Press\"**.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1f86c295-5a59-45d2-bb40-f9f8acc30b55",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "---",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "886f37b2-a464-4cf9-b79e-d12a0a37a789",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### Lord Auckland (1836–1842)\n* Known for the **First Afghan War**, which proved to be a major military disaster for the British.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c0d45492-c747-49a6-a766-d46a0bc573d3",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "---",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "082de4a8-c22d-4abc-8ec3-376753c868b5",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### Lord Ellenborough (1842–1844)\n* Brought an end to the Afghan War.\n* Conducted the War with **Gwalior (1843)**.\n* **Annexation of Sind** in **1843** by Charles Napier.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "625e0f86-c0b0-44be-a171-4964d938312a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "---",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "96267d1e-2cca-4795-8cd7-ab6ea5553a3e",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "### Lord Hardinge-I (1844–1848)\n* Fought the **First Anglo-Sikh War (1845–46)**, which concluded with the **Treaty of Lahore (1846)**.\n* Issued administrative decrees giving preference to English-educated persons in government employment.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,

      "text": "Physical quantities are classified into two major categories based on their dimensional and directional properties:",

      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "2.1 Newton's Laws of Motion",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",

    },
    {
      "id": "e16a9567-d0ac-4ef5-bcb4-7ce57ca865a7",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "First Law (Law of Inertia)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "221b6bf9-ab2f-43c3-aa4e-9b7bdd3e54dd",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Statement: Every body retains its state of rest or of uniform motion in a straight line unless it is compelled to change that state by an external force applied to it.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT",
      "spans": [
        {
          "start": 0,
          "end": 10,
          "isBold": true,
          "isItalic": false,
          "isUnderline": false,
          "isStrikethrough": false,
          "textColorHex": "",
          "highlightColorHex": ""
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "fecbbd09-ed7a-4a9a-8f4a-df2ff78b97cd",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Alternative Names: This law is also known as the Law of Inertia or the Law of Galileo.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT",
      "spans": [
        {
          "start": 0,
          "end": 18,
          "isBold": true,
          "isItalic": false,
          "isUnderline": false,
          "isStrikethrough": false,
          "textColorHex": "",
          "highlightColorHex": ""
        },
        {
          "start": 49,
          "end": 63,
          "isBold": true,
          "isItalic": false,
          "isUnderline": false,
          "isStrikethrough": false,
          "textColorHex": "",
          "highlightColorHex": ""
        },
        {
          "start": 71,
          "end": 85,
          "isBold": true,
          "isItalic": false,
          "isUnderline": false,
          "isStrikethrough": false,
          "textColorHex": "",
          "highlightColorHex": ""
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "711b1ce7-1732-4f99-b158-5e672d9c7296",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Significance: Newton's First Law provides the qualitative definition of inertia.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT",
      "spans": [
        {
          "start": 0,

          "isBold": true,
          "isItalic": false,
          "isUnderline": false,
          "isStrikethrough": false,
          "textColorHex": "",
          "highlightColorHex": ""
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "468684a4-04a4-45b6-a2e5-d49fe9d3ad7a",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Example: When a moving car stops suddenly, a passenger sitting inside falls forward. This occurs because the feet of the passenger come to rest instantaneously along with the car (due to friction), whereas the upper part of the body tends to remain in motion due to the inertia of motion.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT",
      "spans": [

          "isItalic": false,
          "isUnderline": false,
          "isStrikethrough": false,
          "textColorHex": "",
          "highlightColorHex": ""
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "9e6eeb99-fe1e-4f86-b749-4c86185e53a4",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Second Law (Force and Acceleration)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "59c2ee8c-72af-45cd-b708-dcec6578ef38",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Statement: The net force applied on a body is directly proportional to the rate of change of its linear momentum. Quantitatively, force is equal to the product of the mass of the body and the acceleration produced in it.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT",
      "spans": [
        {
          "start": 0,
          "end": 10,
          "isBold": true,
          "isItalic": false,
          "isUnderline": false,
          "isStrikethrough": false,
          "textColorHex": "",
          "highlightColorHex": ""
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "dee02dd0-fc55-44e9-9db0-77c691f5132a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "$$F = ma$$",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8493aa41-29af-41d5-9277-38da783a8b90",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Example 1 (Catching a Ball): A cricket fielder moves his hands backward while catching a fast-moving cricket ball. By pulling his hands back, the fielder increases the time of contact\/impact, which reduces the rate of change of momentum (impulse), thereby exerting less force on his hands.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT",
      "spans": [
        {
          "start": 0,
          "end": 28,
          "isBold": true,
          "isItalic": false,
          "isUnderline": false,
          "isStrikethrough": false,
          "textColorHex": "",
          "highlightColorHex": ""
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "8b6dabda-78fa-4e09-acfe-dd71d9ff54b6",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Example 2 (Athletic Landings): During athletic meets, high jumpers and long jumpers land on foam cushioning or a heap of sand. This increases the deceleration time upon landing, decreasing the impact force on their bodies to prevent injury.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT",
      "spans": [
        {
          "start": 0,

          "isItalic": false,
          "isUnderline": false,
          "isStrikethrough": false,

          "highlightColorHex": ""
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "fc9709d0-35e4-41bd-8788-e841448c4c8a",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Third Law (Action & Reaction)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e78957fc-d6aa-435f-bf49-2791a1bb7b6d",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Statement: To every action, there is always an equal and opposite reaction. Action and reaction forces act simultaneously on different bodies.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT",
      "spans": [
        {
          "start": 0,
          "end": 10,
          "isBold": true,
          "isItalic": false,
          "isUnderline": false,
          "isStrikethrough": false,
          "textColorHex": "",
          "highlightColorHex": ""
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "ea79b1f3-33b1-49fd-9463-7c1d49c823c0",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Example 1 (Gun Recoil): On firing a bullet from a gun, the bullet is propelled forward (action), and the gunner is pushed in the backward direction with an equal force (reaction).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT",
      "spans": [
        {
          "start": 0,
          "end": 23,
          "isBold": true,
          "isItalic": false,
          "isUnderline": false,
          "isStrikethrough": false,
          "textColorHex": "",
          "highlightColorHex": ""
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "e332ae51-7bfb-4012-bb5e-15f4b0156c8b",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Example 2 (Stepping off a Boat): When a boatman jumps forward from a boat onto the shore, his feet exert a backward force on the boat (action), pushing the boat away, while the boat pushes him forward (reaction).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT",
      "spans": [
        {
          "start": 0,
          "end": 32,
          "isBold": true,
          "isItalic": false,
          "isUnderline": false,
          "isStrikethrough": false,
          "textColorHex": "",
          "highlightColorHex": ""
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "d79a7999-1abd-49b9-9eaf-a32ac402dfec",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Example 3 (Rocket Propulsion): The propulsion of a rocket is based on the principle of action and reaction. High-velocity exhaust gases escape downward (action), generating an upward thrust on the rocket (reaction).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT",
      "spans": [
        {
          "start": 0,

          "isBold": true,
          "isItalic": false,
          "isUnderline": false,

          "highlightColorHex": ""
        }
      ]

    {
      "id": "ac5a1e83-741b-4465-bda4-3aa60beb2c73",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "2.2 Escape Velocity",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "598172c1-a47b-4af8-a35c-a16ee5c0a462",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Definition: The minimum velocity that must be given to a body to enable it to escape permanently from a planet's\/celestial body's gravitational field is called Escape Velocity.",

      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,

      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT",

        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "8d77e093-aa67-4556-bab4-fcd2b20ad7aa",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Mass Independence: The value of escape velocity does not depend on the mass of the escaping body.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT",
      "spans": [

{
  "chapterId": "chap_ad7be688",
  "title": "Time And Work",
  "elements": [
    {
      "id": "a473fdaa-b51b-41c9-b16c-7f4d38689b73",
      "type": "HEADING_1",
      "text": "Chapter 10: Time and Work",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4c379bf7-2f5f-464d-9c57-9270816764df",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Basic Concepts",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f3672251-c63e-4b5f-bed9-b69a7583ffe1",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Work is defined as the total assignment or job to be done, generally counted as 1 unit.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1ec26220-c4f2-44ba-b056-f0d0d2f6bd24",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "A person is assumed to do an equal amount of work each day.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e57d6d4f-4394-4b6d-be71-08e88bcde152",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Proportional Relationships: Work and men are directly proportional; Work and days are directly proportional; Men and days are inversely proportional.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2367c638-a12c-4638-af6e-6041c2fe95eb",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Core Rules",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5cb7ba05-f9e1-45b0-a5f8-14623b9f7104",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "Day-Work Inversion Rule",
      "content": "If a person takes x days to complete a task, their 1-day work is 1\/x. Conversely, doing 1\/x work per day means completing the job in x days."
    },
    {
      "id": "fefe7095-caee-431c-9961-2f4620e64d0c",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "Efficiency and Time Rule",
      "content": "If A is x% more efficient than B, A takes 1\/x times less time than B for the same task."
    },
    {
      "id": "48283843-70fd-429a-8858-5c7f1bbec1be",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Core Formulas",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2b3787cf-3b48-4003-a9e3-66274bc5c786",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Formula 1: Two People Combined Work",
      "content": "If A and B complete a task individually in x and y days, together they take: (x * y) \/ (x + y) days."
    },
    {
      "id": "b80da31f-33b8-48c9-8d12-5321847fde1f",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Formula 2: Three People Combined Work",
      "content": "If A, B, and C complete a task individually in x, y, and z days, together they take: (x  y  z) \/ (xy + yz + z*x) days."
    },
    {
      "id": "55e3a807-a9af-4f50-abae-a69eda5a4e7d",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Formula 3: Leaving Work Mid-way",
      "content": "If A and B take x and y days individually, start together, and A leaves after t days, the remaining time taken by B is: (y \/ x)  (x - t) days. (Note: If B leaves after t days instead, the remaining time taken by A is (x \/ y)  (y - t) days)."
    },
    {
      "id": "2a437c6d-75b3-4ced-aa56-01b75b78c1f4",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Formula 4: Group Work Comparison (MDH Rule)",
      "content": "If M1 persons complete W1 work in d1 days working h1 hours\/day earning R1, and M2 persons complete W2 work in d2 days working h2 hours\/day earning R2: (M1  d1  h1) \/ (W1  R1) = (M2  d2  h2) \/ (W2  R2)."
    },
    {
      "id": "446de325-4c3c-44ec-89d5-48b0d32b98fb",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Formula 5: Efficiency Shift",
      "content": "If A takes x days, and B is y% faster than A, then B completes the work in: (x * 100) \/ (100 + y) days."
    },
    {
      "id": "d06c4e56-3b29-4e15-9cfa-2c66eb8b0985",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Formula 6: Wages Distribution",
      "content": "If A, B, and C complete a job in x, y, and z days and earn ₹ k total, their shares are distributed in the ratio of their 1-day work: (1\/x) : (1\/y) : (1\/z). Note: For two workers taking x and y days, Share of A = (y  k) \/ (x + y) and Share of B = (x  k) \/ (x + y). Wages are directly proportional to daily work done and inversely proportional to the time taken."
    },
    {
      "id": "48312fcc-39e7-40c2-82bd-1e7e8fcfff16",

      "text": "Pipes and Cisterns",

    {
      "id": "fde611ae-bb43-4861-b7fe-6af2fe3ec9c2",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The mathematical principles governing Pipes and Cisterns are identical to those of Time and Work. Instead of people doing work, we have pipes filling or emptying a tank.",

    {
      "id": "35661100-f066-4263-80be-48f2e3ce237a",

      "text": "Inlet Pipe: Fills the tank (Work done is positive).",

    {
      "id": "c7468cc9-eb96-4121-911a-8d25d01b67e9",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 1: Combined Work of Two People",
      "isBold": false,

    {
      "id": "a24f32bd-f650-427f-a714-cb56f5557bfd",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A takes 4 days to complete a work, and B takes 6 days. How long will they take to complete the work together?",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2d47a9e5-7781-42d6-896b-3bfa02423b9c",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution",
      "content": "Using Formula 1:\nTogether they take = (4 * 6) \/ (4 + 6) = 24 \/ 10 = 12 \/ 5 = 2(2\/5) days.\nAnswer: (c) 2(2\/5) days"
    },
    {
      "id": "fdfc12e0-0701-46a5-912d-fd6e8090d76d",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 2: Combined Work of Three Entities",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2a8584a9-2fc0-47f9-9f38-5746943bf91b",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A man, a woman, and a boy together take 3 days to complete a task. If the man alone takes 6 days and the boy alone takes 18 days, how long will the woman take alone?",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "76871fcf-b1f8-43d0-8ddf-0791a6e6b23e",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution",
      "content": "1-day work of the woman = (1\/3) - (1\/6 + 1\/18) = (1\/3) - (3\/18 + 1\/18) = (1\/3) - (4\/18) = (6\/18) - (4\/18) = 2\/18 = 1\/9.\nThus, the woman alone takes 9 days.\nAnswer: (a) 9 days"
    },
    {
      "id": "f402468b-3cd3-48dc-a5e5-27cca1b1f825",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 3: Leaving Work Mid-way",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9cbcbf57-f982-4686-a98a-236b28be5c72",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A takes 15 days and B takes 10 days to complete a work. They start together, but B leaves after 2 days. How long does A take to complete the remaining work?",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "86c73899-061a-4b76-b38c-c18677f00883",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution",
      "content": "Using Formula 3 (with roles reversed since B leaves):\nRemaining time taken by A = (x \/ y)  (y - t) = (15 \/ 10)  (10 - 2) = 1.5 * 8 = 12 days.\nAnswer: (c) 12 days"
    },
    {
      "id": "d849467f-0a6b-477d-8015-139c02607be2",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 4: Group Work Comparison",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f8c119bb-a88e-4dda-9178-1b6322e7ddc1",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "If 15 men take 16 days to complete a work, how many days are required for 24 men to complete the same work?",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ea5b3823-9854-48e0-929d-16a9c22831a1",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution",
      "content": "Using the MDH formula (M1  d1 = M2  d2):\n15  16 = 24  d2\nd2 = (15 * 16) \/ 24 = 240 \/ 24 = 10 days.\nAnswer: (c) 10 days"
    },
    {
      "id": "8acb66e9-40a7-4ae9-8fed-f26797b13505",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 5: Efficiency Comparison",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dfa02bdd-d9e4-47a3-8814-23072c24916e",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "x takes 16 days to complete a work. y is 60% more efficient than x. How many days will y take to complete the same work?",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "11b8dc1f-a6b8-405a-a70f-32c03713c718",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution",
      "content": "Using Formula 5:\nDays taken by y = (16 * 100) \/ (100 + 60) = 1600 \/ 160 = 10 days.\nAnswer: (a) 10 days"
    },
    {
      "id": "2fd47979-86bf-4606-afde-e0ad66d22c9d",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 6: Wages Distribution",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "07c1452d-1665-466b-aaed-a315d0bd1b06",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A, B, and C complete a job in 2, 3, and 4 days respectively. If their total earnings are ₹ 3900, what is the share of B?",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a2b67ebc-61b2-4bee-b982-cb90cd21650c",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution",
      "content": "Ratio of their 1-day work = 1\/2 : 1\/3 : 1\/4 = 6 : 4 : 3 (multiplying by LCM 12).\nSum of ratio terms = 6 + 4 + 3 = 13.\nShare of B = (4 \/ 13)  3900 = 4  300 = ₹ 1200.\nAnswer: (b) ₹ 1200"
    },
    {
      "id": "b01d23ae-30e9-42a0-af24-98cd31c1b5f5",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 7: Alternative Group Work",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "effe3d1e-7662-4ae6-82e9-ba54c14a9c7e",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "If 3 men or 4 women can reap a field in 43 days, how long will 7 men and 5 women take to reap the same field?",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2ba65d9a-1955-4622-b9b1-37d17c985497",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution",
      "content": "3 men = 4 women => 1 man = 4\/3 women.\n7 men + 5 women = 7 * (4\/3) women + 5 women = 28\/3 + 5 = 43\/3 women.\nUsing M1  d1 = M2  d2:\n4 women  43 days = (43\/3) women  d2\nd2 = (4  43  3) \/ 43 = 12 days.\nAnswer: (c) 12 days"
    },
    {
      "id": "4433de47-51ec-41d7-a93b-a7562c0d2fd4",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 8: Pipes Filling a Tank",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e2e2d6cf-49df-4876-94bb-b9d093d89af3",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Pipe A fills a tank in 20 minutes, and Pipe B fills it in 30 minutes. If both pipes are opened together, how long will they take to fill the tank?",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7d098a80-95f1-4392-a56c-8b4faec92ca9",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution",
      "content": "Using the combined work formula:\nTime taken = (20 * 30) \/ (20 + 30) = 600 \/ 50 = 12 minutes.\nAnswer: (b) 12 min"
    },
    {
      "id": "13c9fa4c-3067-4a18-bef1-a0ca165fe359",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 9: Inlet and Outlet Pipes",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b8c20894-c335-4c00-a10f-7e7535c06026",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "An inlet tap fills a tank in 60 minutes (1 hour), while an outlet pipe empties it in 30 minutes.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f4762a79-eb23-4a71-95e5-f80e22c9997d",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution",
      "content": "Net work per minute = 1\/60 - 1\/30 = -1\/60 (negative sign indicates emptying).\nThus, it takes 60 minutes to completely empty the full tank.\nAnswer: (a) 60 min"
    }
  ]
}

      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "In the following question, choose the related word from the given alternatives.\nOptions:\n(a) Down\n(b) Leave\n(c) Attract\n(d) Clear",

    {

      "text": "College is related to student, in the same way as Hospital is related to:\nOptions:\n(a) Doctor\n(b) Nurse\n(c) Medicine\n(d) Patient",

    {

      "text": "Select the answer pair that expresses a relationship most similar to that expressed in the given pair.\nOptions:\n(a) Canada : Ottawa\n(b) Afghanistan : Tehran\n(c) Egypt : Athens\n(d) Iraq : Kabul",

    {
      "id": "fb8a8e06-4dd8-43aa-8631-6875ed1f05ee",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "In letter analogy, letters are generally moved some steps forward or backward, reversed in whole or in sections, or have some common identity between each other. To solve these questions, the candidate must remember the positional value of letters in the English alphabetical order.",
