    {
      "id": "7f15feba-e236-41f3-8a20-7604c1c8e7f6",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Kernel",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3bc66513-79bf-46f8-814c-17edf0a2294f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The core, central component of an operating system that maintains low-level control over system hardware, CPU scheduling, memory management, and system security.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "558c36a1-de14-4d94-85c2-e6c2e19c1a13",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Memory Protection",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f1a17a9e-3cac-4deb-b4f1-db505f8ed9de",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Hardware and software mechanisms that prevent one running process from accessing, modifying, or corrupting the physical memory allocated to another process or the OS kernel.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "810e0c58-dfce-458b-9a89-0612fef4ab82",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Paging",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6d230cc2-fc80-449c-af3c-75bca81c8596",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A non-contiguous memory management scheme where physical memory is divided into fixed-size blocks called frames, and logical memory is divided into equal-sized blocks called pages.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8bddc3d0-f837-4f62-87d1-ffe509bdb752",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Thrashing",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "23713b03-52fa-4f42-a807-dde562153c74",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A state where an operating system spends more time swapping virtual memory pages back and forth between RAM and secondary storage than actually executing instructions.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "091348d1-85fa-42b7-9c18-416a5869222a",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Fragmentation & De-fragmentation",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e51a9867-449b-4d93-87ae-f7a2e1988f71",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Memory allocation issues and their resolution. This includes:",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "36d94e94-bdc6-456c-8ae0-55ed3565217a",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Internal Fragmentation: unused space left inside a fixed-size allocated memory page or block.\nExternal Fragmentation: free memory exists to satisfy a process request, but the available space is split into non-contiguous blocks.\nDe-fragmentation: rearranging stored files and memory blocks to consolidate scattered free space into continuous blocks.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dc12dfc0-3a2f-40cc-b2cb-89250c79527c",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Segmentation Fault",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7983ec83-af6d-493f-af5e-767bd688af9f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A memory violation error raised when a program tries to read or write to an unallocated or restricted memory address.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6ffcd503-80a9-48bb-bc94-fc5561d1cb4d",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Swapping",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a141b42d-b741-4a8c-adbb-80c1f82ebe91",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Moving an entire idle or suspended process out of main memory to secondary storage (swap space) to free up RAM for other active processes.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ee75f11f-73d8-4d1d-babb-168b6d1cd932",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Dynamic Memory Allocation Strategies",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7d2b3a69-231b-4f4d-a3fb-9dbb55fec672",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "COMPARISON",
      "title": "Dynamic Memory Allocation Strategies",
      "nodes": [
        "First Fit",
        "Best Fit",
        "Worst Fit"
      ],
      "rawContent": "Available Memory Blocks: [ 10 MB ]   [ 25 MB ]   [ 15 MB ]\nIncoming Process Size:   12 MB\n\n• First Fit:  Allocates [ 25 MB ]  (First block that fits)\n• Best Fit:   Allocates [ 15 MB ]  (Smallest block that fits, minimizing waste)\n• Worst Fit:  Allocates [ 25 MB ]  (Largest block available)"
    },
    {
      "id": "f6ecc54c-65e7-4cf1-b21d-ba0e1a17124f",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "First Fit",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d51a6702-ce73-4e42-9b46-196e8b53b7b9",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Scans memory from the beginning and allocates the first available block that is large enough to hold the process. It is fast and efficient in execution.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9ef9523e-5a48-49a7-bb28-92f4439da58b",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Best Fit",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "02934849-ac25-4482-89cd-db571b36317d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Searches all available memory blocks and allocates the smallest block that is large enough for the process. This minimizes leftover space within the block, though it can create tiny, unusable free memory holes.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3b10922c-93ad-4689-bfc5-233ef7f2cff9",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Worst Fit",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "54501d51-2fef-4bb8-b64a-f4b30df72127",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Searches all available memory blocks and allocates the largest available block. This leaves behind a large remaining free block, but can quickly fragment memory over time.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    }
  ]
}

{
  "chapterId": "chap_09dc63dc",
  "title": "Articles",
  "elements": [
    {
      "id": "8bc1ac27-0c07-4146-8504-f8513a2ad61a",
      "type": "HEADING_1",
      "text": "ARTICLES",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9f71f414-22f7-40cc-8851-a2348a58a034",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "1. INTRODUCTION TO ARTICLES",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "eab67bfa-271d-4813-a4ae-39b29bebd677",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "What is an Article?",
      "content": "An Article is a word placed before a noun to show whether we are talking about a noun in a general sense, an unspecified sense, or a specific\/particular sense."
    },
    {
      "id": "d75ad9eb-f6f5-4c65-91f8-8b29ff13af39",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "English has three articles: a, an, and the. These are divided into two main categories: Indefinite Articles and Definite Articles.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1738e4d6-6960-4359-8efd-0b2437952931",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "1.1 Indefinite Articles — A \/ An",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "bd130754-1e04-4002-aebc-1d73dc761b29",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A and An are called Indefinite Articles because they refer to a person, place, thing, or idea that is not specific or not previously identified. They are generally used before singular countable nouns.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a5f1221f-6d6b-4ea1-a031-9cb773179734",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "I saw a dog.\nShe bought a book.\nHe is an engineer.\nI need an umbrella.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a6861cd0-0003-4fdc-ad0e-8b9170345585",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "In these examples, we are not talking about a particular dog, book, engineer, or umbrella, but rather any member of that group.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7167cc0a-5d06-49e8-b78e-b2a22398e51a",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "1.2 Definite Article — The",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d813d5d0-d7f5-42ae-83f1-2a2b6eb68c71",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The is called the Definite Article because it refers to a specific or particular noun that the speaker or listener can identify.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "903ec453-0f8a-4b3b-85dd-dc0c6f89ec4f",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Give me the book on the table.\nThe boy standing outside is my brother.\nI saw a dog. The dog was black.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5a450c5e-7c35-4c21-a836-f3024aead366",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "2. THE SOUND RULE: A VS. AN",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "583de321-f0bd-451e-a2d4-e95278b6a98f",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "IMPORTANT",
      "title": "Sound > Spelling",
      "content": "The choice between 'A' and 'An' depends entirely on the sound of the first letter\/syllable of the following word, not simply on whether the word begins with a vowel or consonant letter."
    },
    {
      "id": "d7cab815-6839-418b-8918-b215e43838a5",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "2.1 Use 'An' Before a Vowel Sound",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a8ef2e75-5757-4d44-aa96-05521aaf87ff",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Use 'an' before words beginning with a vowel sound such as \/a\/, \/e\/, \/i\/, \/o\/, or \/u\/.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "bbf98796-e0ed-485d-ae50-5f681138c86b",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "an apple\nan elephant\nan intelligent girl\nan orange\nan umbrella",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "46536868-1f93-4561-96ae-1365cf270141",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "2.2 Use 'A' Before a Consonant Sound",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "927c0c07-1288-4a96-b4b7-3c507672d29f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Use 'a' before a word beginning with a consonant sound.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "15959bc8-34c3-468c-8609-e9c29a9d6365",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "a boy\na book\na nice girl\na computer",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5fc9c120-538a-4e9d-a973-86c7cfce5612",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "2.3 Important Exceptions Based on Pronunciation",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "af0d0520-5515-40ea-aeaa-d484c26d25f8",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Words Starting with Vowel Letters but Consonant Sounds",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2235b31e-cf01-4f9b-91e4-74c5bfaff7c7",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Some words begin with a vowel letter but have an initial consonant sound (such as the \/y\/ sound in 'you' or the \/w\/ sound in 'won'). These words take 'a' instead of 'an'.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "19178242-d681-4daa-8c9b-6d172c0e09f2",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "a university student (pronounced 'you-niversity')\na European\na useful book\na uniform\na one-rupee coin (pronounced with a \/w\/ sound)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cf8e4736-cd3f-4fb7-abd6-98f18eb1976b",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Words Starting with Consonant Letters but Vowel Sounds",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "15b015ba-d7f6-47bc-94f1-e215e61456e5",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Some words begin with a consonant letter but are pronounced with an initial vowel sound (often due to a silent 'h' or the pronunciation of individual letters in abbreviations). These words take 'an' instead of 'a'.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "20d3fa57-7c4c-4fe5-af95-73b00c865d0b",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "an hour (silent 'h')\nan honest man (silent 'h')\nan honour (silent 'h')\nan heir (silent 'h')\nan MP (pronounced 'em-pee')\nan MLA (pronounced 'em-el-ay')\nan FIR (pronounced 'ef-eye-ar')",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2db750a9-1b41-4192-b1f3-0e68b19f800b",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "3. USES OF INDEFINITE ARTICLES (A \/ AN)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "45f2be54-31a3-423e-8bee-fb6a639f6727",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Rule 1: First Mention of a Singular Countable Noun",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "afc24226-1c68-4153-b8cf-f74badb73701",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Use 'a\/an' when a singular countable noun is mentioned for the first time and is not specific. When the same noun is mentioned again, it becomes specific and takes 'the'.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "762ca48f-4ead-494c-b6b2-62d19fd349df",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "First vs. Second Mention Pattern",
      "content": "First\/general mention → A\/An\nSecond\/specific mention → The\nExample: I saw a dog near the road. The dog was barking loudly."
    },
    {
      "id": "1d208066-558b-4839-b473-b901be3a9255",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Rule 2: Before Singular Countable Nouns (Class Representation)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "35c47884-d4bc-45be-aa68-038ba1047f39",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A\/An can be used before a singular countable noun when we are referring to one member of a class. We cannot use a singular countable noun alone without an article in such sentences.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f91da89a-edfd-4314-acb5-c3d0c06b7139",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Correct: He is a teacher. | Incorrect: He is teacher.\nCorrect: She bought a book. | Incorrect: She bought book.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "facf4000-8393-48e2-b729-ac1fd23583d8",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Rule 3: Before Names of Occupations or Professions",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5345681a-ad5f-462b-8cc8-47304a517f19",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "He is a doctor.\nShe is an engineer.\nMy brother is a teacher.\nHe became an officer.\nShe is a lawyer.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "23208447-2d3f-4075-9a3f-07fd155b5efd",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Rule 4: Proper Noun Used as a Common Noun",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4a1873dd-21fd-4903-9d00-75b5c0da825d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A proper noun can sometimes be used as a common noun when it refers to a person who possesses the qualities or characteristics associated with a famous person.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7e27871d-43e9-431a-a94d-8c7f486b462e",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Ritu is a Lata Mangeshkar because she sings beautifully.\nHe is a Newton in mathematics.\nMy neighbour is a Daniel (meaning a wise judge).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a75ec21f-8a52-4a23-b672-f92809e2a7ba",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Rule 5: In Exclamatory Sentences",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c86c13f1-08c1-438a-a698-69092331e411",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Use 'a\/an' after 'What' or 'How' when followed by a singular countable noun.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "95e3cb0e-d692-4625-816e-c0c89e3aba03",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "What a beautiful girl! (Correct) vs. What beautiful girl! (Incorrect)\nWhat an interesting movie! (Correct) vs. What interesting movie! (Incorrect)\nWhat a wonderful idea!\nWhat an amazing experience!",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9d884736-2ae4-4d34-a6e5-9e35c504df81",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Rule 6: Numerical Sense of 'One' and Expressions of Rate",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "21d74bb2-13aa-404b-bc34-7a1929270974",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A\/An can indicate the numerical value of 'one' or mean 'per' in expressions of rate or quantity.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "658bb284-e392-429b-b252-77e24563d549",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "I need a pen. (= one pen)\nHe bought an apple. (= one apple)\n60 kilometres an hour (= per hour)\n₹100 a day (= per day)\ntwice a week\nthree times a month",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5205d80c-5f43-4fcc-9020-5beb53771a68",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "4. USES OF THE DEFINITE ARTICLE (THE)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7cdd8c63-ef47-4e40-b451-0a1afce6a9b2",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Rule 1: Specific or Previously Mentioned Nouns",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ee456cbb-bef2-464b-b5a7-5eb3766aac7e",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Use 'the' when the noun refers to a particular or specific person, place, or thing, or when the situation itself makes it clear which noun is meant.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6f6ae0b9-204b-464b-ae2f-f8e8d5a2bc9b",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Give me the book on the table.\nClose the door. \/ Turn off the fan. (The situation makes it clear which one is meant)\nWhere is the phone?\nThe dress you want is out of stock.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "523673ad-d20e-4d44-865e-e6b6aaa95459",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Rule 2: Singular Noun Representing an Entire Class",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "47255bb6-8242-44b3-a776-4d5225b54881",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The + singular countable noun can represent an entire species or class of things.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "089e9e5d-3bca-4cd6-b1f4-2bc555de6b51",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The cow is economically useful.\nThe lion is a dangerous animal.\nThe lotus is a beautiful flower.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "eb4b3588-23fd-4a45-9484-ce9400e9c2f5",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Rule 3: Noun + Preposition + Noun Construction",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "062650e6-2cbf-4e99-ac81-f57e6d56b59d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "When a noun is made specific by a following phrase (especially starting with 'of'), 'the' is used before the first noun.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ba946636-806a-4d7e-aec8-b6901a3e6daa",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The gold of India is famous.\nThe water of this river is clean.\nThe history of India is fascinating.\nThe Bharat of the Ramayana is an ideal brother.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d5e63e9a-a7b4-4763-a53c-172ae162b189",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "5. USE OF 'THE' WITH GEOGRAPHICAL NAMES",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1317068b-e903-4bef-9ba4-fce48880f4ef",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "5.1 Mountain Ranges vs. Individual Peaks",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "499be620-4966-48e4-a86c-aaaa05b66a50",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Use 'the' before mountain ranges, but omit it before individual mountain peaks.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c414415f-3835-42ca-9f26-d2134bdf11e5",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Mountain Ranges (Use 'The'): the Himalayas, the Alps, the Andes, the Rockies\nIndividual Peaks (Zero Article): Mount Everest, Mount Kilimanjaro, Mount Fuji",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5bd721f6-1c7b-4733-9c02-fde209605f6c",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "5.2 Water Bodies (Rivers, Seas, Oceans, Gulfs, Bays)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7c332e44-9c9e-4581-b79a-2e5307380d5f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Use 'the' before names of rivers, seas, oceans, gulfs, and bays.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "30765126-9a6e-47ab-9b21-21abd439b188",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Rivers: the Ganges, the Nile, the Amazon, the Yamuna, the Thames\nSeas & Oceans: the Arabian Sea, the Red Sea, the Indian Ocean, the Atlantic Ocean, the Pacific Ocean\nGulfs & Bays: the Persian Gulf, the Gulf of Mexico, the Bay of Bengal",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "90d488e4-ed75-4943-bb53-907cf7582771",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "5.3 Deserts and Island Groups",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8c143b8b-6466-41e7-ac5d-623f4adebe2d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Use 'the' before deserts and groups of islands, but omit it for individual islands.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e134d29d-0502-424d-8ca6-b7ea4fc841d5",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Deserts: the Sahara, the Thar Desert, the Gobi Desert\nIsland Groups (Use 'The'): the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, the Philippines, the Maldives, the West Indies\nIndividual Islands (Zero Article): Sri Lanka, Madagascar",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0268f28b-9590-4f15-a6a2-21bc60c1392d",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "5.4 Plural or Descriptive Country Names",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4c6dfd03-b628-4327-b45a-756b40f68ba6",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Ordinary country names do not take 'the', but plural or descriptive country names (containing words like United, Kingdom, Republic, Netherlands) do.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6f2db11c-feae-4990-9b78-f000c1ef489a",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Descriptive\/Plural Countries (Use 'The'): the Netherlands, the United States, the United Kingdom, the United Arab Emirates\nOrdinary Countries (Zero Article): India, Pakistan, Nepal, France, Japan",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3f1aea5c-f161-4d14-9909-8b7ed76ac464",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "6. 'THE' WITH BOOKS, CELESTIAL OBJECTS, AND DIRECTIONS",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "03f221de-7df7-4a08-a3d9-b5f806a14ae5",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "6.1 Holy Books and Newspapers",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ad468377-96a3-4492-a09d-070922a88124",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Holy Books: the Bible, the Quran, the Vedas, the Ramayana, the Mahabharata\nNewspapers: The Times of India, The Hindustan Times, The Statesman, The Hindu",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e8236cf2-047f-4179-949e-677b8d767871",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "6.2 Celestial Objects and Unique Entities",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e7f1e7b3-3851-4f28-95ad-e53903c4c387",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "the Sun, the Moon, the Earth, the Equator, the sky, the atmosphere",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cdd1c969-a1ed-4ed8-89c9-e5f6ca1433d7",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "6.3 Directions",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f79ff195-cacf-4000-a506-fec3b3d5f06a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Use 'the' when the direction refers to a specific region or geographical area. Omit it when indicating simple movement\/direction after a verb, or in proper names containing a direction.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3e90705b-8551-44c4-a287-b3fa7fc71f58",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Specific Region: He lives in the North. \/ The sun rises in the East.\nMovement\/Direction (No Article): Go East. \/ Travel North.\nProper Names (No Article): West Bengal, North India, South Africa",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "22c33515-f728-4224-8502-7c63770fc227",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "7. SPECIAL RULES: MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS & OMISSION WORDS",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dffabaf3-8d09-45b5-bf0c-016bfc5ce18f",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "7.1 Musical Instruments: Playing vs. Physical Object",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d75e91d9-f6e8-4a9e-a6de-121bb7ba499b",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Musical Instrument Rule",
      "content": "Playing\/musical activity → Use 'the' (e.g., He plays the guitar.)\nOne physical instrument → Use 'a\/an' (e.g., He bought a guitar.)"
    },
    {
      "id": "7127a5f7-ba72-4825-a737-cc80af74b4f5",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "7.2 Special Words Where 'The' is Omitted",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e88d9aa8-a06a-4e0b-b397-801acacfe3d8",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The article is omitted before words like Heaven, Hell, God, and Parliament when used in their established general or institutional sense.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "86bce03f-abd7-4aa0-a828-d8797765d3a8",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Go to heaven.\nGo to hell.\nHe believes in God.\nHe will raise the issue in Parliament.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "faa07248-4a06-4bf8-8ed6-2023a7d63bc8",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "8. OMISSION OF ARTICLES (ZERO ARTICLE)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "11d283b0-67d9-479b-9439-06198ecb4bae",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "8.1 Proper Nouns, Languages, Subjects, and Sports",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9a4b3f79-e517-4f14-b51e-5beb1ebd2c0c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Articles are generally omitted before proper names of people, cities, states, individual mountains\/islands, languages, academic subjects, and sports.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ff3b264e-4060-4a61-ba8c-6bf9b224516f",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Proper Nouns: Delhi is the capital of India. (Not: The Delhi)\nLanguages: She speaks English fluently. (Not: the English)\nSubjects: He studies Mathematics.\nSports: He plays cricket. (Not: the cricket)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "02ea4a60-bb9f-447f-b95b-f87459d41d08",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "8.2 Abstract and Material Nouns",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "82c7af3c-dacc-4bab-9294-9ec8c805ede8",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Uncountable abstract and material nouns do not take an article when used in a general sense, but take 'the' when made specific.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5fd9c4e6-376c-478c-8b91-8216ea801f65",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "General (Zero Article): Honesty is the best policy. \/ Gold is a precious metal.\nSpecific (Use 'The'): The honesty of the boy impressed everyone. \/ The gold of this ring is pure.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c861ad8a-9132-4102-a069-64f8c2e179a8",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "8.3 Names of Meals",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a090d029-9c3b-4895-8bd1-fbc65f9acca7",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Omit articles before standard meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) in a general sense. Use an article if the meal is described or made specific.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8ae9f19c-3975-4ccc-9e28-19cc5be11e2e",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "General: We had breakfast at 8 AM. \/ We had lunch at 2 PM.\nSpecific\/Described: We had a big lunch. \/ The lunch we ordered was excellent.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "177eca21-f2f6-400e-9deb-fe172d6ca4e1",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "8.4 Primary vs. Secondary Purpose (School, College, Hospital, Church, Prison)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d3afbe41-ee2e-47a1-aa63-08f441fdbb3d",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "IMPORTANT",
      "title": "Primary vs. Secondary Purpose Rule",
      "content": "Do not use articles if referring to the primary purpose of the institution (e.g., going to school to study, hospital for treatment, church to worship, prison as an inmate). Use 'the' if visiting the physical building for a secondary purpose."
    },
    {
      "id": "09ce3fd3-aed8-46f2-898a-c96699de25d8",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "Core Concept: Primary Purpose vs. Specific Building",
      "nodes": [
        "Core Concept: Primary Purpose",
        "No Article (Primary Purpose)",
        "Use an Article (Secondary Purpose)"
      ],
      "rawContent": "Core Concept: Primary Purpose\n├── No Article (Primary Purpose): Focus on main function (e.g., study, worship, treatment)\n└── Use an Article (Secondary Purpose): Focus on physical building (e.g., visiting, touring)"
    },
    {
      "id": "ae72d9d9-e907-409c-b613-aed5c2e2d208",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "School: 'She is in school.' (studying) vs. 'My mother went to the school.' (visiting)\nHospital: 'He was rushed to hospital.' (patient) vs. 'I went to the hospital to visit him.' (visitor)\nChurch: 'They go to church.' (worship) vs. 'The tourists took photos of the church.' (sightseeing)\nPrison: 'The thief was sent to prison.' (inmate) vs. 'She works as a guard at the prison.' (employee)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cf6c188b-f2a7-40dc-b275-1f8042c0fa2f",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "9. ADDITIONAL USES OF THE",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c32d8f65-4efc-4cc8-9816-43ec05f38d22",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Superlative Degree: He is the tallest boy in the class. \/ This is the best book.\nOrdinal Numbers: the first chapter, the second question, the third floor\nWords like 'Only', 'Same', 'Very': He is the only person who knows. \/ We live in the same house. \/ This is the very book I wanted.\nHistorical Periods & Events: the Middle Ages, the Industrial Revolution, the First World War\nAdjectives representing a group: the rich, the poor, the elderly, the young (e.g., The government should help the poor.)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "01ac6980-58b8-487d-9e69-939839a3a91d",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "10. COMPARISON & COMMON MISTAKES",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2c9697f4-3d90-4638-b108-414cff6f7f7c",
      "type": "TABLE",
      "title": "A\/An vs. The Comparison",
      "headers": [
        "Situation",
        "Article",
        "Example"
      ],
      "rows": [
        [
          "General, singular countable noun",
          "A\/An",
          "I saw a dog."
        ],
        [
          "First mention",
          "A\/An",
          "She bought a book."
        ],
        [
          "Previously mentioned noun",
          "The",
          "The book is interesting."
        ],
        [
          "Specific noun",
          "The",
          "Give me the book on the table."
        ],
        [
          "Vowel sound",
          "An",
          "an apple, an hour"
        ],
        [
          "Consonant sound",
          "A",
          "a boy, a university"
        ],
        [
          "Profession",
          "A\/An",
          "He is a doctor."
        ],
        [
          "Playing an instrument",
          "The",
          "She plays the piano."
        ],
        [
          "Physical instrument",
          "A\/An",
          "She bought a piano."
        ],
        [
          "Mountain range",
          "The",
          "the Himalayas"
        ],
        [
          "Individual mountain",
          "Zero",
          "Mount Everest"
        ],
        [
          "River",
          "The",
          "the Ganges"
        ],
        [
          "Individual country",
          "Zero",
          "India"

      "hasHeaderRow": true
    },
    {
      "id": "8db22886-f7cd-44ed-bcd0-71c2000ec89f",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Common Mistakes to Avoid",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4aeb3e2e-5b38-4776-adb7-04beeb32ca2b",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Mistake 1: Choosing A\/An by letter instead of sound. (Incorrect: an university, a honest man | Correct: a university, an honest man)\nMistake 2: Using 'The' before every proper name. (Incorrect: The Delhi is the capital. | Correct: Delhi is the capital.)\nMistake 3: Forgetting the article before a singular countable noun. (Incorrect: He is teacher. | Correct: He is a teacher.)\nMistake 4: Using 'The' with general uncountable nouns. (Incorrect: The honesty is the best policy. | Correct: Honesty is the best policy.)\nMistake 5: Confusing primary vs. secondary purpose for institutions. (Primary: He goes to school. | Secondary: His father went to the school.)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5d022315-fb4c-4321-bde2-bcff8f23030b",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Revision",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1c96194b-807f-42b0-b156-7ea33e18e07f",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "A\/An is the Indefinite Article, used with singular countable nouns based on sound (An for vowel sounds, A for consonant sounds).\nThe is the Definite Article, used for specific, unique, or previously mentioned nouns.\nSound > Spelling: Words like 'hour', 'honest', 'MP' take 'an'; 'university', 'European', 'one-rupee' take 'a'.\nUse 'the' with mountain ranges, rivers, oceans, deserts, island groups, and descriptive country names.\nOmit articles (Zero Article) for proper nouns, individual mountains\/islands, languages, academic subjects, sports, and general meals.\nOmit articles for school, college, hospital, church, and prison when visited for their primary purpose. Use 'the' for secondary purposes.\nUse 'the' with superlatives, ordinals, and words like 'same', 'only', and 'very'.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    }
  ]
}

{
  "chapterId": "chap_fb4f2ab1",
  "title": "Internet",
  "elements": [
    {
      "id": "b5e3aaa5-6889-4683-8225-a4799a447ce6",
      "type": "HEADING_1",
      "text": "CHAPTER 6: INTERNET",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4996639b-b55b-4c81-8f7f-b6bc629e821f",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "1. Internet Overview",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8c42c02f-d9a9-4f70-bcc0-2fd7d3232c64",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Internet is a global system of interconnected computer networks that utilizes the standardized Transmission Control Protocol\/Internet Protocol (TCP\/IP) suite to enable communication and data exchange among billions of devices worldwide.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2fbb86df-763a-4859-8b7a-7bea2fab3e28",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "TCP\/IP Suite",
      "content": "Standardized rules for formatting, routing, and transmitting data across networks."
    },
    {
      "id": "4c894fda-3d16-41ab-b0f7-85c683209497",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Originating in the late 1960s as ARPANET (Advanced Research Projects Agency Network)—a project funded by the U.S. Department of Defense to establish a resilient communications network—it pioneered packet switching technology.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c2b1d683-0577-4f5c-8248-ebf7c0d7d78b",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "ARPANET & Packet Switching",
      "content": "ARPANET was the early military network that laid the foundation for the modern Internet. Packet switching is a method of grouping data into packets before transmitting it over a digital network."
    },
    {
      "id": "96844464-2be0-4007-8a4b-62ddc0cb7eec",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Often referred to as a 'network of networks,' the modern Internet evolved primarily through the ground-breaking contributions of Vinton Gray Cerf and Bob Kahn, who are widely recognized as the fathers of the Internet for co-designing the core TCP\/IP protocols that allow disparate local, regional, national, and international networks to seamlessly link into a single unified architecture.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "13866727-a8eb-40f9-be75-00689ce2f663",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "2. Advantages of Internet",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2cac60df-ce40-4486-99e5-76baf6d296ee",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Global Communication: Enables real-time global connectivity through email, instant messaging, and voice\/video calling services.\nInformation Accessibility: Provides access to educational resources, digital libraries, research papers, and news repositories.\nE-Commerce and Banking: Supports online shopping, digital payments, electronic banking, and direct financial transactions.\nRemote Work and Collaboration: Allows remote employment, cloud-based file sharing, and virtual team collaboration across geographically distant locations.\nDigital Entertainment: Delivers multimedia streaming, online gaming, digital publishing, and interactive media services.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c36e2d23-8c91-49d6-88d6-a257da4d3609",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "3. Disadvantages of Internet",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c26a34f3-9e42-49a5-ae15-328454829fb3",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Cybersecurity Threats: Exposes systems to malicious software, computer viruses, phishing scams, ransomware, and unauthorized data breaches.\nPrivacy Risks: Risk of personal data theft, identity fraud, and illegal tracking of online activities.\nSpread of Misinformation: Rapid distribution of unverified news, fake content, and fraudulent online schemes.\nDigital Addiction & Isolation: Potential for excessive screen time, reduced real-world social interaction, and digital burnout.\nExposure to Inappropriate Content: Risk of encountering harmful, illegal, or age-inappropriate material without adequate filtering.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "21b61576-1c62-4dcf-84ec-c427b930bcec",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "4. Internet Connections & Access Technologies",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "519ba541-7e98-4b27-a682-96fecfabc059",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Dial-up Connection",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "73fed8e3-97cb-4ded-b860-d046d26636e7",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "An early internet access method that utilizes standard analog copper telephone lines to establish a connection to an Internet Service Provider (ISP) via a dial-up modem. It offers limited data transfer speeds of up to 56 Kbps and prevents simultaneous use of the voice telephone line while active.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "700367eb-20a9-43fa-944e-1487852c0ee4",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "Internet Service Provider (ISP)",
      "content": "A company that provides access to the internet."
    },
    {
      "id": "226bb98c-1877-4d0c-a194-08a4990bfbe5",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Broadband Connection",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8b435e51-992f-482f-99f5-9008f9ae1fd0",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "High-speed, always-on internet access capable of transmitting large volumes of data simultaneously across wide frequency bandwidths.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0d3df098-f36d-496b-bb8b-351f5d165f25",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "Bandwidth",
      "content": "The maximum capacity of a communications link to transmit data."
    },
    {
      "id": "0ef1e134-4eff-485e-9b55-73c12621472b",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "Broadband Connection Types",
      "nodes": [
        "Broadband Types",
        "DSL",
        "Cable",
        "BPL"
      ],
      "rawContent": "[Broadband Types]\n  \/   |   \\\n[DSL] [Cable] [BPL]"
    },
    {
      "id": "ba7d1bd0-e989-41f2-ac7a-d30b5ae388ae",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Digital Subscriber Line (DSL)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2e7eb718-46c6-47a6-bbb4-f95a2be09157",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Transmits digital data over existing local copper telephone lines using higher frequencies, allowing concurrent voice calls and high-speed internet access.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9bef58fb-d3bf-40a4-8ad4-c94188d37558",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Cable Modem",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cfeac70c-de9d-4dbc-8aaa-a0b1a41f53de",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Delivers broadband internet service over the coaxial cable infrastructure used for cable television networks, providing high data transfer rates.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "99197f1c-b7e1-45ae-87b2-b87af0f87320",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "Coaxial Cable",
      "content": "A type of copper cable built with a metal shield to block signal interference."
    },
    {
      "id": "d51c59be-73b2-47a5-8490-509d0f9965c6",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Broadband over Power Line (BPL)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "49ce8bd1-d316-4139-934f-4f530a5b6627",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Transmits high-speed digital data through existing low and medium-voltage electrical power distribution networks, delivering internet access via power outlets.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6189f07e-fda3-47c0-987f-6cea405844d4",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Wireless Connection",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "482add0b-5198-4001-b917-c7f773d63226",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Wireless internet connections transmit data signals through electromagnetic radio waves, eliminating the need for physical cabling between user devices and network infrastructure. This framework provides device mobility, flexibility, and coverage across residential, commercial, and outdoor spaces.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8014c9e9-b5dc-42b4-8ad4-24e5080ce313",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "Wireless Connection Ways",
      "nodes": [
        "Ways to Connect",
        "Wi-Fi",
        "WiMAX",
        "Mobile Wireless"
      ],
      "rawContent": "[Ways to Connect]\n  \/   |   \\\n[Wi-Fi] [WiMAX] [Mobile Wireless]"
    },
    {
      "id": "978dea83-6121-4a12-878b-268ce59aecf1",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Wireless Fidelity (Wi-Fi)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ff938ff5-50b4-4d17-8c36-20e2160c53aa",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Uses radio frequency signals based on the IEEE 802.11 standard to connect local devices to a central wireless access point or router within a short-to-medium range.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c116f3fe-83cb-408f-88a9-8f5f67614086",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "IEEE 802.11",
      "content": "The industry standard specifications for wireless local area networks."
    },
    {
      "id": "15d24f53-6c2e-4a16-b52c-f27a66d8d57e",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Worldwide Interoperability for Microwave Access (WiMAX)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d5d5e2e1-c1b7-40c4-8b7b-9b29a3efce8f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A long-range wireless communication standard based on IEEE 802.16 designed to provide high-speed wireless broadband access across large metropolitan areas (MANs).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d2c21610-b23e-4ef9-9eba-8a0f8503201d",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "IEEE 802.16",
      "content": "The industry standard specifications for wireless metropolitan area networks."
    },
    {
      "id": "22380728-3263-4b46-88b4-bb7ddc7413ed",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Mobile Wireless Broadband Services",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6117e809-7eee-48d6-87b8-7d2d34a4cd76",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "High-speed cellular networks (3G, 4G LTE, 5G) operated by telecommunications carriers that enable continuous mobile internet access using cellular towers.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "23c74935-c29b-41d6-86c0-b6e2ec8eff4f",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "5. Interconnecting Protocols",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f3d5e1f3-6581-411e-8272-a2bd33ee23d6",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Interconnecting protocols are standardized sets of rules, formats, and procedures that govern how data packets are formatted, addressed, transmitted, routed, and received across computer networks.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e2f1af28-fc24-4e49-bac3-d274c05f5d94",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Transmission Control Protocol \/ Internet Protocol (TCP\/IP)\nFile Transfer Protocol (FTP)\nHypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP)\nTelnet Protocol\nUsenet Protocol\nPoint-to-Point Protocol (PPP)\nSimple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP)\nWireless Application Protocol (WAP)\nVoice over Internet Protocol (VoIP)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "185758a1-8196-4cb5-a8f5-53ead648dedd",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Transmission Control Protocol \/ Internet Protocol (TCP\/IP)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b24e7e14-a2e4-4cfa-b003-3c5aca3bfb0b",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "TCP\/IP Suite Components",
      "nodes": [
        "TCP\/IP Suite",
        "TCP Protocol",
        "IP Protocol"
      ],
      "rawContent": "[TCP\/IP Suite]\n  \/       \\\n[TCP Protocol] [IP Protocol]"
    },
    {
      "id": "690f5d38-38ed-4e2a-b719-3b477e5adc45",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "58ff2514-3074-43c4-8ee4-b40bd6f5e091",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A connection-oriented transport layer protocol that breaks large data files into smaller packets, tracks packet delivery, manages flow control, retransmits lost packets, and reassembles them in exact sequence at the destination.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f411106f-0b85-437c-8f85-d3f240145718",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Internet Protocol (IP)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f3231f21-bf4c-4a00-b33c-a5557955d5e2",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "An internet layer protocol responsible for logical network addressing and packet routing, ensuring individual data packets reach their destination across interconnected networks based on their IP addresses.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6ec0d507-b038-47db-b023-afff08c8879e",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "File Transfer Protocol (FTP)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {

      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Uniform Resource Locator (URL) is a standardized string address specifying the exact location of a specific resource or web page on the Internet. Example: https:\/\/www.example.com\/about.html",
