      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,

    },
    {
      "id": "a490d4fc-f888-43a8-871d-d4a47a385e92",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Time: The duration in hours, minutes, or seconds spent to cover a certain distance.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dd91289a-764b-47e0-8b87-e8c0797d8b35",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Distance: The length of path covered by a person or an object between two places. (Units: m or km)",

      "isStrikethrough": false,

    },
    {

    {

      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Conversion Factors",
      "content": "To convert km\/h to m\/s: Multiply by 5\/18\nTo convert m\/s to km\/h: Multiply by 18\/5"
    },
    {
      "id": "917e3cdf-cd11-4632-a49c-72fda9264657",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "CORE RELATIONSHIPS",

      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Speed & Distance: Directly proportional when time is constant.",

      "text": "Distance & Time: Directly proportional when speed is constant.",

      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Average Speed Formula",
      "content": "When a certain distance is covered at speed A and the exact same distance is covered at speed B:\nAverage Speed = (2  A  B) \/ (A + B)"
    },
    {
      "id": "033ed91a-96f8-4094-abeb-acf8e7f7a698",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Relative Speed",
      "isBold": false,

      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "99b6dbb4-7d87-4d16-bba4-e09feff349bc",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "For two moving objects with speeds a km\/h and b km\/h:",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5b0ad33a-312c-45b4-b80a-1ef3bc3c106c",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Opposite Directions: Relative Speed = a + b km\/h",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a3f5cf60-35a0-4a9b-923a-9c81054d9278",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Same Direction (where a > b): Relative Speed = a - b km\/h",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a44fed7a-294e-4436-8378-d2588c77a5e0",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Relative Speed in Motion of Trains",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "17711c69-972c-40dc-8b4d-951132bd58b8",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Crossing in Opposite Directions: Two trains of lengths x km and y km moving in opposite directions at u km\/h and v km\/h cross each other in Time = (x + y) \/ (u + v) hours.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d7f9d3c0-91aa-4797-9524-f9c8739629d0",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Crossing in Same Direction (u > v): Two trains of lengths x km and y km moving in the same direction cross each other in Time = (x + y) \/ (u - v) hours.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,

    },
    {
      "id": "e6e9ec0a-7ee6-4811-b0ed-84b32c4aad91",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Ratio of Speeds After Crossing: If two trains start at the same time from A and B towards each other, and after crossing take 'a' and 'b' hours to reach B and A respectively, then: Speed of Train A \/ Speed of Train B = sqrt(b \/ a)",
      "isBold": false,

      "textColorHex": "",

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9dd1b434-5c90-4722-8550-a7f76b02a586",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Boats and Streams",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "84efda89-3781-4d1d-90fb-f1b5dc2723c7",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Let the speed of the boat in still water be x km\/h and the speed of the stream be y km\/h:",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f259a39e-7282-47f7-a3fb-8830ebaf41c1",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Downstream Speed (u) = (x + y) km\/h",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "375f1e87-6b19-45d1-baa6-fef8773f1088",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Upstream Speed (v) = (x - y) km\/h",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "adc577c2-d626-4d1b-b8f4-7d66b7465f35",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Speed of Boat in Still Water (x) = (u + v) \/ 2 km\/h",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6fe30ffb-347c-4acb-af0c-4b671a788eca",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Speed of Stream (y) = (u - v) \/ 2 km\/h",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fe83db0a-d679-4620-bd85-00d3f9a1b536",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "IN-TEXT SOLVED EXAMPLES",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6f956cb8-457c-4e74-9d13-5f719a7afedf",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 1: Basic Speed Calculation",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2b7388cf-3551-4515-b3bb-953fd5060ae0",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Arnav covers 150 km in 1.5 hours. Find his speed.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9cbc5430-3c93-4ffe-ac40-bc3e61626405",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Solution",
      "content": "Speed = Distance \/ Time\nSpeed = 150 km \/ 1.5 h = 100 km\/h\n\nCorrect Option: (b) 100 km\/h"
    },
    {
      "id": "2871645b-9e80-4465-b10a-2b50a7ace6a0",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 2: Late and Early Concept",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b0c21e29-285f-4645-87c4-06c469cc10b5",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A person walking at 5 km\/h misses a train by 7 minutes. If he walks at 6 km\/h, he reaches 5 minutes early. Find the distance to the station.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "55e7c93f-ed60-4bd7-b9de-6adf213398bc",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution & Shortcut",
      "content": "Let the required distance be d km.\nDifference in time = 7 min (late) + 5 min (early) = 12 minutes = 12\/60 hours = 1\/5 hours.\n\nUsing the formula:\n(d \/ 5) - (d \/ 6) = 1\/5\nd \/ 30 = 1\/5\nd = 6 km\n\nCorrect Option: (b) 6 km"
    },
    {
      "id": "abc98ba8-82ff-4f74-b16b-a7b7e224ec69",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 3: Average Speed for Equal Distances",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e67cc317-42cb-48ba-80dc-74b4d4ba9366",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A person goes to a destination at 60 km\/h and returns to the starting point at 50 km\/h. Find the average speed of the entire journey.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c5cba922-f4d2-4a08-a3f2-c48883a234ef",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Solution",
      "content": "Average Speed = (2  A  B) \/ (A + B)\nAverage Speed = (2  60  50) \/ (60 + 50) = 6000 \/ 110 = 54.54 km\/h\n\nCorrect Option: (a) 54.54 km\/h"
    },
    {
      "id": "b4d77390-53fd-4047-8c98-cc0b49bbf077",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 4: Relative Speed in Opposite Directions",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "285ca895-6e7c-44b9-83d9-a70b693c55bb",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Two persons are moving in opposite directions at speeds of 5 km\/h and 3 km\/h respectively. Find their relative speed.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "000fe56b-1f62-4929-aa90-a0bcbe3d3255",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Solution",
      "content": "When moving in opposite directions, relative speed is the sum of individual speeds.\nRelative Speed = 5 km\/h + 3 km\/h = 8 km\/h\n\nCorrect Option: (c) 8 km\/h"
    },
    {
      "id": "fad3aa44-4306-469c-ab45-4b49c430b637",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 5: Train Crossing a Platform",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4355c49e-16bd-4952-9845-bf67936746b0",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A train 140 m long running at 60 km\/h passes a 260 m long platform. Find the time taken by the train to cross the platform.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c97fc7c5-9e00-4540-9820-6f061d33ac82",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Solution",
      "content": "Total distance to be covered = Length of train + Length of platform = 140 m + 260 m = 400 m.\nSpeed of train in m\/s = 60 * (5\/18) = 50\/3 m\/s.\n\nTime taken = Distance \/ Speed = 400 \/ (50\/3) = (400 * 3) \/ 50 = 24 seconds.\n\nCorrect Option: (b) 24 s"
    },
    {
      "id": "b0337632-3df5-489a-9a00-7f04de117ad4",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 6: Ratio of Speeds After Crossing",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8f165d2f-aabf-4e82-b535-bc83e64e1f09",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Two trains start at the same time from A and B towards each other. After passing each other, they complete their journeys in 9 hours and 4 hours respectively. Find the ratio of their speeds.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "737fa82d-72d1-4b28-a73a-344e3a7b642a",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Solution",
      "content": "Using the formula: Speed of Train A \/ Speed of Train B = sqrt(Time taken by B \/ Time taken by A)\nRatio of speeds = sqrt(4 \/ 9) = 2 \/ 3 = 2:3\n\nCorrect Option: (d) 2:3"
    },
    {
      "id": "c8997cf2-b459-4f81-8b24-83634502acec",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 7: Boat and Stream Ratio",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "33094cfd-25d6-41b1-9fe5-4bad152e6d8d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The speed of a boat in still water is 15 km\/h. It takes twice as long to row up as to row down the river. Find the speed of the stream.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "54e0b8ff-acf5-407b-b52e-cd4c809827ab",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution",
      "content": "Let the speed of the stream be y km\/h.\nDownstream speed (u) = 15 + y\nUpstream speed (v) = 15 - y\n\nSince distance is constant, Time is inversely proportional to Speed.\nTime (Upstream) = 2 * Time (Downstream)\nTherefore, Downstream Speed = 2 * Upstream Speed\n15 + y = 2 * (15 - y)\n15 + y = 30 - 2y\n3y = 15\ny = 5 km\/h\n\nCorrect Option: (d) 5 km\/h"
    }
  ]
}

    {
      "id": "a8a560fd-9df1-429d-bc90-1df03d4ac613",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "What is a Percent?",
      "content": "Per cent literally means 'for every hundred'. It is a fraction whose denominator is always 100. The numerator of this fraction is called the rate per cent, and it is denoted by the symbol %."
    },
    {
      "id": "1cb0a19c-441b-4a20-9e80-04c888d25fbb",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Basic Percentage Formula",
      "content": "To calculate the percentage of a value relative to a total:\nPercentage (%) = (Value \/ Total Value) * 100"
    },
    {
      "id": "a09454d8-2bf0-4317-a9e4-35915cd1adb4",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Percentage Conversions",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dc2447fa-a84b-46dc-a7f9-eeb6543eac99",
      "type": "TABLE",
      "title": "Conversion Rules and Examples",
      "headers": [
        "Conversion Type",
        "Rule",
        "Example"
      ],
      "rows": [
        [
          "Fraction to Percentage",
          "Multiply the fraction (a\/b) by 100 and attach the % sign.",
          "3\/5 * 100 = 60%"
        ],
        [
          "Percentage to Fraction",
          "Divide the rate per cent by 100 and remove the % sign.",
          "45% = 45\/100 = 9\/20"
        ]
      ],
      "hasHeaderRow": true
    },
    {
      "id": "80a54df9-3355-425d-9f6c-95cf337777a4",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "PERCENTAGE INCREASE AND DECREASE",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "42a38886-90ef-4a5d-9561-62fc33a91ccc",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Percentage increase or decrease is always calculated with respect to the base (original\/previous) value, unless specified otherwise in the problem statement.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b78b1aa0-6d65-4f8f-a118-608783502b97",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Increase and Decrease Formulas",
      "content": "Percentage Increase = (Increase \/ Original Value) * 100\n\nPercentage Decrease = (Decrease \/ Original Value) * 100"
    },
    {
      "id": "0ba7773a-fd5f-4af9-b17f-41895edfecd0",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "SUCCESSIVE INCREASE AND DECREASE",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0edbe65f-866b-4e65-bc40-28217b88a18d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "When a quantity undergoes multiple percentage changes one after another, these successive changes can be consolidated into a single net percentage change.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e2df9485-85a7-47e4-b9e6-be9139673ea5",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Successive Percentage Formula",
      "content": "Net Percentage Change = [x + y + (x * y) \/ 100] %"
    },
    {
      "id": "605777a5-e957-4530-bffc-b5ca32851319",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "IMPORTANT",
      "title": "Sign Convention for Successive Changes",
      "content": "Always use positive values (+) for increments\/increases, and negative values (-) for decrements\/decreases when substituting into the successive percentage formula."
    },

    {
      "id": "e40f5e26-860f-4dd5-81e7-0a84426ae8c6",

      "text": "Example 1: Water in Milk Mixture",

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "73bb04a9-db72-490c-baf7-eb0e587cc628",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Quantity of water in milk constitutes 6 parts of every 20 parts of mixture. What is the percentage of water in the mixture?",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e9fce0a6-2609-4e81-ae7d-1e1fa3cd9a9b",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution for Example 1",
      "content": "Required percentage = (6 \/ 20) * 100 = 30%\n\nCorrect Answer: (a) 30%"
    },
    {
      "id": "06d507b4-63b0-4c48-8c77-6062bd8636aa",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 2: Income Comparison",
      "isBold": false,

      "isStrikethrough": false,

    },
    {
      "id": "3c9ec288-6c0a-454a-b280-e61d4adc5c4d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "If A's income is 20% more than that of B, then how much per cent is B's income less than that of A?",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e01c48f7-281f-4f6c-87be-5bec5a311583",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution for Example 2",
      "content": "Let B's income = ₹ 100\nThis implies A's income = ₹ 120.\n\nRequired percentage less = [(120 - 100) \/ 120]  100 = (20 \/ 120)  100 = 16 2\/3%\n\nCorrect Answer: (a) 16 2\/3%"
    },
    {
      "id": "d2dca5ed-c658-4a3c-b787-1149a93c52ed",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 3: Single Price Increase",

    },
    {
      "id": "5c740ea7-5bb4-429b-ae77-fc57044671ad",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The price of a product is increased by 20%. If the original price is ₹ 300, what is the final price of the product?",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "17d54228-f387-4bb4-8696-5403d35a6fbc",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution for Example 3",
      "content": "New price = 300  (1 + 20\/100) = 300  1.2 = ₹ 360\n\nCorrect Answer: (b) ₹ 360"
    },
    {
      "id": "49a17f81-bf58-4538-9c56-3bd8d9809906",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 4: Successive Wage Changes",

    {
      "id": "acc89ad3-12b6-4834-80d7-c3ea2a2c2775",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The wages of a worker is first increased by 20% and subsequently reduced by 20%. If the original monthly wages is ₹ 500, what is the final wages?",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ce8b7abb-9dbe-4d39-821c-b32e45097c81",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution for Example 4",
      "content": "Final wages = 500  (1 + 20\/100)  (1 - 20\/100)\nFinal wages = 500  (6\/5)  (4\/5) = ₹ 480\n\nCorrect Answer: (c) ₹ 480"
    },
    {
      "id": "7c7ac2c0-f623-4252-87bd-1d8a07f3b3dc",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 5: Area Change of a Rectangle",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "35d517ba-daa7-4e58-bb27-bfd5d23c9b04",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The length of a rectangle is increased by 20% and breadth is decreased by 10%. Calculate the percentage change in the area.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5b1e27ca-9196-4c39-9239-ef5dc91700c7",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution for Example 5",
      "content": "Using the successive percentage formula where x = +20 and y = -10:\nPercentage change in area = 20 - 10 + [20 * (-10)] \/ 100\nPercentage change in area = 10 - 2 = 8%\n\nCorrect Answer: (d) 8%"
    },
    {
      "id": "c7c4722f-e6e5-4f8a-b57e-2b843e9a88ea",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 6: Commodity Price and Consumption",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dbe190d2-c708-4b36-afd2-0f679c859ead",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "If the price of a commodity is increased by 20%, find by how much per cent must a housewife reduce her consumption, so as not to increase the expenditure?",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "53c7478e-6b43-424f-a321-eb4d6816aeb0",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution for Example 6",
      "content": "Let original price = ₹ 100\nIncreased price = ₹ 120\n\nTo keep expenditure the same, consumption must be reduced by the increased amount relative to the new price:\nRequired percentage reduction = (20 \/ 120) * 100 = 16 2\/3%\n\nCorrect Answer: (c) 16 2\/3%"
    }
  ]
}

      "id": "826eb178-ca4f-4ef7-95cc-ee2f71585fa7",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "Blood Relation",
      "content": "Blood relation between two individuals is defined as a relation between them by virtue of their birth. Relations on the Mother's side are termed Maternal, while relations on the Father's side are termed Paternal."
    },
    {
      "id": "83a53051-d020-45df-9a07-d547c9e05fae",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Standard Notation Symbols",

    {
      "id": "a1ff3349-de47-4127-8e43-870214bf4ca2",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "To solve blood relation problems efficiently, standard symbols are used to construct family trees representing gender and generational gaps.",

    {

      "text": "Instruction: Decode the spoken relational chain to identify the speaker's relationship to the listener.",

    {
      "id": "33b03776-3457-4037-a1a4-fe930b87ef43",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Question: Gopal said, pointing to Govind, 'His father is my father's only son'. How is Gopal related to Govind?",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cb8b7b1c-4f7f-4736-b1aa-822d52cd0ea0",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "(a) Grandfather\n(b) Grandson\n(c) Son\n(d) Father",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e988a140-931c-430d-bb94-44db0674a9ac",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution & Explanation",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (d)\n\nExplanation:\n- 'My father's only son' implies Gopal himself.\n- Therefore, Govind's father is Gopal. Gopal is the Father of Govind."
    },
    {
      "id": "6dcc0959-6b86-42c1-a667-6aeab8ac5635",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Example 2: Family Tree Construction",
      "isBold": false,

    },
    {
      "id": "d1521cc4-b58b-4b1b-85e1-0f96953f7dee",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Construct a family tree diagram to trace the relationship between C and D.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2ed90481-36df-4c1d-b20c-b2d379cea3f6",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Question: C is the mother of A and B. If D is the husband of B, then how is C related to D?",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ca7a4403-f093-4908-b95d-2107c1b6bd4e",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "(a) Mother\n(b) Aunt\n(c) Mother-in-law\n(d) Sister",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "83c10000-8981-4c65-a256-cc46caa61973",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution & Explanation",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (c)\n\nExplanation:\n- C is the mother of B.\n- D is the husband of B.\n- C is the mother of D's wife, which makes C the Mother-in-law of D."
    },
    {
      "id": "9988c9b9-5ed0-4f43-9a17-f123cd506fc2",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Example 3: Coded Relationships",

    {
      "id": "03055b14-1207-4530-a948-58b9ec407f93",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Decode the coded string using given operator relations to determine how U is related to Z.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "060761b2-5344-4817-b95e-3a51d1e68ead",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Directions: 'A + B' means 'A is the daughter of B'; 'A x B' means 'A is the son of B'; 'A - B' means 'A is the wife of B'.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fee05fe0-4ee3-49f7-b2c8-4bf6304f7734",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Question: If Z x T - S x U + P, then how is U related to Z?",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fdf3a999-8128-46a7-823f-44d265e044e2",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "(a) Mother\n(b) Grandmother\n(c) Father\n(d) Cannot be determined",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "21f2ec88-664f-469f-a974-0be8f10bb277",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution & Explanation",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (b)\n\nExplanation:\n- Z x T implies Z is the son of T.\n- T - S implies T is the wife of S.\n- S x U implies S is the son of U.\n- U + P implies U is the daughter of P (female).\n- U is the mother of Z's father (S). Thus, U is the Grandmother of Z."
    },
    {
      "id": "8a10189c-bc37-43f3-a599-b4228925290f",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Practice Exercise",
      "isBold": false,

    {

    {
      "id": "5d6b94e8-0dbb-4241-acba-efafacf8f0ca",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Decode the statement to determine Monika's relation to Reena.\n\nQuestion: Introducing Reena, Monika said, 'She is the only daughter of my father's only daughter'. How is Monika related to Reena?",
      "isBold": false,

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "03387acc-0d95-410e-940b-ab18113ddc77",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "(a) Aunt\n(b) Niece\n(c) Daughter\n(d) Mother",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0b214251-979f-4469-89d8-5bc7c71d1fb8",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (d)\n\nExplanation:\n- 'Monika's father's only daughter' implies Monika herself.\n- Reena is the daughter of Monika, which means Monika is the Mother of Reena."
    },
    {
      "id": "563f2731-c9e5-4334-ac64-90fa45d78779",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Question 2",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,

      "isStrikethrough": false,

      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a966d827-6174-4036-b47a-05bdc7d32373",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Trace the generational connections from husband to brother's son.\n\nQuestion: A woman introduces a man as the son of the brother of her mother's husband. How is the man related to the woman?",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ad1097db-1773-47ed-81ad-5572f0b2fb23",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "(a) Brother\n(b) Cousin\n(c) Father\n(d) Son",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3e267c17-33fb-4895-b232-5c9c8adfd9fe",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (b)\n\nExplanation:\n- 'Mother's husband' implies Woman's Father.\n- 'Brother of her father' implies Uncle.\n- 'Son of Uncle' implies Cousin."
    },
    {
      "id": "92542241-da87-4120-93c9-519cb94f8e59",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Question 3",
      "isBold": false,

    },
    {
      "id": "f576e649-904a-4295-90e1-ab69f44b39dc",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Trace the family relationship from husband to daughter's brother.\n\nQuestion: Pointing to a man in the photograph, Nikita said, 'He is the brother of the daughter of the wife of my husband'. How is the man in the photograph related to Nikita?",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e0f1e138-b9e2-4da9-9c88-aeba3d3a9808",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "(a) Son\n(b) Father\n(c) Husband\n(d) None of these",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,

    {
      "id": "04ce8341-0b04-4e25-8adb-a7212706bb4f",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (a)\n\nExplanation:\n- 'Wife of my husband' implies Nikita herself.\n- 'Daughter of Nikita' implies Nikita's daughter.\n- 'Brother of Nikita's daughter' implies Nikita's Son."
    },
    {
      "id": "b0d4bfe8-cb66-4ecf-baf6-3e2858748632",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Question 4",
      "isBold": false,

    },
    {
      "id": "d58b9f9b-5e98-41c9-b93c-d58d5f80f671",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Use the aunt reference statement to find the lady's relation to the man.\n\nQuestion: A man said to a lady, 'Your mother's husband's sister is my aunt'. How is the lady related to the man?",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2fcf3da3-93c9-4c67-b1ad-70444e175a36",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "(a) Sister\n(b) Mother\n(c) Cousin\n(d) Either (a) or (c)",

      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9bee2cf6-f939-4669-b53a-99ffe686432d",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (d)\n\nExplanation:\n- 'Lady's mother's husband' implies Lady's Father.\n- 'Father's sister' implies Lady's Aunt.\n- Since this aunt is also the man's aunt, the lady could be his Sister or Cousin."
    },
    {
      "id": "cd7edd17-ddde-44bc-b333-f6ecd96e8b8b",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Question 5",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,

    },
    {
      "id": "41ce21b2-dd6c-4594-9427-59ba48a4fbb6",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Break down the statement to determine the woman's relationship to the man.\n\nQuestion: Introducing a man to her husband, a woman said: 'His brother's father is the only son of my grandfather'. How is the woman related to that man?",
      "isBold": false,

      "isUnderline": false,

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b32d41e4-b497-4caa-b830-7ac05b6c59ec",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "(a) Mother\n(b) Sister\n(c) Cousin\n(d) Daughter",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,

      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c4869d8d-715b-4467-845c-7dc7404164d1",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (b)\n\nExplanation:\n- 'His brother's father' implies Man's Father.\n- 'Only son of my grandfather' implies Woman's Father.\n- Both share the same father, so the woman is his Sister."
    },
    {
      "id": "b0f7bea8-9fb3-49e6-8586-a4d3c2e0a9f9",

    {

      "text": "Instruction: Map the speaker's family relationship through son Mohan.\n\nQuestion: Pointing to Shyam, Kala said, 'His mother's brother is the father of my son Mohan'. How is Shyam related to Kala?",

      "text": "Instruction: Decode the generational description to find the relation of the lady to the girl.\n\nQuestion: Pointing out to a lady, a girl said, 'She is the only daughter-in-law of the grand mother of my father's only son'. How is the lady related to the girl?",

      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Position Calculation Formulas",
      "content": "- n-th letter to the left of m-th letter from right end = (m + n)-th letter from the right end.\n- n-th letter to the right of m-th letter from left end = (m + n)-th letter from the left end.\n- n-th letter to the left of m-th letter from left end = (m - n)-th letter from the left end.\n- n-th letter to the right of m-th letter from right end = (m - n)-th letter from the right end."

      "text": "Question: Three of the following four are alike in a certain way based on their positions in the above arrangement and so form a group. Which is the one that does not belong to that group?\n(a) G Ⓒ 3\n(b) X @ R\n(c) R * U\n(d) B # S",

      "content": "Correct Answer: (c)\n\nExplanation:\nAnalyzing positional gaps in the original series:\n- (a) G -> (+2) -> Ⓒ -> (+2) -> 3\n- (b) X -> (+2) -> @ -> (+2) -> R\n- (c) R -> (+3) -> * -> (+2) -> U [ODD ONE]\n- (d) B -> (+2) -> # -> (+2) -> S\n\nClearly, R * U is the odd one out as it uses a +3, +2 gap instead of +2, +2."

      "content": "A Venn diagram shows all possible logical relations among a given collection of sets or groups in a single visual layout using geometric shapes such as circles, triangles, squares, and rectangles."
    },

      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Venn diagram problems are broadly divided into two major categories: Relation-Based Venn Diagrams and Analysis-Based Venn Diagrams.",

      "text": "Instruction: Determine the subset\/disjoint relationship among the three items and choose the correct diagram.",

    {
      "id": "29cef36d-9894-4b08-95a5-8a5824df0b56",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Question: Which of the following diagrams best depicts the relationship among Table, Chair and Furniture?\n(a) Three intersecting circles\n(b) One large circle containing two separate inner circles\n(c) Three separate non-overlapping circles\n(d) Three overlapping circles in a line",

      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Answer & Explanation",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (b)\n\nExplanation: Table and Chair are completely distinct items from each other (disjoint sets), but both belong fully to the broader category of Furniture."
    },
    {

      "text": "Question: Which of the following diagrams best depicts the relationship among Seconds, Minutes and Hours?\n(a) Three separate circles\n(b) Three overlapping circles\n(c) Two small circles inside one circle\n(d) Three concentric circles",

    {
      "id": "307a5912-cb97-4de9-a74d-3b2e4dcd7146",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "INTRODUCTION TO ORDER AND SEQUENCE",
      "isBold": false,

    },
    {
      "id": "82010af9-61b6-4309-8198-555ae45a3d4d",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "What is Order and Sequence?",
      "content": "The process of determining the position or place of a person or a thing on the basis of comparison or relative position of other persons or things is called order and sequence. In these questions, relative positions or ranks of persons or objects are given. Students are required to find the position or rank of a person with respect to one another."
    },
    {
      "id": "775ff025-cc9e-45e2-8b0c-0eccd7ff0e07",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "IMPORTANT FORMULAS",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ee9099a9-e373-4e3d-94d7-b82618e7594d",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Total Number of Persons",
      "content": "Total number of persons in a row or class = (Rank from top\/left) + (Rank from bottom\/right) - 1"
    },
    {
      "id": "b986afc8-dfc7-45e2-b6c7-6a17a859a2ba",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Rank from Top or Left End",
      "content": "Rank from top or left end = (Total persons) - (Rank from bottom\/right) + 1"
    },
    {
      "id": "e87e387d-ffbc-4f64-b158-8d9195c425ed",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Rank from Bottom or Right End",
      "content": "Rank from bottom or right end = (Total persons) - (Rank from top\/left) + 1"
    },
    {
      "id": "d6d4a42c-dff1-472e-a077-0276ba8354e6",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "SOLVED EXAMPLES",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3360db14-799a-46d3-937d-f6ded853735e",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 1: Comparing Attributes",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "eebe0d8f-6f3d-49bc-8e1c-c057f3f6c1ba",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Compare the given attributes relative to each other to determine the extreme value.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f0dab9de-172d-407f-9a76-2cc5c5a9a421",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Question: In a group of five districts, Akbarpur is smaller than Fatehpur. Dhanbad is bigger than Palamu and Bara Banki is bigger than Fatehpur but not as big as Palamu. Which district is the biggest?\n(a) Akbarpur\n(b) Fatehpur\n(c) Dhanbad\n(d) Palamu",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ac544fc6-d91c-41c1-b14b-5e2134a0b656",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Correct Answer: (c)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d4eb547f-679f-4758-bee9-56918f6bbf5e",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Explanation: Comparing sizes step-by-step:\n- Fatehpur > Akbarpur\n- Dhanbad > Palamu\n- Palamu > Bara Banki > Fatehpur\n\nCombining all inequalities: Dhanbad > Palamu > Bara Banki > Fatehpur > Akbarpur.\n\nHence, Dhanbad district is the biggest amongst them.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "79602208-d7b7-44a2-945c-cd3be62cd359",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 2: Identical Ranks from Both Ends",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "bd031a8d-79be-401e-b516-955af642d0a0",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Apply the total count formula when the rank from both ends is identical.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c187faa9-c5e0-4129-b89b-33d678de1924",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Question: In a row of girls, Rina's rank is 11th from each end. How many girls are there in the row?\n(a) 20\n(b) 21\n(c) 22\n(d) 23",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "836604b2-ca44-45e7-b726-1a66b297a68a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Correct Answer: (b)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8a24616b-8838-445a-847e-ddd4993f7b2b",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Explanation: Using the formula:\nTotal = (Rank from Left) + (Rank from Right) - 1\nTotal = 11 + 11 - 1 = 21.\n\nTherefore, there are 21 girls in the row.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8927da9e-81f3-4ec6-89ff-a5ed0cf990f8",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 3: Calculating Reverse Rank",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "650ade6a-8056-4924-bb0b-a70dcd14687e",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Calculate the reverse rank using the total count and top rank.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "eec38dd3-9f14-4a9a-9030-3a4bff96884e",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Question: In a class of 42 students, Lokesh's rank is 16th from the top. What is his rank from the bottom?\n(a) 24\n(b) 25\n(c) 27\n(d) 26",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2864df58-20a4-44f8-8da9-8746641b822e",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Correct Answer: (c)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "34c1f4f4-e255-43f3-b9cd-f104b498dc97",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Explanation: Using the formula:\nRank from bottom = (Total students) - (Rank from top) + 1\nRank from bottom = 42 - 16 + 1 = 27.\n\nTherefore, his rank from the bottom is 27th.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "157a8a95-2861-4969-a1c0-61d499d34839",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 4: Linear Seating Arrangement",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "378a7c79-2adf-46e4-8c74-5bd836c92729",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Arrange persons linearly according to left\/right conditional instructions.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a9d44def-b054-4fc2-bc98-a6b26fbc64ce",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Question: A, P, R, X, S and Z are sitting in a row. S and Z are in the centre and A and P are at the ends. R is sitting to the left of A, S is sitting to the left of Z. Then, who is sitting on the right of P?\n(a) A\n(b) S\n(c) X\n(d) Z",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d87a523b-7819-44ce-8980-54a840aab567",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Correct Answer: (c)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "29d0100c-bcb0-4dba-b596-445a23d527c9",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Explanation:\n- A and P are at the ends. Since R is to the left of A, A must be at the extreme right end. So P is at the extreme left end.\n- S and Z are in the centre, with S to the left of Z (S Z).\n- Placing the remaining person X: P X S Z R A.\n\nClearly, X is sitting on the right of P.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fc8bb218-8fc8-4909-a13e-d569c8048668",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 5: Circular Seating Arrangement",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a02ac6b7-0b81-4d8d-9093-64d0babe10b9",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Map circular seating positions facing the centre to determine the facing direction.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "64e7f0d0-5ea7-4437-8a86-1d610b675690",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Question: A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting in a circle facing towards centre. D is between F and B. A is second to the left of D and second to the right of E. B is the immediate neighbour of E. Who is facing towards D?\n(a) C\n(b) A\n(c) E\n(d) B",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e88fdaf9-8d5b-42a7-a97e-b375ad7439be",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Correct Answer: (a)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7a38ce50-c7a8-4502-a999-6f013a94e9d8",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Explanation: Arranging 6 positions in a circle facing inward:\n- D is between F and B.\n- A is 2nd to the left of D.\n- A is 2nd to the right of E.\n- B is a neighbour of E.\n- C occupies the remaining position opposite D.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3ef3af05-3cdc-414f-9f26-0c858a906c10",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "FLOWCHART",
      "title": "Circular Seating Arrangement",
      "nodes": [
        "C (Top)",
        "F (Top-Left)",
        "E (Top-Right)",
        "A (Bottom-Left)",
        "B (Bottom-Right)",
        "D (Bottom)"
      ],
      "rawContent": "      C\n   F     E\n   A     B\n      D"
    },
    {
      "id": "9f0dce68-8c52-4fae-848b-e78c0c08be2d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Hence, C is facing directly towards D.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9d808fae-a07d-4e14-b18d-4dbacfef2d84",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "PRACTICE EXERCISE",
      "isBold": false,

    {
      "id": "d7e00d41-93d1-4fe4-a3b8-4009054a8937",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Question 1: Height Ordering",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ffb1469f-59d0-495f-adc9-249349364e7d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Order all individuals by height to find the middle person in descending order.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3f95eb61-d020-41a7-9139-9df4e1fa0c07",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Question: Shrikant is shorter than Nilima. Pratima is taller than Shrikant. Subhash is taller than Nilima but shorter than Heramb. Nilima is taller than Pratima. Who will be in the middle if they stand in a row according to descending order of height?\n(a) Pratima\n(b) Subhash\n(c) Shrikant\n(d) Nilima",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "68f158dd-bb04-428f-bad9-f1ae86689c99",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Correct Answer: (d)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5d724812-dfbe-4f5c-b979-c5fb0ebb7423",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Explanation: Height order:\n- Heramb > Subhash > Nilima\n- Nilima > Pratima > Shrikant\n\nDescending Order (5 people): Heramb > Subhash > Nilima > Pratima > Shrikant.\n\nThe person in the middle (3rd position) is Nilima.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9958236f-e1d1-46f7-a0cb-00ed12a67edb",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Question 2: Height Comparison",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "83305ab6-cb80-4d2f-ba2e-40d4d1c146ed",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Compare given height relations to evaluate the relation between Kalpana and Anita.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9cd2804a-083b-42ce-ae7e-66fb7fb9fa16",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Question: If Anita is taller than Surjit but shorter than Kusum and Surjit is just as tall as Kalpana but taller than Vanita, then Kalpana is:\n(a) just as tall as Anita\n(b) taller than Kusum\n(c) shorter than Anita\n(d) shorter than Surjit",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "964e0bec-8971-4902-a96e-e3a614cf4dad",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Correct Answer: (c)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e155f1fd-394c-4f17-9feb-e6d4d25d41aa",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Explanation:\n- Kusum > Anita > Surjit\n- Surjit = Kalpana > Vanita\n\nSince Anita > Surjit and Surjit = Kalpana, Kalpana is shorter than Anita.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "eb02c440-9ab0-42b8-b18c-876d15c5b64d",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Question 3: Age Ordering",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "355a4630-67a5-4e28-bce6-232fda80d228",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Order individuals by age to find the fourth person in descending order.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7753924d-ea03-4bea-9168-c2648563393a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Question: Among five friends, Mohan is older than Raju but not as old as Lalit. Lalit is older than Neelesh and Kabir. Neelesh is younger than Raju but not the youngest. Who is the fourth in the descending order of age?\n(a) Mohan\n(b) Raju\n(c) Kabir\n(d) Neelesh",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f90528a2-afb1-4f05-8e91-5accf73fcb33",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Correct Answer: (d)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ece85f7b-8872-4fe8-9ca3-648caf2de46d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Explanation: Age comparison:\n- Lalit > Mohan > Raju\n- Raju > Neelesh > Kabir (since Neelesh is not the youngest, Kabir must be the youngest).\n\nDescending Order: Lalit > Mohan > Raju > Neelesh > Kabir.\n\nThe 4th person in descending order is Neelesh.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9ffcf9e0-93ee-46f5-9426-2c0382eec04c",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Question 4: River Lengths",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "323d2472-934c-4d27-8123-a0f7a0dfae88",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Compare river lengths to find the shortest river.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b45cd159-c5ac-4a52-92e4-3c8aeb825b7b",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Question: A, B, C, D and E are five rivers. A is shorter than B but longer than E. C is the longest and D is little shorter than B and little longer than A. Which is the shortest river?\n(a) B\n(b) C\n(c) D\n(d) E",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "54d61ea8-3320-4147-a83c-65c019507d42",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Correct Answer: (d)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b3d53a0a-8d6b-49e6-8b3f-5f924bd8885d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Explanation: Comparing river lengths:\n- C is longest\n- B > D > A > E\n\nFull length sequence: C > B > D > A > E.\n\nThe shortest river is E.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ea98bf98-4c50-4c95-8d1e-4132a5fb45b3",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Question 5: Tallest Individual",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "09f874e6-c2e5-43f5-aca6-4ae209166d84",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Compare given height relations to identify the tallest individual.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "14179842-2c2c-4dda-a079-f88d01c5305e",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Question: Shyam is taller than Pradeep and Pradeep is equal to Anurag. But Anand is smaller than Suresh who is equal to Anurag. If Pradeep is taller than Praveen, who is the tallest of all?\n(a) Pradeep\n(b) Praveen\n(c) Suresh\n(d) Shyam",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "67b66903-dbff-49be-9a48-5535096d7de0",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Correct Answer: (d)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "96f37f2d-15f2-4fc4-8143-d83b8cba1eb0",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Explanation:\n- Shyam > Pradeep = Anurag = Suresh\n- Pradeep > Praveen\n- Suresh > Anand\n\nSince Shyam is taller than Pradeep (who is equal to Suresh and Anurag), Shyam is the tallest of all.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f9802d1c-a9c5-48a6-a129-0bc158fa46a0",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Question 6: Shortest Friend",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6314187e-9d28-454e-a51a-9288217ec7dc",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Order the five friends by height to identify the shortest friend.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c65552be-674a-4410-9d2a-263d199f87d4",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Question: There are five friends Suresh, Kaushal, Madhur, Amit and Ramesh. Suresh is shorter than Kaushal but taller than Ramesh. Madhur is the tallest. Amit is a little shorter than Kaushal but little taller than Suresh. If they stand in the order of their heights, who will be the shortest?\n(a) Amit\n(b) Madhur\n(c) Ramesh\n(d) Kaushal",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1919d2a5-5b42-4ca5-a055-3f6bb1582946",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Correct Answer: (c)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "83ceab02-2ad6-48ff-ad9a-9f9b29b04791",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Explanation: Height order: Madhur > Kaushal > Amit > Suresh > Ramesh.\n\nThe shortest person is Ramesh.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a1c8c0c4-41ec-47af-bd41-a9a805652eb6",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Question 7: Total Students Calculation",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "10d74a89-c70a-4fc4-9d8f-90d113e23976",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Calculate the total number of students given ranks from both ends.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "44aaed6d-58fe-424e-a004-676b5dd611f1",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Question: Sumit ranked ninth from top and thirty eighth from the bottom in a class. How many students are there in the class?\n(a) 47\n(b) 48\n(c) 45\n(d) 46",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ac9f93a0-aa8a-4a0e-bf76-83dc43d98ea7",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Correct Answer: (d)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "53d7ce9a-b18f-435e-8776-956d382636be",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Explanation: Total = (Rank from top) + (Rank from bottom) - 1\nTotal = 9 + 38 - 1 = 46.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e5de2829-cc41-4c3f-ab26-6ffed7417ef3",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Question 8: Queue Length Adjustment",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "13a9c969-275b-499d-a0c5-78aa8d8fe190",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Determine the current queue length first, then calculate additional boys needed to reach target total.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "05ea9604-8f7a-4db1-8d66-2f3d4866bb5c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Question: If Atul finds that he is twelfth from the right in a queue of boys and fourth from the left, how many boys should be added to the queue, so that there are 28 boys in the queue?\n(a) 12\n(b) 13\n(c) 14\n(d) 20",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c556c69f-bada-4498-9f1b-188381d69db8",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Correct Answer: (b)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1eaf8619-4619-4e73-9f9c-8753737c006f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Explanation:\n- Current total boys = 12 + 4 - 1 = 15.\n- Boys to be added = 28 - 15 = 13.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "09139d7b-8248-45dd-b861-c52b373a55d3",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Question 9: Total Boys in Class",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "64a05510-6d89-4f05-9257-304687503e41",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Combine passed candidates with non-participants and failed candidates to find total boys.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4760e9fe-cd4b-452a-b4f3-04af4c031439",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Question: Manish ranked sixteenth from the top and twenty ninth from the bottom among those who passed an examination. Six boys did not participate in the competition and five failed in it. How many boys were there in the class?\n(a) 40\n(b) 44\n(c) 50\n(d) 55",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "86c1901a-218b-45f3-a327-77b9a08d13ee",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Correct Answer: (d)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5bfffa53-f8c1-4a9a-afa1-05e517e5d57e",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Explanation:\n- Total passed = 16 + 29 - 1 = 44.\n- Total boys in class = Passed + Did not participate + Failed = 44 + 6 + 5 = 55.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5e478d38-fefa-4b20-9183-fb2c1e625c84",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Question 10: Reverse Rank Calculation",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6f9c0fb4-96b3-47d2-9fcd-6684229c3b1b",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Calculate reverse rank from the last given total class size and top rank.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6982c8b2-58c6-4c03-b69b-3f1bef1a8639",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Question: Aruna ranks twelfth in a class of forty six. What will be her rank from the last?\n(a) 33\n(b) 34\n(c) 35\n(d) 37",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2840936f-1749-4203-baac-6ba3e9ffd0a3",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Correct Answer: (c)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ab14c015-ed0f-4338-8f14-86a8149704f1",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Explanation: Rank from last = (Total students) - (Rank from top) + 1\nRank from last = 46 - 12 + 1 = 35.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },

    {

      "text": "Clockwise Movement: When a person moves in the direction of motion of a clock (e.g., North to East).",

      "title": "Shadow Rules",
      "content": "Morning (Sunrise in East): Shadow falls towards the West.\nEvening (Sunset in West): Shadow falls towards the East."

    {
      "id": "cbe833fe-5175-4297-a576-3bbc686cc18f",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "3. Shortest Distance (Pythagoras Theorem)",
      "isBold": false,

      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "46aee547-c8cc-443c-beb8-06c0da46ae7a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Displacement is the minimum distance between the initial and final position of a person.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b45af6eb-e81e-4010-9b81-b5609fada559",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Pythagoras Theorem Formula",
      "content": "AC² = AB² + BC² or AC = √(AB² + BC²)\nWhere AC is the shortest distance (hypotenuse), AB is the horizontal base, and BC is the vertical height."
    },
    {
      "id": "6ac4140b-5495-4d66-beec-3cd7f5b9051c",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Question Types & Solved Examples",

    },
    {
      "id": "968029d7-7d4d-4f4d-a084-fd6d6c1adb94",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Type 1: To Find the Direction",

    {
      "id": "b2401f60-e400-46a6-9695-fcf6e34e18a5",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The candidate is required to find the final direction during the course of a journey or the direction of one point with respect to another.",
