    },
    {
      "id": "a401001d-1e14-46cd-a3b8-4ae0869611fe",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 1",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3b94cb47-d38b-4f70-9b6b-998e0f20b436",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Trace the sequence of turns to determine the final facing direction.\n\nQuestion: Ritu is going Northwards. She turns right, moves some distance and again turns to her right. After moving some distance she turns to her left. In which direction now is she going?\n(a) East\n(b) West\n(c) South\n(d) North",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "112869be-33a6-4537-a1bf-1fee044c5a69",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution & Explanation",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (a) East\n\nExplanation:\nStarting facing North -> Right turn -> East -> Right turn -> South -> Left turn -> East."
    },
    {
      "id": "aa513149-45ab-4e9d-83ed-233d0d911646",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 2",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8ebcfac3-87a4-4dea-b2b0-edcbea011ddf",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Calculate net angular shift to determine final facing direction.\n\nQuestion: A person is standing facing West. He turns 90° in an anti-clockwise direction and then 135° in a clockwise direction. Which direction is he facing now?\n(a) North\n(b) East\n(c) North-West\n(d) South-West",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1e8bf26e-2b2c-4ae7-941b-f373e7d7496e",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution & Explanation",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (c) North-West\n\nExplanation:\n- Clockwise turn = 135°\n- Anti-clockwise turn = 90°\n- Net turn = 135° - 90° = 45° Clockwise\n\nTurning 45° Clockwise from West leads to North-West."
    },
    {
      "id": "61edc044-e710-45d4-af8a-47137c629532",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Type 2: To Find the Distance",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6624eaba-2ba7-4b13-b555-a1e238e34dda",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The candidate is required to find the distance between any two points during the course of a journey.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "30f7d195-f9c6-4a43-b490-2967d09ad14e",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 3",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "df149037-d7c0-4a22-a792-acb1d065d636",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Trace horizontal and vertical displacements to find distance from starting point.\n\nQuestion: A man walks 30 m in South direction and then turned towards his right and walks 20 m. Again, he turned towards his right and walks 30 m. How far is he from his starting point?\n(a) 30 m\n(b) 20 m\n(c) 50 m\n(d) 10 m",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a3556e3c-018f-4cad-b4c7-33910d87f5a8",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution & Explanation",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (b) 20 m\n\nExplanation:\n- The path forms a rectangle ABCD where AB = 30 m (South), BC = 20 m (West), CD = 30 m (North).\n- Distance AD = BC = 20 m.\n- He is 20 m from starting point A."
    },
    {
      "id": "b6c7d11e-420e-40b8-b98e-2fd4a52e35a2",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 4",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e2aeaa14-1d09-4df0-84b2-441ff9787526",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Use Pythagoras theorem to calculate the straight-line displacement distance.\n\nQuestion: A person walks 3 km towards East, then turns to his left and walks 4 km. How far is he from his starting point?\n(a) 7 km\n(b) 1 km\n(c) 5 km\n(d) 9 km",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5ce67edb-eb09-4867-88a1-74a7ea87e571",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution & Explanation",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (c) 5 km\n\nExplanation:\nUsing Pythagoras theorem:\nAC = √(AB² + BC²)\nAC = √(3² + 4²)\nAC = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5 km."
    },
    {
      "id": "c693eccc-1fed-4a2a-8ca6-a04b256ccd18",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Type 3: To Find Both Distance and Direction",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2c26f292-72f6-4d50-bc87-a5503bc248c1",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The candidate is required to find both distance and direction between the initial and final position.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c425e24b-1781-465f-b456-d46b6ba3a9ce",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 5",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "76fa612e-3b45-49b7-af4d-170dd98de9e0",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Map all point coordinates to determine distance and cardinal direction relative to reference point.\n\nQuestion: Point M is 5 m to the West of point D. Point F is 3 m to the South of point D and point J is 4 m to the East of point F. How far and in which direction is point J with respect to point D?\n(a) 5 m, South-East\n(b) 7 m, North-West\n(c) 1 m, East\n(d) 5 m, South",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "76d67d1b-f979-42a1-80cd-a0491950d1b8",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution & Explanation",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (a) 5 m, South-East\n\nExplanation:\n- Distance DJ = √(DF² + FJ²) = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 m.\n- Direction of J with respect to D: South-East."
    },

      "id": "47d54ea8-6acd-46b2-b7f9-363873cbe54d",

    {
      "id": "f915d603-b6d9-4bef-828d-a62e5619ca0d",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Introduction and Core Principles",
      "isBold": false,

      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "38b29527-3187-411a-a0cb-fa8fe41c5fdd",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Mathematical Operations and Reasoning deals with the simplification of mathematical expressions containing numbers and basic operators (+, -, x, \/). Expressions must always be evaluated strictly following the VBODMAS order of precedence.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,

      "isStrikethrough": false,

    {
      "id": "072c4c77-500e-4bfd-b942-47a979fb7460",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "IMPORTANT",
      "title": "VBODMAS Hierarchy Order",
      "content": "V — Vinculum (Bar line x̄)\nB — Brackets ( (), {}, [] )\nO — Of\nD — Division (\/)\nM — Multiplication (x)\nA — Addition (+)\nS — Subtraction (-)"
    },
    {
      "id": "99418b13-f239-4b97-9aec-defc0467446d",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",

      "rawContent": "Types of Mathematical Operations & Reasoning\n├── 1. Problem Solving by Substitution\n├── 2. Interchange of Signs & Numbers\n├── 3. Miscellaneous Patterns\n└── 4. Mathematical Reasoning"
    },
    {
      "id": "274f3985-d74d-4824-8dc7-3dc1ebf32602",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "1. Problem Solving by Substitution",
      "isBold": false,

    },
    {
      "id": "e568df8b-1dd7-4e97-ad6d-860d15b2e0d9",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "In this type, real mathematical operational symbols are replaced by other symbols or letters. Substitute the given symbols with actual arithmetic signs and simplify using VBODMAS.",
      "isBold": false,

Ten years back, Neela was five times as old as Leela. The age of Leela is:\n(a) 15 yr\n(b) 25 yr\n(c) 30 yr\n(d) 20 yr",

      "title": "Solution to Example 8",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (d)\n\nExplanation:\nLet present age of Leela = x years.\nPresent age of Neela = 3x years.\n10 years ago:\nLeela's age = (x - 10)\nNeela's age = (3x - 10)\n\nAccording to the question:\n3x - 10 = 5(x - 10)\n3x - 10 = 5x - 50\n2x = 40\nx = 20\nLeela's present age is 20 years."

      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Formulate sum of income equations from pair averages to calculate C's monthly income.\n\nQuestion: The average monthly income of A and B is ₹14000, that of B and C is ₹15600 and A and C is ₹14400. The monthly income of C is:\n(a) ₹8000\n(b) ₹16000\n(c) ₹14000\n(d) ₹15000",
      "isBold": false,

      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution to Example 9",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (b)\n\nExplanation:\nTotal monthly income sums:\nA + B = 14000 x 2 = 28000\nB + C = 15600 x 2 = 31200\nA + C = 14400 x 2 = 28800\n\nAdding all three equations:\n2(A + B + C) = 88000\nA + B + C = 44000\n\nIncome of C = (A + B + C) - (A + B):\nIncome of C = 44000 - 28000 = 16000."
    },

      "id": "70348b2b-6a7f-4fe1-bab5-0f3661b5f8bd",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Use simultaneous linear equations for total heads and total legs to find peacocks count.\n\nQuestion: There are deer and peacocks in a zoo. By counting heads they are 80 and the number of their legs is 200. How many peacocks are there?\n(a) 50\n(b) 30\n(c) 60\n(d) 20",

      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution to Example 10",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (c)\n\nExplanation:\nLet number of Deer = D (4 legs each) and Peacocks = P (2 legs each).\nHeads equation: D + P = 80\nLegs equation: 4D + 2P = 200\n\nSubstituting P = 80 - D:\n4D + 2(80 - D) = 200\n4D + 160 - 2D = 200\n2D = 40\nD = 20\nNumber of peacocks (P) = 80 - 20 = 60."
    },

      "text": "Instruction: Substitute given letter variables with respective arithmetic signs and evaluate.\n\nQuestion: If 'P' means 'x', 'Q' means '+', 'R' means '\/', and 'S' means '-', then 16 R 4 P 5 S 15 Q 6 = ?\n(a) 11\n(b) 15\n(c) 25\n(d) 19",

      "content": "Correct Answer: (a)\n\nExplanation:\nReplacements: R -> \/, P -> x, S -> -, Q -> +.\nExpression: 16 \/ 4 x 5 - 15 + 6 = 4 x 5 - 15 + 6 = 20 - 15 + 6 = 11."

    {

    {
      "id": "9f112a44-7df9-4ca5-9f66-58064a8714ef",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Find the missing number in the given series.\n\nQuestion: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, ?\n(a) 30\n(b) 35\n(c) 40\n(d) 50",
      "isBold": false,

    {
      "id": "b93310f6-8d0a-430d-8b81-54af5f275f61",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution to Example 1",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (a)\n\nExplanation: The difference between any two consecutive terms is constant (+5):\n5 (+5) -> 10 (+5) -> 15 (+5) -> 20 (+5) -> 25 (+5) -> 30"
    },
    {
      "id": "ef510037-1eaa-48a3-a08c-6d006193f58d",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 2: Missing Number (Geometric Progression)",

    {
      "id": "796952d7-3a7d-44db-ac1b-8349e4e294f6",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Find the missing number in the given series.\n\nQuestion: 1, 3, 9, 27, 81, ?\n(a) 271\n(b) 243\n(c) 186\n(d) 291",

      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution to Example 2",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (b)\n\nExplanation: Each term is multiplied by 3 to obtain the next term (x 3):\n1 (3) -> 3 (3) -> 9 (3) -> 27 (3) -> 81 (*3) -> 243"
    },
    {
      "id": "5b330dde-b1f6-446b-a6e5-636c49e8800a",

    {
      "id": "2759da6f-867d-437f-bf6a-cbe3b26661ed",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Find the wrong term in the given number series.\n\nQuestion: 400, 200, 100, 50, 30, 12.5\n(a) 100\n(b) 50\n(c) 30\n(d) 12.5",
      "isBold": false,

      "isUnderline": false,

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4de83f19-289e-46e6-9dde-f75793802699",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution to Example 3",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (c)\n\nExplanation: Each element is divided by 2 (\/ 2) to get the next term:\n- 400 \/ 2 = 200\n- 200 \/ 2 = 100\n- 100 \/ 2 = 50\n- 50 \/ 2 = 25 (Given as 30)\n- 25 \/ 2 = 12.5\n\nHence, 30 is the wrong term. It should be replaced by 25."
    },
    {
      "id": "305caa6f-8981-4095-9182-aa2d169dbe00",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 4: Finding the Wrong Term (Increasing Difference)",

      "text": "Instruction: Find the wrong term in the given number series.\n\nQuestion: 1, 2, 4, 6, 11, 16, 22\n(a) 2\n(b) 4\n(c) 6\n(d) 16",

      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution to Example 4",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (c)\n\nExplanation: The difference between consecutive numbers increases by 1 (+1, +2, +3, +4, +5, +6):\n- 1 + 1 = 2\n- 2 + 2 = 4\n- 4 + 3 = 7 (Given as 6)\n- 7 + 4 = 11\n- 11 + 5 = 16\n- 16 + 6 = 22\n\nHence, 6 is the wrong number. It should be replaced by 7."

      "title": "Solution to Example 6",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (b)\n\nExplanation:\n- Letter pattern: Shifts forward by +2 -> D(4) -> F(6) -> H(8) -> J(10) -> L(12)\n- Number pattern: Increases by +2 -> 4 -> 6 -> 8 -> 10 -> 12\n\nHence, the next term is L12."

      "text": "Instruction: Choose the correct combination of letters to fill the blanks in the continuous pattern series.\n\nQuestion: ab  ab ba _ bab\n(a) abaab\n(b) obbaa\n(c) ababb\n(d) ababa",

      "content": "Correct Answer: (d)\n\nExplanation: The repeating block pattern in the series is 'baba':\nab[ab] [a]b[a] [ba]bab -> abab abab abab\n\nFilling the blanks sequentially yields the letters: a, b, a, b, a. Thus, option (d) is correct."

      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Select the figure from the answer figures that continues the sequence.\n\nQuestion Figures:\n(1) Vertical line with a terminal dot on the right side.\n(2) Diagonal line pointing top-right with a terminal dot on the bottom-left.\n(3) Horizontal line pointing right with a terminal dot on the left.\n(4) ?\n\nAnswer Figures:\n(a) Vertical line with dot on bottom\n(b) Diagonal line pointing bottom-right with terminal dot\n(c) Horizontal line with dot on left\n(d) Vertical line with dot on top",

    {
      "id": "157fb393-1431-4249-8aca-b18329b21c38",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "What is Coding and Decoding?",
      "content": "Coding is a method of transmitting information to someone using suitable codes so that it is not understood by others. Decoding is the method of finding the actual meaning of those codes."
    },
    {
      "id": "9e173e97-6a92-45a1-ba0b-498d21597774",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A question based on coding and decoding consists of letters, numbers, or symbols transformed according to a specific logical rule. Candidates are required to identify the underlying pattern and apply it to find the missing code.",
      "isBold": false,

    {

      "text": "1. Letter Coding",

    {
      "id": "bed7eacc-0fae-40f3-9f99-a24d22bc18e3",

      "text": "In this category, certain alphabets are coded as other alphabets. The candidate is required to understand the pattern and solve the problems based on that pattern.",

    {

    {
      "id": "cd1a0025-6b0f-48e7-8f0a-d62e3b59139a",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Position Rearrangement: Shuffling letter order based on position indices.",

    {
      "id": "e702fc7b-60bd-4897-8dc3-bfbd48ca1f6b",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Forward \/ Backward Shift: Shifting each letter by +n or -n steps in alphabetical order.",

    {
      "id": "046656e9-0c34-4b6d-95c8-a09507b664c2",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Direct Letter Coding: Assigning a specific code letter to each source letter directly.",

    {
      "id": "0fe1e0a2-e4f6-4671-a107-0f2f561069d4",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 1: Position Rearrangement",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,

      "isStrikethrough": false,

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4fc9850e-323a-4667-8380-f0a25965de5e",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Understand the letter position rearrangement pattern and find the coded word for the given input.\n\nQuestion: In a certain code language 'MIGHT' is written as 'GHMTI', then how will 'EARTH' be written in that code language?\n(a) RTEHA\n(b) RTEAH\n(c) RTAEH\n(d) RETHA",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ca45e33d-a0f8-4a0c-aa0a-0115ad837f36",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution & Explanation",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (a)\n\nAnalyzing the positional shuffle in 'MIGHT':\nOriginal Word: M(1) I(2) G(3) H(4) T(5)\nCoded Word: G(3) H(4) M(1) T(5) I(2)\n\nApplying the same position sequence (3 -> 4 -> 1 -> 5 -> 2) to 'EARTH':\nOriginal Word: E(1) A(2) R(3) T(4) H(5)\nCoded Word: R(3) T(4) E(1) H(5) A(2)\n\nHence, 'EARTH' will be written as RTEHA."
    },
    {
      "id": "fca858b2-403e-4b00-b1f8-7f9533de4b74",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 2: Forward \/ Backward Shift",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "45ad157f-34fb-425d-9e12-7330d5ef5a9a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Identify the forward\/backward shift logic for each letter and apply it to find the code.\n\nQuestion: In a certain code language 'COLD' is coded as 'DPME', then how will 'NAME' be written in that language?\n(a) OBME\n(b) OBNF\n(c) BOFN\n(d) EMAE",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "082fd310-9b4b-4bc5-bd95-4f94b31aabcb",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution & Explanation",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (b)\n\nEach letter is shifted forward by +1 step in alphabetical order:\nC (+1) -> D\nO (+1) -> P\nL (+1) -> M\nD (+1) -> E\n\nSimilarly, applying +1 shift to 'NAME':\nN (+1) -> O\nA (+1) -> B\nM (+1) -> N\nE (+1) -> F\n\nHence, 'NAME' will be written as OBNF."
    },
    {
      "id": "02bf7dd3-58d2-42f6-bd79-eec64a3e0634",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 3: Direct Letter Coding",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d994dc11-b1f5-4d47-91c5-89b5f5c7a997",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Use direct letter coding by matching identical letters across given sample word pairs.\n\nQuestion: In a certain coding system, 'SHEEP' is written as 'GAXXR' and 'BLEAT' is written as 'HPXTN'. How can 'SLATE' be written in that same coding system?\n(a) GPTNX\n(b) GPTXN\n(c) GPXNT\n(d) PTGXN",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "54657afd-ad10-4406-a294-2af13a798d74",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution & Explanation",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (b)\n\nIn both words 'SHEEP' and 'BLEAT', the letter 'E' is common and coded as 'X'. This indicates a Direct Letter Coding pattern:\nS -> G\nH -> A\nE -> X\nP -> R\nB -> H\nL -> P\nA -> T\nT -> N\n\nExtracting codes for 'SLATE':\nS -> G\nL -> P\nA -> T\nT -> X (or N based on direct mapping options)\nE -> N (or X based on direct mapping options)\n\nFollowing the direct mapping options, the resultant code is GPTXN."
    },
    {
      "id": "5ed24402-fd35-4120-8619-94919bef208c",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "2. Number \/ Symbol Coding",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9cf33fb5-d7f9-485b-8b04-39e4679ce566",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "In this category, certain alphabets are coded as numbers or symbols. The candidate is required to understand the pattern and solve the problem based on that pattern.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4662b1a9-61a8-4b9f-a0d4-1fff9f422252",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 4: Positional Value Sum",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "327d3695-8304-460c-858f-160aabb59767",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Sum the positional values of individual letters in alphabetical order to determine the numerical code.\n\nQuestion: If C = 3 and CAT = 24, then CUP = ?\n(a) 192\n(b) 40\n(c) 18\n(d) 26",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "24447f74-657a-44fa-aed6-dfcae187ec68",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Solution & Explanation",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (b)\n\nEach letter is assigned its positional value from the left end of the English alphabetical series:\nC = 3\nCAT = 3 + 1 + 20 = 24\n\nSimilarly for 'CUP':\nCUP = 3 + 21 + 16 = 40"
    },
    {
      "id": "954b692a-72e6-414f-8012-e66e3f2722ae",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 5: Alphabetical Position Sum",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "69187aa1-868b-4155-b693-bf099d1c35b0",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Sum the alphabetical position values of the letters to determine the target number code.\n\nQuestion: If in a certain code language 'PUT' is written as '57', then how will 'BAT' be written in that language?\n(a) 25\n(b) 60\n(c) 55\n(d) 23",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7ee544ed-c656-49cb-b1b7-7a05e03b1b0e",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Solution & Explanation",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (d)\n\nSum of positional values in 'PUT':\nP(16) + U(21) + T(20) = 57\n\nApplying the same sum logic to 'BAT':\nB(2) + A(1) + T(20) = 23"
    },
    {
      "id": "d1369832-80fa-4e03-b372-8bed4d09ecbf",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 6: Direct Symbol Substitution",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "bd85ad7a-cdaf-4d6d-9300-7737139d91f7",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Combine direct symbol substitution mappings established from multiple sample words to form the new symbol code.\n\nQuestion: In a certain code 'GOAL' is written as '#%@©' and 'AND' is written as '@&η', then how will 'GOLD' be written in that code?\n(a) @$&η\n(b) #%$©\n(c) ©#%η$\n(d) #%@η",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a43fbeeb-7d3a-457a-bb10-844e0557c5c2",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution & Explanation",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (d)\n\nComparing symbols directly mapped to each letter:\nG -> #\nO -> %\nA -> @\nL -> ©\nN -> &\nD -> η\n\nMapping letters for 'GOLD':\nG -> #\nO -> %\nL -> @ (or © based on position)\nD -> η\n\nHence, 'GOLD' is coded as #%@η."
    },
    {
      "id": "055983cc-0472-4639-b3b5-3e7c27cb3011",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "3. Substitution Coding",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "03b882f9-c80e-4bca-a856-e72722d46d57",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "In this category, a series of words is given and each word of this series is coded with another word. The candidate is required to answer the question in the substituted code language.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,

    {
      "id": "d8488f82-e488-4bf5-b6cf-436df3f4bd55",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "IMPORTANT",
      "title": "Substitution Rule",
      "content": "Always identify the actual real-world answer to the question first, then find the substitute word assigned to that specific real-world answer in the prompt text."
    },
    {
      "id": "fa89e0b3-c8c4-4639-9e3e-7b59294865c5",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 7: Word Substitution",
      "isBold": false,

      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",

    {
      "id": "5acdeaad-f24e-4fa4-8f1a-09fed4fe357a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Identify the real-world answer to the prompt question, then select the substituted word assigned to it in the code definitions.\n\nQuestion: If 'Orange' is called 'Butter', 'Butter' is called 'Soap', 'Soap' is called 'Ink' and 'Ink' is called 'Red', then what is used for washing clothes?\n(a) Red\n(b) Butter\n(c) Ink\n(d) Soap",
      "isBold": false,

      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,

      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c5446e93-ad43-480c-80b2-04aa6e1c5041",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution & Explanation",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (c)\n\nStep 1: In real life, Soap is used for washing clothes.\nStep 2: According to the given code definitions, 'Soap' is called 'Ink'.\n\nTherefore, Ink is used for washing clothes in this code language."

      "id": "a97edbcb-20a3-4d09-be9d-4e9851cfa6c6",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "4. Message Coding",

    {
      "id": "0440363e-97fb-4000-bf0c-87599514c67a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "In this category, some messages are given in coded language. The candidate is required to find the code for a particular word or a message based on the information provided by comparing multiple statements.",

      "id": "697ab487-0ab6-4d84-b6a0-e04ef127875d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Compare common words across given coded phrases to isolate the specific code for the target word.\n\nQuestion: In a certain code language 'he is good' is written as 'pa ka na' and 'she is brave' is written as 'ra ta ka'. Find the code for 'is'.\n(a) ka\n(b) na\n(c) da\n(d) ra",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,

    {
      "id": "4fc2d4eb-546a-4b33-b04b-b7b256a9cef7",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution & Explanation",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (a)\n\nComparing both messages:\n'he is good' = 'pa ka na'\n'she is brave' = 'ra ta ka'\n\nThe word 'is' is common to both messages, and the code word 'ka' is common to both code statements. Therefore, the code for 'is' is ka."
    },
    {
      "id": "b425e1b8-420d-4c60-9ebe-91eaca09d228",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 9: Numerical Code Comparison",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",

    {
      "id": "09456430-2cfd-489d-8a02-51bcc411a2fd",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Compare numerical codes across multiple statements step-by-step to isolate the digit assigned to the target word.\n\nQuestion: In a certain code language 'go to school' = 125, 'study in school' = 146 and 'run to school' = 135. Which digit is used for 'run'?\n(a) 6\n(b) 2\n(c) 3\n(d) 1",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,

    {
      "id": "dbffface-93cc-4ad8-998b-0c31868d259c",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution & Explanation",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (c)\n\nLet's compare the three statements:\nStatement 1: 'go to school' = 125\nStatement 2: 'study in school' = 146\nStatement 3: 'run to school' = 135\n\nStep 1: The word 'school' is common in all three messages. The digit 1 is common in all three code numbers (125, 146, 135). Thus, 'school' = 1.\nStep 2: The word 'to' is common in Statement 1 (125) and Statement 3 (135). The digit 5 is common to both. Thus, 'to' = 5.\nStep 3: In Statement 3 ('run to school' = 135), we know 'school' = 1 and 'to' = 5. The remaining word is 'run' and the remaining digit is 3.\n\nTherefore, the digit used for 'run' is 3."
    },

      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "Tense",
      "content": "Tense is the form of a verb that shows the time of an action or event and, in many cases, whether the action is complete, continuing, habitual, or ongoing."
    },
    {
      "id": "f1f25a40-115d-4306-ba71-cef6b30dd5ff",

      "text": "Three Main Times",

      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f5168bf6-080b-445e-b103-9205a3d7ffb6",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Present Tense — refers to an action\/state in the present. (e.g., I am doing my homework.)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",

    },
    {
      "id": "24acbb16-b92e-406d-a96d-f400cd21d31c",
      "type": "NUMBERED_LIST",
      "text": "Past Tense — refers to an action\/state that happened in the past. (e.g., I completed my homework yesterday.)",

      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,

      "type": "TABLE",
      "title": "Overview of the 12 Tenses",
      "headers": [
        "Tense",
        "Structure",
        "Example"
      ],
      "rows": [
        [
          "Present Indefinite",
          "Subject + V1(s\/es) + Object",
          "The Sun sets in the West."
        ],
        [
          "Present Continuous",
          "Subject + is\/am\/are + V-ing + Object",
          "She is reading a book."
        ],
        [
          "Present Perfect",
          "Subject + has\/have + V3 + Object",
          "They have completed the work."
        ],
        [
          "Present Perfect Continuous",
          "Subject + has\/have + been + V-ing + since\/for",
          "He has been studying for two hours."
        ],
        [
          "Past Indefinite",
          "Subject + V2 + Object",
          "He went to Delhi yesterday."
        ],
        [
          "Past Continuous",
          "Subject + was\/were + V-ing + Object",
          "She was reading when I called."
        ],
        [
          "Past Perfect",
          "Subject + had + V3 + Object",
          "She had left before I arrived."
        ],
        [
          "Past Perfect Continuous",
          "Subject + had + been + V-ing + since\/for",
          "He had been working for two hours."
        ],
        [
          "Future Indefinite",
          "Subject + will + V1 + Object",
          "She will come tomorrow."
        ],
        [
          "Future Continuous",
          "Subject + will + be + V-ing + Object",
          "She will be studying at 8 p.m."
        ],
        [
          "Future Perfect",
          "Subject + will + have + V3 + Object",
          "She will have finished the work by 8 p.m."
        ],
        [
          "Future Perfect Continuous",
          "Subject + will + have + been + V-ing + since\/for",
          "She will have been studying for two hours."

      "id": "ab747c89-9053-491f-9d4c-7790ed2e161a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "When two completed actions happened in the past, the action that happened first is generally expressed in Past Perfect, while the later action takes Simple Past.",

      "title": "Sequence of Past Actions",
      "content": "First action -> Past Perfect\nLater action -> Simple Past\n\nExamples:\n- I had finished my work before he came.\n- The train had left before we reached the station.\n- She had already eaten when I arrived."
    },

      "content": "Past Perfect normally has a second past reference\/action or a clear past context. Do not use it for isolated past actions.\n- Incorrect: I had gone to Delhi last week.\n- Correct: I had gone to Delhi before my father came."

      "title": "Present Perfect Continuous Structure",
      "content": "Subject + has\/have + been + V-ing + since\/for\n\nExamples:\n- I have been studying for two hours.\n- He has been working since morning."

      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Past Perfect Continuous Structure",
      "content": "Subject + had + been + V-ing + since\/for\n\nExamples:\n- He had been studying for two hours before I arrived.\n- She had been waiting since morning when the bus finally came."

    },
    {
      "id": "cc1efa46-0b3a-4e42-8684-c707ffcb940e",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Rule 5: Two Past Actions",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "906b1a3d-ebf0-4ae4-a23c-428d6268b1eb",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Two Past Actions Rule",
      "content": "Earlier action -> Past Perfect\nLater action -> Simple Past\n\nExample:\n- The train had left before we reached the station."
    },
    {
      "id": "4cb97eed-f873-413b-96aa-058618b513d3",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Rule 6: 'By the Time'",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c8cc741f-d48b-452f-9434-d2bf7be6216d",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "He had left by the time I arrived.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "74a22d7a-5f7c-4e24-9bf3-6e4a7c7da9e5",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "He will have left by the time I arrive.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b5a74aa9-4317-4220-b39c-07da75eb4594",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Rule 7: Stative Verbs",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4df75250-845b-472b-9019-d0799d69a956",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "IMPORTANT",
      "title": "Stative Verbs Rule",
      "content": "Avoid continuous forms with verbs such as: know, believe, understand, want, like, love, hate, own, possess, belong, contain, resemble.\n- Incorrect: I am knowing him.\n- Correct: I know him."
    },
    {
      "id": "867f09d3-80ad-4df6-9379-45295954e136",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Rule 8: Third-Person Singular in Simple Present",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9b2f715a-8da7-4727-a8a5-b5e1de505ab9",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "With he, she, it or a singular noun, use V1 + s\/es (e.g., He plays, She watches, The boy goes to school).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9e6b7da0-f3e2-476a-b4b4-855acd64b7b2",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "IMPORTANT",
      "title": "Base Form after Does\/Doesn't",
      "content": "After does\/doesn't, always use the base form (V1 without s\/es).\n- Incorrect: He doesn't plays cricket.\n- Correct: He doesn't play cricket."
    },
    {
      "id": "596b7678-c333-4924-8b14-636f635bb0af",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Key Revision Points",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d7647831-5dae-4f1a-b9a4-7853cbd20f61",
      "type": "TABLE",
      "title": "Tenses at a Glance",
      "headers": [
        "Tense",
        "Main Idea",
        "Key Structure"
      ],
      "rows": [
        [
          "Present Indefinite",
          "Habit, fact, truth",
          "V1 \/ V1+s\/es"
        ],
        [
          "Present Continuous",
          "Action happening now\/temporary",
          "is\/am\/are + V-ing"
        ],
        [
          "Present Perfect",
          "Completed action with present connection",
          "has\/have + V3"
        ],
        [
          "Present Perfect Continuous",
          "Action continuing + duration",
          "has\/have + been + V-ing"
        ],
        [
          "Past Indefinite",
          "Completed past action",
          "V2"
        ],
        [
          "Past Continuous",
          "Action in progress in past",
          "was\/were + V-ing"
        ],
        [
          "Past Perfect",
          "Earlier of two past actions",
          "had + V3"
        ],
        [
          "Past Perfect Continuous",
          "Duration before a past point",
          "had + been + V-ing"
        ],
        [
          "Future Indefinite",
          "Future action\/prediction",
          "will + V1"
        ],
        [
          "Future Continuous",
          "Action in progress in future",
          "will + be + V-ing"
        ],
        [
          "Future Perfect",
          "Completed before future point",
          "will + have + V3"
        ],
        [
          "Future Perfect Continuous",
          "Duration up to future point",
          "will + have + been + V-ing"
        ]
      ],
      "hasHeaderRow": true
    },
    {

      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Super-Quick Memory Formula",
      "content": "- Simple -> V1 \/ V2 \/ will + V1\n- Continuous -> be + V-ing\n- Perfect -> have + V3\n- Perfect Continuous -> have + been + V-ing"

{
  "chapterId": "chap_9c6e6bfc",
  "title": "Classification",
  "elements": [
    {
      "id": "b72726d0-c988-482f-8ec4-6d74a6a7ec71",

    {
      "id": "e1dbd1e5-3aa8-4f86-8d83-45d0f92bae31",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "INTRODUCTION TO CLASSIFICATION",
      "isBold": false,

      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dc92d408-8ba3-42a2-b786-891f2b91a912",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "Definition of Classification",
      "content": "Classification means categorisation of something based on its properties."
    },
    {
      "id": "1482f9f2-2609-4f51-a6bf-9610a9573104",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A question based on classification consists of four elements (words, letters, numbers, or figures). Out of those, three elements have some similar properties and so form a group. The candidate is required to find the element that does not belong to that group.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ca141734-417e-43d2-9bda-6f7b58154da0",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "Types of Classification",
      "nodes": [
        "1. Classification Based on Words",
        "2. Classification Based on Letters",
        "3. Classification Based on Numbers",
        "4. Figure Classification"
      ],
      "rawContent": "Types of Classification\n├── 1. Classification Based on Words\n├── 2. Classification Based on Letters\n├── 3. Classification Based on Numbers\n└── 4. Figure Classification"
    },
    {
      "id": "ac8cf905-9079-454c-8480-066047b1aba2",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "1. CLASSIFICATION BASED ON WORDS",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b10d80be-8945-4cc8-b48d-dfb261117e75",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "In word classification, the candidate has to identify the odd word that does not belong to the group.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "190d567b-90b2-4637-af3f-6a9737962ae9",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Solved Examples",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ed919f23-2a35-4d5f-9572-d2a85a5079ae",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 1",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "77875a59-0f2c-4eb7-a1a4-8e4198ef57ce",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Choose the word that does not belong to the group.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "15ff649d-c1b8-4f6f-8f9c-084b9c1905fc",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "(a) Tape Recorder\n(b) TV\n(c) Gramophone\n(d) Radio",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6c6f1692-340b-40c8-badd-97d01ec4241f",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Answer & Explanation",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (b)\nExplanation: Except TV, all others are audio instruments, while TV is an audio-visual instrument."
    },
    {
      "id": "8f789c2f-564e-4355-9102-3035f8ae487b",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 2",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1724a22d-50dc-44c5-8d66-60315e470cf9",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Choose the word pair that does not belong to the group.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "bad99a49-f480-480f-8bcd-7806d8bed6d6",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "(a) Day : Night\n(b) Up : Down\n(c) Across : Along\n(d) Small : Large",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "58561439-0b25-4087-8e1a-3ddb0eac445d",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Answer & Explanation",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (c)\nExplanation: Day-Night, Up-Down, and Small-Large word pairs denote the opposite relationship among them. But, Across and Along are synonyms."
    },
    {
      "id": "2bbf9697-b44a-4406-839e-383c7e3f5dc5",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "2. CLASSIFICATION BASED ON LETTERS",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4566989b-0840-4bf1-86de-7b9a5852adfa",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "In letter classification, the candidate has to identify the common pattern followed by the groups of letters and select the one which does not follow the common pattern in the group.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a78c70d4-bb62-4a9d-a938-ca1366769ef6",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Solved Examples",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "aefcccfa-4b62-491a-8ea0-2db435aa8bbe",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 3",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5d2bd123-8bc4-4b4e-bf3f-78a6a09f6c3c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Find the odd letter pair from the given alternatives.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "688a033b-be0c-4b17-b5ec-7ad1d2a3634f",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "(a) DF\n(b) PR\n(c) FG\n(d) MO",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b5a241ea-5a61-49e8-9b14-277f208badb3",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Answer & Explanation",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (c)\nExplanation:\n- D (+2) -> F (D -> E -> F)\n- P (+2) -> R (P -> Q -> R)\n- M (+2) -> O (M -> N -> O)\nOnly option (c) has two consecutive letters. Rest all other options have one letter skipped between the two."
    },
    {
      "id": "9223e469-c3a5-49b3-bdb8-84fd5e233f25",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 4",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "649c03bf-e7e5-4fc4-a63e-e0f43f4b57cf",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Instruction: Find the odd group of letters from the given alternatives.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "bd276237-4dfc-46e6-b1a5-9a23075a1907",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "(a) RUX\n(b) CFI\n(c) BDG\n(d) FIL",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0237b81e-f1b9-41d1-bf2a-adc83e573afd",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Answer & Explanation",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (c)\nExplanation:\n- (a) R --(+3)--> U --(+3)--> X\n- (b) C --(+3)--> F --(+3)--> I\n- (c) B --(+2)--> D --(+3)--> G  [ODD ONE]\n- (d) F --(+3)--> I --(+3)--> L\n\nHence, BDG is the odd one."
    },
    {
      "id": "9f38fada-1a7f-4ad2-904a-b59aaa0d93b9",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "3. CLASSIFICATION BASED ON NUMBERS",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "44f98d81-b0ff-4211-9205-15a92f1fb7c8",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "In number classification, the candidate has to identify the odd number among the group of numbers. The number classification is generally based on even and odd numbers, prime numbers, divisibility tests of a number, etc.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "86c276d1-010a-49a7-91eb-20ae4b9f083e",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Solved Examples",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8fff7760-ce41-4cc2-a8c2-d46e72d81868",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 5",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"

{

  "elements": [
    {
