    },
    {
      "id": "6d73424e-d3cc-481f-b9a2-ee457f3d243f",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "Definition of Ratio",
      "content": "A ratio is the number of times one quantity contains another quantity of the same kind. Alternatively, it is the fraction that one quantity is of another in the same units. It is written as a : b = a\/b, where 'a' is the antecedent (first term) and 'b' is the consequent (second term)."
    },
    {
      "id": "d07b8934-b0e8-4d0a-9073-8c8dcbd4add4",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "Definition of Proportion",
      "content": "A proportion is the expression of equality between two ratios. It is written as a : b :: c : d, which implies a\/b = c\/d."
    },
    {
      "id": "92ac45a1-2373-4840-b414-7dff5149b2e4",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "PROPERTIES OF RATIO",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "27ec0bfe-5c8d-43fb-8aa3-bacc3e75edcd",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "FLOWCHART",
      "title": "Types of Derived Ratios",
      "nodes": [
        "Duplicate Ratio (a² : b²)",
        "Sub-duplicate Ratio (√a : √b)",
        "Triplicate Ratio (a³ : b³)",
        "Sub-triplicate Ratio (∛a : ∛b)",
        "Inverse Ratio (b : a)",
        "Compounded Ratio (ac : bd)"
      ],
      "rawContent": "Ratios\n├── Duplicate Ratio (a² : b²)\n├── Sub-duplicate Ratio (√a : √b)\n├── Triplicate Ratio (a³ : b³)\n├── Sub-triplicate Ratio (∛a : ∛b)\n├── Inverse Ratio (b : a)\n└── Compounded Ratio (ac : bd)"
    },
    {
      "id": "5e3af13b-1b60-4e92-8779-1e6ca7b0e791",
      "type": "TABLE",
      "title": "Derived Ratios and Formulas",
      "headers": [
        "Ratio Type",
        "Formula \/ Condition",
        "Description"
      ],
      "rows": [
        [
          "Unchanged Value",
          "(a  k) \/ (b  k) or (a \/ k) \/ (b \/ k)",
          "Value remains unchanged if terms are multiplied or divided by the same non-zero constant k."
        ],
        [
          "Duplicate Ratio",
          "a² : b²",
          "Square of the original terms."
        ],
        [
          "Sub-duplicate Ratio",
          "√a : √b",
          "Square root of the original terms."
        ],
        [
          "Triplicate Ratio",
          "a³ : b³",
          "Cube of the original terms."
        ],
        [
          "Sub-triplicate Ratio",
          "∛a : ∛b",
          "Cube root of the original terms."
        ],
        [
          "Inverse Ratio",
          "b : a",
          "Reciprocal of the original ratio terms."
        ],
        [
          "Compounded Ratio",
          "ac : bd",
          "Product of antecedents to the product of consequents of ratios a:b and c:d."
        ]
      ],
      "hasHeaderRow": true
    },
    {
      "id": "dc3c52d3-6e4d-422d-af47-e030b03dc805",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "COMPARISON OF RATIOS",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b5c2c2b5-5119-4036-b701-7a00c047d28f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "To compare two ratios a\/b and c\/d, we can use cross-multiplication of their terms:",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "550b9e45-bfb2-49b0-99d5-30108dd0932d",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "If ad > bc, then a : b > c : d",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "467eebbd-3566-4671-b3eb-1eb60d7c989e",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "If ad < bc, then a : b < c : d",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a64f816c-3ba7-45f3-abd1-da8a59c2eef1",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "If ad = bc, then a : b = c : d",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "35c1fcb2-ea5c-4e0d-9eb2-18e0188b39fb",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "PROPERTIES OF PROPORTION",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "acc82a99-76b9-4a05-8db2-7cfb71e2cf24",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Product Rule of Proportion",
      "content": "In the proportion a : b :: c : d, the terms 'a' and 'd' are called extremes, and 'b' and 'c' are called means. The product of extremes equals the product of means: a  d = b  c."
    },
    {
      "id": "0f8cc561-f833-4876-b90e-8d73d94af7b3",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Proportional Calculations",
      "content": "Mean Proportional between a and b: √(ab)\nThird Proportional (x) to a and b (where a : b :: b : x): x = b² \/ a\nFourth Proportional (d) to a, b, and c (where a : b :: c : d): d = (b * c) \/ a"
    },
    {
      "id": "8525226f-7a43-420e-a05d-4834cba4de99",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Combining Multiple Ratios",
      "content": "Combining 2 Ratios: If A : B = N1 : D1 and B : C = N2 : D2, then A : B : C = (N1  N2) : (D1  N2) : (D1 * D2).\nCombining 3 Ratios: If A : B = N1 : D1, B : C = N2 : D2, and C : D = N3 : D3, then A : B : C : D = (N1  N2  N3) : (D1  N2  N3) : (D1  D2  N3) : (D1  D2  D3)."
    },
    {
      "id": "d74b5fcf-f0bb-4a10-bcee-8d519a177620",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Componendo and Dividendo Rule",
      "content": "If a\/b = c\/d, then (a + b) \/ (a - b) = (c + d) \/ (c - d)."
    },
    {
      "id": "89e57d40-d249-4b93-8dc1-130da090c1ed",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "SPECIAL EXAM TIPS & SHORTCUTS",
      "isBold": false,

      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Coin Denomination Shortcut",
      "content": "When the total value of coins V is given with the ratio of the number of coins x : y : z for denominations d1, d2, d3, convert all rupee\/paise amounts into identical units (either all rupees or all paise) before calculating! Total Value V = xd1 + yd2 + z*d3."

{
  "chapterId": "chap_0dcca65d",
  "title": "Simple and Compound Interest",
  "elements": [
    {
      "id": "9c9b4364-300a-48d8-84a8-0bb550be391b",
      "type": "HEADING_1",
      "text": "Chapter 9: Simple and Compound Interest",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "17b6f549-feb3-463e-931b-8a075b9c2a51",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "1. Introduction to Interest",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5f90641c-30ea-42ad-bcab-cb21add219f3",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "What is Interest?",
      "content": "Interest is the money paid by the borrower to the lender for the use of money."
    },
    {
      "id": "dd753626-5a57-44dc-97e2-ffb4ad5679a4",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "2. Simple Interest (SI)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3700cbb3-1a72-4c5a-8ffb-5d54977e342c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "If the interest is calculated on the original principal at any rate of interest for any period of time, then it is called simple interest.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a8aea20d-9c4e-448c-8b9d-3cce66e4baf0",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Simple Interest Formula",
      "content": "Simple Interest (SI) = (P  R  T) \/ 100\n\nAmount (A) = P + SI = P  (1 + (R  T) \/ 100)\n\nWhere:\n- P = Principal (the original sum of money borrowed or lent)\n- R = Rate of interest per annum (expressed as a percentage)\n- T = Time period (expressed in years)"
    },
    {
      "id": "fb604e21-83e4-4bdd-939a-136b5189de47",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Solved Examples (Simple Interest)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5a7188f4-c482-4f3f-830e-449dccbd3280",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 1: Calculating Simple Interest",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c465a3dd-f1c1-4063-9d0f-f77b40d78129",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Calculate the simple interest on ₹ 7200 at 12(3\/4)% per annum for 9 months.\n\nOptions:\n(a) ₹ 700\n(b) ₹ 688.5\n(c) ₹ 710.5\n(d) ₹ 680",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "61ba24c2-986b-4478-ae3c-ca177083ca7e",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution for Example 1",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (b) ₹ 688.5\n\nStep-by-step Calculation:\n- Principal (P) = ₹ 7200\n- Rate (R) = 12(3\/4)% = 51\/4% per annum\n- Time (T) = 9 months = 9\/12 years = 3\/4 years\n\nUsing the formula:\nSI = (P  R  T) \/ 100\nSI = (7200  (51\/4)  (3\/4)) \/ 100\nSI = (7200  51  3) \/ (100  4  4)\nSI = (7200 * 153) \/ 1600\nSI = 4.5 * 153 = ₹ 688.5"
    },
    {
      "id": "68b3e770-5bc2-441e-b2fe-0f9953300d9b",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "IMPORTANT",
      "title": "Key Shortcut Rule for Rate and Multiples",
      "content": "If a sum of money at r1% rate becomes n1 times of itself in a certain time, and becomes n2 times of itself at r2% in the same time, then:\n\nr1 \/ r2 = (n1 - 1) \/ (n2 - 1)"
    },
    {
      "id": "024f87e0-caf3-4c97-8a66-b10fa09e8504",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 2: Rate Change and Multiples",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e928cd28-d1fe-436b-9f74-522dfbd0e365",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A sum of money on a certain time at 10% rate becomes 3(1\/2) times. Now, at what rate per cent does it become 2(1\/2) times on that same given time?\n\nOptions:\n(a) 5%\n(b) 6%\n(c) 7%\n(d) 18%",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3a3a5995-2a94-4ca7-9772-8f90cc7ae2de",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Solution for Example 2",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (b) 6%\n\nStep-by-step Calculation:\nUsing the shortcut formula:\nr1 \/ r2 = (n1 - 1) \/ (n2 - 1)\n\nHere:\n- r1 = 10%\n- n1 = 3(1\/2) = 3.5\n- n2 = 2(1\/2) = 2.5\n- r2 = ?\n\nSubstitute the values:\n10 \/ r2 = (3.5 - 1) \/ (2.5 - 1)\n10 \/ r2 = 2.5 \/ 1.5\n10 \/ r2 = 5 \/ 3\nr2 = (10 * 3) \/ 5\nr2 = 6%"
    },
    {
      "id": "5065c42a-f0f0-4833-ba16-8a9ae8e3f2ab",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "3. Compound Interest (CI)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cf259138-87d0-4c21-b8cf-4fe8a907efcb",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "What is Compound Interest?",
      "content": "Compound Interest is the interest calculated on a sum of money (principal) which includes the accumulated interest of the previous periods. Essentially, it is interest earned on interest."
    },
    {
      "id": "7d545f2a-0ecf-40a8-907a-6b81de7aafe7",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Important Compound Interest Formulas",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ff5c7176-01dc-4769-a744-b55021a52a81",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Let Principal = P, Rate = R% per annum, Time = n years, and Amount = A.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "771b3888-bf69-41b4-a347-6796490a6648",
      "type": "TABLE",
      "title": "Compounding Formulas based on Intervals",
      "headers": [
        "Compounding Condition",
        "Formula for Amount (A)"
      ],
      "rows": [
        [
          "When interest is compounded annually",
          "A = P * (1 + R\/100)^n"
        ],
        [
          "When interest is compounded half-yearly",
          "A = P * (1 + R\/200)^(2n)"
        ],
        [
          "When interest is compounded quarterly",
          "A = P * (1 + R\/400)^(4n)"
        ],
        [
          "When interest is compounded annually but time is in fraction (e.g., 3(2\/5) years)",
          "A = P  (1 + R\/100)^3  (1 + (2\/5 * R)\/100)"
        ],
        [
          "If rates of interest are R1%, R2%, and R3% for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd year respectively",
          "A = P  (1 + R1\/100)  (1 + R2\/100) * (1 + R3\/100)"
        ]
      ],
      "hasHeaderRow": true
    },
    {
      "id": "e1785587-0ee2-4a8a-a56e-8a4520769696",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Difference Between CI and SI (For 2 Years)",
      "content": "On a certain sum of money, the difference (D) between Compound Interest (CI) and Simple Interest (SI) for 2 years at r% per annum is given by:\n\nD = P * (r \/ 100)^2"
    },
    {
      "id": "eb75fffc-4c30-4af8-b52b-a73a3df31114",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Solved Examples (Compound Interest)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "82130d89-ba5f-44d9-95a9-61821fca20c3",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 3: Doubling Time under Compound Interest",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "bb3d7cb4-f3ca-45a4-a0a0-d74949c913f8",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A sum of money placed at CI doubles itself in 4 years. In how many years will it amount to 8 times itself?\n\nOptions:\n(a) 12\n(b) 14\n(c) 16\n(d) 10",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c18a9735-5cc9-4a95-aa19-66200c447707",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Solution for Example 3",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (a) 12\n\nShortcut Rule:\nIf a sum becomes n times in t years at CI, then it will become (n^m) times in (m * t) years.\n\nHere:\n- The sum doubles (n = 2) in 4 years (t = 4).\n- We want it to become 8 times (which is 2^3, so m = 3).\n\nRequired time = m  t = 3  4 = 12 years."
    },
    {
      "id": "41f99d7b-5e0b-49e2-bea6-b736c03ec9f8",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 4: Finding SI from Given CI",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d5c451ca-fd86-442d-bfe3-0535f906de82",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "If the compound interest on a certain sum for 2 years at 3% is ₹ 101.50, what would be the simple interest on the same sum for the same rate and time?\n\nOptions:\n(a) 100\n(b) 100.5\n(c) 90\n(d) 99.5",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a87fce02-88f8-4fff-bde3-ff2ac342baec",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Solution for Example 4",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (a) 100\n\nStep-by-step Calculation:\nLet Principal = P\n\nCI on ₹ 1 for 2 years at 3%:\n= (1 + 3\/100)^2 - 1\n= (1.03)^2 - 1\n= 1.0609 - 1 = 0.0609 (or 609\/10000)\n\nSI on ₹ 1 for 2 years at 3%:\n= (1  3  2) \/ 100\n= 6\/100 = 0.06 (or 600\/10000)\n\nRatio of SI to CI:\nSI \/ CI = 0.06 \/ 0.0609 = 600 \/ 609\n\nGiven CI = ₹ 101.50\nSI = (600 \/ 609) * 101.50\nSI = ₹ 100"
    },
    {
      "id": "f91910a0-11ea-4cc7-94b6-e136431f328b",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Example 5: Difference between CI and SI",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c0126391-ecea-46f3-9c09-52a259b6d817",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The difference between the CI and the SI on a certain sum of money at 5% per annum for 2 years is ₹ 1.50. Find the sum.\n\nOptions:\n(a) 600\n(b) 500\n(c) 700\n(d) 640",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f6894a44-2d97-4c9d-b9e6-a46c422b0325",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "FORMULA",
      "title": "Solution for Example 5",
      "content": "Correct Answer: (a) 600\n\nStep-by-step Calculation:\nUsing the difference formula for 2 years:\nDifference (D) = P * (R \/ 100)^2\n\nGiven:\n- D = ₹ 1.50\n- R = 5%\n\nSubstitute the values:\n1.50 = P * (5 \/ 100)^2\n1.50 = P * (1 \/ 20)^2\n1.50 = P * (1 \/ 400)\nP = 1.50 * 400\nP = ₹ 600"
    },
    {

{
  "chapterId": "chap_cb88d761",
  "title": "Basics of Computer",
  "elements": [
    {
      "id": "7698e295-fbac-4b6a-9466-f00168920015",
      "type": "HEADING_1",
      "text": "CHAPTER 1: BASICS OF COMPUTER",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "edb9258a-b160-4c3d-8974-399e1abd8491",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Definition of Computer",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cef5f8f6-6ecb-4118-9860-acd66967807e",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A computer is an electronic, programmable data-processing device designed to automatically accept raw data, process it according to a stored sequence of instructions (a program), store the data and results, and produce meaningful information as output.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6c954f60-0b33-4203-8809-f6e27726e198",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Data vs. Information",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e013be18-8b94-4834-8986-24b817acb567",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "Data vs. Information",
      "nodes": [
        "Data vs. Information",
        "Data",
        "Information"
      ],
      "rawContent": "     [Data vs. Information]\n            \/       \\\n       [Data]       [Information]"
    },
    {
      "id": "f6fc5d38-467e-42be-8b01-18163f5c05e3",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Data",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "569a941e-90a6-4339-bffb-58ecdedeedd4",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Data refers to raw, unorganized, and unstructured facts, numbers, symbols, or observations (e.g., 85, 92, 78). It lacks contextual meaning on its own.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "86f83d66-947f-43dc-acc7-564f8083ccf5",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Information",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a1bd1167-90eb-4b99-9cd2-539f8f964a83",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Information refers to processed, organized, and structured data that has context and utility (e.g., \"Average Examination Score = 85%\").",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6918d3df-00d7-409f-a245-1eb0bce9c32e",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Core Characteristics of a Computer",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "35434fab-9a69-472f-a819-eb9cb5855654",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Speed: A computer can execute millions or billions of instructions per second. Computer processing speed may be measured using units such as MIPS (Millions of Instructions Per Second) or GFLOPS (Giga Floating-Point Operations Per Second).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f1843fd5-42a4-4018-a143-b5d06fa59ecb",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Accuracy: Operates with high precision, governed by the GIGO principle.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b4bf0c8a-7b73-4ac9-ae02-7b9abc1f4ab8",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Diligence: Free from human fatigue, boredom, or lack of concentration.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "bd551942-8e20-4a73-8600-1a2e686a34e6",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Versatility: Capable of performing a wide range of tasks from simple arithmetic to complex simulations.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "05c7f105-d51c-42e6-af06-dc29f21933c1",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Zero IQ & Lack of Feelings: Lacks innate intelligence or emotions, relying entirely on predefined algorithms and instructions.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b6d7c71f-80e7-4e62-9919-cf90d3c96380",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "IMPORTANT",
      "title": "The GIGO Principle",
      "content": "A computer operates under the GIGO (Garbage In, Garbage Out) principle. This means that if incorrect, incomplete, or faulty data or instructions are provided as input, the computer will produce an incorrect result. Errors generally occur due to human logic errors or faulty input rather than the computer's hardware processing."
    },
    {
      "id": "8e436e6b-262b-491a-a332-65798041ac0d",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Basic Computer Organisation: The 5 Fundamental Functions",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2b951605-7541-4c2f-8530-9a92d5418120",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "Von Neumann Model",
      "content": "The architecture of modern digital computers is based on the Von Neumann Model, which outlines five essential functional operations: Inputting, Storing, Processing, Outputting, and Controlling."
    },
    {
      "id": "87a8e4f1-bfca-41fe-96f3-9650ed5743f6",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "1. Inputting",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "15b48124-c8eb-49ff-a006-ea7ad5934373",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Inputting is the process of feeding raw data, programs, and user commands into the computer system.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5c484f28-bd54-46d3-9fd2-25d35823021c",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Mechanism: Peripheral input devices (Keyboard, Mouse, Scanner, Barcode Reader) capture physical inputs or user gestures.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "12a3f48c-df68-4474-a373-b9411bf55441",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Interface Conversion: The input unit's electronic interface converts human-readable signals into computer-readable binary code (0s and 1s).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "046d0df4-a831-4130-a54b-c89670b6e168",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Destination: Converted binary data is routed to Primary Storage (RAM) or CPU registers for immediate processing.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dac4eb5f-37a2-43ff-9404-1a6acb05da64",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "2. Storing",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d4c64260-6d39-415e-98cd-11909fea1230",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Storing is the retention of data, instructions, intermediate calculations, and final results within the system's memory architecture.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "872ce36e-2a84-4e00-bb00-7e682ca943ab",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "Storage Types",
      "nodes": [
        "Storage Types",
        "Primary",
        "Intermediate",
        "Secondary"
      ],
      "rawContent": "               [Storage Types]\n             \/        |        \\\n     [Primary]  [Intermediate]  [Secondary]"
    },
    {
      "id": "a3c07daf-498f-4911-9507-cffbf33bd544",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Primary Storage (Main Memory \/ RAM)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "56bde197-6908-4bfd-9f4e-02318efab4e6",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Primary Storage holds currently executing instructions and active data. It is fast and directly accessible by the CPU via the data bus, but it is volatile, meaning it loses its contents when power is turned off.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4bb827c4-bf19-47c4-b435-b96ffea41bd0",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Intermediate Storage",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "bc3a14e1-23af-453e-9b67-f43de6417043",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Intermediate Storage holds temporary operational results generated by the ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) before final execution completes.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6e44a65e-b50a-4953-9fdb-6a0b58d7070f",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Secondary Storage (Auxiliary Memory \/ HDD, SSD)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d03297d9-bc8a-4f4a-9b60-01ea1868d367",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Secondary Storage holds long-term programs, operating system files, and persistent user data. It is non-volatile and has a larger capacity than primary storage, but it is slower to access.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9b620a43-e73a-4d6e-8ac4-e879f563c8f6",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "3. Processing",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "35381156-1132-447f-8d40-e3265ce10e38",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Processing is the core operational phase where raw data is converted into actionable information by executing arithmetic and logical computations. It is performed by the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) inside the Central Processing Unit (CPU).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "679b7b88-4b39-4ea9-9e40-ea0aa3e31782",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "Processing Operations",
      "nodes": [
        "Processing Operations",
        "Arithmetic",
        "Logical"
      ],
      "rawContent": "          [Processing Operations]\n                 \/         \\\n     [Arithmetic]           [Logical]"
    },
    {
      "id": "c823878f-315a-4fcf-aef4-52fa1a644c4c",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Arithmetic Operations",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f9a5efae-1b1e-4036-98b1-63c6681d079c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Arithmetic operations include basic and complex mathematical tasks such as addition (+), subtraction (-), multiplication (*), division (\/), and exponentiation.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7a1f49b5-2f0e-4939-a6bf-0448dc42314f",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Logical Operations",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9f78e485-599c-4efe-9998-fdc225da7226",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Logical operations involve decision-making, evaluations, and comparative operations.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "aa83eb53-caf0-4186-b148-2acc456d8f0d",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "Logical Operations Categories",
      "nodes": [
        "Logical Operations",
        "Relational",
        "Boolean"
      ],
      "rawContent": "          [Logical Operations]\n                 \/         \\\n     [Relational]           [Boolean]"
    },
    {
      "id": "e9ab0db7-cabb-4b6d-aec8-0b1242db6b8c",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Relational Operations: Equal to (=), Not equal to (!=), Greater than (>), and Less than (<).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fdd1c70a-25a9-4a4d-b70b-a99e008aa6dc",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Boolean Operations: AND, OR, NOT, and XOR logic gate evaluations.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e6c341ea-4af1-4ad7-bb7d-14ea58001cc2",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "4. Outputting",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ea91d13e-4283-47ee-84ca-162dfea6cd21",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Outputting is the process of retrieving processed results from memory and presenting them to the user or sending them to an external system.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "afd2bfba-fbe8-4651-b478-a6b8bcfb7033",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "Types of Output",
      "nodes": [
        "Types of Output",
        "Soft Copy",
        "Hard Copy"
      ],
      "rawContent": "          [Types of Output]\n                 \/         \\\n           [Soft Copy]     [Hard Copy]"
    },
    {
      "id": "3323890a-fc74-49c1-8acd-e3e7290a25c0",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Soft Copy",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e9466b29-22f1-42ff-b3e6-246cdfb3afef",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Soft Copy is temporary, non-persistent output displayed electronically on screens such as Monitors and Projectors, or audio emitted through Speakers.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "71a2731f-99a7-4398-88be-012c9ad6826d",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Hard Copy",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "359e413c-760f-4bc4-8e64-b8ea42e2ea6b",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Hard Copy is permanent, physical output generated on paper or physical media using devices such as Printers and Plotters.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dafda433-9187-4e07-9f4c-dcbf2f3a156e",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "5. Controlling",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1d0b4107-3f2e-4799-9139-dd2b0b8d6beb",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Controlling is the management, direction, and synchronization of all internal and external functional units of the computer. It is performed by the Control Unit (CU), often referred to as the Nerve Centre or Manager of the computer system.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2d6ed356-3201-4dbf-9e06-a9d94e3dfac9",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The Control Unit does not process or store data directly.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "da6f9796-dc4b-4bcf-a950-1ac0140ef00c",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "It issues command and timing signals via the Control Bus to direct the Input Unit when to read, the ALU when to process, Memory where to store, and the Output Unit when to display.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c52b0c74-25f6-48f8-b682-9f552ece2d64",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "It governs the exact step-by-step sequence of the machine instruction cycle: Fetch -> Decode -> Execute -> Store.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4ac36546-d026-4686-b5b9-4e231ceec6f5",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "FLOWCHART",
      "title": "Control Unit Execution Workflow",
      "nodes": [
        "Fetch",
        "Decode",
        "Execute",
        "Store"
      ],
      "rawContent": "[Fetch] -> [Decode] -> [Execute] -> [Store]"
    },
    {
      "id": "5dac60ac-6e52-40fc-b501-fe82006d7a0d",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Input Unit",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "51ace203-b301-4885-8113-a8f8a27c6428",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Input Unit is the module responsible for receiving raw data, instructions, and user commands from the outside environment. Its function is to convert human-readable inputs into computer-readable binary code (0s and 1s) through input interfaces and pass them to primary storage or the CPU. Examples include Keyboard, Mouse, Optical Mark Reader (OMR), Magnetic Ink Character Reader (MICR), Scanner, and Barcode Reader.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "19948bc9-0f5e-4f05-a033-5cf0ef240024",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Output Unit",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d4b0fffb-7964-46b8-a366-55bc0d512dad",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Output Unit is the module responsible for delivering processed results (information) from the computer to the user or external systems. Its function is to convert machine-readable binary signals back into human-understandable visual, printed, or auditory forms.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "59f002eb-d32b-4899-9d80-896c6d276532",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "Output Classifications",
      "nodes": [
        "Output Classifications",
        "Soft Copy",
        "Hard Copy"
      ],
      "rawContent": "          [Output Classifications]\n                 \/         \\\n           [Soft Copy]     [Hard Copy]"
    },
    {
      "id": "0871c861-0ce7-41ed-8730-4866703f71eb",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Soft Copy",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4ec6b87b-203c-43b5-93aa-9997a427779a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Soft Copy is temporary, non-persistent output such as Display Monitors, Speakers, and Projectors.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "eb1a6c5c-39cf-4c4d-b025-3a1b3d7d9830",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Hard Copy",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6c18a6e2-ef0f-4abc-baec-096bd2f04b95",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Hard Copy is permanent, physical output on paper or physical media such as Printers and Plotters.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "acd570e1-5921-457e-a3af-d09a75d3839b",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Central Processing Unit (CPU)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b6485123-4512-41a4-80eb-35ce0cf53705",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Central Processing Unit (CPU) is the electronic microchip often termed the Brain of the Computer. It executes instructions, processes data, and controls overall operations.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "de7959be-a1df-475b-87c7-3a6e25cd71ec",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "CPU Components",
      "nodes": [
        "CPU Components",
        "Arithmetic Logic",
        "Control Unit"
      ],
      "rawContent": "               [CPU Components]\n                 \/         \\\n     [Arithmetic Logic]   [Control Unit]"
    },
    {
      "id": "f18be42c-68c6-4f35-a86c-a29ff309e499",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dc5a04a9-6d7e-481c-8f53-d0efe62e4f7c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) performs all actual computational and logical processing.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "89925d60-8f40-4527-83ae-ae200a476793",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "ALU Operations",
      "nodes": [
        "ALU Operations",
        "Arithmetic",
        "Logic"
      ],
      "rawContent": "               [ALU Operations]\n                 \/         \\\n     [Arithmetic]           [Logic]"
    },
    {
      "id": "a36288ab-c582-4b31-9407-1977b81f08a5",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Arithmetic Operations",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "52fffb9a-207e-453b-96fc-da0c9578a54c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The ALU executes mathematical operations such as addition (+), subtraction (-), multiplication (x), and division (\/).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4e6a2b3a-4cd1-430f-accc-5fe88b54209d",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Logic Operations",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e654e24b-0285-4f7b-aeae-7447faf9156f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The ALU evaluates logical conditions and comparisons such as greater than (>), less than (<), equal to (=), and not equal to (!=), as well as Boolean operations such as AND, OR, and NOT.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "baf85485-674e-4bda-afbd-a38c191a1a4f",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Control Unit (CU)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ed7a33c0-4a9e-4a1d-9c76-068582988828",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Key Characteristic: The Control Unit does not process or store data itself.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f6280358-86cc-4ab1-9c30-7f33a6ed2388",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Role: It generates timing and control signals via the Control Bus to direct data flow between the ALU, memory, and I\/O devices.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "31f265f6-65d4-4293-92ee-aa0c98ac81a2",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "It manages the Instruction Cycle: Fetch -> Decode -> Execute -> Store.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fbea455e-39f6-4c9f-a2f8-4f804be1e4cc",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Storage Unit",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3a9266a3-940d-4b29-85e7-a4c6ce134984",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Storage Unit holds raw data, operating system instructions, intermediate processing steps, and final results.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "32b477a4-0d1b-49ea-96b7-730aade6063c",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "Storage Unit Classifications",
      "nodes": [
        "Storage Unit",
        "Primary",
        "Secondary"
      ],
      "rawContent": "               [Storage Unit]\n                 \/         \\\n           [Primary]     [Secondary]"
    },
    {
      "id": "b64c8681-28a9-45e3-98ea-6f70ab2fab78",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Primary Storage (Main Memory)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e7553017-7282-4788-bd60-70befe93b559",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Primary Storage is memory directly accessible by the CPU via internal buses. It holds currently executing programs, active OS tasks, and temporary data. It features high speed but limited capacity.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8b38eca5-db4e-47ae-bd10-b5799739138a",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "Primary Storage Types",
      "nodes": [
        "Primary Storage",
        "RAM",
        "ROM"
      ],
      "rawContent": "              [Primary Storage]\n                 \/         \\\n              [RAM]       [ROM]"
    },
    {
      "id": "7d7f153d-edb0-467c-90b7-cdd6e3434461",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "RAM (Random Access Memory)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dbbfe12a-8f77-4931-84b8-2ed18061fca4",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "RAM is volatile memory, meaning it loses its contents when power is lost. It is used as the active workspace of the computer.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4c863370-01b3-441b-8684-281d23012bc5",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "ROM (Read Only Memory)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3bca0860-73ef-419b-8fe8-7d32d600824b",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "ROM is non-volatile memory. It contains startup firmware such as BIOS\/POST (Basic Input\/Output System \/ Power-On Self-Test).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2e221e5f-f9a0-4138-9ddf-a973657e07fc",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Secondary Storage (Auxiliary Storage)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8989616b-2fa2-4182-8df6-8cd8d02bc29e",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Secondary Storage is persistent, external storage that is not directly addressed by the CPU for execution. Data must first be loaded into RAM before it can normally be used for execution.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b43151e5-0266-4836-bf6c-eb22fc0c8bde",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Function: It retains user files, software applications, and Operating System files permanently.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "337271a2-cd18-4614-be8b-a9bb0dcc6f8f",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Characteristics: Secondary storage is non-volatile, has high storage capacity, has a lower cost per unit, and is slower to access compared to RAM.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7dc41a05-9c4b-40c9-93f9-e901e37e76d7",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Examples: Hard Disk Drive (HDD), Solid State Drive (SSD), Optical Disks (CD\/DVD), and Pen Drives.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f95ded4b-c9f9-4966-908f-4ca972e025cb",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Bus Architecture",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c9a65586-25ba-4093-9595-596f561d5e79",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Bus is a collection of parallel physical wires or conductors on the motherboard that acts as a shared signal transmission pathway between computer components.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "00cd86ce-2955-4f1b-b758-56a926382a85",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "Bus Classifications",
      "nodes": [
        "Bus Architecture",
        "Internal",
        "External"
      ],
      "rawContent": "              [Bus Architecture]\n                 \/         \\\n           [Internal]     [External]"
    },
    {
      "id": "da4a180d-5443-4834-b906-1c09c029f1c4",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Internal Bus (System Bus)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cff63deb-0fe1-4e94-96a1-9e86f4e990f9",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Internal Bus, also called the System Bus, connects internal CPU elements such as the CU, ALU, and Registers to each other and links the CPU directly to Main Memory (RAM) and Cache. It operates at ultra-high clock speeds matching the internal system speed.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "05d7fc85-594c-4296-83c5-38abe274ca63",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "External Bus (Expansion Bus)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "883c7397-1c00-427e-9e3d-a66d7ddc75da",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The External Bus, also called the Expansion Bus, connects the CPU\/System Bus to external peripheral devices, expansion slots such as PCIe (Peripheral Component Interconnect Express), and peripheral controllers such as USB (Universal Serial Bus) and SATA (Serial AT Attachment). It operates at lower speeds compared to the internal system bus.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "736a17fb-505c-4afc-ba37-79d1943e6044",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Types of Buses (Functional Classification)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7037459c-b4bc-4db5-b69a-91f4986d2d8b",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "Functional Bus Types",
      "nodes": [
        "Functional Buses",
        "Data Bus",
        "Address Bus",
        "Control Bus"
      ],
      "rawContent": "               [Functional Buses]\n             \/         |         \\\n       [Data Bus] [Address Bus] [Control Bus]"
    },
    {
      "id": "e82794bc-9a1f-4d37-ab38-0e4cc15e8bd8",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Data Bus",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "167eaa22-0037-4486-b3aa-f993fc594e99",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Data Bus transfers actual data bytes between the CPU, RAM, and I\/O devices. It is bi-directional, meaning data can travel in both directions. Its width, such as 32-bit or 64-bit, determines how much data can move in a single clock cycle.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c8217954-d10f-46d1-bee5-1b0ef8fff782",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Address Bus",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "150e3135-bdee-4859-b454-3c62f9c36d66",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Address Bus carries physical memory location addresses from the CPU to RAM or peripherals. It is uni-directional (CPU -> Memory\/Devices). Its width determines the total addressable memory space, represented as 2^n locations for n address lines.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "99fe1f4a-ca80-4f54-a4e4-443925c8f239",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Control Bus",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "42ed493d-fef4-4d99-b529-e2e23f910897",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Control Bus transmits command, status, timing, and interrupt signals, such as Read\/Write signals. It may be bi-directional or uni-directional depending on the individual control line. Its primary purpose is to ensure synchronized operation between computer components.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "27306096-481b-4e95-8a93-290243f4cabf",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "The Instruction Cycle",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a0a7ddcb-0ad1-4dfc-9b9c-ee8de82c263b",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The Instruction Cycle, also known as the Fetch-Decode-Execute Cycle, is the basic operational process through which a CPU processes a machine instruction. It represents the continuous sequence of actions the processor executes from system startup until shutdown.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9b01f842-f483-4e62-8118-cb1b8b192834",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "FLOWCHART",
      "title": "The Instruction Cycle",
      "nodes": [
        "Fetch",
        "Decode",
        "Execute",
        "Store"
      ],
      "rawContent": "[Fetch] -> [Decode] -> [Execute] -> [Store] --(Next)--> [Fetch]"
    },
    {
      "id": "b967ebf1-1a1b-47e3-924d-5795576c2f26",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "1. Fetch",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "25b9a366-0ed9-40cc-915d-c639e63b7d32",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Action: During the Fetch phase, the CPU retrieves the instruction opcode\/data from primary storage (RAM) using the memory address currently held in the Program Counter (PC) register.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cdb8c306-dc53-4df5-ad0b-9ee00637bdc5",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Mechanism: The memory address is placed on the Address Bus, and the retrieved instruction code is sent back via the Data Bus into the Instruction Register (IR).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "abe4cf23-b657-4230-bd0b-24050b8efaf1",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Update: Immediately after fetching, the Program Counter (PC) increments automatically to point to the address of the next instruction in sequence.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9cb4ee87-d36c-4bf2-bd84-166fbccbbe15",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "2. Decode",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7c731913-7473-4ab8-b90f-f8537544740f",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Action: During the Decode phase, the instruction stored in the Instruction Register (IR) is analyzed and interpreted.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a6a191f9-f185-445e-939a-64857b7f6c0a",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Mechanism: The Control Unit (CU) decodes the binary operational code (opcode) to determine what action needs to be performed, identifies required operands, and determines which functional unit, such as the ALU, is needed.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9d828c53-be01-45db-9a43-7b8811a0f0db",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "3. Execute",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "00924a44-9938-4f2a-a23b-098f97e99de8",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Action: During the Execute phase, the CPU performs the required operation according to the decoded command.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b6dd0e2f-e360-4f7d-ab6a-3fcb7790f9e2",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Mechanism: If arithmetic or logical comparisons are needed, the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) executes the calculation. If data movement or branch instructions are decoded, data is shifted between registers or memory blocks.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "92a3f185-6b88-458c-8f97-b3e4b1fa8f68",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "4. Store (Write-Back)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3f27aa6f-e794-47e9-9e6b-a0f3db7afdd7",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Action: During the Store (Write-Back) phase, the output generated during execution is written to a permanent or temporary location.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "764b480e-6755-43bd-be9a-ad5d8c96c06d",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Mechanism: The result is stored back into internal CPU Registers or routed to Main Memory (RAM) via the Data Bus for future use.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5c92210e-66ec-45d1-8c71-d9bd4fa11259",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Sequential Order",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2e74fd5c-ebcd-476a-b6ad-f839c6767db9",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "The strict sequential order of the instruction cycle is: Fetch -> Decode -> Execute -> Store.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "64e2808c-34e3-4c96-a029-1a3c61fe789b",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Revision: Computer Fundamentals",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5ad4aca1-33e7-49bc-9741-6ebf4ccb2482",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Computer: An electronic, programmable data-processing device that accepts data, processes it, stores data\/results, and produces meaningful information.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "177403a9-6d40-4731-9a70-d3a1bb5c67e1",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Data vs. Information: Data is raw, unorganized facts; Information is processed, structured data with context.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "87ab9089-8edd-47de-a41b-87392d313cc1",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Speed Metrics: Measured in MIPS (Millions of Instructions Per Second) or GFLOPS (Giga Floating-Point Operations Per Second).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5b6408be-6140-4c11-b7c0-b8a9b05a0bfc",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Accuracy & GIGO: Computers operate under the Garbage In, Garbage Out principle.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cc36ed9b-0b35-4ca3-be8b-3201ec14bdc4",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Five Fundamental Functions: Inputting, Storing, Processing, Outputting, and Controlling.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1492d603-0795-4298-9172-d871858943b7",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "CPU Components: Composed of the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) for calculations and the Control Unit (CU) for coordination.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "55e50ae9-7a4e-4c6e-8c69-cf26bb497c5d",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Primary vs. Secondary Storage: Primary (RAM) is volatile, fast, and directly accessible; Secondary (HDD, SSD) is non-volatile, high-capacity, and persistent.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "be55b600-d252-4110-b1d8-725383d1e27c",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Bus Architecture: System Bus (Internal) connects CPU, RAM, and Cache. Expansion Bus (External) connects peripherals.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "48aea1e8-8d0d-45b0-bd56-faa41b41a973",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Bus Types: Data Bus (bi-directional data transfer), Address Bus (uni-directional memory addressing), and Control Bus (synchronization signals).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b6dc9fe3-1899-4e0b-b7b6-4bfaad995f56",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Instruction Cycle: Fetch -> Decode -> Execute -> Store.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "944f32fb-e5cb-4ee1-8ba4-6de03fac1f71",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f0df4fc0-6a32-43d0-adb2-29791ab9871c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "",
      "isBold": false,
