{
  "chapterId": "chap_48f55386",
  "title": "Computer Hardware",
  "elements": [
    {
      "id": "06889471-c9a8-46fb-abde-099f9a09c6f9",
      "type": "HEADING_1",
      "text": "CHAPTER 3: COMPUTER HARDWARE",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c13374f9-27f9-4b42-9c02-1c85fe6926ad",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "1. Definition of Computer Hardware",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9f706730-0b35-4333-927e-97c89cb95aed",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "Computer Hardware",
      "content": "Computer Hardware refers to the tangible, physical microelectronic and mechanical components of a computer system that can be touched, seen, and handled. It forms the physical infrastructure required to run software and process data."
    },
    {
      "id": "1ba29438-b186-48ca-ae3e-cd2840b6b615",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Examples of computer hardware include the Central Processing Unit (CPU), which acts as the computer's brain; Random Access Memory (RAM), which is temporary volatile memory used to store working data; the motherboard, which is the main printed circuit board; hard drives for high-capacity storage; and keyboards for input.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "94c8fefd-8c93-4ec5-a935-dc43a8c431a8",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "2. Input Devices: Overview",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "efac5103-9cec-4cd4-bf65-1f060b54067d",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "Input Device",
      "content": "An Input Device is an electromechanical peripheral device used to feed raw data, instructions, and control commands into a computer system."
    },
    {
      "id": "0686ec93-f784-4c29-842c-3fc065f418b6",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "It captures physical actions, gestures, acoustic signals, or optical data and translates them into machine-readable binary code (0s and 1s) for CPU processing.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cd10bda4-b8e4-4dde-bbc5-fc026cb3bd6f",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "3. Comprehensive Breakdown of Input Devices",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fc59a456-7533-456f-84c3-4ea42f082b15",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "A. Keyboard",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6b71e511-064b-41ef-b36b-a2b62902a3c6",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Function: The keyboard is the primary text-entry and command device.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c2c0e781-097b-44ea-9645-cc362a9562da",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Mechanism: A keyboard contains an array of switches arranged in a standard layout, such as QWERTY. Pressing a key completes a circuit, generating a unique matrix scan code that is converted into ASCII or Unicode binary values.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "178021c8-055b-408b-8ae0-9ec89bcd33ef",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "B. Pointing Devices",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a9ed8be8-599a-445e-8235-b5f5387515ce",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Pointing Devices are a class of input hardware specifically designed to control the movement of an on-screen cursor or pointer within a Graphical User Interface (GUI). They are used to select, draw, or execute actions.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0beb7674-fe42-4ce8-a739-063f76cb86dd",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Mouse\nTrackball\nJoystick\nLight Pen\nTouch Screen",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8ebac4f1-4f3d-4330-9762-233cde5c22bd",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Mouse",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dd4c30e0-44e6-4a64-ba71-2de7ee5798c9",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Mouse is a handheld pointing device that is moved across a flat surface. It uses optical sensors or laser diodes to detect 2D motion coordinates (X and Y axes). A mouse normally includes left and right click buttons and a scroll wheel.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "86be6290-b64d-449d-b1f6-29a83f4bd529",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Trackball",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9393cc49-1d38-471e-95c8-eb93294f0eec",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Trackball is a stationary pointing device featuring an exposed, freely rotating ball resting in a socket. The user rotates the ball directly using the fingers or palm while the base remains stationary. This makes it useful where desk space is limited and in applications such as CAD (Computer-Aided Design) workstations.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2e1a0c8e-2e18-465c-ab80-09cd5d02fb0a",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Joystick",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d39848a0-6fbe-447e-b76f-1956cff4a7a6",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Joystick is a vertical stick pivoted on a movable base that reports its tilt angle and direction to the computer. It is widely used for flight simulation, video gaming, robotic controls, and industrial crane operations.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e4236069-67b3-4765-b024-12991b66a857",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Light Pen",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7b0f8f20-0bde-4d56-a5ad-5682b868b5cf",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Light Pen is a light-sensitive wand connected to a computer and historically used directly on CRT display monitors. It detects screen raster updates and sends spatial coordinates to the CPU. It can be used to draw graphics or select menu options.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6e09a5d1-23d6-4cec-ab8d-becd2fcde0ff",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Touch Screen",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6beedef4-e8bd-41cf-866b-e235844870d7",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Touch Screen is a dual input-output panel placed over a display screen that senses physical touch from a finger or stylus. Touch screens can use different technologies:",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7a45a99a-22f3-411c-910a-39d629959405",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Resistive: Uses pressure to detect touch.\nCapacitive: Uses the electrical charge of the human body to detect touch.\nInfrared: Uses an infrared grid to detect touch coordinates.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fe402244-7cef-465d-b9c4-1c370e5453c1",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "C. Optical & Character Recognition Devices",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "77d03cb6-5af2-4b77-bfe5-dbfd57543de4",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Barcode Reader (BCR)\nOptical Mark Reader (OMR)\nOptical Character Recognition (OCR)\nMagnetic Ink Character Recognition (MICR)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "06f20b9f-24d3-4f9e-978d-bcd9569323c1",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Barcode Reader (BCR)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5b87be75-e5e8-4a15-bd6b-bc291b280b71",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Barcode Reader (BCR) is a handheld or stationary optical scanner that shines a red light beam across the parallel black-and-white lines of a barcode. It measures reflected light intensity and decodes Universal Product Codes (UPC) into digital alphanumeric data. It is commonly used for inventory management and retail billing.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ff80672f-7bb0-4ce1-a625-06e8162f7ec8",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Optical Mark Reader (OMR)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0b210134-0c46-44ff-94dd-e1abe87aab14",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "An Optical Mark Reader (OMR) is a specialized optical device that detects the presence or light reflectivity of dark pencil or pen marks on pre-printed forms. It is commonly used for multiple-choice objective examination answer sheets and survey forms.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "039cac05-77b1-4a1e-92d8-250b22f07417",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Optical Character Recognition (OCR)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "2ecd84ee-03c8-4dea-834e-071a70313fc2",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is a hardware-software mechanism that optically scans printed or handwritten text documents and converts the visual image of characters into editable and searchable digital text formats.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "63a2b970-9cd7-4dfe-9daa-5fa74aa21b93",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Magnetic Ink Character Recognition (MICR)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b8584e20-cda4-47b1-84ee-a747bbead62c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Magnetic Ink Character Recognition (MICR) is a specialized character-reading technology that reads characters printed with magnetic iron-oxide ink. It is primarily used in banking systems to read the bottom line of cheques rapidly and securely, including routing numbers, account numbers, and cheque numbers.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT",
      "spans": [
        {
          "start": 123,
          "end": 146,
          "isBold": false,
          "isItalic": false,
          "isUnderline": false,
          "isStrikethrough": false,
          "textColorHex": "#D97706",
          "highlightColorHex": ""
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "f594b0fd-fd72-4e03-a4f8-5f3caea432e3",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "D. Identity, Security & Interface Devices",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4b51c20a-c275-4561-ad9a-8dcdddf6b06e",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Smart Card Reader",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6d4fb331-ce99-49ec-beae-01d4c3ac8f74",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Smart Card Reader is an electronic reading terminal that accesses stored data from an embedded Integrated Circuit (IC) microchip located on plastic smart cards. Examples include EMV debit cards, EMV credit cards, SIM cards, and identity cards.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "bea2cfc6-a862-406f-a95d-ce70ba95475d",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Biometric Sensor",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "54567422-fea6-4ee7-b8d6-b90644103904",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Biometric Sensor is a security input device that captures, scans, and digitizes unique biological or behavioral human traits for identity authentication. Examples include fingerprints, iris patterns, facial structure, and voice resonance.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f12c18f0-e963-4995-8f8e-6623d12c9272",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "E. Imaging & Multimedia Input Devices",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1b12cb27-b5c9-47db-ad58-240d36caa630",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Scanner\nMicrophone\nWebcam\nPC Card (PCMCIA Card)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d1823343-393f-410f-9c1b-5781ab0710b1",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Scanner",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d1e39ae7-d9a1-45a1-8bd8-6a8c9fa382a0",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Scanner is an optical device that converts physical paper documents, photographs, or graphics into high-resolution digital raster image files, also called soft copies. Common output formats include JPEG and PDF.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "6fa2cb03-6207-4bb8-a06d-083bdf590b75",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Microphone",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "deb04474-1be5-42f4-9f26-8173a727236b",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Microphone is an acoustic transducer that converts sound waves, such as human voice or environmental audio, into analog electrical signals. These signals are then digitized by the computer's sound card.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b350452e-f69a-4283-aa78-3780eb9d3ef2",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Webcam",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "652d3483-4c2a-4314-b6e5-6731dcdf178d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Webcam is a compact digital video camera connected through USB or built into a display lid. It captures real-time video and still images. It is commonly used for video conferencing, streaming, and security recording.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cff5faf9-f61b-4fec-82d0-fb6c42e90f5c",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "PC Card (PCMCIA Card)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4ff14b3f-f409-47af-8d46-c1431787ab20",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A PC Card (PCMCIA Card) is a removable, credit-card-sized expansion hardware interface used primarily in legacy laptops to add extra capabilities such as extra memory, network cards, Wi-Fi, Ethernet, or modem capabilities.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3a750653-2fc7-4436-8474-da379b64242b",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "4. Output Devices Overview",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3ace3814-f3cd-4e90-94af-930d34d0ad48",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "DEFINITION",
      "title": "Output Device",
      "content": "An Output Device is a peripheral hardware component that receives processed binary data (0s and 1s) from the CPU, translates it into a human-understandable format, and presents it to the user."
    },
    {
      "id": "4acdcae1-209a-4334-bb3c-6104fa7dda8e",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Soft Copy vs. Hard Copy",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c7e227d1-7d56-4686-8b5c-d0a9872f2590",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Soft Copy",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e9e9bf7c-24a3-44d2-976d-0f5e19a279a9",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Soft Copy is temporary, non-persistent electronic visual or audio output. Examples include display monitors, projectors, and speakers.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "20407bdc-ddb3-4a62-be53-6c462af09272",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Hard Copy",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ea715acc-6481-47db-a92b-7e3779ab55f4",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Hard Copy is permanent, physical output generated on paper or other physical media. Examples include printer printouts and plotter engineering sheets.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "735218eb-5761-44c6-aea4-6bf5f8da3d94",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "5. Visual Display Units (Monitors \/ VDU)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "88b3f040-335f-4e27-a7c6-4455a0c5f87e",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Visual Display Unit (VDU) or Monitor is the primary soft-copy visual output hardware connected to a computer system. It displays text, graphics, and video output.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "470d95c5-f589-429b-9695-f2cac2346fc3",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "A. Display Modes",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5d5c4a54-7470-4873-a223-e542aded72d6",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Monochrome Display Monitor",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "14f8e986-b769-4c51-bf0e-19f537092bf8",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Monochrome Display Monitor displays images using a single active foreground color, such as white, green, or amber, against a dark background. It relies on different intensity levels of one color to render text and simple shapes.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "727479b8-9088-40c9-b1e3-33991e16eea5",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Color Display Monitor",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e8b887b4-a31f-4820-a9e4-acedd2112527",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Color Display Monitor uses combinations of RGB (Red, Green, Blue) color signals to generate millions of distinct colors for individual pixels on the screen.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7a5ca107-7a4c-41d5-a36e-364c54ca0af0",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "B. Technical Specifications of Monitors",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e197e65e-f254-4232-8aa4-092fc1bc4495",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "Technical Specifications of Monitors",
      "nodes": [
        "Monitor Specs",
        "Screen Resolution",
        "Dot Pitch",
        "Refresh Rate"
      ],
      "rawContent": "             [Monitor Specs]\n             \/      |      \\\n[Screen Resolution] [Dot Pitch] [Refresh Rate]"
    },
    {
      "id": "778d3c72-3164-43cf-b3f7-63b46c54bed7",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Screen Resolution",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5a5aa075-262d-42b5-bbed-6895f8b01e94",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Screen Resolution refers to the total number of individual pixels (Picture Elements) arranged horizontally and vertically across a display. For example: Full HD = 1920 × 1080 pixels. Higher resolution generally provides clearer and more detailed images.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7b0d6152-ea15-4843-913c-678fa41a6c84",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Dot Pitch",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "4eb808c6-f783-4ae1-ad88-e28399260392",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Dot Pitch is the distance measured in millimeters between two adjacent sub-pixels or dots of the same color on a display screen. A smaller dot pitch generally results in a sharper and clearer image.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d87f325d-cee6-4f71-94e9-37834567feac",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Refresh Rate",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ecd51620-4166-4bfb-a5f6-432978d74b95",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Refresh Rate is the frequency at which a monitor repaints or redraws the displayed image per second. It is measured in Hertz (Hz). Examples include: 60 Hz, 144 Hz. Higher refresh rates reduce visual flickering and motion blur.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fda15cfa-f433-41e1-a6a4-8f270b5c4bbf",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "C. Types of Display Monitors",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b455ad73-34b8-4bb3-8a16-cab442a852be",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "CRT — Cathode Ray Tube\nLCD — Liquid Crystal Display\nLED — Light Emitting Diode\nTFT — Thin Film Transistor\n3D Monitor — Three-Dimensional Monitor",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "af3ebb11-72cb-4d21-9c81-59dbcf40f29e",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "CRT — Cathode Ray Tube",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "66d05a01-6d68-46b6-8cc1-9257022f2c22",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Operational Mechanism: CRT monitors use electron guns that emit streams of electrons toward a phosphorescent glass screen.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7e8c4fda-524a-4222-85dc-68b23d188bac",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Bulky and heavy\nHigh power consumption\nProduces heat\nHigher display latency compared to modern panels",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "263f2a99-9748-44b4-9ff5-8f1946a19ac0",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "LCD — Liquid Crystal Display",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a14bf71a-64d0-42ff-99b6-ea19e79d840a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Operational Mechanism: LCD monitors use liquid crystals placed between two polarizing filter sheets. Electric currents align the crystals to block or allow light to pass through.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "687b6ba3-3427-4664-ba44-b1913f9008d1",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Flat-panel design\nEnergy-efficient and lightweight\nProduces minimal eye strain\nRequires background backlighting",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "84ec0be6-e001-44d5-9836-f424c210aab4",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "LED — Light Emitting Diode",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fbaf6c0a-0f32-457d-b715-973cd222bb00",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Operational Mechanism: LED monitors are an advanced variant of LCD monitors that use energy-efficient Light Emitting Diodes as backlighting instead of CCFL (Cold-Cathode Fluorescent Lamp) tubes.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8500e6d4-9437-498f-9ada-968223ff2056",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "High contrast ratio\nThinner profile\nLower energy consumption\nSuperior color reproduction",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b17137aa-b1b7-4aff-98ec-2685e4f18b39",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "TFT — Thin Film Transistor",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e4ca9bd5-22bc-4be5-bcbc-a2a28b238dc1",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Operational Mechanism: TFT is an Active-Matrix LCD technology in which each pixel is controlled by its own dedicated microscopic transistor.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9ab22645-1eac-4a10-90f1-16714b2864f7",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "High contrast\nFaster response times\nHelps eliminate ghosting in moving visuals",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b50b1c00-1a42-424f-b4af-aae09f3df6e9",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "3D Monitor — Three-Dimensional Monitor",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "eb280d8a-aa17-4388-a229-d90e7fb3e16e",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Operational Mechanism: A 3D monitor uses stereoscopic or autostereoscopic, glasses-free, display technology to project slightly offset images to each eye.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "92bee2c7-1c2b-4aa4-9711-6e01e43ab01d",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Creates an illusion of depth\nProvides spatial dimensions\nUsed in CAD, medical imaging, and gaming",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fda77a0f-2dcd-4f3a-9624-9bc60192f290",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "6. Printers",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8b79c499-cacd-460e-bb85-14598a427c9a",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Printer is an external hard-copy output device that receives processed text and image data from a computer and transfers it onto paper or transparency sheets.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "1970a348-f74a-4f91-8f0d-a8e89d4c8b48",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "Printer Classification",
      "nodes": [
        "Printer Types",
        "Impact Printers",
        "Non-Impact"
      ],
      "rawContent": "     [Printer Types]\n        \/        \\\n[Impact Printers] [Non-Impact]"
    },
    {
      "id": "a2bec0c6-f436-4992-b6af-61199633143c",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Impact Printers",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "dce54d64-651a-4d58-b049-31b050cbc1c2",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Impact Printers form characters or images through physical mechanical contact. They strike an inked ribbon directly against the paper using pins or print hammers.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b5d082d3-108b-44e4-85ae-092150500bff",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Extremely noisy\nSlow speed\nLower print quality\nLow operational cost per page\nCapable of printing multi-part carbon copies",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "85584f26-4df7-4a07-8e45-f3aa361294d2",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "Impact Printer Types",
      "nodes": [
        "Impact Printers",
        "Dot Matrix",
        "Daisy Wheel",
        "Line Printers"
      ],
      "rawContent": "             [Impact Printers]\n             \/       |       \\\n[Dot Matrix]   [Daisy Wheel]   [Line Printers]"
    },
    {
      "id": "0d930412-8bfd-4057-a142-64bdc07a5fe4",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Dot Matrix Printer",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9d5d9d04-776c-4198-9188-39349211caa2",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Dot Matrix Printer uses a printhead containing a vertical column of pins, usually 9 to 24 pins. The pins strike an inked ribbon to form characters using matrix dot patterns.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fad26a68-5b30-4025-8878-7085eedc3d77",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Daisy Wheel Printer",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b4bb4372-06f6-48d2-b44c-614a9891f400",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Daisy Wheel Printer uses a wheel with petaled arms containing pre-formed raised characters. The wheel rotates to position the required character, which is then struck by a tiny hammer against the ribbon.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "726a37ba-f56b-46d8-b8fc-de58461c0cba",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Line Printers (Drum \/ Chain Printers)",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "50640ece-e473-44da-8322-77c987ff145c",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Line Printers print an entire line of text at a time. They use either a fast-rotating character drum or a continuous print chain.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b853af86-47a2-4bc7-94c2-6cd77f14857c",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Non-Impact Printers",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "483f99fe-f826-47d6-8757-ce07d4adbcf7",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Non-Impact Printers produce characters and graphics on paper without using physical mechanical striking mechanisms.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b3b2295a-94ed-455a-9706-9165e3bea527",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Very quiet\nHigh speed\nOutstanding print quality\nHigher hardware cost\nCannot produce physical carbon-copy duplicates",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b460972b-bbf4-494b-ae9b-bd6726d9e2be",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "Non-Impact Printer Types",
      "nodes": [
        "Non-Impact Printers",
        "Laser Printer",
        "Inkjet Printer",
        "Thermal Printer"
      ],
      "rawContent": "             [Non-Impact Printers]\n             \/         |         \\\n[Laser Printer] [Inkjet Printer] [Thermal Printer]"
    },
    {
      "id": "1bbfc7c9-f058-49fb-bd63-42776e2d4e0e",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Laser Printer",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"

    {
      "id": "0800da57-041e-4b9d-9590-848478db417d",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Laser Printer uses a rotating electrostatic photoreceptor drum, a laser beam, and dry pulverized powder called Toner. Heat and pressure rollers fuse the toner onto paper, producing crisp text and graphics at high speeds.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9f736071-828c-4387-9ef8-3d5b3bfe7fc4",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Inkjet Printer",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f1d7387f-545a-4d3b-83ce-d37dba635938",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "An Inkjet Printer sprays microscopic droplets of liquid ink from specialized nozzles directly onto paper to create images.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d3ca9ba6-aab2-4d78-9af5-db3192b76b7e",
      "type": "HEADING_4",
      "text": "Thermal Printer",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "31728d56-caa3-40ee-b443-e21a3f47b7ac",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Thermal Printer uses heat-activated paper, also called thermo-chromic paper, which is pushed against a heated printhead. The paper darkens where it is heated. Common uses include ATM receipts and POS terminals.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "83855828-d26c-475e-8159-2c7f357ddda1",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "7. Plotters",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e698527c-b1d4-4b41-820d-d57a9d6857cc",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Plotter is a specialized, vector-graphic hard-copy output device designed to produce high-precision blueprints, engineering schematics, architectural layouts, and GIS maps. Unlike standard printers that generate raster images line-by-line, plotters use automated continuous pen mechanisms to draw precise continuous lines directly onto paper.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {

    {
      "id": "2419b39e-d74c-435a-b1cc-42e6d28b1e7e",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Flatbed Plotter",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "3b7bbbd2-bfd3-4848-b258-8519c7848d3b",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Flatbed Plotter holds the paper flat on a stationary rectangular bed. A mechanical arm carrying pens moves across the X-axis (Horizontal) and Y-axis (Vertical) to draw graphics.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0dad993a-e19e-46b4-bf4b-d11323203dbb",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Drum Plotter",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d135a7a3-7c01-4769-947b-415bf8ef97be",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Drum Plotter wraps the paper around a cylindrical rotating drum. The drum moves the paper back and forth along the Y-axis, while a pen carriage slides left and right along the X-axis on a fixed horizontal beam.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,

      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b610b53a-ab7f-48b2-9bf7-1eb24ccc1486",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "8. Audio & Visual Output Hardware",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "b6bba188-b6cd-4757-ba32-336b842c6482",
      "type": "DIAGRAM",
      "diagramType": "TREE",
      "title": "Audio & Visual Output Hardware",
      "nodes": [
        "Audio & Visual Hardware",
        "Speaker",
        "Headphones",
        "Projector"

      "rawContent": "             [Audio & Visual Hardware]\n             \/           |           \\\n        [Speaker]   [Headphones]   [Projector]"

    {
      "id": "77ab803f-5227-43a0-969b-52bf2c89a246",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Speaker",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c60eb3d7-6cad-4ab9-9bde-a525fd69c887",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Speaker is an electro-acoustic transducer output device that converts digital audio signals processed by the sound card into physical audible sound waves.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9eba50b3-cd5e-43f4-9dfa-f03eb80c4af7",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Headphones",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c0bbba7b-0261-4259-9319-740b74b153c8",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "Headphones are personal audio output transducers designed to be worn over or inside a user's ears for private audio listening.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cb421a98-058d-4ce9-9c6b-ef7b81b44e4e",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Projector",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c4ec5372-8d09-43d0-b74f-5d42eb40b1b6",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "A Projector is an optical soft-copy output device that receives video signals from a computer and projects enlarged images onto a wall or large projection screen. It uses powerful lamps or laser light sources to produce the projected image.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "68ae0f7e-4e45-4596-8bb7-2a8ba0b3aaf7",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "Key Revision Points",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "65a4ec24-deff-4796-a26f-4708bde4a422",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Computer Hardware: Physical and tangible components of a computer system that can be touched, seen, and handled.\nInput Device: Hardware used to enter raw data, instructions, and commands into a computer.\nKeyboard: Primary text-entry and command device; commonly uses the QWERTY layout.\nMouse: Pointing device that detects 2D movement using optical sensors or laser technology.\nTrackball: Stationary pointing device with a rotating ball operated by the fingers or palm.\nJoystick: Pointing\/control device used mainly in gaming, flight simulation, robotics, and industrial systems.\nLight Pen: Light-sensitive input device historically used with CRT monitors.\nTouch Screen: Input-output device that detects touch using technologies such as resistive, capacitive, and infrared.\nBarcode Reader (BCR): Reads barcodes using reflected light and converts them into digital data.\nOMR: Detects marked areas on pre-printed forms, commonly used for objective examination sheets.\nOCR: Converts printed or handwritten text into editable and searchable digital text.\nMICR: Reads characters printed with magnetic ink, mainly used for processing bank cheques.\nSmart Card Reader: Reads information stored on an IC chip embedded in a smart card.\nBiometric Sensor: Captures unique biological or behavioral characteristics for identity authentication.\nScanner: Converts physical documents, photographs, and graphics into digital image files.\nMicrophone: Converts sound waves into electrical signals that can be processed by a computer.\nWebcam: Captures real-time video and still images.\nPC Card (PCMCIA): Removable expansion interface historically used in laptops for memory, networking, and modem capabilities.\nOutput Device: Hardware that presents processed computer data in a human-understandable form.\nSoft Copy: Temporary electronic output such as monitor, projector, and speaker output.\nHard Copy: Permanent physical output such as printed documents and plotter drawings.\nVDU: Visual Display Unit; another name for a computer monitor.\nMonochrome Monitor: Displays information using a single foreground color.\nColor Monitor: Uses RGB (Red, Green, Blue) signals to produce multiple colors.\nScreen Resolution: Number of pixels arranged horizontally and vertically on a display.\nDot Pitch: Distance between adjacent dots\/sub-pixels of the same color; smaller dot pitch generally gives sharper images.\nRefresh Rate: Number of times a monitor refreshes its display per second, measured in Hz.\nCRT: Older display technology using electron guns and a phosphorescent screen.\nLCD: Flat-panel display technology using liquid crystals and backlighting.\nLED: LCD-based display technology using LEDs for backlighting.\nTFT: Active-Matrix LCD technology in which individual pixels are controlled by dedicated transistors.\n3D Monitor: Creates an illusion of depth by presenting slightly different images to each eye.\nPrinter: Hard-copy output device that transfers computer-generated text and images onto physical media.\nImpact Printer: Prints through physical mechanical contact with an inked ribbon.\nDot Matrix Printer: Impact printer that forms characters using pins and dot patterns.\nDaisy Wheel Printer: Impact printer using a wheel containing raised characters.\nLine Printer: Prints an entire line at a time using a drum or chain mechanism.\nNon-Impact Printer: Prints without physically striking the paper.\nLaser Printer: Uses laser technology, an electrostatic drum, and toner to produce high-quality prints.\nInkjet Printer: Produces images by spraying tiny droplets of liquid ink onto paper.\nThermal Printer: Uses heat-sensitive paper and a heated printhead; commonly used for receipts.\nPlotter: Specialized output device used for high-precision engineering, architectural, and GIS drawings.\nFlatbed Plotter: Holds paper flat while a pen mechanism moves across X and Y axes.\nDrum Plotter: Uses a rotating cylindrical drum to move paper while the pen carriage moves across the other axis.\nSpeaker: Converts processed digital audio signals into audible sound.\nHeadphones: Provide private personal audio output.\nProjector: Enlarges computer-generated visual output onto a wall or projection screen.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e29098fc-9f04-42b1-a23c-9f9e94f537c1",
      "type": "CALLOUT",
      "calloutType": "EXAM_TIP",
      "title": "Exam Focus Quick Reference",
      "content": "• Input = Data goes INTO the computer\n• Output = Processed information comes OUT of the computer\n• Soft Copy = Electronic output\n• Hard Copy = Physical output\n• OMR = Marks\n• OCR = Text\n• MICR = Cheques\n• BCR = Barcodes\n• Impact Printer = Physical contact\n• Non-Impact Printer = No physical striking\n• Laser Printer = Toner\n• Inkjet Printer = Liquid ink\n• Thermal Printer = Heat\n• CRT = Electron gun\n• LCD = Liquid crystals\n• LED = LED backlighting\n• TFT = Transistor-controlled pixels\n• Plotter = Precision drawings"
    }
  ]
}

{
  "chapterId": "chap_0d5f4dcf",
  "title": "history of kashmir",
  "elements": [
    {
      "id": "dbfe3b26-4873-4aed-8640-9fe42b35eff0",
      "type": "HEADING_1",
      "text": "CHAPTER 2: HISTORY OF KASHMIR",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "442269d8-6db9-4095-9b2f-16b9711b4d96",
      "type": "HEADING_2",
      "text": "1. INTRODUCTION AND SOURCES OF KASHMIR HISTORY",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "f602cef2-7d07-4582-8f57-a3ed38cec4ec",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "There are several ways of reconstructing the past of Kashmir. Kashmiris, who distinguished themselves in many branches of Sanskrit learning, were also meticulous historians who left an almost continuous written record of the valley's history. These histories are supplemented by archeological, numismatic, and foreign accounts.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "06651f77-55f3-4388-a237-aa07ee729854",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Primary Historical Sources",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0d2f766a-6728-48af-aee8-ebdaee3a2b6f",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Written Records: Comprehensive court chronicles, religious texts, and dynastic biographies.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ea9b7ef2-3876-400b-a386-1ac0fa457293",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Archaeological Evidence: Excavations of ancient cities, temples, and megalithic sites.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "79c5a86a-6d62-4c66-ac6d-f3edc5258e76",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Numismatic Evidence: Ancient coins providing chronological markers and economic indicators.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "78af3cad-ff87-4c02-bd72-167ca7ae5eef",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Foreign Accounts: Travelogues of Chinese pilgrims, Tibetan scholars, Mughal chroniclers, and European explorers.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9f8eec0c-07a8-44b6-ba69-23b94bd4c905",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Sanskrit and Early Chronicles",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c9f78223-9289-42fe-b527-67800abb91eb",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Kalhana and the Rajatarangini: Written by the 12th-century poet-historian Kalhana between AD 1148 and 1149, the Rajatarangini (The River of Kings) is a landmark historical chronicle. Written in Sanskrit, it contains valuable political, social, and cultural information. Kalhana consulted eleven earlier chronicles, most of which are now lost, to construct his narrative.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "5e3eb4f7-f901-44a5-9bb9-398d12315b04",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "The Nilamat Purana: The earliest known text of Kashmir. It contains sacred legends regarding the origin of the valley and details the religious rites, festivals, and worship ceremonies prescribed by Nila, the Lord of the Kashmir Nagas.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a3c2392d-aaf1-4d7b-8bda-a94805493e14",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Haracharitachintamani: Authored by Jayadratha, this text deals specifically with sacred sites, pilgrimages, and local Shaivite traditions.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "8752b57b-0008-46a6-92c7-4c1de468033a",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Muslim Period Chronicles",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "279826a9-1704-4d6e-a69c-62203daf5176",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "During the Muslim period, Persian replaced Sanskrit as the language of the court. However, rulers like Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin actively patronized scholars of both languages and commissioned updates to the historical record:",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "d270b73b-cd1e-4b2d-901c-8758a49eb5fb",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Jonaraja: A Sanskrit chronicler who brought the Rajatarangini up to date. His work, the Dvitiya Rajatarangini (Second Rajatarangini \/ Rajavali), covers the reigns of late Hindu rulers from Jayasimha to Queen Didda.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "be0c7a71-6a73-4529-b44a-f6690ac5e0d9",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Mulla Ahmad: A Persian scholar who translated Kalhana’s Rajatarangini into Persian under the title Bahr-ul-Asman (The Ocean of Activity) at the behest of Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "295f993e-23e4-4fa2-a735-4ef278d1ea70",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Malik Haider: Wrote the Tarikh-i-Kashmir (History of Kashmir) in Persian, providing a valuable internal perspective on the transition to Mughal rule.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "929f3a11-ca0c-49b0-8453-4d7f2c312dac",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Mughal Imperial Records: Abul Fazl’s Akbarnama and Ain-e-Akbari offer highly detailed assessments of Kashmir’s revenue system, geography, administration, crafts, and arts following its integration into the Mughal Empire.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "fa0727db-d9d0-455f-ae31-76444bdb8681",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Accounts of Foreign Travellers",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "9db4190d-9fca-4d54-8437-83284a1ff3bf",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang): Visited the valley in AD 631 during the Karkota dynasty. He entered through the stone gate at Baramulla and recorded the historical conversion of Kashmiris to Buddhism by the missionary Majjhantika.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "0fcf8c89-ee00-476b-b1e8-291fd3593987",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Ou-Kong: Visited Kashmir in the middle of the 8th century AD. He described Kashmir as a secure kingdom enclosed by a ring of mountains and mapped out mountain routes leading to Tibet (East), Baltistan (North), and Gandhara (West).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "af03dc57-11ee-4c1d-a432-dfbdc6388b5a",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Alberuni: In his treatise Kitab-ul-Hind, he gave an accurate account of the valley's geography, customs, and isolationist policies, confirming contemporaneous Sanskrit records.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "cb490412-8894-4fac-acce-ebe5532ee73a",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "European Travellers:",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "ecdbc2f7-77fb-4571-ba54-843b9aa07b03",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Father Jerome Xavier: Accompanied Emperor Akbar to the valley.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e81acfc6-cd88-4ed6-8c2b-042ac3da69f9",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Francois Bernier: Visited during the reign of Aurangzeb (AD 1665).",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "141771b0-7934-4952-953e-d6d88573a9b4",
      "type": "BULLET_LIST",
      "text": "Later Observers: Desideri, George Forester, G.T. Vigne, Frederic Drew, Sir Walter Lawrence, and Alexander Cunningham visited Kashmir during the Dogra and British periods, leaving comprehensive records of the state's geography, flora, and administration.",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "82fadb57-3027-410d-97b1-a1d39ee7ac86",
      "type": "HEADING_3",
      "text": "Important Books & Authors on Kashmir History",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },

    {

      "isStrikethrough": false,

    },
    {
      "id": "aadf7a27-dbf5-44aa-9f5c-decda93753b1",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "| Rajatarangini (English) | M.A. Stein | Definitive translation with critical notes and geographical identifications. |",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,

      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "79e5f864-d9ce-42ab-93cf-7d255f9f998f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "| Rajatarangini (Kashmiri) | Dr. Bashar Basheer | Kashmiri translation of the 1st, 2nd, and 8th parts of the chronicle. |",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,

      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e5f0e7d5-8fd4-436f-b588-6b35c17b7369",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "| Twarikh-i-Kashmir | Malik Haider | Medieval Persian chronicle written during the Mughal transition. |",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a522588a-4ecc-4bad-a480-61f0d18f24ba",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "| Waqt-e-Kashmir | Khawaja Mohammad | Historical development and administrative structures of the valley. |",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "94c158e0-c526-4010-b698-f4df5aff5283",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "| Muktasar Tarikh-i-Kashmir | Birbal Kachru | Concise Persian account of the socio-political shifts in Kashmir. |",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "7ef51d6a-3533-4b6b-aa81-8f72aaf3764f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "| Tarikh-i-Hassan | Pir Hassan Shah | Highly regarded, multi-volume history of Kashmir's dynasties. |",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "c2658c3b-6971-45bd-85a1-1ec0cfe31331",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "| Zaffar Nama | Sharif-ud-din Yazdi | Detailed military history of Central Asia, Timur, and interactions with Kashmir. |",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "e427b91a-2beb-4ca2-a255-d596eab2cc4f",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "| Valley of Kashmir | Sir Walter Lawrence | Extensive land settlement records, socioeconomic analysis, and folklore. |",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
      "id": "a91120d0-1160-440c-bb0b-3fb77e809bdb",
      "type": "PARAGRAPH",
      "text": "| Land of Lamas | Alexander Cunningham | Geographical and cultural study of Ladakh, Baltistan, and surrounding areas. |",
      "isBold": false,
      "isItalic": false,
      "isUnderline": false,
      "isStrikethrough": false,
      "textColorHex": "",
      "highlightColorHex": "",
      "alignment": "LEFT"
    },
    {
